Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and generating residue sets of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.

- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.
- N(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- O(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, one has $\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)=\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)$.

(ii) Consequently $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis of $V(\lambda)$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a crystal lattice of $V(\lambda)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$, the operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ and the partial-inverse axiom, and $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ for all $\mu$. The lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ are free $A_0$-modules.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S$ generated by $\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

derivations.claim: Clause (a). Since the grand loop holds for every $r$, clause L(r) at $r=\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$ is exactly $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

Clause (b). Clause M(r) is the first congruence, and clause O(r) is the second equality in the crystal limit; the equivalence with $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on the residue classes of $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ follows because both sides of the congruence are computed modulo $q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i$ preserves both lattices by their defining lowering-word construction.

Clause (c). Clause N(r) states precisely that $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection from the surviving elements of $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$; its proof applies J(r) and therefore the AC-dependent form comparison, while nothing in (a), (b) or (d) needs it.

Clause (d). For large weights the grand-loop large-weight computation gives that $\pi_\lambda$ is an isomorphism on the component and a bijection on its residue bases; those congruences are used as an input inside the loop to derive the general clauses, and the present clauses (a)-(c) do not assume the largeness.

Choice. All congruences in (a), (b) and (d) take place between finitely generated $A_0$-modules and use only the operators and the string decomposition, so they are choice-free; clause (c) inherits the declared axiom of choice through J(r) and the negative-half form comparison.

boundaries.evidence: At $\alpha=0$ one has $\mathcal L(\infty)_0=A_0\mathbf 1$ and $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\lambda=A_0v_\lambda$ with $\pi_\lambda(\mathbf 1)=v_\lambda$; step 1.1's clause L(r) is the identity between these one-dimensional modules, and clauses (b)-(d) are vacuous or scalar there.

Step 1.2: Raising compatibility is restricted to nonzero projected basis residues. Lowering compatibility holds for all residues, including killed ones. Zero component and empty surviving-fibre cases are covered by the same linear congruences.

Step 1.1: The simple-root half lattice is $A_0F_i$. Its module image is $A_0F_iv_\lambda$ when $\lambda(h_i)>0$ and zero when that label is zero; the surviving residue fibre is correspondingly a singleton or empty.

No largeness hypothesis is used in clauses (a)-(c): step 1.4 records that the large-weight isomorphisms of clause (d) are computations used inside the grand loop, not assumptions of the general clauses.

The endpoint of the surviving range is the transition $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$ versus $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$: step 1.3's bijection is from exactly the surviving set, and step 1.2's $\tilde f_i$-compatibility is stated on all of $\mathcal B(\infty)_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$, including elements whose images may leave the surviving range.

Step 2.1 records the exact split: clauses (a), (b) and (d) are choice-free congruences between finitely generated $A_0$-modules, while clause (c) inherits the declared axiom of choice through J(r) and the negative-half form comparison.

boundaries.reason: The lemma transports clauses L, M, N and O of the grand loop as inputs and proves no new biconditional; step 1.2's "equivalently" restates the $\tilde f_i$-compatibility on residue classes rather than asserting an implication pair.

No converse direction is proved or needed: the two halves of clause (b) are the raising and lowering compatibilities, which are independent equalities modulo $q$, and clause (c) is a bijection statement.

risk_review.notes: Read all five steps with reviewed grand-loop L/M/N/O clauses and current lattice/negative-half definitions. Each claimed quantifier matches its exact clause: lowering compatibility is general, raising only for surviving residues, and basis projection is restricted to survivors. Both lattices have lowering stability from prepending words, so passage modulo q is justified independently of raising clauses A/B. Degree-zero and absent root-component cases hold; large lambda degree injection uses the singular-generator bound. JKK pp.34–35,40–41,47 and Kashiwara Theorem 5 p.488 confirm the survival caveat. Conservative AC dependency remains; the current loop gives a finite constant-term alternative when establishing the clauses described as choice-free. Reader correction of the lattice-stability justification is sound.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.
Every finitely generated torsion-free module over a principal ideal domain is finite free.

Let $q$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$$A_0:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}=\Big\{\frac fg\ :\ f,g\in\mathbb Q[q],\ g(0)\neq0\Big\}\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$$
be the localisation of the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q[q]$ at the prime ideal $(q)$ ([[def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal]]). By [[ex-the-local-ring-of-polynomials-at-x]] with $F=\mathbb Q$, the ring $A_0$ is exactly the ring of rational functions regular at $q=0$, it is a local ring ([[def-local-ring]]) with unique maximal ideal $qA_0$, and evaluation at $0$ induces an isomorphism $A_0/qA_0\cong\mathbb Q$. Since $\mathbb Q[q]$ is a principal ideal domain ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-pid]]) with nonzero prime ideal $(q)$, the ring $A_0$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal; by the discrete valuation ring characterisations it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser $q/1$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]], [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and in particular a principal ideal domain ([[cor-dvr-is-a-pid]], [[def-principal-ideal-domain]]), with field of fractions $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field]]).

By [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] a discrete valuation ring is the valuation ring $V_v=\{x:v(x)\ge0\}$ of a discrete valuation $v$ on its fraction field. The discrete valuation of $\mathbb Q(q)$ with $V_v=A_0$ and $v(q)=1$ is the **$q$-adic valuation**; write it $\operatorname{ord}_q$, so that
$$\operatorname{ord}_q:\mathbb Q(q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\cup\{\infty\},\qquad A_0=\{h\in\mathbb Q(q):\operatorname{ord}_q(h)\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_q(q)=1 .$$
Equivalently, $\operatorname{ord}_q$ is the vanishing order at $q=0$. The units of $A_0$ are exactly the fractions $f/g$ with $f(0)\neq0$ and $g(0)\neq0$, and $qA_0$ is the maximal ideal, so $q$ is a uniformiser of $A_0$ ([[thm-localisation-at-a-prime-is-local]]).

This ring $A_0$ is the **crystal limiting ring** of the crystal development below, and it is different from the Laurent ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ of [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]: $q^{-1}\in A\setminus A_0$, while $(1+q)^{-1}\in A_0\setminus A$; neither ring contains the other, and both are subrings of $\mathbb Q(q)$. For every free $A_0$-module $L$ the canonical map
$$\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L\longrightarrow L/qL,\qquad c\otimes\ell\mapsto c\,\ell+qL,$$
is an isomorphism, and for every $\lambda\in\mathbb Q(q)^\times$ one has $\lambda L/q\lambda L\cong L/qL$; passing from $L$ to $L/qL$ is the **crystal limit**. No freeness of any further module, no lattice and no choice principle is asserted here.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and generating residue sets of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.

- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.
- N(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- O(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, one has $\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)=\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)$.

(ii) Consequently $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis of $V(\lambda)$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a crystal lattice of $V(\lambda)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$, the operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ and the partial-inverse axiom, and $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ for all $\mu$. The lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ are free $A_0$-modules.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

We also write $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ for the datum's integer pairing $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Freeness and scalar extension. Each component is finitely generated and torsionfree, hence free over the PID $A_0$ by [F1]. As in the grand-loop conclusion [F2], enumerate $A_0$ and the finite ordered word generators of each component and take the first finite tuple of their linear combinations that is a basis. These uniquely specified component bases unite to a basis of the graded direct sum without simultaneous choice. For field spanning, use the grand-loop field-spanning argument [F2]: if $x=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n$ is homogeneous, then $F_ix=\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_n[n+1]_iF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr)$, and the vector in parentheses has the same root degree as $x$. Thus every positive-height component, being the sum of the $F_i$-images of preceding components, is also spanned by their $\tilde f_i$-images. Induction from $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\mathbf1$ shows that the lowering words span each field component. The canonical map $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\to U_q^-[-\alpha]$ is therefore surjective. It is injective by clearing denominators: a finite tensor sum equals $d^{-1}\otimes z$ for some $0\ne d\in A_0$ and $z\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$, and its image $d^{-1}z$ vanishes only when $z=0$. Taking graded direct sums gives the claimed scalar-extension isomorphism.

Stability and residue basis. Stability under $\tilde f_i$ holds by construction, since a $\tilde f_i$-image of a lowering monomial is a lowering monomial; stability under $\tilde e_i$ is clause H(r). Clause K(r) says that $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$, and clause I(r) gives $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$. For $\tilde f_i$, the image of a monomial is a monomial and $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ prevents it from vanishing modulo $q$: if $\tilde f_ib\in q\mathcal L(\infty)$ then $b=\tilde e_i\tilde f_ib\in q\mathcal L(\infty)$, contradicting $b\neq0$ in the crystal limit.

The partial-inverse axiom. If $\tilde f_ib=b'$ with $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$, then applying $\tilde e_i$ and [F3] gives $b=\tilde e_i\tilde f_ib=\tilde e_ib'$. Conversely, if $b=\tilde e_ib'\neq0$, then $b'=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib'$ by clause J(r), so $\tilde f_ib=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib'=b'$ by [F3]; hence $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, and this is the only place where the grand-loop clause J(r), and with it the inherited axiom of choice, is used.

The projection statements. The lattice projection, surviving-residue bijection and operator compatibilities in (iii) are [F4]. To see that zero is also attained, fix $i\in I$: by step 1.2 every $\tilde f_i^n\mathbf1$ has nonzero negative-half residue, while lowering compatibility projects it to $\tilde f_i^nv_\lambda$. The latter is zero for sufficiently large $n$ because the module lowering length is finite by [F5]. Thus the image is exactly $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$.

The rank formula. By [F1] and clause K(r), the free rank of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$, and by step 1.1 the scalar extension is $U_q^-[-\alpha]$, so this number is also $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\alpha]$; this is (ii).

The infinite chain. By [F3] the operator $\tilde f_i$ is injective on $U_q^-$ and $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$, and by step 1.2 no iterate of a residue element vanishes; hence $\ell_i^-=+\infty$ for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$, while $\varepsilon_i(b)<\infty$ by the finite string structure of the negative half (the height bound). The formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ is the convention of [F5] and is not the lowering-chain length.

boundaries.evidence: The degree-zero component is $\mathcal L(\infty)_0=A_0\mathbf 1$ with the single residue class of the unit, and step 1.1's freeness argument includes $\nu=0$; the root-graded sum has one term in degree zero, so the empty-word case is the top of the crystal.

The zero element is not a basis element: step 1.2 applies clause K(r), which makes $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ a $\mathbb Q$-basis of the component's crystal limit, and the operator values land in $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ with the zero reserved for killed elements.

For a simple root $\alpha_i$ the component is $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha_i}=A_0F_i$ with a single residue element; steps 1.2 and 1.3 verify the axioms on it, and step 2.1's rank formula reads $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha_i}=1=\dim U_q^-[-\alpha_i]$.

Step 3.1: No residue lowering iterate vanishes because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ on the quotient. Hence $\ell_i^-=\infty$; the formal integer $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ remains finite and may be negative.

The top of a string is a residue $b$ with $\tilde e_ib=0$, i.e. the residue of an element of $\ker e_i'$ by [F3]; step 3.1 reads the infinite chain from this top, and in (iii) the endpoint of the surviving range is the class with $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$, handled by the bijection onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$.

The axiom of choice enters only through the partial-inverse axiom in (i), via clause J(r): step 1.3 proves the forward direction with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}$ from [F3] and the converse with J(r); the freeness and rank statements of steps 1.1 and 2.1 are choice-free.
The forward direction of the biconditional in (i): if $\tilde f_ib=b'$ then applying $\tilde e_i$ gives $b=\tilde e_i\tilde f_ib=\tilde e_ib'$ by [F3], as computed in step 1.3.

The converse direction: if $b=\tilde e_ib'\ne0$ then $b'=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib'$ by clause J(r) of the grand loop, hence $\tilde f_ib=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib'=b'$ by [F3]; step 1.3 states both directions of the partial-inverse axiom.

risk_review.notes: Read all six steps against reviewed grand-loop H/I/J/K, projection L/M/N/O, negative-half strings and graph conventions. The grand-loop field span and explicit least-index component bases establish full free lattice and ranks even for the infinite graded direct sum. e-tilde f-tilde=id descends to residues and prevents all lowering iterates from vanishing; J supplies the reverse partial-inverse direction. Phi-free projection package is exactly the reviewed survivor statement; zero images exist beyond any fixed simple highest string. Degree zero has unit residue, epsilon is height-bounded, formal phi stays an integer and is distinct from infinite lowering length. Sources JKK §§6–7 pp.22–48 and Kashiwara Theorems 4–5 pp.486–488 confirm conclusions. Reader removal of the false infinite formal-phi assertion is correct; inherited AC remains declared.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $q$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$$A_0:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}=\Big\{\frac fg\ :\ f,g\in\mathbb Q[q],\ g(0)\neq0\Big\}\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$$
be the localisation of the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q[q]$ at the prime ideal $(q)$ ([[def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal]]). By [[ex-the-local-ring-of-polynomials-at-x]] with $F=\mathbb Q$, the ring $A_0$ is exactly the ring of rational functions regular at $q=0$, it is a local ring ([[def-local-ring]]) with unique maximal ideal $qA_0$, and evaluation at $0$ induces an isomorphism $A_0/qA_0\cong\mathbb Q$. Since $\mathbb Q[q]$ is a principal ideal domain ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-pid]]) with nonzero prime ideal $(q)$, the ring $A_0$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal; by the discrete valuation ring characterisations it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser $q/1$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]], [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and in particular a principal ideal domain ([[cor-dvr-is-a-pid]], [[def-principal-ideal-domain]]), with field of fractions $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field]]).

By [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] a discrete valuation ring is the valuation ring $V_v=\{x:v(x)\ge0\}$ of a discrete valuation $v$ on its fraction field. The discrete valuation of $\mathbb Q(q)$ with $V_v=A_0$ and $v(q)=1$ is the **$q$-adic valuation**; write it $\operatorname{ord}_q$, so that
$$\operatorname{ord}_q:\mathbb Q(q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\cup\{\infty\},\qquad A_0=\{h\in\mathbb Q(q):\operatorname{ord}_q(h)\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_q(q)=1 .$$
Equivalently, $\operatorname{ord}_q$ is the vanishing order at $q=0$. The units of $A_0$ are exactly the fractions $f/g$ with $f(0)\neq0$ and $g(0)\neq0$, and $qA_0$ is the maximal ideal, so $q$ is a uniformiser of $A_0$ ([[thm-localisation-at-a-prime-is-local]]).

This ring $A_0$ is the **crystal limiting ring** of the crystal development below, and it is different from the Laurent ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ of [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]: $q^{-1}\in A\setminus A_0$, while $(1+q)^{-1}\in A_0\setminus A$; neither ring contains the other, and both are subrings of $\mathbb Q(q)$. For every free $A_0$-module $L$ the canonical map
$$\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L\longrightarrow L/qL,\qquad c\otimes\ell\mapsto c\,\ell+qL,$$
is an isomorphism, and for every $\lambda\in\mathbb Q(q)^\times$ one has $\lambda L/q\lambda L\cong L/qL$; passing from $L$ to $L/qL$ is the **crystal limit**. No freeness of any further module, no lattice and no choice principle is asserted here.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

derivations.claim: The standard lattice. By [F1] and [F2], $\tilde e_1(v+w)=\tilde e_1v+\tilde e_1w=0+v=v$ and $\tilde e_1w=v$, while $L=A_0(v+w)\oplus A_0(qv)$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $2$ because $v+w$ and $qv$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-independent; it generates $V(\omega)$ because $v=q^{-1}(qv)$ and $w=(v+w)-v$.

Weight decomposition without operator stability. The lattice $L'=A_0(qv)\oplus A_0w$ generates $V(\omega)$ because $v=q^{-1}(qv)$, and it is the direct sum $L'_\omega\oplus L'_{\omega-\alpha_1}$ with $L'_\omega=A_0qv$ and $L'_{\omega-\alpha_1}=A_0w$ by distinct weights; but $\tilde e_1w=v$, and $v=aqv+bw$ with $a,b\in A_0$ forces $1=aq$ and $a=q^{-1}\notin A_0$, so $v\notin L'$ and $L'$ violates exactly (iii), not (ii).

Operator stability without weight decomposition. In the datum of [F4], take one-dimensional modules $M_0=\mathbb Q(q)u$, $M_\delta=\mathbb Q(q)w$ of labels $0,\delta$, with $E_1=F_1=0$, $K_h=1$ on both and $K_d$ acting by $1,q$, respectively. The toral and mixed relations hold, so these are integrable label modules. All Kashiwara operators vanish by [F5]. Hence $L^{\prime\prime}:=A_0(u+w)\oplus A_0(qu)$ is operator stable; its displayed generators are independent and span $M_0\oplus M_\delta$ over the field. In $a(u+w)+bqu$ the coordinates are $(a+bq,a)$, so $L^{\prime\prime}\cap M_0=A_0qu$ (set $a=0$), whereas $L^{\prime\prime}\cap M_\delta=qA_0w$ (set $a=-bq$). Their direct sum omits $u+w$, whose coordinates are both $1\notin qA_0$. Thus this free generating lattice satisfies (iii) and violates (ii).

The lattice is not operator stable. If $v=a(v+w)+bqv$ with $a,b\in A_0$, comparison of the coefficients of $w$ gives $a=0$, and then $1=bq$, that is $b=q^{-1}\notin A_0$; hence $v\notin L$ while $\tilde e_1(v+w)=v$, so (iii) fails.

The lattice is not weight decomposed. The weight pieces are $L_\omega=L\cap\mathbb Q(q)v=\{a(v+w)+bqv:a=0\}=A_0qv$ and $L_{\omega-\alpha_1}=L\cap\mathbb Q(q)w=\{a(v+w)+bqv:a+bq=0\}=\{-bq(v+w)+bqv:b\in A_0\}=qA_0w$. If $v+w=aqv+bqw$ with $a,b\in A_0$, comparison of the coefficients of $v$ gives $a=q^{-1}

eq L_\omega\oplus L_{\omega-\alpha_1}$: (ii) fails too.

No crystal basis on $L$. By steps 2.1 and 2.2 the lattice $L$ violates the crystal-lattice axioms (ii) and (iii); since a crystal basis $(L,B)$ requires $L$ to be a crystal lattice by [F3], there is no set $B$ with $(L,B)$ a crystal basis of $V(\omega)$.

Conclusion. The lattice $L$ shows that neither axiom is automatic for a free generating lattice, and steps 1.2 and 1.3 exhibit, respectively, a lattice satisfying (ii) but not (iii) and a lattice satisfying (iii) but not (ii); hence the two axioms are independent in the class of allowed graded quantum data. All maps and vectors are displayed or the zero operators, so no choice principle is used.

boundaries.evidence: The witness lattices are free of rank two with displayed generators and no sum is empty; the refuted claim is a universal assertion about free generating lattices of integrable modules, and the single explicit lattice $L$ refutes it by steps 2.1-3.1.

Zero structures are used twice: the label modules of step 1.3 have $E_1=F_1=0$ by construction, and the coordinate comparisons of steps 2.1-2.2 force the coefficient $a=0$ before the nonzero coordinate $1$ forces $b=q^{-1}\notin A_0$.

The ambient module $V(\omega)=L_1(1)$ is the smallest nontrivial case, with one-step strings, and the rank-two witness lattices are the smallest free submodules able to mix the two weight classes $v$ and $w$; no larger example is needed.

The auxiliary datum of step 1.3 is deliberately degenerate: the positive and negative operators vanish on it, which makes every $A_0$-submodule operator stable and isolates the failure of the weight decomposition; this is exactly the independence witness for axioms (ii) and (iii).

The endpoint element is $q^{-1}\notin A_0$: step 1.2 forces $a=q^{-1}$ for $v\in L'$, and step 2.2 forces $a=q^{-1}$ for $v+w\in L_\omega\oplus L_{\omega-\alpha_1}$; the same unit boundary is the reason the displayed generators cannot be replaced by dividing by $q$.
Step 4.1 records that all maps and vectors are displayed or the zero operators, so no choice principle is used; the three witness lattices are named explicitly rather than selected from a family.

boundaries.reason: The counterexample refutes a universal implication between the two lattice axioms; no biconditional is asserted, and the two independence directions are proved directly in steps 1.2 and 1.3 rather than as implications.
There is no converse implication to prove: the statement exhibits witnesses for (ii)-not-(iii) and (iii)-not-(ii), which together with steps 2.1-2.2 establish independence in a single pass.

risk_review.notes: Read all seven witness steps and current rank-one, crystal and datum/DJ definitions. Coordinate pair (a+bq,a) gives intersections A0 qv and qA0 w, so the mixed generator is absent from their sum and raising gives v outside L. The graded L-prime violates only stability; the auxiliary labels 0,delta have simple-coroot value zero, central torus eigenvalues 1,q and zero E/F, satisfying the mixed relation and all Serre relations. Its operators vanish but intersections again are q-scaled, establishing independence of the two axioms. Generators are independent, determinants nonzero and field spans full. Source crystal axioms JKK pp.15–17/Kashiwara pp.473–474 were read; these witnesses are locally computed. Current intersection repair is correct and choice-free.

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

We also write $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ for the datum's integer pairing $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.
