The assignments of the statement satisfy the defining relations of [F1] on the three basis vectors: the toral actions are the stated labels; $[E_1,F_1]$ equals $e_1\mapsto e_1$, $e_2\mapsto-e_2$, $e_3\mapsto0$, which is $(K_1-K_1^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$; $[E_2,F_2]$ equals $e_1\mapsto0$, $e_2\mapsto e_2$, $e_3\mapsto-e_3$, which is $(K_2-K_2^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$; the mixed commutators $[E_1,F_2]$, $[E_2,F_1]$ vanish on all three basis vectors; and the Serre relations hold because $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$ for $i=1,2$ and every word with three or more factors from $\{E_1,E_2\}$ (or from $\{F_1,F_2\}$) kills every basis vector.

Action table. Computing $\Delta E_i,\Delta F_i$ on the six displayed vectors gives $F_1v_{11}=v_{12}$, $F_1v_{12}=[2]v_{22}$, $F_1v_{13}=v_{23}$, $F_2v_{12}=v_{13}$, $F_2v_{22}=v_{23}$, $F_2v_{23}=[2]v_{33}$ and $E_1v_{12}=[2]v_{11}$, $E_1v_{22}=v_{12}$, $E_1v_{23}=v_{13}$, $E_2v_{13}=v_{12}$, $E_2v_{23}=[2]v_{22}$, $E_2v_{33}=v_{23}$, with all other positive and negative actions on the six vectors zero; for instance $\Delta F_1(v_{13})=F_1e_3\otimes e_1+K_1e_3\otimes F_1e_1+qF_1e_1\otimes e_3+qK_1e_1\otimes F_1e_3=v_{23}$ and $\Delta E_2(v_{23})=E_2e_3\otimes K_2^{-1}e_2+qE_2e_2\otimes K_2^{-1}e_3+q\,e_2\otimes E_2e_3=(q^{-1}+q)v_{22}$. Cyclicity and dimension. The table gives $v_{12}=F_1v_{11}$, $v_{22}=F_1^{(2)}v_{11}$, $v_{13}=F_2v_{12}$, $v_{23}=F_1v_{13}=F_2v_{22}$ and $v_{33}=F_2^{(2)}v_{22}$, so all six vectors lie in the cyclic submodule of $v_{11}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

derivations.claim: The string components. $V_{2\omega}=\mathbb Q(q)v_2$ with $E_1v_2=0$, so the decomposition of $v_2$ is $v_2=F_1^{(0)}v_2$ with top component $v_2\in H_{2\omega}$. Since $v_1=F_1v_2=F_1^{(1)}v_2$ and $V_0=\mathbb Q(q)v_1$, the decomposition of $v_1$ is $v_1=F_1^{(1)}v_2$ with top component $v_2\in H_{2\omega}$; likewise $v_0=F_1^{(2)}v_2$ is the decomposition of $v_0$ with top component $v_2\in H_{2\omega}$.

The six formulas. Reading the definitions off the decompositions of step 1.1: $\tilde e_1v_2=0$, $\tilde e_1v_1=F_1^{(0)}v_2=v_2$, $\tilde e_1v_0=F_1^{(1)}v_2=v_1$ and $\tilde f_1v_2=F_1^{(1)}v_2=v_1$, $\tilde f_1v_1=F_1^{(2)}v_2=v_0$, $\tilde f_1v_0=F_1^{(3)}v_2=0$. In particular $F_1v_1=[2]_1v_0$ while $\tilde f_1v_1=v_0$, and $E_1v_0=v_1=\tilde e_1v_0$ and $F_1v_0=0=\tilde f_1v_0$ show the bottom agreements; the interior difference is exactly the factor $[2]_1\neq1$.

Lattice and residue basis. Since $v_2,v_1,v_0$ have distinct weights, $\mathcal L(2\omega)=A_0v_2\oplus A_0v_1\oplus A_0v_0$ and it generates $V$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$; step 2.1 shows that $\tilde e_1$ and $\tilde f_1$ preserve it, so it is a crystal lattice. The classes $b_2,b_1,b_0$ of the three basis vectors are $\mathbb Q$-independent in $L/qL$ because $L$ is free with those basis vectors and the crystal-limit map is an isomorphism, so they form a $\mathbb Q$-basis; the operator action of step 2.1 lies in $\{b_2,b_1,b_0\}\cup\{0\}$, and the only nonzero arrows are $b_2\to b_1$ and $b_1\to b_0$, whose inverses under $\tilde e_1$ hold, giving the partial-inverse axiom.

The invariants. From the chain $b_2\to b_1\to b_0$ the values $\varepsilon_1(b_2)=0$, $\varepsilon_1(b_1)=1$, $\varepsilon_1(b_0)=2$ and $\varphi_1(b_2)=2$, $\varphi_1(b_1)=1$, $\varphi_1(b_0)=0$ are immediate, and the weights are those of step 3.1; the equalities $\varphi_1(b)=\varepsilon_1(b)+\langle h_1,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle$ read $2=0+2$, $1=1+0$, $0=2-2$.

Partial inverses. Evaluating step 2.1 gives $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_2=v_2$, $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_1=v_1$, $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_0=0=v_0-p_{\mathrm{bot}}v_0$, and $\tilde f_1\tilde e_1v_2=0=v_2-p_0v_2$, $\tilde f_1\tilde e_1v_1=v_1=v_1-p_0v_1$, $\tilde f_1\tilde e_1v_0=v_0=v_0-p_0v_0$; by linearity these are the stated identities, and no choice is used because everything is computed on the three displayed vectors.

The two zero operator values sit at the string ends: step 2.1 computes $\tilde e_1v_2=0$ and $\tilde f_1v_0=0$ from the decomposition, and step 5.1's projection identities evaluate the corresponding top and bottom corrections on all three basis vectors.

The forward direction of the partial-inverse axiom along the two edges $b_2\to b_1\to b_0$: step 5.1 verifies $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_2=v_2$ and $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1v_1=v_1$, so the inverse of each edge is the raising edge.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). (i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$

so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

We also write $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ for the datum's integer pairing $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: The negative-half crystal. By [F1], the divided monomials $F_1^{(n)}$ form a field basis of the polynomial algebra, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}A_0F_1^{(n)}$. Reducing this free direct sum modulo $q$ shows that the residue classes $b_n=F_1^{(n)}+q\mathcal L(\infty)$ ($n\ge0$) are nonzero and linearly independent modulo $q$; the operators act as $\tilde f_1b_n=b_{n+1}$ and $\tilde e_1b_{n+1}=b_n$, $\tilde e_1b_0=0$. Hence $\mathcal B(\infty)\cong\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, with weights $\mathrm{wt}(b_n)=-n\alpha_1=-2n\omega$, $\varepsilon_1(b_n)=n$, formal $\varphi_1(b_n)=n-2n=-n$ and $\ell_1^-(b_n)=\infty$.

The module crystal. By [F2], $\pi_m(F_1^{(n)})=v_n$ for $n\le m$ and $0$ for $n>m$; so $\pi_m(b_n)=0$ for $n>m$ and $\pi_m(b_n)=v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ for $0\le n\le m$. The classes $v_0,\dots,v_m$ are a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(m\omega)/q\mathcal L(m\omega)$, and the operator action on them is the string action, so the surviving residues map bijectively onto $\mathcal B(m\omega)$; this is (a).

Raising compatibility and its failure. For $0\le n\le m$ one has $\tilde e_1\pi_m(b_n)=\tilde e_1(v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega))=v_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ and $0$ for $n=0$, while $\pi_m(\tilde e_1b_n)=v_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ and $0$ for $n=0$; hence the two sides agree for every surviving residue. At the killed residue $n=m+1$, the left side is $\tilde e_1\pi_m(b_{m+1})=\tilde e_1\cdot0=0$, while the right side is $\pi_m(\tilde e_1b_{m+1})=\pi_m(b_m)=v_m\neq0$ modulo $q$; this is the stated boundary failure. Lowering: $\tilde f_1\pi_m(b_n)=v_{n+1}$ for $n<m$ and $0$ for $n\ge m$, while $\pi_m(\tilde f_1b_n)=v_{n+1}$ for $n<m$ and $0$ for $n\ge m$, so both sides agree for every $n$.

Isomorphism in fixed degree. In root degree $-n\alpha_1$ the free $A_0$-module $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-n\alpha_1}$ is the one-dimensional span of $F_1^{(n)}$ with residue $b_n$, and $\mathcal L(m\omega)_{m\omega-n\alpha_1}$ is the one-dimensional span of $v_n$ with residue $v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ for $m\ge n$; the map $\pi_m$ sends $F_1^{(n)}$ to $v_n$, an isomorphism on these one-dimensional free modules, and its surviving-residue set is $\{b_n\}$ when $m\ge n$ and empty otherwise. Together with step 3.1 this is the large-weight instance of the projection lemma.

Choice. The computations of steps 1.1 through 4.1 use only explicit monomials, divided powers and one-dimensional free modules, so they are choice-free; the axiom of choice is declared because the cited general suppliers [F3] inherit it from the grand loop.

boundaries.evidence: The case $m=0$ kills every $b_n$ with $n>0$ and leaves the singleton surviving set $\{b_0\}$: step 2.1's bijection maps it onto the one-dimensional crystal $\mathcal B(0)$ of the trivial module, and step 4.1's degree isomorphism is the identity on the degree-zero component $A_0$.

The killed residues are exactly $\pi_m(b_n)=0$ for $n>m$ by step 2.1; on the negative half no $\tilde f_1$-image vanishes, since $\tilde e_1\tilde f_1=\operatorname{id}$ in step 1.1, and the zero value of $\tilde e_1$ occurs only at the top $b_0$.

The case $m=1$: the surviving residues $\{b_0,b_1\}$ map onto the two-vertex crystal of $V(\omega)$, and the failure of raising first appears at $b_2$, where $\pi_1(b_2)=0$ while $\pi_1(\tilde e_1b_2)=v_1\ne0$ by step 3.1.

The negative-half crystal is the degenerate infinite-string case: step 1.1 records the formal $\varphi_1(b_n)=-n$, negative for $n\ge1$ and not a chain length, together with $\ell_1^-=\infty$; this is exactly the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition and is kept separate from the module crystals.

The endpoint of the surviving range is $n=m+1$: step 3.1 shows that raising fails exactly there, while lowering commutes for every $n$, and step 4.1 identifies the degree isomorphism on the one-dimensional components for $m\ge n$ and the empty surviving fibre for $m<n$.

Step 5.1 records that the computations of steps 1.1 through 4.1 use only explicit monomials, divided powers and one-dimensional free modules and are choice-free; the axiom of choice is declared only because the cited general suppliers [F3] inherit it from the grand loop.

The bijection of (a) is proved in step 2.1 from both sides: forward, the classes $\pi_m(b_n)=v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ for $0\le n\le m$ are distinct because the residue basis $\{v_0,\dots,v_m\}$ is linearly independent, so the map is injective onto its image.

Reverse reading of the same step 2.1: every residue $v_n+q\mathcal L(m\omega)$ of $\mathcal B(m\omega)$ is the image of the surviving class $b_n$, so the map is surjective onto $\mathcal B(m\omega)$; together with the killed classes $n>m$ the two directions give the stated bijection.

risk_review.notes: Read all five steps using reviewed rank-one polynomial/string suppliers. Divided monomials are a field basis and their free A0 sum gives independent nonzero residues; projection to F^(n)h_m is exact, with surviving n<=m and killed n>m. Raising commutes for every survivor including n=0, fails precisely at b_(m+1), and lowering commutes for all n. In fixed root degree -n alpha the survivor set is the singleton {b_n}, including n=m=0; it is empty for n>m. The renamed highest h_m avoids collision with bottom v_m. JKK Proposition 6.1/Definition 6.2, Corollary 7.14/Proposition 7.34 and Kashiwara Theorem 5 were independently read. Current reader corrections of interface and residue independence are complete. Direct reference consumer B-page already describes the correct truncation; no outside logical consumer exists in current run manifests. Explicit computation is choice-free with conservative AC from general suppliers.

citations.quote:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $R$ be a unital ring, $M$ a right $R$-module, and $N$ a left $R$-module. Let

$$F:=\mathbb Z^{(M\times N)}$$

be the free $\mathbb Z$-module on the set $M\times N$ ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]], [[thm-universal-property-of-free-modules]]), and write $e_{(m,n)}$ for its standard basis elements. The additive group of $F$ is abelian. Let $H$ be the subgroup generated ([[def-generated-subgroup]]) by all elements

$$e_{(m+m',n)}-e_{(m,n)}-e_{(m',n)},$$

$$e_{(m,n+n')}-e_{(m,n)}-e_{(m,n')},$$

and

$$e_{(mr,n)}-e_{(m,rn)}$$

as $m,m'$ range over $M$, $n,n'$ over $N$, and $r$ over $R$. Since every subgroup of an abelian group is normal, the quotient group $F/H$ is defined ([[def-quotient-group]]). The **tensor product of $M$ and $N$ over $R$** is

$$M\otimes_RN:=F/H.$$

The coset of $e_{(m,n)}$ is the **elementary tensor** $m\otimes n$. Every tensor is a finite sum of elementary tensors, because every element of $F$ is a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of basis elements and integer coefficients may be absorbed into either additive variable. The defining relations give

$$(m+m')\otimes n=m\otimes n+m'\otimes n,\qquad m\otimes(n+n')=m\otimes n+m\otimes n',$$

and

$$(mr)\otimes n=m\otimes(rn).$$

In particular $0\otimes n=0=m\otimes0$. No $R$-module structure on $M\otimes_RN$ is part of this arbitrary-ring definition; at this stage it is an abelian group.

Let $R$ be a unital ring, $M$ a right $R$-module, $N$ a left $R$-module, and

$$\tau:M\times N\longrightarrow M\otimes_RN,\qquad \tau(m,n)=m\otimes n.$$

The map $\tau$ is balanced ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]]). For every abelian group $A$ and every balanced map $b:M\times N\to A$, there is a unique group homomorphism

$$\overline b:M\otimes_RN\longrightarrow A$$

such that $\overline b(m\otimes n)=b(m,n)$ for all $m,n$. Consequently composition with $\tau$ is a bijection

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ab}}(M\otimes_RN,A)\cong\operatorname{Bal}_R(M,N;A).$$

Let $t$ be an indeterminate over $\mathbb Q$, and let $A$ be a unital associative $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra. For $N\ge0$ and $0\le r\le N$, set

$$B_{N,r}(t):=\frac{[N]_t!}{[r]_t![N-r]_t!},\qquad [m]_t:=1+t+\cdots+t^{m-1},\quad [m]_t!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_t,\quad [0]_t:=0,\quad [0]_t!:=1,$$

and set $B_{N,r}(t)=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>N$. If $x,y\in A$ satisfy $yx=txy$, then for every $N\ge0$,

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}B_{N,r}(t)x^ry^{N-r}.$$

For a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, any unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra can be viewed as a $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra via $t\mapsto q_i^2$. In that algebra, if $yx=q_i^2xy$, then

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-r)}\binom{N}{r}_i x^ry^{N-r},$$

using the symmetric Gaussian binomials of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. If instead $yx=t^{-1}xy$, the same expansion has coefficients $B_{N,r}(t^{-1})=t^{-r(N-r)}B_{N,r}(t)$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ be any family of $R$-modules, and let $N$ be an $R$-module. The homomorphism induced by the coordinate inclusions is a natural $R$-module isomorphism

$$\Phi:\bigoplus_{i\in I}(M_i\otimes_RN)\longrightarrow\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i\right)\otimes_RN,$$

$$\Phi\bigl(\jmath_i(m\otimes n)\bigr)=\jmath_i(m)\otimes n.$$

The same holds with the direct sum in the second variable: there is a natural $R$-module isomorphism

$$\Phi':\bigoplus_{i\in I}(N\otimes_RM_i)\longrightarrow N\otimes_R\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i\right),\qquad \Phi'\bigl(\jmath_i(n\otimes m)\bigr)=n\otimes\jmath_i(m).$$

The assertion includes $I=\varnothing$, when both sides are zero.

Let $R$ be a unital ring, $M$ a right $R$-module, $N$ a left $R$-module, and

$$\tau:M\times N\longrightarrow M\otimes_RN,\qquad \tau(m,n)=m\otimes n.$$

The map $\tau$ is balanced ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]]). For every abelian group $A$ and every balanced map $b:M\times N\to A$, there is a unique group homomorphism

$$\overline b:M\otimes_RN\longrightarrow A$$

such that $\overline b(m\otimes n)=b(m,n)$ for all $m,n$. Consequently composition with $\tau$ is a bijection

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ab}}(M\otimes_RN,A)\cong\operatorname{Bal}_R(M,N;A).$$

Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$.

A vertex $b\in B$ is a **highest weight element** (a highest vertex, a maximal vector) of weight $\lambda\in P$ if $wt(b)=\lambda$ and $\tilde e_ib=0$ for every $i\in I$. The **lowering-generated set** of $b$ is

$$F(b):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}b:\ r\ge0,\ i_1,\dots,i_r\in I\}\setminus\{0\},$$

the set of all nonzero iterated lowering images of $b$; it contains $b$ and is closed under nonzero images of every $\tilde f_i$. It need not be closed under raising: at the bottom $b$ of a two-vertex rank-one string, $F(b)=\{b\}$ while $\tilde e_i b$ is the top vertex. The **connected component** $C(b)$ of $b$ is the smallest subset of $B$ containing $b$ and closed under nonzero images of $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ for all $i$; by the partial-inverse axiom this is the connected component of the underlying coloured graph.

$B$ is a **highest weight crystal of highest weight $\lambda$** if $B$ has a highest weight element $b$ of weight $\lambda$ and $B=F(b)$.

The definition deliberately separates two conditions. Always $F(b)\subseteq C(b)$, and a highest vertex need not generate $B$: in a tensor product $B_1\otimes B_2$ a vertex with $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\varphi_i(b_1)$ for all $i$ is highest while $B_1\otimes B_2$ is in general larger than its lowering-generated set (the companion page computes both cases). If $p\ge s$, then $S\tilde f_i((b_1\otimes b_2)^\vee)=S((\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2)^\vee)=b_2^\vee\otimes\tilde f_i(b_1^\vee)$; the target $\tilde f_i$ selects its second factor because $\varphi_i(b_2^\vee)=s\le p=\varepsilon_i(b_1^\vee)$. If $p<s$, then $S\tilde f_i((b_1\otimes b_2)^\vee)=\tilde f_i(b_2^\vee)\otimes b_1^\vee$, and the target selects its first factor because $s>p$. For raising, if $p>s$, then $S\tilde e_i((b_1\otimes b_2)^\vee)=b_2^\vee\otimes\tilde e_i(b_1^\vee)$ and the target selects its second factor because $s<p$; if $p\le s$, then $S\tilde e_i((b_1\otimes b_2)^\vee)=\tilde e_i(b_2^\vee)\otimes b_1^\vee$, and the target selects its first factor because $s\ge p$. These formulas also hold at zero endpoints. The target weight is $-wt(b_1)-wt(b_2)$, equal to the weight of the dual input; maximal string lengths are preserved because both operators are intertwined.

Conclusion. The map $S$ is a bijection of vertex sets by construction, and step 3.1 shows that it intertwines $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ for every $i$; it preserves weights by step 2.1, hence it is an isomorphism of crystals $(B_1\otimes B_2)^\vee\to B_2^\vee\otimes B_1^\vee$, which is (ii). Because $s$ and $p$ range over finite nonnegative integers, the case analysis covers all vertices, including the tie $p=s$ where both readings agree. All constructions are explicit set-theoretic operations on the vertex set $B$ and the fixed operator maps, so no choice principle is used; the construction is stated only for crystals of integrable-module crystal bases, the negative-half case being excluded in the Statement.

Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$.

Let $B$ be a crystal, meaning the data $(B,wt,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ attached to a crystal basis or to a tensor product of such data ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]], [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]).

A vertex $b\in B$ is a **highest weight element** (a highest vertex, a maximal vector) of weight $\lambda\in P$ if $wt(b)=\lambda$ and $\tilde e_ib=0$ for every $i\in I$. The **lowering-generated set** of $b$ is

$$F(b):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}b:\ r\ge0,\ i_1,\dots,i_r\in I\}\setminus\{0\},$$

the set of all nonzero iterated lowering images of $b$; it contains $b$ and is closed under nonzero images of every $\tilde f_i$. It need not be closed under raising: at the bottom $b$ of a two-vertex rank-one string, $F(b)=\{b\}$ while $\tilde e_i b$ is the top vertex. The **connected component** $C(b)$ of $b$ is the smallest subset of $B$ containing $b$ and closed under nonzero images of $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ for all $i$; by the partial-inverse axiom this is the connected component of the underlying coloured graph.

$B$ is a **highest weight crystal of highest weight $\lambda$** if $B$ has a highest weight element $b$ of weight $\lambda$ and $B=F(b)$.

The definition deliberately separates two conditions. Always $F(b)\subseteq C(b)$, and a highest vertex need not generate $B$: in a tensor product $B_1\otimes B_2$ a vertex with $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\varphi_i(b_1)$ for all $i$ is highest while $B_1\otimes B_2$ is in general larger than its lowering-generated set (the companion page computes both cases). Conversely, for abstract crystals the two conditions do not determine $B$ up to isomorphism: the source literature records that not every connected crystal with a highest weight element of weight $\lambda$ is isomorphic to $B(\lambda)$. In this library crystals come from crystal bases of modules, and uniqueness for those is a theorem proved later on this page, not a consequence of this definition.

For the canonical objects, $B(\lambda)=\mathcal B(\lambda)$ denotes the crystal of the simple highest weight module $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]) and $P^+$ the dominant integral labels ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); that $B(\lambda)$ is a highest weight crystal of highest weight $\lambda$ is the next theorem. The operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ used throughout are those of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]. No choice principle is used.

boundaries.evidence: The zero module (or empty constituent family) is included: the splitting of step 4.1 is vacuous, step 6.1 produces an empty index set with the zero direct sum, and step 8.1 records that no selection is needed.
At a fixed label, step 5.1 uses basis independence and spanning of the two residue summands, without subtraction of infinite cardinalities; it permits an empty remaining basis.
The rank-one case $m=1$ of the top isotypic part is the base of steps 2.1-3.1; the multiplicity-one top is exactly the situation in which the single lift generates the whole top component.

The degenerate case of non-maximal weights is handled by the maximality choice in step 1.1: weights outside $\lambda-Q_+$ have zero $N_0$-component (step 4.1), and the argument never assumes $\lambda$ regular or the module finite dimensional.
The boundary is the top weight $\lambda$ (steps 1.1 and 2.1) and the finite upper cone bounds used in the local weight-finiteness argument of step 6.1; both are treated explicitly.

The Statement and Semisimplicity uses AC to select a maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC also permits simultaneous finite top-residue lifts over the possibly infinite constituent-top family; subsequent splittings are local finite inductions.

risk_review.notes: Reviewed the complete eight-step proof, current semisimplicity supplier and all other exact cited interfaces, plus Kashiwara91 pp.478-479 complete Lemmas 2.6.1-2.6.3. Maximal lambda has no complementary lambda weight. Finite residue lifts form a unit-determinant top basis. Minimal pole descent works off lambda, and standard lowering generators provide field generation of L0. Height induction splits lattice projections even for weights outside the lambda cone. The repaired residue induction is essential: a nonzero L0 component raises to B0 and partial inversion returns b to B0; independence alone would not suffice. D(nu)=max of cone heights strictly increases down the root order and has finite levels; finitely many constituent tops contribute to any fixed mu. Under the modified rule $\tilde f_1^{\prime}$ acts on the first factor at this vertex, because it uses $\varphi_1\ge\varepsilon_1$: $\tilde f_1^{\prime}(v_1\otimes w_1)=v_2\otimes w_1$.

At $v_2\otimes w_1$ one has $\varphi_1(v_2)=0$ and $\varepsilon_1(w_1)=1$, so both the modified and the original rule select a factor by the comparison of $0$ with $1$; the modified $\tilde e_1^{\prime}$ acts on the first factor only when $\varphi_1>\varepsilon_1$, which fails, so it acts on the second: $\tilde e_1^{\prime}(v_2\otimes w_1)=v_2\otimes w_0$.

Therefore $\tilde e_1^{\prime}\tilde f_1^{\prime}(v_1\otimes w_1)=v_2\otimes w_0\ne v_1\otimes w_1$, contradicting [F5]. For the strict-for-both variant use $v_0\otimes w_1$: lowering gives $v_1\otimes w_1$, but strict raising at the tie acts on the second factor and gives $v_1\otimes w_0$. Compare component sizes: the original rank-one tensor rule of [F3] gives $\tilde f_1(v_j\otimes w_k)=v_{j+1}\otimes w_k$ if $2-j>k$ and $v_j\otimes w_{k+1}$ otherwise; through $v_0\otimes w_1$ this is $v_0\otimes w_1\to v_1\otimes w_1\to v_1\otimes w_2$, a chain of three, which is the component $B(2)$ in the decomposition of $V(2)\otimes V(2)=V(4)\oplus V(2)\oplus V(0)$. Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be crystals, meaning the data $(B,wt,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ attached to a crystal basis $(L,B)$ of an integrable module by [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] and [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $wt:B\to P$ is the weight function, $\varepsilon_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde e_i^nb\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde f_i^nb\ne0\}$ are finite, $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$, and $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ are the partial maps $B\to B\cup\{0\}$ of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]].

The **tensor product crystal** $B_1\otimes B_2$ is the following data on $B_1\times B_2$, whose elements are written $b_1\otimes b_2$:

(i) $wt(b_1\otimes b_2):=wt(b_1)+wt(b_2)$;

(ii) $\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2)$, and $\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2)$;

(iii) $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2)$, and $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2)$.

By convention a product is $0$ as soon as the operator applied to the selected factor is $0$; the **left factor is preferred** exactly in the displayed cases, so the assignment is left-to-right, matching the left-to-right order of the module tensor product $M_1\otimes M_2$ under the coproduct of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. The **equality case** $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is split: $\tilde e_i$ acts on the first factor while $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second. The asymmetry is not free: with the same strict or non-strict comparison used for both operators the partial-inverse axiom fails, as the counterexample on the companion page records, while the displayed convention is internally consistent by the lemma on this page computing $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of $B_1\otimes B_2$.

The functions $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of $B_1\otimes B_2$ are read off from the two-case operators as maximal iterated powers, exactly as in [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]. This definition only fixes combinatorial data and asserts nothing about an arbitrary pair of crystals: it does not claim that every such datum arises from a module tensor product. When $B_1,B_2$ are the crystals of crystal bases of integrable modules, the tensor product theorem later on this page proves that $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$ with these operators, and only through that theorem are the values finite and nonnegative a priori. No choice principle is used.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

We also write $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ for the datum's integer pairing $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.
