Let $B$ be the crystal of a crystal basis $(L,B)$ of an integrable module ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]); its operators are the partial maps $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i:B\to B\cup\{0\}$ satisfying $\tilde e_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde f_ib'$, and $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ satisfy $\varphi_i(b)-\varepsilon_i(b)=\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$.

Define the **dual crystal** $B^\vee:=\{b^\vee:b\in B\}$ by

$$wt(b^\vee):=-wt(b),\qquad \varepsilon_i(b^\vee):=\varphi_i(b),\qquad \varphi_i(b^\vee):=\varepsilon_i(b),\qquad \tilde f_i(b^\vee):=(\tilde e_ib)^\vee,\qquad \tilde e_i(b^\vee):=(\tilde f_ib)^\vee,$$

with $0^\vee:=0$. Then:

(i) $B^\vee$ satisfies the crystal axioms: $(\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ are partial inverses, the arrows of $B^\vee$ are the arrows of $B$ with orientation reversed, the displayed $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ are exactly the maximal iterated powers, and $(B^\vee)^\vee=B$ canonically;

(ii) **tensor products reverse order.** For crystals $B_1,B_2$ as above the map $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto b_2^\vee\otimes b_1^\vee$ is an isomorphism of crystals $(B_1\otimes B_2)^\vee\to B_2^\vee\otimes B_1^\vee$ for the tensor product of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]].

The construction is stated for crystals of crystal bases of integrable modules, where $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ are finite and nonnegative. For the negative-half crystal of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]] only the formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,wt\rangle$, which may be negative, is defined, and no dual is asserted there. No choice principle is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$, $I=\{1\}$, with fundamental weight $\lambda_1$ and simple root $\alpha_1=2\lambda_1$. Let $V(1)$ be the two-dimensional simple integrable module with highest vector $v_0$ and crystal $B(1)=\{v_0,v_1\}$, where $v_1=F_1v_0$; the $i$-string is $v_0\xrightarrow{1}v_1$ with $wt(v_0)=\lambda_1$, $wt(v_1)=-\lambda_1$ and $\varepsilon_1(v_0)=0,\ \varphi_1(v_0)=1,\ \varepsilon_1(v_1)=1,\ \varphi_1(v_1)=0$ (JKK Example 5.1(a) with $m=1$).

Compute the tensor crystal $B(1)\otimes B(1)$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]] with the two-case rule of [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]]. Writing the four vertices as $v_j\otimes v_k$ with $j,k\in\{0,1\}$, the rule gives

$$\tilde f_1(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}v_{j+1}\otimes v_k,&1-j>k,\\ v_j\otimes v_{k+1},&1-j\le k,\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_1(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}v_{j-1}\otimes v_k,&1-j\ge k,\\ v_j\otimes v_{k-1},&1-j<k.\end{cases}$$

Consequently: $v_0\otimes v_0$ is the unique highest vertex of weight $2\lambda_1$ and generates the chain $v_0\otimes v_0\to v_1\otimes v_0\to v_1\otimes v_1$; the remaining vertex $v_0\otimes v_1$ has weight $0$, is killed by $\tilde e_1$ and by $\tilde f_1$, and forms a one-element component; and $\varepsilon_1,\varphi_1$ of the four vertices are $(0,2),(1,1),(2,0),(0,0)$ at $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ respectively. Hence $B(1)\otimes B(1)=B(2)\sqcup B(0)$, matching the classical decomposition $V(1)\otimes V(1)=V(2)\oplus V(0)$ of dimensions $4=3+1$; here $B(2)$ is the three-element $1$-chain of weights $2\lambda_1,0,-2\lambda_1$ and $B(0)$ the one-element crystal of weight $0$.

Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ with simple roots $\alpha_1=2\lambda_1-\lambda_2$, $\alpha_2=-\lambda_1+2\lambda_2$ and $\langle h_i,\lambda_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$. The three-dimensional simple module $V(\lambda_1)$ has crystal $B(\lambda_1)=\{u_1,u_2,u_3\}$ with weights $\lambda_1,\ \lambda_2-\lambda_1,\ -\lambda_2$ and arrows $u_1\xrightarrow{1}u_2\xrightarrow{2}u_3$; its only nonzero $\varepsilon$-values are $\varepsilon_1(u_2)=1,\ \varepsilon_2(u_3)=1$, and $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$.

In the tensor crystal $B(\lambda_1)\otimes B(\lambda_1)$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]] the criterion of [[thm-highest-weight-components-in-a-tensor-product-crystal]](a) applies. A vertex $b_1\otimes b_2$ is highest exactly when $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ for $i=1,2$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\langle h_i,wt(b_1)\rangle$ for $i=1,2$. Since $\varepsilon_1(u_2)=1$ and $\varepsilon_2(u_3)=1$, only $b_1=u_1$ can occur, so the highest vertices are

$$u_1\otimes u_1\quad(\text{weight }2\lambda_1),\qquad u_1\otimes u_2\quad(\text{weight }\lambda_2),$$

the second because $\varepsilon_1(u_2)=1\le\langle h_1,wt(u_1)\rangle=1$ and $\varepsilon_2(u_2)=0\le\langle h_2,wt(u_1)\rangle=0$, while $u_1\otimes u_3$ fails since $\varepsilon_2(u_3)=1>\langle h_2,wt(u_1)\rangle=0$. By [[thm-highest-weight-components-in-a-tensor-product-crystal]](b) the two generated components are the highest weight crystals $B(2\lambda_1)$ and $B(\lambda_2)$, so the nine vertices split as $B(\lambda_1)\otimes B(\lambda_1)=B(2\lambda_1)\sqcup B(\lambda_2)$, matching $V(\lambda_1)\otimes V(\lambda_1)=V(2\lambda_1)\oplus V(\lambda_2)$ with dimensions $9=6+3$.

We also write $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ for the datum's integer pairing $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be crystals, meaning the data $(B,wt,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ attached to a crystal basis $(L,B)$ of an integrable module by [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] and [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $wt:B\to P$ is the weight function, $\varepsilon_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde e_i^nb\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde f_i^nb\ne0\}$ are finite, $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$, and $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ are the partial maps $B\to B\cup\{0\}$ of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]].

The **tensor product crystal** $B_1\otimes B_2$ is the following data on $B_1\times B_2$, whose elements are written $b_1\otimes b_2$:

(i) $wt(b_1\otimes b_2):=wt(b_1)+wt(b_2)$;

(ii) $\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2)$, and $\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2)$;

(iii) $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2)$, and $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2)$.

By convention a product is $0$ as soon as the operator applied to the selected factor is $0$; the **left factor is preferred** exactly in the displayed cases, so the assignment is left-to-right, matching the left-to-right order of the module tensor product $M_1\otimes M_2$ under the coproduct of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. The **equality case** $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is split: $\tilde e_i$ acts on the first factor while $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second. The asymmetry is not free: with the same strict or non-strict comparison used for both operators the partial-inverse axiom fails, as the counterexample on the companion page records, while the displayed convention is internally consistent by the lemma on this page computing $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of $B_1\otimes B_2$.

The functions $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of $B_1\otimes B_2$ are read off from the two-case operators as maximal iterated powers, exactly as in [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]. This definition only fixes combinatorial data and asserts nothing about an arbitrary pair of crystals: it does not claim that every such datum arises from a module tensor product. When $B_1,B_2$ are the crystals of crystal bases of integrable modules, the tensor product theorem later on this page proves that $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$ with these operators, and only through that theorem are the values finite and nonnegative a priori. No choice principle is used.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle\mathrm{wt}(u_n),h_i\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

derivations.claim: (A) Apply $\tilde f_1(b^\vee)=(\tilde e_1b)^\vee$ and $\tilde e_1(b^\vee)=(\tilde f_1b)^\vee$ of [F1] to $b=v_0,v_1$: $\tilde e_1v_0=0$ gives $\tilde f_1(v_0^\vee)=0$; $\tilde e_1v_1=v_0$ gives $\tilde f_1(v_1^\vee)=v_0^\vee$; $\tilde f_1v_0=v_1$ gives $\tilde e_1(v_0^\vee)=v_1^\vee$; $\tilde f_1v_1=0$ gives $\tilde e_1(v_1^\vee)=0$. So the only arrow is $v_1^\vee\xrightarrow{1}v_0^\vee$ and the values $(\varepsilon_1,\varphi_1)=(\varphi_1,\varepsilon_1)$ are $(1,0)$ at $v_0^\vee$ and $(0,1)$ at $v_1^\vee$; weights are negated by [F1]. Comparing with [F2], the map $v_1^\vee\mapsto v_0$, $v_0^\vee\mapsto v_1$ preserves arrows, weights and $\varepsilon/\varphi$, so $B(1)^\vee\cong B(1)$ with highest vertex $v_1^\vee$.

(B) By [F1] the arrows become $u_3^\vee\xrightarrow{2}u_2^\vee\xrightarrow{1}u_1^\vee$, with weights $\lambda_2,\lambda_1-\lambda_2,-\lambda_1$ along that chain. The pairs $(\varepsilon_1,\varphi_1)$ at $(u_1^\vee,u_2^\vee,u_3^\vee)$ are $(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)$, and the color-two pairs are $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)$. Construct a module on $w_1,w_2,w_3$ with these successive weights: set $F_2w_1=w_2$, $F_1w_2=w_3$, $E_2w_2=w_1$, $E_1w_3=w_2$, all other $E_i,F_i$ images zero, and $K_hw_j=q^{\langle wt(w_j),h\rangle}w_j$. These maps satisfy [F6]: the weight shifts give the toral relations, the same-color commutators have diagonal entries $(0,1,-1)$ and $(1,-1,0)$, matching $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, and the cross-color commutators vanish. Each $E_i^2,F_i^2$ and each alternating triple $E_iE_jE_i,F_iF_jF_i$ with $i\ne j$ vanishes, proving both $A_2$ Serre relations. The module is nonzero, integrable and generated by its highest vector $w_1$ of dominant weight $\lambda_2$, so [F6](ii) identifies it with $V(\lambda_2)$. Each color has one length-one string and one trivial string; [F7] therefore makes the canonical lattice $\bigoplus_jA_0w_j$ with residue crystal $B(\lambda_2)$. The map $u_3^\vee\mapsto w_1$, $u_2^\vee\mapsto w_2$, $u_1^\vee\mapsto w_3$ preserves all crystal data. To check the module-dual description as well, realize the standard module by $F_1u_1=u_2$, $F_2u_2=u_3$, $E_1u_2=u_1$, $E_2u_3=u_2$, the given weights and zero remaining images. The same relation check with colors exchanged identifies this cyclic integrable module with $V(\lambda_1)$ by [F6]. For its linear dual basis $u_j^*$, [F8] gives the displayed $w$-actions on $w_1=u_3^*$, $w_2=-q_1u_2^*$, $w_3=q_1^2u_1^*$ (here $q_1=q_2$). Thus $V(\lambda_2)$ is the dual three-dimensional module, without a crystal-component uniqueness or AC premise.

(C) The swap sends $(v_j\otimes v_k)^\vee$ to $v_k^\vee\otimes v_j^\vee$. On the right the three-element lowering chain is $(v_1^\vee\otimes v_1^\vee)\to(v_0^\vee\otimes v_1^\vee)\to(v_0^\vee\otimes v_0^\vee)$, with weights $2\lambda_1,0,-2\lambda_1$; each next raising reverses the preceding arrow by [F4]. The remaining vertex $v_1^\vee\otimes v_0^\vee$ has weight zero and both operators vanish there: the tie $\varphi_1(v_1^\vee)=\varepsilon_1(v_0^\vee)=1$ selects the bottom second factor for lowering and the top first factor for raising. This is the image of the isolated dual vertex $(v_0\otimes v_1)^\vee$. The reversed three-element chain is $B(2)$ and the isolated vertex is $B(0)$ by [F5], so both sides have the claimed decomposition.

The arrow and tensor calculations are finite applications of [F1]; the canonical identification in (B) uses the explicit relation check, highest-weight module universality [F6] and lowering-word construction [F7]. No choice principle or general crystal-component uniqueness theorem is invoked.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be
the semilinear maps of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so
that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$
and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$,
with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$ be
the Lusztig divided-power integral form with its generators $E_i^{(r)}$,
$F_i^{(r)}$, $K_h^{\pm1}$ and toral binomials $T_{i,c,t}$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and
$\tau(U_A)=U_A$. Explicitly, on the generators,

$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$

$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$

In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$: $\psi$ to a semilinear
algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of
$U_A$, while $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two
involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the
later constructions are taken; neither formula is the Chevalley involution
$\omega$, which changes signs, exchanges the two halves and is treated in
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
No choice is used.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S$ generated by $\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]

[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

For a balanced triple, the two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If the triple is balanced and $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

derivations.claim: Since $q^{\pm1}M=M$, we have $M\cap qL_0=q(M\cap L_0)$, and similarly at infinity. Under [A1], $E\cap qL_0=0$. For $x\in M\cap L_0$ surjectivity gives $x=e+qx_1$ with $e\in E$ and $x_1\in M\cap L_0$. If also $x\in q^nL_\infty$ with $n\ge1$, then $e\in q^nL_\infty$ and $x_1\in q^{n-1}L_\infty$. Induction, starting with $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty=E$, therefore gives $M\cap L_0\cap q^nL_\infty=\sum_{k=0}^nq^kE$. The sum is direct: in a vanishing sum its constant coefficient belongs to $E\cap qL_0=0$, and division by $q$ removes successive coefficients.

For (2), identify $F$ with its image, since its residue map is injective. In any finite Laurent sum $x=\sum_kq^kf_k$ with $f_k\in F$, the least exponent cannot be negative when $x\in L_0$: multiplying by its inverse power gives a constant coefficient in $F\cap qL_0=0$. Removing that coefficient repeatedly proves $M\cap L_0=\mathbb Z[q]F$. The mirror argument at infinity gives $M\cap L_\infty=\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]F$. These expressions are unique by the same residue injections, so the simultaneous intersection is $F$, and its integral residue map is an isomorphism. This proves (2); only the integral residue, rather than the entire rational residue, is identified with $F$.

Every vector has finite infinity-pole order, so step 1.1 gives $M\cap L_0=\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$. Clearing a vector's zero-pole order by a power of $q$ gives $M=AE\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$. Also $E\cap q^{-1}L_\infty=0$: if $e$ lies there, then $qe\in E\cap qL_0=0$. In a Laurent expansion of $x\in M\cap L_\infty$, a largest positive exponent $n$ would give, after multiplication by $q^{-n}$, a nonzero coefficient in $E\cap q^{-1}L_\infty$; hence no such exponent occurs. Thus $M\cap L_\infty=\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$, with infinity residue $E$.

For (3), the assumed canonical isomorphism $A\otimes E_N\to N$ forces $E_N$ to inject into both chart residues. Indeed, if $e\in E_N\cap qL_0$, then $q^{-1}e\in E_N$ as well, contradicting Laurent independence unless $e=0$; the mirror argument handles infinity. Apply (2) to $N$ in its field span, with the induced lattices, to obtain its balancedness and $N=(N\cap L_0)+(N\cap L_\infty)$. If $x=l_0+n_0=l_\infty+n_\infty$ lies in $M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$, write $n_0-n_\infty=a+b$ with $a\in N\cap L_0$ and $b\in N\cap L_\infty$. Then $x-(n_0-a)=l_0+a=l_\infty-b$ is a simultaneous lift. Thus this intersection is $N+E_M$.

The injection $E\to L_0/qL_0$ extends injectively over $\mathbb Q$, by clearing integer denominators. A rational basis $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ of $\mathbb Q E$ has field-independent images: a rational-function dependence, after clearing denominators, would be a polynomial dependence, contradicting step 1.1. Since $M=AE$ spans $V$, this family is a field basis of $V$, so $t=\dim V$. Its residues are a rational basis of $L_0/qL_0$; expressing the $e_j$ in a free chart basis yields a square matrix invertible modulo $q$, hence with determinant a unit in $A_0$. Its adjugate gives $L_0=A_0E$ and the asserted tensor isomorphism. The same argument uses the infinity injection in step 2.1 to give $L_\infty=A_\infty E$. This proves (1), including its finite-free conclusions.

First restrict to a finitely generated subgroup $F'\subseteq F$ and $M'=N+A\varphi(F')$. The quotient-residue injection makes $F'$ torsionfree, hence a finite free abelian group. Modify the images of a finite basis of $F'$ by elements of $N$, using step 2.2, to obtain simultaneous lifts. Together with $E_N$ they generate $M'$. Their direct sum injects into $L_0/qL_0$: a vanishing residue first has zero $F'$ coordinate by the injection into $(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$, and then has zero $E_N$ coordinate by step 2.2. The infinity proof is identical. Criterion (2) now gives $E_{M'}\cong E_N\oplus F'$ and balancedness of $M'$.

Every element of $M$ belongs to some such $M'$, because its expression modulo $N$ uses finitely many images of $F$. The preceding balancedness proves injectivity and surjectivity of the residue map for $M$ element by element. Its residue decompositions also prove the stated exact sequence: the kernel of the quotient-residue map is precisely the residue of $N$, and its image is precisely the image of $F$. When $F$ and $E_N$ are finite free, take $F'=F$ in step 3.2; then $E_M\cong E_N\oplus F$ is finite free and (1) makes $M$ free over $A$. This proves (3) and completes the lemma.

Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, with rational discrete valuation rings $A_0$ at $q=0$ and $A_\infty$ at $q=\infty$. Put $M_A=U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and $L^-=\psi(L)$, the bar lattice, as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]].

The **integral residue lattice** is $L_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L$, a $\mathbb Z[q]$-module, and its **bar lattice** is $L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M_A\cap L^-$, a $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-module. The **balanced intersection** is $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$, a $\mathbb Z$-module. Since $q^{-1}M_A=M_A$, one has $M_A\cap qL=qL_{\mathbb Z}$; consequently the residue map $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to L/qL$ is injective and is $\mathbb Z$-linear. Its image is an integral subgroup of the rational crystal space, not the entire $\mathbb Q$-space. No Laurent-$A$-linearity is asserted on the residue lattice or on the residue map.

The field projection $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, restricts to an $A$-linear surjection $U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and it sends $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)$ into $L_{\mathbb Z}(\lambda)$ by the already-proved grand-loop lattice projection ([[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]). The module $V_A(\lambda)$ is $U_A$-stable: the divided-power and toral reordering identities of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] reduce the action on $v_\lambda$ to negative divided powers and Gaussian scalars in $A$, with all positive generators killing the highest vector except through the unit, and the residue compatibility of the projection is [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]]. No global freeness, residue spanning or balancedness is assumed here. The integral residue subgroup for the negative half is proved below to be $\mathbb Z B(\infty)$; the module subgroup $\mathbb Z B(\lambda)$ is a consequence of globalization.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ over $A$ is assumed or asserted.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

For the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices, their respective normalized polarizations take values in $A_0$ and their crystal residue bases are orthonormal. On every finite label or root component the Gram determinant is a unit of $A_0$, the $A_0$-pairing is perfect and $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. Moreover $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension of the lattice. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Only the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis is retained.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S$ generated by $\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i'$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$\varepsilon\colon U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the **augmentation**, the projection
onto the degree-zero component $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\cdot1$ (so
$\varepsilon(Q)=0$ on all positive-height components and $\varepsilon(1)=1$).

The **normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form** on $U_q^-$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon U_q^-\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(H) $B$ is **homogeneous**: $B\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu]\bigr)=0$ whenever
$\nu\ne\mu$;

(N) $B(1,1)=1$;

(R) $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ for all $i\in I$ and all $P,Q\in U_q^-$.

Equivalently, axioms (H) and (N) may be replaced by the single **counit
normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

in the presence of (R) (Verification, step 1.1).

Axioms (H) and (N) (equivalently (C)) are essential and not redundant: the
recursion (R) together with $B(1,1)=1$ alone neither forces symmetry nor
uniqueness, as the rank-one witness of step 2.2 shows.

The axioms determine $B$ uniquely: peeling first letters in the first argument
writes every positive-height $P$ as a finite sum $P=\sum_iF_iP_i$ and evaluates
$B(P,Q)=\sum_iB(P_i,e_i'Q)$, reducing the height; the base of the induction is
(C) (Verification, step 2.1). The **existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy** of
$B$ on $U_q^-$ for the actual quotient by the Serre ideal are not proved here:
they are the content of the negative-half form theorem
`thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral`,
the declared justification of this definition, which also settles the exact
integrality normalization ($A$-valuedness on the word lattice and the
Gaussian-factorial denominators on the divided-power lattice). That theorem
is proved on this page, and its statement is the declared supplier of
existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy; this definition itself claims only that
(H), (N) and (R) determine $B$ and that the normalization cannot be relaxed.

derivations.claim: **Integral representatives of the crystal basis.** By [F2] every divided-power lowering word $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ lies in $U_A^-$, and by [F3] it lies in $\mathcal L(\infty)$; hence its class lies in $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ and is a nonzero element of $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$ is represented by such a word.

**The value rings.** The explicit rank-one divided-word norms $B(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(a)})=1/[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})^{-1}$ and the word Gram expansion of [F5] show that every value on $U_A^-$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-combination of reciprocal products $\prod(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$ with bounded $r$, i.e. lies in $K_{\mathbb Z}$; and every value on $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ lies in $A_0\cap K_{\mathbb Z}$ by [F4]. The intersection is $A_{\mathbb Z}$: clearing denominators in $A_0\cap K_{\mathbb Z}$ writes the value as a Laurent polynomial with denominator $\prod(1-q^{2n})^{e}$ of constant term $1$, regularity at $q=0$ forces the Laurent polynomial to have no negative powers, and evaluation at $0$ gives an integer. Hence the residue pairing of $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued.

**Integrality of coefficients against representatives.** For $x\in L_{\mathbb Z}$ with rational residue $\sum_ba_bb\in\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$, choose for each $b$ an integral representative $w_b$ of $b$ from step 1.1 and pair modulo $q$: by [F4] the residue form is the positive definite form with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, so $a_b=(x,w_b)$ modulo $q$, and by [F5] this value lies in $A_{\mathbb Z}$; evaluating the resulting $\mathbb Z[q]$-element at $q=0$ gives an integer because $A_{\mathbb Z}$ consists of quotients with denominator $\equiv1\pmod q$. Hence every coefficient $a_b$ is an integer and the image of the injection of [F1] is contained in $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$; conversely finite integer combinations of the classes of the $w_b$ lie in the image, so the image is exactly $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$.

**Norm-one residue classes.** For an integral residue $\bar x=\sum_ba_bb$, step 2.1 gives $a_b\in\mathbb Z$, and [F4] gives $B_0(\bar x,\bar x)=\sum_ba_b^2$. This equals $1$ exactly when $\bar x=\pm b$ for one crystal element. This class statement does not characterize the exact norm of its lattice representatives: in rank one $F^{(2)}$ represents a crystal element but has norm $1/(1+q^2)$. In particular an exact norm-$1$ lattice vector has a signed basis residue, while the converse need not hold.

**Operator stability and conclusion.** By [F2] and [F3] the operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve both $U_A^-$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)$, hence preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ and descend to the integral residue subgroup, which by steps 1.1–1.2 is the free $\mathbb Z$-module $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$; tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ gives the full rational crystal space by [F3]. Together with steps 2.1 and 3.1 this proves all the assertions, with the stated $\mathbb Z$-valued pairing and signed norm-$1$ characterization.

citations.quote: For the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices, their respective normalized polarizations take values in $A_0$ and their crystal residue bases are orthonormal. On every finite label or root component the Gram determinant is a unit of $A_0$, the $A_0$-pairing is perfect and $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. Moreover $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension of the lattice. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Only the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis is retained.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S$ generated by $\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], with $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ the canonical injection. Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the norm-$1$ elements of the integral residue $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

derivations.claim: **$\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution.** The assignment $F_i\mapsto F_i$ extended antimultiplicatively is defined on the free algebra, and applying it to a negative Serre relation $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ and reversing the order of each monomial gives $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{r}F_jF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}$, which is $(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}$ times the same relation after the substitution $r\mapsto1-a_{ij}-r$ and the exact symmetry $\binom{m}{r}_i=\binom{m}{m-r}_i$ of the Gaussian binomials. Hence $\star$ descends to $U_q^-$, fixes $F_i$, and is an anti-involution: it reverses words and its square is the identity.

**Integral and bar compatibility.** Since $\star$ fixes each divided power $F_i^{(r)}$ (it fixes $F_i$ and the scalar $[r]_i!$), it maps each generator of $U_A^-$ to a generator, so $\star(U_A^-)=U_A^-$. It commutes with $\psi$ because $\star$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear while $\psi$ sends $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, and on generators $\psi\star(F_i)=\psi(F_i)=F_i=\star\psi(F_i)$.

**Isometry for the half form.** Write $P=F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$, $Q=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_s}$ as words. Reversing both words, $P^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, $Q^\star=F_{j_s}\cdots F_{j_1}$, and the word Gram formula of [F1] expands both $B(P,Q)$ and $B(P^\star,Q^\star)$ as sums over bijections between matched colors with the same crossing exponents read backwards; reversing a permutation preserves the weight and the crossing number, so the two sums are termwise equal. Hence $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$ on words and, by bilinearity and descent through the Serre ideal, on all of $U_q^-$.

**Lattice stability.** For $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ one has $B(P^\star,P^\star)=B(P,P)\in A_0$ by step 2.1 and the norm characterization of [F1]; hence $P^\star\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ and $\star$ preserves $\mathcal L(\infty)$. It preserves $U_A^-$ by step 1.2, so it preserves $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$; since it commutes with $\psi$ and $\psi(L_{\mathbb Z})=L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, it also preserves the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$.

**The signed residue permutation.** Steps 2.1–3.1 induce an integral involutive isometry of $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$. Each $b$ has residue norm $1$, so its image also has residue norm $1$ and is $\pm b'$ by [F2]. Involutivity makes this a signed permutation. No representative of $b$ is required to have exact field norm $1$.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 prove that $\star$ is an anti-involution preserving $U_A^-$ and commuting with bar, step 2.1 proves that it is an isometry of the normalized half form, step 3.1 proves preservation of $\mathcal L(\infty)$, $L_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, and step 4.1 gives the signed permutation of the integral crystal residue. No unsigned star-crystal theorem is asserted.
