citations.quote: Grouping the sum by the cardinality of $T$, the subsets of cardinality $a$ form a single $S_n$-orbit with stabilizer the ordered block subgroup $S_{\{0,\dots,a-1\}}\times S_{\{a,\dots,n-1\}}\cong S_a\times S_{n-a}$, so the orbit summand is identified with an induced module ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]]): $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ where $W_a:=W(\{0,\dots,a-1\})$ is the value of the FB-module on an $a$-element set, the first factor acts on $W_a$ through $W$ and the second factor acts trivially, and $\boxtimes$ is the external tensor product of modules for the two direct factors ([[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

Equivalently $\Phi_a(V)_n=k\otimes_{kS_n} V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$, the two descriptions being identified by the balancing argument of [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]] and the corresponding identification for $\mathbb Z$ in [[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]];

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\lambda\vdash n$, and let
$S^\lambda_F$ be the corresponding field-valued Specht module
([[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]]).

(i) For every $k\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of $FS_{n+k}$-modules

$$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n\times S_k}^{S_{n+k}}\bigl(S^\lambda_F\boxtimes F\bigr)\cong\bigoplus_{\mu}S^\mu_F,$$

summed over the partitions $\mu\vdash n+k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by adding
one box to each of $k$ different columns (equivalently, $\mu\supseteq\lambda$
and $\mu/\lambda$ is a horizontal $k$-strip).

(ii) For every $0\le k\le n$ there is an isomorphism of $FS_{n-k}$-modules

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_{n-k}\times S_k}S^\lambda_F\bigr)_{S_k}\cong\bigoplus_{\nu}S^\nu_F,$$

summed over the partitions $\nu\vdash n-k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by removing
one box from each of $k$ different columns, where the outer subscript denotes
$S_k$-coinvariants of the restriction to the ordered block subgroup
$S_{n-k}\times S_k\le S_n$ ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]]);
the left-hand side is an $FS_{n-k}$-module because the two blocks commute. All
multiplicities are $0$ or $1$. No choice principle is used.

For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ the field-valued Specht module $S^\lambda_F$ of [[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] is nonzero and irreducible, distinct partitions give non-isomorphic modules, and every irreducible $FS_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them.

Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Read $|\varnothing|=0$ and $\alpha_1=0$ when
$\alpha=\varnothing$. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: for nonempty $\alpha$, at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments; no FI-module structure or generation
degree is asserted here.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and
$n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$,
the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), with
$|\varnothing|=\varnothing_1=0$ and $\varnothing[0]=\varnothing$, and let

$$V(\lambda)_n:=k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$$

be the scalar extension of the rational Specht model of $\lambda[n]$
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]).
By the classification lemma, $V(\lambda)_n$ is the irreducible $kS_n$-module
with label $\lambda[n]$, and every irreducible $kS_n$-module is isomorphic to
exactly one $V(\lambda)_n$: indeed, every partition $\mu=(\mu_1,\mu_2,\dots)$
of $n$ is uniquely $\lambda[n]$ for the partition
$\lambda=(\mu_2,\mu_3,\dots)$ obtained by deleting the first row, and
$n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ holds precisely because $\mu_1\ge\mu_2$;
consequently the labels $\lambda[n]$ run over the partitions of $n$ without
repetition. At $n=0$ the only label and its tail are both $\varnothing$,
and $V(\varnothing)_0=k$ with the trivial $S_0$-action.

Say that $V(\lambda)_n$ **occurs as a constituent** of $V_n$ when there are
$kS_n$-submodules $U\subseteq W\subseteq V_n$ with
$W/U\cong V(\lambda)_n$ ([[def-submodule]], [[def-quotient-module]]); this is a
condition on subquotients and requires no decomposition or finite-dimensionality
of $V_n$. The **weight** of $V$ is

$$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\bigl\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\bigr\},$$

the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed. The set of integers
displayed is a set of nonnegative integers, so the supremum is well defined in
$\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$; it is $0$ for $V=0$, and $\operatorname{weight}(V)=\infty$
exactly when the displayed set is unbounded. No finiteness of
$\operatorname{weight}(V)$ is asserted.

If $W$ is a **subquotient** of $V$, meaning that $W\cong U'/U$ for sub-FI-modules
$U\subseteq U'\subseteq V$ computed pointwise, then
$\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$: a constituent of $W_n$ is
a subquotient of the subquotient $U'_n/U_n$ of $V_n$, hence a subquotient of
$V_n$, so it contributes the same label $|\lambda|$ to the supremum for $V$. No
choice principle is used: the labels $\lambda[n]$, constituents and the
supremum are set-theoretic data, and no bases or decompositions are chosen.

Let $G$ be a finite group, let $k$ be a field with $\operatorname{char} k \nmid |G|$, let $\rho:G \to \operatorname{GL}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$, and let $W \le V$ be a subrepresentation.

derivations.claim: The $S_n$-orbits of the subset summands of $M(W)_{\mathbf a\sqcup[n]}$ are indexed by $(U,r)$, where $U\subseteq\mathbf a$ and $0\le r\le n$: take the representative $U\sqcup[r]$ with $[r]$ in the moving block. Its stabilizer is $S_r\times S_{n-r}$, and the second factor acts trivially on $W(U\sqcup[r])$. Transporting the orbit summands to the representative identifies their coinvariants with $(W(U\sqcup[r]))_{S_r}$: different transports differ by a stabilizer element, so they give the same map after quotienting, and the representative inclusion is inverse. Thus $\Phi_aM(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{U\subseteq\mathbf a}\bigoplus_{r=0}^n(W(U\sqcup[r]))_{S_r}$. Choosing a single bijection $\mathbf b\to U$, with $b=|U|$, identifies this factor with $\Phi_b(W)_r:=(W(\mathbf b\sqcup[r]))_{S_r}$; for an FB-module this denotes only a degreewise quotient, without transition maps. The standard inclusion $[n]\hookrightarrow[n+1]$ fixes every representative with $r\le n$, so $T$ acts as the identity on every existing factor and only adds factors with $r=n+1$. [F1, F2, given]

Let $k$ have characteristic $0$ and let $|\lambda|=m$. For $n\ge m$ the identification $M(S^\lambda_k)_n\cong\operatorname{Ind}^{S_n}_{S_m	imes S_{n-m}}(S^\lambda_k oxtimes k)$ of [F1] together with the branching rule [F3] shows that the constituents of $M(\lambda)_n$ are the Specht modules $S^{
u}$ over the partitions $
u\vdash n$ obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box in each of $n-m$ different columns; for $n<m$ the value is $0$. For such a $
u$, the added boxes occupy $n-m$ distinct columns, so $
u_1\ge n-m$; writing $
u=\eta[n]$ this gives $|\eta|=n-
u_1\le m$. Hence every constituent $V(\eta)_n$ of any $M(\lambda)_n$ has $|\eta|\le m$, so $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))\le m$ by [F5]. [F1, F3, F5, given]

By step 1.1 the map $T\colon\Phi_aM(W)_n\to\Phi_aM(W)_{n+1}$ is injective for all $a,n$, since it is the identity on every direct summand and maps distinct summands to distinct summands; hence $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$. If $W_i=0$ for $i>m$, then $\Phi_{|U|}(W)_r=0$ for $r>m$, so for $n\ge m$ the direct-sum decomposition of step 1.1 is independent of $n$ and $T$ is an isomorphism; hence $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$. For $M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ the factor $\Phi_0(k[S_m])_m=(k[S_m])_{S_m}\cong k$ is nonzero when $k\ne0$, and it occurs in $\Phi_0(M(m))_n$ only when $n\ge m$; so for $m>0$ the map $T\colon\Phi_0(M(m))_{m-1}\to\Phi_0(M(m))_m$ is not surjective, giving $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(m))\ge m$ and hence equality, and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$. For $m=0$ the upper bound already gives equality $0$; no negative degree is used. Over the zero ring all modules vanish, so all these degrees are $0$ instead. [F2, step 1.1]

Conversely, for $n\ge m+\lambda_1$ the padded partition $\lambda[n]=(n-m,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box in each of the first $n-m$ columns, so $V(\lambda)_n$ occurs in $M(\lambda)_n$ by step 1.2; therefore $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))\ge m$, and with step 1.2, $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=m$. [F3, F5, step 1.2]

For the stability degree, fix $a\ge0$ and use the decomposition of step 1.1 for $W=S^\lambda_k$: the factor indexed by $U\subseteq\mathbf a$ is $\Phi_{|U|}(S^\lambda_k)_r=(S^\lambda_k)_{S_r}$ when $|U|+r=m$ (and $0$ otherwise), where $S_r$ acts on the last $r$ points. By the branching rule [F3], $(S^\lambda_k)_{S_r}$ is the sum of the Specht modules obtained from $\lambda$ by removing one box from each of $r$ different columns, and by the strip criterion [F4] such a removal exists exactly when $r\le\lambda_1$; hence $(S^\lambda_k)_{S_r}=0$ for  $r>\lambda_1$ and is nonzero for  $r=\lambda_1$ provided $m\ge\lambda_1$. Consequently, for every $n\ge\lambda_1$ all nonzero factors of $\Phi_aM(\lambda)_n$ already occur in $\Phi_aM(\lambda)_{\lambda_1}$, and $T$ acts as the identity on them, so $T$ is surjective for all $n\ge\lambda_1$; thus $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(\lambda))\le\lambda_1$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

Sharpness: if $\lambda_1>0$, take $a=m-\lambda_1\ge0$. The factor with $U=\mathbf a$ and  $r=\lambda_1$ equals $(S^\lambda_k)_{S_{\lambda_1}}\ne0$ and occurs in $\Phi_aM(\lambda)_n$ exactly when $n\ge\lambda_1$; in particular $T\colon\Phi_aM(\lambda)_{\lambda_1-1}\to\Phi_aM(\lambda)_{\lambda_1}$ has a nonzero target summand not met by $T$, so it is not surjective and $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(\lambda))\ge\lambda_1$. Hence $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$, and by step 2.1, which gives injectivity degree $0$, $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. For $\lambda=\varnothing$ we have $m=\lambda_1=0$, $M(\varnothing)=M(k)$ has all transition maps isomorphisms and stability degree $0$. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.3]

Step 2.1 gives the general injectivity and surjectivity bounds and the exact stability degree of $M(m)$; steps 1.2 and 2.2 give $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$; steps 2.3 and 3.1 give $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. [step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1] ∎

citations.quote:
Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]) and let
$\Sigma$ be a set of supported elements $(S,v)$, where $S$ is a finite set and
$v\in V_S$. The support $S$ is part of the generator data, even when distinct
values of $V$ have overlapping underlying sets. Write
$\Sigma_S:=\{v\in V_S:(S,v)\in\Sigma\}$; a sub-FI-module $W$ contains
$\Sigma$ when $v\in W_S$ for every $(S,v)\in\Sigma$. The
**sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written
$\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of
$V$ that are subfunctors and contain $\Sigma$
([[def-submodule]], [[lem-submodule-criterion-sums-and-intersections]] for the
objectwise intersection of submodules). The family is nonempty because $V$
itself qualifies, and the intersection is a sub-FI-module, since each
transition map $f_*$ preserves every member and hence their intersection;
thus $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$ is the smallest sub-FI-module of $V$
containing $\Sigma$.

Explicitly, $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)_T$ is the $k$-span of all elements
$f_*(v)$ with $(S,v)\in\Sigma$ and $f\colon S\to T$ a morphism of $FI$: the
set of all finite $k$-linear combinations of such elements is a sub-FI-module
of $V$ containing $\Sigma$, because $g_*(f_*(v))=(g\circ f)_*(v)$, and every
sub-FI-module containing $\Sigma$ contains each $f_*(v)$; hence it equals the
intersection. Call $V$ **finitely generated** when
$\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$ for some finite $\Sigma$, and **generated in
degree $\le d$** when $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le d})=V$, where
$V_{\le d}=\{([m],v):0\le m\le d,\ v\in V_{[m]}\}$ uses the finite skeleton of FI;
transport by bijections shows that its span also contains every $V_S$ with
$|S|\le d$. The **generation degree** of
$V$ is the least $d\ge0$ such that $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, and
$\infty$ when no such $d$ exists
([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]).

Finite generation of $V$ and pointwise finite generation of the individual
$k$-modules $V_S$ are different conditions: the pointwise property is implied
by finite generation (as shown below by
[[lem-generated-in-degree-d-is-a-quotient-of-free-fi-modules]]) but does not
imply it, and no pointwise finite generation or finite-dimensionality is built
into either notion. A finite generating set gives a finite degree bound: take the maximum
cardinality of its supporting sets (and $0$ for the empty generating set).
When a generator is written simply as $v\in V_S$, its specified support $S$
is understood, so $\operatorname{span}_V(v)$ means
$\operatorname{span}_V(\{(S,v)\})$.
Generation in bounded degree alone does not imply finite generation. No choice principle
is used: $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$ is defined by an intersection of
subfunctors, and its explicit description involves only finite $k$-linear
combinations.

Then $M(m)_S$ has as $k$-basis the injections $[m]\hookrightarrow S$ — equivalently, the ordered sequences of $m$ distinct elements of $S$ — and for a partition $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=m$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, put $M(\lambda):=M(S^\lambda_k)$, where the FB-module $S^\lambda_k$ is supported on $m$-element sets and $S^\lambda_k(T):= k[\operatorname{Iso}([m],T)]\otimes_{kS_m}S^\lambda_k$.

If $M$ is free with basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ and $N$ is free with basis $(f_j)_{j\in J}$, then $M\otimes_RN$ is free with basis $$\bigl(e_i\otimes f_j\bigr)_{(i,j)\in I\times J}.$$ Equivalently, the canonical map $R^{(I\times J)}\to M\otimes_RN$ sending the standard basis vector at $(i,j)$ to $e_i\otimes f_j$ is an isomorphism.

(b) $V$ is finitely generated if and only if there is a finite family $m_1,\dots,m_r\ge0$ with a surjection $$M(m_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus M(m_r)\twoheadrightarrow V;$$ $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ if and only if there is a surjection $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ with $m_i\le d$ for all $i$.
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $$A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\longrightarrow0$$ be an exact sequence of $R$-modules, and let $N$ be an $R$-module.

The homomorphism induced by the coordinate inclusions is a natural $R$-module isomorphism $$\Phi:\bigoplus_{i\in I}(M_i\otimes_RN)\longrightarrow\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i\right)\otimes_RN,$$ $$\Phi\bigl(\jmath_i(m\otimes n)\bigr)=\jmath_i(m)\otimes n.$$ The same holds with the direct sum in the second variable: there is a natural $R$-module isomorphism $$\Phi':\bigoplus_{i\in I}(N\otimes_RM_i)\longrightarrow N\otimes_R\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i\right),\qquad \Phi'\bigl(\jmath_i(n\otimes m)\bigr)=n\otimes\jmath_i(m).$$ The assertion includes $I=\varnothing$, when both sides are zero.

Let $$F:=\mathbb Z^{(M\times N)}$$ be the free $\mathbb Z$-module on the set $M\times N$ ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]], [[thm-universal-property-of-free-modules]]), and write $e_{(m,n)}$ for its standard basis elements.

derivations.claim: $V\otimes W$ is an FI-module: $(V\otimes W)(\mathrm{id}_S)=\mathrm{id}_{V_S}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{W_S}=\mathrm{id}_{V_S\otimes W_S}$, and $(g\circ f)_*\otimes(g\circ f)_*=(g_*\otimes g_*)(f_*\otimes f_*)$ for composable injections; the pointwise tensor product of $k$-linear maps and the functor axioms in each variable give the claim. [given, algebra]

Let $U:=M(m_1)\otimes M(m_2)$, with $(U)_S$ having $k$-basis the pairs $(f_1,f_2)$ of injections $f_1\colon[m_1]\hookrightarrow S$, $f_2\colon[m_2]\hookrightarrow S$ [F2]. For a basis element $(f_1,f_2)$, put $T:=\operatorname{im}(f_1)\cup\operatorname{im}(f_2)\subseteq S$, so $|T|\le m_1+m_2$; the maps $f_i$ factor as $f_i=\iota\circ g_i$ with $g_i\colon[m_i]\hookrightarrow T$ injective and $\iota\colon T\hookrightarrow S$ the inclusion, and functoriality gives $(f_1,f_2)=(\iota_*\otimes\iota_*)(g_1,g_2)$ with $(g_1,g_2)\in U_T$. Hence every basis element of $U_S$ lies in the span of the images of the $U_T$ with $|T|\le m_1+m_2$, so $\operatorname{span}_U(U_{\le m_1+m_2})=U$ by [F1]: $U$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

Now let $V$ be generated in degree $\le m_1$ and $W$ in degree $\le m_2$, so that by [F3] there are surjections $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ and $\bigoplus_{j\in J}M(n_j)\twoheadrightarrow W$ with $m_i\le m_1$, $n_j\le m_2$. Tensoring them pointwise and distributing the direct sums [F4] gives a surjection $\bigoplus_{i,j}\bigl(M(m_i)\otimes M(n_j)\bigr)\twoheadrightarrow V\otimes W$. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

Each summand $U_{ij}:=M(m_i)\otimes M(n_j)$ is generated in degree $\le m_i+n_j\le m_1+m_2$ by step 2.1, hence so is their direct sum; and a quotient of a module generated in degree $\le d$ is generated in degree $\le d$, because the image of $\operatorname{span}(U_{\le d})=U$ under a surjective map of FI-modules is $\operatorname{span}$ of the images of $U_{\le d}$, which is the whole quotient. Therefore $V\otimes W$, being a quotient of the sum of the $U_{ij}$, is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$. [F1, step 2.1, step 2.2]

If $V$ and $W$ are finitely generated, they are generated in degrees $\le m_1$ and $\le m_2$ for suitable finite $m_1,m_2$, and [F3] allows finite index sets $I,J$ in step 2.2. For each pair $(i,j)$, the finitely many basis pairs of injections into the finitely many sets $[t]$ with $t\le m_i+n_j$ generate $M(m_i)\otimes M(n_j)$ by step 2.1 and transport by a bijection $[|T|]\to T$. Their union over the finite $I\times J$ is finite and its image generates $V\otimes W$; hence $V\otimes W$ is finitely generated, with the stated degree bound. [F1, F3, step 3.1] ∎

boundaries.evidence: step 2.1: m_1 = 0 or m_2 = 0 makes one factor M(0) = M(k), and the union T of images covers the empty-image case without exception.
step 1.1: V = 0 or W = 0 yields V_S tensor W_S = 0 and the zero FI-module, included in the functoriality verification.
Step 2.1: M(1) tensor M(1) has both equal-image pairs generated at rank 1 and distinct-image pairs generated at rank 2; one rank-2 equal-image pair alone does not generate it.
step 2.2: the surjections supplied by the presentation lemma may have zero summands when a factor is 0, and empty finite sums of modules are allowed.
step 3.1: the degree bound m_1 + m_2 is inclusive, with equality in T = im f_1 union im f_2 when the two images are disjoint.
Step 4.1: use the finite basis pairs in the finitely many ranks t<=m_i+n_j for a finite free presentation; these give a finite generating set for the tensor quotient.

boundaries.reason: The proposition asserts that a tensor product of finitely generated modules is finitely generated; no biconditional is claimed.
No converse necessary condition is stated or used in the proof.

risk_review.notes: Read six proof steps and seven suppliers. Basis pairs factor through the union of their images, of size <=m_1+m_2; tensor right exactness and direct-sum distribution pass the bounded degree result to arbitrary-index presentations. Finite generation separately uses finite presentations and the finite union of low-rank injection pairs, so it never follows merely from bounded generation. citations.quote: An **FI-module over a commutative ring $k$** ([[def-commutative-ring]]) is a covariant functor $V\colon FI\to k\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]).

it satisfies $V_n\cong k^n$ with the permutation action of $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) and is generated by $V_{\{0\}}$ in degree $\le1$ ([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
A pure tensor with $v_i=v_j$ maps to the pure tensor with $T(v_i)=T(v_j)$, so $T^{\otimes k}(W_k(V))\subseteq W_k(W)$ for the relation subspaces of [[def-kth-exterior-power-by-quotient]].

The **$k$th exterior power** of $V$ is the quotient vector space $$\Lambda^kV:=V^{\otimes k}/W_k,$$ and the **basic wedge map** is $$\wedge:V^k\longrightarrow\Lambda^kV,\qquad (v_1,\ldots,v_k)\longmapsto v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_k+W_k.$$
Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring and let $F$ be a finite free $R$-module with ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$.
For every $p$, the wedges $e_I$ with $|I|=p$ form an $R$-basis of $\bigwedge^pF$;

The **$k$th exterior power** of $V$ is the quotient vector space $$\Lambda^kV:=V^{\otimes k}/W_k,$$ and the **basic wedge map** is $$\wedge:V^k\longrightarrow\Lambda^kV,\qquad (v_1,\ldots,v_k)\longmapsto v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_k+W_k.$$

For $i\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ let $X_i\colon S_n\to\mathbb N$ be the function sending a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ to the number $X_i(\sigma):=c_i(\sigma)$ of $i$-element orbits in its cycle type ([[def-permutation-support-disjoint-cycles-and-cycle-type]], [[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]], [[def-natural-numbers]]);

When $|X|=n$, the **cycle type** of $\sigma$ is the list of natural numbers $c_1(\sigma),\ldots,c_n(\sigma)$, where $c_k(\sigma)$ is the number of $k$-element orbits of the action generated by $\sigma$.

For a square matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(F)$, its **trace** is the sum of its diagonal entries, $$\operatorname{tr}(A):=\sum_{i\in n}a_{ii}.$$ For $n=0$, this is the empty sum, so the unique empty matrix has trace $0$.

derivations.claim: $W$ is a functor: $W(\mathrm{id}_S)=\Lambda^2(\mathrm{id}_{V_S})=\mathrm{id}_{W_S}$ and $W(g\circ f)=\Lambda^2(V(g)V(f))=\Lambda^2V(g)\circ\Lambda^2V(f)=W(g)W(f)$, using that $V$ satisfies the functor axioms [F1] and that $\Lambda^2$ preserves identities and composites [F2]; hence $W$ is an FI-module with values $W_S=\Lambda^2V_S$, and for $S=[n]$ this is $W_n=\Lambda^2(k^n)$ with the action induced by the permutation action of $S_n$ on $k^n$. [F1, F2]

Fix $n$ and $\sigma\in S_n$. By [F3], applied to the free module $V_n$ with basis $e_0,\dots,e_{n-1}$, the elements $e_i\wedge e_j$ with $i<j$ form a $k$-basis of $W_n$; and $\sigma\cdot(e_i\wedge e_j)=e_{\sigma(i)}\wedge e_{\sigma(j)}$. Hence the diagonal entry of the matrix of $\sigma$ at the basis element $e_i\wedge e_j$ is the coefficient of $e_i\wedge e_j$ in $e_{\sigma(i)}\wedge e_{\sigma(j)}$, which can be nonzero only when $\{\sigma(i),\sigma(j)\}=\{i,j\}$. In that case $\sigma$ restricts to a bijection of the two-element set $\{i,j\}$: it is either the identity, giving coefficient $+1$, or the transposition $(\,i\ j\,)$, giving $e_j\wedge e_i=-e_i\wedge e_j$ and coefficient $-1$. There is no other possibility, so the diagonal entry is $+1$ exactly for the unordered pairs of distinct fixed points of $\sigma$, is $-1$ exactly for the $2$-cycles of $\sigma$, and is $0$ otherwise. [F3, F4, given, algebra]

By [F5] the trace of $\sigma$ on $W_n$ is the sum of the diagonal entries computed in step 1.2, namely the number $\binom{X_1(\sigma)}{2}$ of unordered pairs of distinct fixed points minus the number $X_2(\sigma)$ of $2$-cycles: $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma;W_n)=\binom{X_1(\sigma)}{2}-X_2(\sigma)$. For $n=0$ and $n=1$ the module $W_n$ is $0$ and both sides are $0$, since then $X_1(\sigma)\le1$. This holds for every $n$, and $\binom{X_1}{2}-X_2$ is a character polynomial of weighted degree $2$, so the trace function of $W$ is given by that character polynomial. [F4, F5, step 1.2]

Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 show that $W=\Lambda^2V$ is an FI-module with $W_n\cong\Lambda^2(k^n)$ whose character is the weighted-degree-two character polynomial $\binom{X_1}{2}-X_2$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

If $T_{\Phi_a(V)}$ is surjective, then $T_{\Phi_a(W)}$ is surjective as well, because every element of $\Phi_a(W)_{n+1}$ is the image under the surjection $q_{n+1}$ of an element hit by $T_{\Phi_a(V)}$. Hence the threshold controlling surjectivity of $T$ for $W$ is at most that for $V$, i.e. $\operatorname{surj-deg}(W)\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$. [F1, given]

Let $k$ have characteristic $0$ and let $W$ be a finite-dimensional $kS_m$-module regarded as an FB-module supported on cardinality $m$. By [F5] $W\cong\bigoplus_\lambda c_\lambda S^\lambda_k$ (finite sum), and by the additivity in [F3] $M(W)\cong\bigoplus_\lambda M(S^\lambda_k)^{\oplus c_\lambda}$; hence $\operatorname{weight}(M(W))=\max(\{0\}\cup\{|\lambda|:c_\lambda\ne0\})\le m$ by [F4] and [F6]. [F3, F4, F5, F6]

Let $W$ be an arbitrary $kS_m$-module (characteristic zero) and let $V(\eta)_N$ be a constituent of $M(W)_N$. Let $P/Q\subseteq M(W)_N$ be a subquotient isomorphic to $V(\eta)_N$ and choose $x\in P\setminus Q$. The $S_N$-orbit span $X$ of $x$ is a finite-dimensional $S_N$-submodule of $M(W)_N$, and $X/(X\cap Q)$ is a nonzero submodule of the simple $V(\eta)_N$, hence is isomorphic to $V(\eta)_N$; in particular $V(\eta)_N$ is a constituent of $X$. Now $X$ lies in the direct sum $\bigoplus_{T\subseteq[N]}W(T)$ of [F3] over finitely many $T$, and for each of those $T$ the projection of $X$ to $W(T)$ is finite-dimensional; let $W'$ be the $kS_m$-submodule of $W$ generated by the finitely many images of these projections under bijections $[m]\to T$ chosen for the finitely many $m$-subsets $T$. Then $W'$ is finite-dimensional and $X\subseteq M(W')_N$, so $V(\eta)_N$ is a constituent of $M(W')_N$; by step 1.2 and [F6], $|\eta|\le m$. Therefore $\operatorname{weight}(M(W))\le m$ for every $kS_m$-module $W$. [F3, F6, step 1.2]

For (b), suppose $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$. By [F3] the evaluation map $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\twoheadrightarrow V$ is surjective, and each $V_m$ is supported in degree $m\le d$, so $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(V_m))\le m\le d$ by [F4]; by [F2] the finite direct sum has surjectivity degree at most $d$, and step 1.1 applied to the quotient gives $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le d$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

For (c), the same surjection $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\twoheadrightarrow V$ and [F6] give $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le\operatorname{weight}\bigl(\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\bigr)$. A simple subquotient of a finite direct sum occurs in one summand: lift a nonzero vector of that quotient and take its finite group-orbit span. The component projections lie in finite-dimensional invariant subspaces of the summands; their finite direct sum is semisimple by [F5], so the simple quotient is isomorphic to a simple summand occurring in one component. Thus the weight of the finite direct sum is $\max_{m\le d}\operatorname{weight}(M(V_m))\le d$ by step 2.1. Hence $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$. [F3, F5, F6, step 2.1]
Step 1.1 proves (a); step 2.2 proves (b); step 3.1 proves (c). [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

$\Sigma$ be a set of supported elements $(S,v)$, where $S$ is a finite set and
$v\in V_S$. The support $S$ is part of the generator data, even when distinct
values of $V$ have overlapping underlying sets. Write
$\Sigma_S:=\{v\in V_S:(S,v)\in\Sigma\}$; a sub-FI-module $W$ contains
$\Sigma$ when $v\in W_S$ for every $(S,v)\in\Sigma$. The
**sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written
$\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of
$V$ that are subfunctors and contain $\Sigma$
([[def-submodule]], [[lem-submodule-criterion-sums-and-intersections]] for the
objectwise intersection of submodules). The family is nonempty because $V$
itself qualifies, and the intersection is a sub-FI-module, since each
transition map $f_*$ preserves every member and hence their intersection;
thus $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$ is the smallest sub-FI-module of $V$
containing $\Sigma$.

Explicitly, $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)_T$ is the $k$-span of all elements
$f_*(v)$ with $(S,v)\in\Sigma$ and $f\colon S\to T$ a morphism of $FI$: the
set of all finite $k$-linear combinations of such elements is a sub-FI-module
of $V$ containing $\Sigma$, because $g_*(f_*(v))=(g\circ f)_*(v)$, and every
sub-FI-module containing $\Sigma$ contains each $f_*(v)$; hence it equals the
intersection. Call $V$ **finitely generated** when
$\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$ for some finite $\Sigma$, and **generated in
degree $\le d$** when $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le d})=V$, where
$V_{\le d}=\{([m],v):0\le m\le d,\ v\in V_{[m]}\}$ uses the finite skeleton of FI;
transport by bijections shows that its span also contains every $V_S$ with
$|S|\le d$. The **generation degree** of
$V$ is the least $d\ge0$ such that $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, and
$\infty$ when no such $d$ exists

[F2, F3, F5, step 1.1]

Since $\Phi_a(W)$ is a $k[T]$-submodule of the finitely generated module $\Phi_a(V)$ over the Noetherian ring $k[T]$, it is a finitely generated $k[T]$-module; writing a finite generating set as finite sums of homogeneous components, the homogeneous components of the generators form a finite generating set consisting of elements $x_1,\dots,x_r$ with $x_i\in\Phi_a(W)_{n_i}$. [F1, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

For each $i$ choose a lift $w_i\in W_{a+n_i}$ of $x_i$ (possible because $\Phi_a(W)_{n_i}$ is a quotient of $W_{a+n_i}$), and for each $n<a$ choose a finite generating set of the $k$-module $W_n$, which is possible by step 1.1; let $\widetilde W\subseteq W$ be the sub-FI-module generated by all these elements. Then $\Phi_a(\widetilde W)=\Phi_a(W)$: the inclusion gives $\Phi_a(\widetilde W)\subseteq\Phi_a(W)$, while each $x_i$ is the image of $w_i\in\widetilde W$, so $\Phi_a(\widetilde W)$ contains a generating set of $\Phi_a(W)$. By exactness [F1], applied to $0\to\widetilde W\to W\to W/\widetilde W\to0$, we get $\Phi_a(W/\widetilde W)=0$. [F1, step 1.1, step 3.1]

Let $U:=W/\widetilde W$. Restricting scalars to $\mathbb Q$ gives an FI-module $U^{\mathbb Q}$ over $\mathbb Q$, a subquotient of $V^{\mathbb Q}$ by construction. The evaluation surjection $\bigoplus_{m\le a}M(V_m)\twoheadrightarrow V$ remains a surjection of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces after restriction, and the restriction of the free $k$-FI-module $M(V_m)$ is the free $\mathbb Q$-FI-module on $V_m^{\mathbb Q}$, because both are the same direct sum of the same coefficient spaces with the same transition maps; hence $V^{\mathbb Q}$ is generated in degree $\le a$ over $\mathbb Q$ by [F2]. Therefore $\operatorname{weight}(V^{\mathbb Q})\le a$ by [F3] applied over the characteristic-zero field $\mathbb Q$, and $\operatorname{weight}(U^{\mathbb Q})\le a$ because weight is monotone under subquotients [F4]. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, step 4.1, given]

By [F6] the coinvariants of $U^{\mathbb Q}$ are the restriction of the coinvariants of $U$, so $\Phi_a(U^{\mathbb Q})=0$ by step 4.1. Hence for every $n\ge a$ the coinvariants $(U^{\mathbb Q}_n)_{S_{n-a}}=\Phi_a(U^{\mathbb Q})_{n-a}$ vanish, and step 5.1 with [F4] gives $U^{\mathbb Q}_n=0$, which forces $U_n=0$; for $n<a$ the module $U_n$ vanishes by the choice of generators of $W_n$ in step 4.1. Thus $U=0$, that is $W=\widetilde W$ is generated by the finite set of elements chosen in step 4.1, so $W$ is finitely generated. [F4, F6, step 4.1, step 5.1]

Steps 1.1–6.1 prove that every sub-FI-module $W$ of a finitely generated FI-module $V$ over a commutative Noetherian ring $k$ containing $\mathbb Q$ is finitely generated, so the category of FI-modules over $k$ is Noetherian. All generating sets and lifts chosen are finite, the Hilbert basis theorem enters only through its choice-free finite-generation form [F5], and no map $k\to\mathbb C$ or basis of an infinite-dimensional rational space is used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and
$n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$,
the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), with
$|\varnothing|=\varnothing_1=0$ and $\varnothing[0]=\varnothing$, and let

$$V(\lambda)_n:=k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$$

be the scalar extension of the rational Specht model of $\lambda[n]$
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]).
By the classification lemma, $V(\lambda)_n$ is the irreducible $kS_n$-module
with label $\lambda[n]$, and every irreducible $kS_n$-module is isomorphic to
exactly one $V(\lambda)_n$: indeed, every partition $\mu=(\mu_1,\mu_2,\dots)$
of $n$ is uniquely $\lambda[n]$ for the partition
$\lambda=(\mu_2,\mu_3,\dots)$ obtained by deleting the first row, and
$n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ holds precisely because $\mu_1\ge\mu_2$;
consequently the labels $\lambda[n]$ run over the partitions of $n$ without
repetition. At $n=0$ the only label and its tail are both $\varnothing$,
and $V(\varnothing)_0=k$ with the trivial $S_0$-action.

Say that $V(\lambda)_n$ **occurs as a constituent** of $V_n$ when there are
$kS_n$-submodules $U\subseteq W\subseteq V_n$ with
$W/U\cong V(\lambda)_n$ ([[def-submodule]], [[def-quotient-module]]); this is a
condition on subquotients and requires no decomposition or finite-dimensionality
of $V_n$. The **weight** of $V$ is

$$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\bigl\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\bigr\},$$

the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed. The set of integers
displayed is a set of nonnegative integers, so the supremum is well defined in
$\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$; it is $0$ for $V=0$, and $\operatorname{weight}(V)=\infty$
exactly when the displayed set is unbounded. No finiteness of
$\operatorname{weight}(V)$ is asserted.

If $W$ is a **subquotient** of $V$, meaning that $W\cong U'/U$ for sub-FI-modules
$U\subseteq U'\subseteq V$ computed pointwise, then
$\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$: a constituent of $W_n$ is
a subquotient of the subquotient $U'_n/U_n$ of $V_n$, hence a subquotient of
$V_n$, so it contributes the same label $|\lambda|$ to the supremum for $V$. No
choice principle is used: the labels $\lambda[n]$, constituents and the
supremum are set-theoretic data, and no bases or decompositions are chosen.
The **stability degree** is $$\operatorname{stab-deg}(V):=\max\bigl(\operatorname{inj-deg}(V),\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\bigr).$$ Each of the three is $+\infty$ when no such $s$ exists;

derivations.claim: The commuting $S_a$-action on $\Phi_a(V)$ makes every $T$ $S_a$-equivariant by [[def-fi-coinvariant-functors-and-transition-maps]], so the isomorphisms used below preserve representation types. Let $K_n:=\ker\varphi_n\subseteq V_n$ and let $\varphi'_n:=\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n}^{S_{n+1}}\varphi_n\colon\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n}^{S_{n+1}}V_n\to V_{n+1}$ with cokernel $C_{n+1}$, so that $C_{n+1}$ is a quotient of $V_{n+1}$. The image of $\varphi'_n$ is the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$, since $\varphi'_n(\sigma\otimes v)=\sigma\cdot\varphi_n(v)$; hence condition (I) is $K_n=0$ for all $n\ge N$ and condition (II) is $C_{n+1}=0$ for all $n\ge N$. [F1, F6, given]
If $|\lambda|>d$, then $c_{\lambda,n}=0$ for every $n$ for which $c_{\lambda,n}$ is defined, so condition (III) is automatic for such $\lambda$; it remains to treat $|\lambda|\le d$. [F3, step 1.1]

Vanishing criteria: for $n\ge d$ one has $K_n=0\iff(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}=0$, and for $n+1\ge d$ one has $C_{n+1}=0\iff(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}=0$. Indeed $K_n$ is a submodule of $V_n$ and $C_{n+1}$ is a quotient of $V_{n+1}$, both are subquotients of modules of weight $d$ ([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]), and [F4](iv) applies with $a=d$. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

Factorization: for $n\ge d$, identify $\Phi_d(V)_{n-d}$ with $(V_n)_{S_{n-d}}$ and $\Phi_d(V)_{n+1-d}$ with $(V_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ along the standard identifications of $\mathbf d\sqcup(n-d)$ with $[n]$ and of $\mathbf d\sqcup(n+1-d)$ with $[n+1]$. The transition map $T\colon(V_n)_{S_{n-d}}\to(V_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}$ factors in two ways: $T=q\circ(\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}$, where $q$ is the quotient map onto coinvariants of the larger subgroup $S_{n+1-d}\ge S_{n-d}$, and $T=(\varphi'_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}\circ\psi$, where $\psi$ is induced by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$. Exactness of coinvariants over $k$ gives $(K_n)_{S_{n-d}}=\ker\bigl((\varphi_n)_{S_{n-d}}\bigr)$ and $(C_{n+1})_{S_{n+1-d}}=\operatorname{coker}\bigl((\varphi'_n)_{S_{n+1-d}}\bigr)$. [F6, given, step 1.1]

We prove (III) by induction on $m=|\lambda|$ in the range $m\le d$. Fix $m\le d$, let $n\ge s+d$ (so $n-m\ge s\ge0$), and assume the multiplicities $c_{\mu,n'}$ are independent of $n'$ in the range for all $|\mu|<m$. Since $n-m\ge s$, the transition maps give isomorphisms $\Phi_m(V)_{n-m}\cong\Phi_m(V)_i$ for all $i\ge s$, so the isomorphism class of $(V_n)_{S_{n-m}}=\Phi_m(V)_{n-m}$ is independent of $n$. This proves (III) for all $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|\le d$ and hence, with step 2.1, for all $\lambda$. [F2, F4, F5, F6, F7, step 2.1]

Let $n\ge s+d$, so that $n-d\ge s$ and $T\colon\Phi_d(V)_{n-d}\to\Phi_d(V)_{n+1-d}$ is an isomorphism by [F2]. citations.quote: The sequence is **uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge N$** when all three of the following hold.

The **sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of $V$ that are subfunctors and contain $\Sigma$ ([[def-submodule]], [[lem-submodule-criterion-sums-and-intersections]] for the objectwise intersection of submodules).

Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]), with free FI-modules $M(m)$ as in [[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]] and span as in [[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]].

Grouping the sum by the cardinality of $T$, the subsets of cardinality $a$ form a single $S_n$-orbit with stabilizer the ordered block subgroup $S_{\{0,\dots,a-1\}}\times S_{\{a,\dots,n-1\}}\cong S_a\times S_{n-a}$, so the orbit summand is identified with an induced module ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]]): $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ where $W_a:=W(\{0,\dots,a-1\})$ is the value of the FB-module on an $a$-element set, the first factor acts on $W_a$ through $W$ and the second factor acts trivially, and $\boxtimes$ is the external tensor product of modules for the two direct factors ([[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$, with surjectivity degree and stability degree as in [[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]] and weight as in [[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]].
the **surjectivity degree** $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$ is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the map $T$ is surjective for all $n\ge s$.

Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$ and let $M(W)$ be the free FI-module of
[[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]]. Then
$\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for all $i>m$ then
$\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular
$M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ over a nonzero ring $k$ satisfies $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$
([[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition,
then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]) and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. No choice principle is used.

Let $k$ be a commutative Noetherian ring containing $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-noetherian-ring]], [[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]), and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ ([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]], [[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]).
Under this natural identification $\Phi_a$ becomes the invariants functor, which is left exact (kernels of equivariant maps are computed pointwise), and therefore $\Phi_a$ is exact;
The **injectivity degree** $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)$ is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective for all $n\ge s$;

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d:=\operatorname{weight}(V)<\infty$ and stability degree $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$ ([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]], [[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).

derivations.claim: $(\Rightarrow)$ Assume that $V$ is finitely generated, say generated in degree $\le g$. By [F3] $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$, and by [F2] there is a finite surjection $M:=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{g}M(i)^{\oplus b_i}\twoheadrightarrow V$; let $K$ be its kernel. The module $M$ is finitely generated (each $M(i)$ is generated in degree $\le i$ by [F2]), so $K$ is finitely generated by [F5] applied over the field $k$; say $K$ is generated in degree $\le r$. These data will bound the injectivity degree of $V$ below. [F2, F3, F5]

$(\Leftarrow)$ Conversely, assume that $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable with range $n\ge N$. For $n\ge N$ condition (II) says that the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$, and every injection $f\colon[n]\to[n+1]$ equals $\sigma\circ f_0$ for the standard inclusion $f_0$ and some $\sigma\in S_{n+1}$, so $V_{n+1}$ is spanned by the images $f_*(V_n)$ over all injections $f\colon[n]\to[n+1]$. The values in degrees $\le N$ lie in $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le N})$ by [F2], and if $V_m\subseteq\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le N})_m$ for some $m\ge N$, then every $f_*(V_m)$ lies in $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le N})_{m+1}$ because the span is a sub-FI-module; the displayed spanning property of condition (II) then gives $V_{m+1}\subseteq\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le N})_{m+1}$. By induction $V_m\subseteq\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le N})_m$ for every $m\ge0$, hence $V=\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le N})$. Each $V_{[m]}$ with $m\le N$ is finite-dimensional, hence generated by finitely many elements; let $\Sigma$ be the finite union of these finitely many finite generating sets, so that $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)\supseteq V_{[m]}$ for every $m\le N$. For a finite set $S$ with $|S|=m\le N$ and a bijection $\beta\colon[m]\to S$ one has $V_S=\beta_*(V_{[m]})\subseteq\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)_S$, so $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)\supseteq V_{\le N}$ and therefore $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$; thus $V$ is finitely generated. [F1, F2, given]

Returning to $(\Rightarrow)$: for every $a$, the exactness of $\Phi_a$ over the characteristic-zero field $k$ gives an exact sequence $0\to\Phi_a(K)\to\Phi_a(M)\to\Phi_a(V)\to0$ by [F6]. The module $M$ is a finite direct sum of copies of the free modules $M(i)$, each of injectivity degree $0$ by [F4], so $T\colon\Phi_a(M)_n\to\Phi_a(M)_{n+1}$ is injective for all $n$ by [F6] and [F7]; and $T\colon\Phi_a(K)_n\to\Phi_a(K)_{n+1}$ is surjective for $n\ge r$ by [F3]. Hence $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective for $n\ge r$: a lift $\tilde x\in\Phi_a(M)_n$ of $x$ with $Tx=0$ has $T\tilde x$ in the image of $\Phi_a(K)$, so $T\tilde x=T\tilde y$ for some $\tilde y\in\Phi_a(K)_n$, and injectivity on $\Phi_a(M)$ gives $\tilde x=\tilde y$, whence $x=0$. Therefore $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)\le r$ by [F7], and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)$ since $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$. [F3, F4, F6, F7, step 1.1]

Under the assumption of step 1.1 the weight is finite, indeed $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le g$ by [F3] over the characteristic-zero field $k$, and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r)<\infty$ by step 2.1. By [F8] the sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable, with stable range $n\ge g+\max(g,r)$. [F3, F8, step 2.1]

Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove that finite generation implies uniform representation stability (through finiteness of stability degree and weight and the preceding proposition), and step 1.2 proves the converse; hence for an FI-module with finite-dimensional values over a characteristic-zero field the two properties are equivalent. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

boundaries.evidence: step 1.2: the range N >= 0 is inclusive and the finite set Sigma of generators of the values up to degree N may be empty when V = 0.
step 1.1: for V = 0 the degree g = 0 works, the free presentation has zero summands and K = 0 is finitely generated.
step 2.1: the exact sequence is applied for one fixed a at a time and the chase uses one lift x-tilde and one correction y-tilde.
step 1.2: the stability range N may be 0, and the induction over m >= N then covers every rank without a base-case exception.
Step 2.1: n>=r is inclusive and gives inj-deg(V)<=r.
step 1.2: finite generating sets of the finite-dimensional values V_{[m]} for m <= N are combined into a single finite Sigma; only finitely many choices occur.
step 3.1: the forward implication from finite generation to uniform representation stability is concluded from the finiteness of weight and stability degree.
step 1.2: the reverse implication from uniform representation stability to finite generation is proved by spanning every value from V_{<= N}.

risk_review.notes: Read every proof step and twelve suppliers, checking both directions. Finite representable presentation has finitely generated kernel by the proved Q-algebra Noetherian result. Its bounded generation gives surjective coinvariant transitions, while free presentation transitions are injective, yielding quotient injectivity by a lift diagram. Hence finite weight and stability degree give uniform stability. Conversely condition II inducts all ranks from <=N; finite-dimensional low-rank spaces have a finite union of bases generating V. Pointwise finiteness and characteristic zero are essential; N=0 and zero V are covered. Accept separation of weight subquotients from quotient-only surjectivity monotonicity.

citations.quote: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]), with free FI-modules $M(m)$ as in [[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]] and span as in [[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]].

The **free FI-module** $M(W)$ assigns to a finite set $S$ the direct sum $$M(W)_S:=\bigoplus_{T\subseteq S}W(T)$$ over all subsets $T\subseteq S$ ([[def-subset-and-proper-subset]], [[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]];

Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$, with surjectivity degree and stability degree as in [[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]] and weight as in [[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]].

Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$ and let $M(W)$ be the free FI-module of
[[def-free-fi-module-generated-by-an-sm-module]]. Then
$\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for all $i>m$ then
$\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular
$M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ over a nonzero ring $k$ satisfies $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$
([[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition,
then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$
([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]]) and
$\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$. No choice principle is used.

Let $k$ be a commutative Noetherian ring containing $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-noetherian-ring]], [[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]), and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ ([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]], [[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]).

If $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$, then $1/n!$ exists in $k$ and the averaging map $s\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$, $s([v])=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\sigma\cdot v$, is a well-defined $k$-linear section of the quotient map that is natural in $V$;
The **injectivity degree** $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)$ is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective for all $n\ge s$;

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d:=\operatorname{weight}(V)<\infty$ and stability degree $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$ ([[def-weight-of-a-characteristic-zero-fi-module]], [[def-injectivity-surjectivity-and-stability-degree-of-an-fi-module]]).
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]).

Then for every $n\ge0$, every irreducible constituent $V(\lambda)_n$ of the $kS_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $$\lambda_1\le s.$$ Equivalently, since the padded partition is $\lambda[n]=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$, the second row of the Specht diagram $\lambda[n]$ has length at most $s$;

For every partition $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=m$ there is a character polynomial $P_\lambda\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $m$ ([[def-character-polynomial-in-cycle-counts]]) such that for every $n\ge m+\lambda_1$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$ $$\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=P_\lambda\bigl(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots\bigr),$$ where $\lambda[n]=(n-m,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$ is the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]) and $\chi^{\lambda[n]}$ is the character of the irreducible Specht module $S^{\lambda[n]}$ ([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]]).

Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Read $|\varnothing|=0$ and $\alpha_1=0$ when
$\alpha=\varnothing$. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: for nonempty $\alpha$, at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments; no FI-module structure or generation
degree is asserted here.

**Agreement with the complex Specht module.** For $R=\mathbb C$ the module $M^\lambda_{\mathbb C}$, the element $\kappa_t$, the polytabloid $e_t$ and the space $S^\lambda_{\mathbb C}$ coincide with $M^\lambda$, $\kappa_t$, $e_t$ and $S^\lambda$ of [[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]: the tabloid set and the left action are the same, the permutation sign used there is the sign of [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]] transported along the order-preserving relabelling described in that item, and the defining formulas are identical.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and
$n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$,
the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), with
$|\varnothing|=\varnothing_1=0$ and $\varnothing[0]=\varnothing$, and let

$$V(\lambda)_n:=k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$$

be the scalar extension of the rational Specht model of $\lambda[n]$
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]).
By the classification lemma, $V(\lambda)_n$ is the irreducible $kS_n$-module
with label $\lambda[n]$, and every irreducible $kS_n$-module is isomorphic to
exactly one $V(\lambda)_n$: indeed, every partition $\mu=(\mu_1,\mu_2,\dots)$
of $n$ is uniquely $\lambda[n]$ for the partition
$\lambda=(\mu_2,\mu_3,\dots)$ obtained by deleting the first row, and
$n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ holds precisely because $\mu_1\ge\mu_2$;
consequently the labels $\lambda[n]$ run over the partitions of $n$ without
repetition. At $n=0$ the only label and its tail are both $\varnothing$,
and $V(\varnothing)_0=k$ with the trivial $S_0$-action.

Say that $V(\lambda)_n$ **occurs as a constituent** of $V_n$ when there are
$kS_n$-submodules $U\subseteq W\subseteq V_n$ with
$W/U\cong V(\lambda)_n$ ([[def-submodule]], [[def-quotient-module]]); this is a
condition on subquotients and requires no decomposition or finite-dimensionality
of $V_n$. The **weight** of $V$ is

$$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\bigl\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\bigr\},$$

the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed. The set of integers
displayed is a set of nonnegative integers, so the supremum is well defined in
$\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$; it is $0$ for $V=0$, and $\operatorname{weight}(V)=\infty$
exactly when the displayed set is unbounded. No finiteness of
$\operatorname{weight}(V)$ is asserted.

If $W$ is a **subquotient** of $V$, meaning that $W\cong U'/U$ for sub-FI-modules
$U\subseteq U'\subseteq V$ computed pointwise, then
$\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$: a constituent of $W_n$ is
a subquotient of the subquotient $U'_n/U_n$ of $V_n$, hence a subquotient of
$V_n$, so it contributes the same label $|\lambda|$ to the supremum for $V$. No
choice principle is used: the labels $\lambda[n]$, constituents and the
supremum are set-theoretic data, and no bases or decompositions are chosen.

For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ the field-valued Specht module $S^\lambda_F$ of [[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] is nonzero and irreducible, distinct partitions give non-isomorphic modules, and every irreducible $FS_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them.

a character polynomial has **weighted degree $\le d$** when every monomial occurring in it has weighted degree at most $d$, and the **weighted degree** of $P\ne0$ is the largest weighted degree of a monomial of $P$.

For a square matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(F)$, its **trace** is the sum of its diagonal entries, $$\operatorname{tr}(A):=\sum_{i\in n}a_{ii}.$$ For $n=0$, this is the empty sum, so the unique empty matrix has trace $0$.

derivations.claim: Since $V$ is generated in degree $\le g$, [F2] gives $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le g$, so $d\le g<\infty$. By [F1] there is a finite surjection $M:=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ with all $m_i\le g$; let $K$ be its kernel. The module $M$ is finitely generated, so $K$ is finitely generated by [F4] applied over the field $k$; say $K$ is generated in degree $\le r'$. [F1, F2, F4]

We show that $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)\le\max(g,r')<\infty$. For every $a$ the exactness of $\Phi_a$ gives an exact sequence $0\to\Phi_a(K)\to\Phi_a(M)\to\Phi_a(V)\to0$ by [F5]. The transition map of $M$ is the direct sum of the transition maps of the finitely many free modules $M(m_i)$, each injective in every degree by [F3] and [F5], so $T\colon\Phi_a(M)_n\to\Phi_a(M)_{n+1}$ is injective for all $n$; and $T\colon\Phi_a(K)_n\to\Phi_a(K)_{n+1}$ is surjective for $n\ge r'$ by [F2]. Then $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective for $n\ge r'$: a lift $\tilde x$ of $x$ with $Tx=0$ has $T\tilde x$ in the image of $\Phi_a(K)$, so $T\tilde x=T\tilde y$ for some $\tilde y\in\Phi_a(K)_n$, and injectivity on $\Phi_a(M)$ gives $\tilde x=\tilde y$, whence $x=0$. Hence $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)\le r'$; since also $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le g$ by [F2], [F6] gives $s\le\max(g,r')<\infty$. [F2, F3, F5, F6, step 1.1]

By [F7] applied with the finite numbers $d$ and $s$ of step 2.1, the consistent sequence of $V$ is uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge s+d$; that is, for every $n\ge s+d$ the multiplicities $c_{\lambda,n}$ of the irreducibles $V(\lambda)_n$ in $V_n$ are independent of $n$, so with $c_\lambda:=c_{\lambda,n}$ one has $V_n\cong\bigoplus_\lambda c_\lambda V(\lambda)_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$, the sum being finite because only labels with $|\lambda|\le d$ occur. Moreover every $\lambda$ with $c_\lambda\ne0$ satisfies $|\lambda|\le d$ by the definition of weight and $\lambda_1\le s$ by [F8]; hence $|\lambda|+\lambda_1\le d+s\le n$ throughout the range. [F7, F8, step 2.1]

For each $\lambda$ with $c_\lambda\ne0$, [F9] and [F10] give a character polynomial $P_\lambda$ of weighted degree at most $|\lambda|$ with $\chi_{V(\lambda)_n}(\sigma)=P_\lambda(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots)$ for all $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and all $\sigma\in S_n$. Define $P_V:=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda P_\lambda$, a finite sum; every summand has weighted degree at most $d$, so $P_V$ does too by [F11], including the empty sum $P_V=0$. For $n\ge s+d$ and $\sigma\in S_n$, additivity of the trace over the direct sum [F12] gives $\chi_{V_n}(\sigma)=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda\chi_{V(\lambda)_n}(\sigma)$, and by step 3.1 every summand satisfies $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$, so this equals $\sum_\lambda c_\lambda P_\lambda(X(\sigma))=P_V(X(\sigma))$. [F9, F10, F11, F12, step 3.1]

The polynomial $P_V$ of step 4.1 has the required degree bound and represents $\chi_{V_n}$ for all $n\ge s+d$ and all $\sigma\in S_n$. It is unique: two character polynomials agreeing on $S_n$ for all $n\ge s+d$ agree on infinitely many $S_n$, hence are equal by [F11]. This proves the theorem. [F11, step 4.1] ∎

boundaries.evidence: Step 4.1: an empty constituent sum gives the zero polynomial, which has weighted degree at most d under the monomial-bound convention.
Step 4.1: V=0 gives P_V=0. A module with only trivial constituents gives the constant polynomial equal to its stable multiplicity, which need not be zero.
step 3.1: the isotypic decomposition may consist of a single label lambda, and the argument applies to one summand without modification.
step 1.1: for V = 0 one may take g = 0 and M = 0 with r-prime = 0, so the degenerate free presentation is admitted.
step 3.1: the range n >= s + d is inclusive, and for each occurring lambda the inequality |lambda| + lambda_1 <= s + d holds with equality possible.
Steps 1.1-2.1 use a finite free presentation, a finite generating set of its kernel and individual lifts in the exact coinvariant sequence. Step 4.1 is a finite sum of local polynomials.
step 4.1: the forward construction of P_V as the finite sum of the P_lambda is carried out there with its degree bound verified.
step 5.1: the uniqueness direction, that two polynomials agreeing on all S_n with n >= s + d coincide, is proved via agreement on infinitely many S_n.

risk_review.notes: Read every proof step and nineteen suppliers. Finite representable presentation and finitely generated kernel bound weight and stability degree by a coinvariant lifting argument. Stable decomposition has finitely many tails, each |lambda|<=d and lambda_1<=s; hence the irreducible polynomial identity applies throughout n>=d+s. Rational Specht matrices give the same traces in arbitrary characteristic-zero fields. Finite trace sums define P_V, and infinite-rank uniqueness determines it. Accept corrected presentation fact and elementary trace derivations. Amended the sum-degree sentence to avoid an undefined maximum over an empty set when V=0; every summand has degree <=d and the zero polynomial satisfies that bound vacuously.

citations.quote: For a square matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(F)$, its **trace** is the sum of its diagonal entries, $$\operatorname{tr}(A):=\sum_{i\in n}a_{ii}.$$ For $n=0$, this is the empty sum, so the unique empty matrix has trace $0$.

For $i\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ let $X_i\colon S_n\to\mathbb N$ be the function sending a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ to the number $X_i(\sigma):=c_i(\sigma)$ of $i$-element orbits in its cycle type ([[def-permutation-support-disjoint-cycles-and-cycle-type]], [[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]], [[def-natural-numbers]]);
Equivalently, the cycle type records the lengths of all cycles after each fixed point is inserted as a one-cycle.
Let $\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ be the polynomial ring on the family of indeterminates indexed by $i\ge1$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]);

derivations.claim: Fix $n\ge s+d$.
