citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work with the finite
classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ tableau blocks of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and with the general translation machinery of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]] and
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]].

Let $V$ be the natural $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-module and $V^{*}$ its dual. For a
residue $i$ define the **residue translation functor** $f_i$ on
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$ by tensoring with $V$ and projecting onto the entry-multiset
central character in which exactly one entry $i$ is replaced by $i+1$; define
$e_i$ by tensoring with $V^{*}$ and the reverse character change ($i+1\mapsto i$,
with the signs of the natural form). Concretely, on a block
$\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ the functor is the exact block projection
$\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha+\alpha_i}(-\otimes V)$ for $f_i$ and
$\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha-\alpha_i}(-\otimes V^{*})$ for $e_i$, where
$\alpha_i$ is the Fock root label of the dictionary item
([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]).

On the direct sum $\mathcal O^\Lambda$ of the blocks these functors are exact
and biadjoint, preserve projective and injective objects, and commute with the
restricted transpose duality
([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]).
Equivalently, $f_i$ is the generalized $i$-eigencomponent of the tensor
Casimir (including the place factors), and $e_i$ is the generalized
$-n-i$-eigencomponent on the dual tensor product.

The functors are **special residue translations**, not automatically ordinary
regular-wall translations; the Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$, and
that label is not the classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work with the finite
classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ category $\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
distinct from the Fock algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$.

Let $x_j$ be the tensor Casimir acting on the $j$-th natural factor of
$M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ together with all preceding factors, and let $T_j$ be
the adjacent place swap. Then the **degenerate affine Hecke relations** hold:
the $x_j$ commute, the $T_j$ satisfy the symmetric-group braid and quadratic
relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$, and distant generators commute. They restrict
naturally to the repeated residue functors $f_i^r$ of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]], where
$x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; the dual actions are the biadjoint mates on
$e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give
multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock
$K_0$ action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's
biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class
generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The exact residue
functors of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] on the
genuine finite-$n$ parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free
generalized-standard flags given by the valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

(1) Their $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock
Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the
standard basis.

(2) For each simple $L(A)$, a residue translate vanishes exactly when the
corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual
indecomposable with simple equal head and socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$, respectively
$L(\tilde e_iA)$.

Here the edges are those of the **source upper tableau crystal** proved in
[[lem-finite-type-a-full-tensor-source-upper-charts-and-string-leading-terms]].
Read columns from left to right, assigning $+$ to an $i$-only column, $-$ to
an $i+1$-only column, and no sign to a column containing both or neither.
Cancel $-+$ pairs successively; $\tilde f_i$ changes the rightmost surviving
$+$, and $\tilde e_i$ the leftmost surviving $-$, with no edge when the
required sign is absent. These are the reverse-order lower tensor labels
transported through the source upper pairing.

(3) The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the
ground-state class, with
$M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one
highest constituent.

No action on labels alone proves the $K_0$ relations or the head/socle
statement.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked cyclotomic PBW supplier. Fix a multiset of complex roots $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_l)$ with $l\ge1$, allowing repeated roots. Write $B=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $A=H_{d+1}(\mathbf a)$ for [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. The generator-preserving tower map embeds $B$ in $A$.

For every generalized eigenvalue $i$ of $x_{d+1}$ in the regular representation of $A$, let $u_i\in\mathbb C[x_{d+1}]$ be its polynomial generalized-eigenspace projector. All such eigenvalues lie in $\bigcup_j(a_j+\mathbb Z)$. These are additive residue chains, separately indexed in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$; coincident roots do not give extra projectors. The $u_i$ are mutually orthogonal, sum to one, commute with $B$ and satisfy $u_i^*=u_i$. They need not be central in $A$.

For finite-dimensional left modules define the residue functors
$$e_i(M)=u_iM,\qquad f_i(N)=Au_i\otimes_BN.$$
Here the first functor takes its $B$-action from the tower inclusion and the second takes its $A$-action from the first factor. They are exact and biadjoint and commute naturally with the generator-fixing $*$-duality. Consequently they preserve projectives and induce adjoint operators for the projective/module Hom pairing. Projecting further by source and target content idempotents gives the supported-block functors. Neither primitivity of a central content projector nor equality $B=u_iAu_i$ is needed or asserted here. Actual image towers in admissible stable realizations use the compatible projected tensor actions of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

For level zero use $H_0(\varnothing)=\mathbb C$ and $H_d(\varnothing)=0$ for $d>0$. The map $H_0\to H_1$ is the zero homomorphism $\mathbb C\to0$, so it is not an embedding. Every positive-degree residue induction and restriction functor is zero; all biadjunction and exactness assertions then hold for zero functors.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each individually self-dual, but it need not be a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines tensoring with finite-dimensional
Cartan-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c$ be an admissible origin, let $P_c$ be the ground
simple projective-injective of the relevant summand of the parabolic category
$\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and let $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with $V=\mathbb C^N$. Write
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ for the image of the right cyclotomic Hecke action of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] and $B_\alpha$ for its central
components. Then the right Hecke action gives an algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d,$$
and on each central component, cut by the central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of
$B_d$ acting on $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$,
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha =f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha,$$
where $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$ is the corresponding block of the cyclotomic Hecke
algebra. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the image is the full cyclotomic
algebra, $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $B_\alpha=H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$; a single
component is not identified with the entire degree-$d$ algebra. Outside the
stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin
corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The maps $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ are surjective in all cases,
and the full action $H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ is
injective precisely when $q_l\ge d$ for a nonempty pyramid. For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the degree-zero objects and algebras are $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$, and for $d>0$ they are $T_d=U_d=H_d=0$. All endomorphism identities hold there, and the raw action is faithful in every degree, including the zero-algebra action; $q_l$ is not defined in this branch.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Let $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$ denote the genuine continuous-dual functor of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], and write
$\mathsf L(A):=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Keep a nonempty pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with $l=p_n>0$ columns of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, the origin $c$, and $U_d=V_c^{\otimes d}$ of [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable range** is $q_l\ge d$: there are at least $d$ rows of maximum length $l$. Put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, $A_d=\operatorname{im}(W(\lambda)\to\operatorname{End}U_d)$ and $B_d=\operatorname{im}(H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}U_d^{\mathrm{op}})$.

For every complex origin the finite image algebras are mutual centralizers, and the raw Hecke action is faithful in the stable range. For an **admissible** origin, meaning $c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_j=c_k$, the following construction defines the central support outside that range. Append $t$ full ground rows of length $l$ until $q_l+t\ge d$, keeping $l$ and $c$ fixed. Then $n$ and every $q_j$ increase by $t$, so every $a_j$ stays fixed. In the enlarged tensor space $U_d^{\mathrm{big}}$, let $e$ be the projection onto tensors using only retained rows, equivalently having zero occupancy in every deleted row. A large tableau is **contractible** if every deleted-row entry is the ground entry $c_j+1-r$ in row $r$ and column $j$. The supporting central idempotent $f$ acts as one on precisely the contractible standard-labelled simples and as zero on the others. Through the faithful enlarged Hecke action it is a central idempotent of $H_d(\mathbf a)$, and
$$B_d\cong fH_d(\mathbf a)f,\qquad\ker\psi_d=(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a).$$

This $f$ is a sum of entire supporting central blocks. Individual residue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ need not be central; they do not individually define this two-sided corner. The unrestricted tensor model does not by itself supply the admissible central-support conclusion.

For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the convention is separate: in degree zero the tensor and image algebras are $\mathbb C$ with the identity corner $f=1$; in positive degree the tensor, image algebras and their module categories are zero and $f=0$. No $q_l$ or nonempty stable-range condition is used in that case.

derivations.claim: **Restriction uses the dual natural module.** For $N$ in the degree-$(d+1)$ summand and a basis $v_a$ of $V$ with dual basis $v^a$, tensor adjunction gives the natural map $\rho_N:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_{d+1},N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_d,N\otimes V^*)$, $\rho_N(h)(t)=\sum_a h(t\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$. Its inverse sends $g$ to $(t\otimes v)\mapsto(1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_v)g(t)$. These maps are basis-independent by coevaluation and evaluation and commute with the first $d$ tower generators, acting on the $T_d$ factors. Thus they identify restriction of $\pi_{d+1}N$ with $\pi_d(N\otimes V^*)$ after the appropriate degree/block projection. The natural and dual natural modules are distinct $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-modules; no identification between them is used.

$$z:=\sum_{i=1}^NE_{ii}\in\mathfrak g$$
be the central element (the identity matrix). The dual basis of $(E_{ij})$
under $B$ is $(E_{ji})$, so the invariant Casimir tensor is
$$\Omega=\sum_{i,j=1}^NE_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}\in U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g),$$
Its action on a tensor product of two $\mathfrak g$-modules commutes with the diagonal action, as computed in [F2]. Multiplying its two factors gives the central Casimir element of [[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]].

Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak g$-module and $V=\mathbb C^N$ the natural module
([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). On the tensor product
$M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]],
[[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]) label the factors
$0,1,\dots,d$, with factor $0$ equal to $M$. For $0\le a\ne b\le d$ let
$\Omega_{ab}$ denote the operator obtained by applying $\Omega$ in the two
labelled factors, and for distinct $1\le a,b\le d$ let $P_{ab}$ denote the
operator that interchanges the two labelled factors (the flip of
$V\otimes V$ on two $V$-factors). Define, for $1\le j\le d$ and
$1\le i\le d-1$,
$$x_j:=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj},\qquad s_i:=P_{i,i+1}.$$
Finally put $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}:=\Omega-\tfrac1Nz\otimes z$ and define the
Arakawa-Suzuki normalized operators
$$y_j:=x_j-\tfrac1Nz_M+\tfrac{N-1}{2},$$
where $z_M$ denotes the endomorphism of $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ given by the
action of $z$ on the factor $M$. This is a central endomorphism, and is a scalar only when $z$ acts scalarly on $M$.

The verification below records the properties of these operators used on this
page: $\Omega$ acts on $V\otimes V$ as the flip; the operators $x_j$ and
$s_i$ are natural in $M$ and commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action; the

A **representation** of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ on $V$ is a Lie-algebra
homomorphism

$$\rho:\mathfrak g\longrightarrow\mathfrak{gl}(V).$$

Writing $xv$ for $\rho(x)(v)$, this is equivalently a $k$-bilinear action

action are allowed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, let $e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be nilpotent with largest
Jordan string length $l\ge1$, let $d\ge0$, and put $E=V^{\otimes d}$. Let
$$B=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$$
act on $E$ by the individual operators $x_i=e$ (in the $i$-th tensor factor)
and the place permutations, and let
$\varphi\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\operatorname{End}(E)$ be the algebra map
induced by the diagonal action of $\mathfrak g^e=\{X:[X,e]=0\}$ and
$\psi\colon B\to\operatorname{End}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the map encoding the
right action. Then
$$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\operatorname{End}_B(E),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B),$$
for every nilpotent Jordan type and every $d$. If $e$ has at least $d$ Jordan
strings of the maximum length $l$, then $\psi$ is injective. For $d=0$ the
identities are scalar identities and injectivity is automatic.

The full converse uses the proved normality and covariant-extension suppliers
of this page; it is not a stable-only claim and it does not assume the double
commutant identity.

Work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition
of $N\ge0$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, where $l=p_n$ for a
nonempty row list and $l=0$ for an empty row list. Zero-length rows have no
boxes. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with matrix units
$e_{i,j}$ in the standard basis
$v_1,\dots,v_N$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]). Number the
boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
Put
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
Finally let $\chi\colon\mathfrak m\to\mathbb C$ be $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$,
where the trace is the trace of the $N\times N$ matrix.

The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$

$$\xi_{a,b}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}=e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)};$$

grading is the type-A pyramid good grading in the degree-one convention:

$r<0$ and surjective for $r\ge0$. For $e\ne0$ it differs from the standard

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Keep a nonempty pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with $l=p_n>0$ columns of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, the origin $c$, and $U_d=V_c^{\otimes d}$ of [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable range** is $q_l\ge d$: there are at least $d$ rows of maximum length $l$. Put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, $A_d=\operatorname{im}(W(\lambda)\to\operatorname{End}U_d)$ and $B_d=\operatorname{im}(H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}U_d^{\mathrm{op}})$.

For every complex origin the finite image algebras are mutual centralizers, and the raw Hecke action is faithful in the stable range. For an **admissible** origin, meaning $c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_j=c_k$, the following construction defines the central support outside that range. Append $t$ full ground rows of length $l$ until $q_l+t\ge d$, keeping $l$ and $c$ fixed. Then $n$ and every $q_j$ increase by $t$, so every $a_j$ stays fixed. In the enlarged tensor space $U_d^{\mathrm{big}}$, let $e$ be the projection onto tensors using only retained rows, equivalently having zero occupancy in every deleted row. A large tableau is **contractible** if every deleted-row entry is the ground entry $c_j+1-r$ in row $r$ and column $j$. The supporting central idempotent $f$ acts as one on precisely the contractible standard-labelled simples and as zero on the others. Through the faithful enlarged Hecke action it is a central idempotent of $H_d(\mathbf a)$, and
$$B_d\cong fH_d(\mathbf a)f,\qquad\ker\psi_d=(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a).$$

This $f$ is a sum of entire supporting central blocks. Individual residue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ need not be central; they do not individually define this two-sided corner. The unrestricted tensor model does not by itself supply the admissible central-support conclusion.

For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the convention is separate: in degree zero the tensor and image algebras are $\mathbb C$ with the identity corner $f=1$; in positive degree the tensor, image algebras and their module categories are zero and $f=0$. No $q_l$ or nonempty stable-range condition is used in that case.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ in step 7.1 below has a
nonprojective left $W_d$-module.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space, let $n\ge0$, and let
$E:=V^{\otimes n}$ carry the left place action of $S_n$
([[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]]). Let $A$ be
the image of the algebra homomorphism $\mathbb C[S_n]\to\operatorname{End}(E)$
extending the place action, and let
$B:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{g^{\otimes n}:g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)\}$
be the linear span of the diagonal operators
$g^{\otimes n}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=gv_1\otimes\cdots\otimes gv_n$.
Then:

1. **(Mutual centralizers.)** $B=\{F\in\operatorname{End}(E):F a=aF\text{ for
   all }a\in A\}$ and $A=\{F\in\operatorname{End}(E):F b=bF\text{ for all
   }b\in B\}$.
2. **(Uniqueness of the identification.)** $B$ is a unital
   $\mathbb C$-subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}(E)$ and equals the image of
   the diagonal action of the universal enveloping algebra
   $U(\mathfrak{gl}(V))$, that is the unital subalgebra generated by the
   operators $\Delta(T)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1^{\otimes(i-1)}\otimes T\otimes
   \mathbf 1^{\otimes(n-i)}$, $T\in\operatorname{End}(V)$
   ([[lem-tensor-place-operators-span-the-symmetric-centralizer]]).

All statements include $n=0$, where $E=\mathbb C$.

Let $G$ be a finite group and let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with
$\operatorname{char} k \nmid |G|$. Then there are positive integers
$n_1,\ldots,n_r$ such that

$$ k[G]\cong\prod_{i=1}^r M_{n_i}(k) $$

as $k$-algebras.

For every $n\ge0$, the modules $\{S^\lambda:\lambda\vdash n\}$ form a
complete irredundant list, up to isomorphism, of finite-dimensional irreducible
complex $S_n$-representations.

derivations.claim: By [F2], the tensor space contains the trivial $S_3$ module with multiplicity four, the standard module with multiplicity two, and no sign module. The decomposition [F3] therefore makes the group-algebra image exactly $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension five. By classical Schur-Weyl duality [F2] this is $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})$, whereas $\dim\mathbb C[S_3]=6$.

The killed sign block. By [F3] the block decomposition of $\mathbb C[S_3]$ is $\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$; the one-dimensional sign block is spanned by the antisymmetrizer $a$ of [F4], which acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by $0$. Hence the kernel of $\psi_3$ contains the sign block; since the image has dimension $5$ by step 1.1, the kernel has dimension $1$ and is exactly the sign block. So $\psi_3$ kills precisely the sign block and is injective on the direct sum of the trivial and standard blocks.

The block idempotent corner. Let $f$ be the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, so that $\mathbb C[S_3]f=\mathbb C[S_3]f^2$ is the corresponding two-sided ideal; its corner $f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ has dimension $1+4=5$ by [F3]. Multiplication by $f$, $x\mapsto fxf$, is an algebra surjection $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ whose kernel contains the sign block and has dimension $6-5=1$, hence is exactly the sign block; therefore $\mathbb C[S_3]/\!\ker\psi_3\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ and the image $H_3(\lambda,c)=\psi_3(\mathbb C[S_3])$ is isomorphic to the block idempotent corner $f\mathbb C[S_3]f$, which is the central-corner form $fH_3(\mathbf a)f$ of the Definition.

The stable-range check. Here $q_l=q_1=2$ while $d=3$, so the stable range fails and the image is not the full algebra $H_3(\mathbf a)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (which has dimension $6$); the corner of step 3.1 realizes the boundary case of the Definition, and the missing dimension $1$ is precisely the killed sign block.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For a weight $\lambda$, define

$$\Phi_\lambda=\{\alpha\in\Phi:\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z\},\qquad W_\lambda=\langle s_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi_\lambda\rangle\subset W.$$

Reflections and coroots are those of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]], with the shift from [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]]. The **integral-reflection linkage class** through $\lambda$ is $W_\lambda\cdot\lambda$. The word integral includes zero and negative integral pairings. If $\Phi_\lambda$ is empty the generated group is $\{1\}$. This definition uses generating reflections; no identification with a root-lattice-coset stabilizer is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a finite-dimensional
complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$,
and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ with the
conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: positive roots $\Phi^+$, simple roots
$\alpha_i$, $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, the root order $\mu\le\lambda$
meaning $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, Weyl vector $\rho$, the dot action
$w\mathbin\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, and category
$\mathcal O$.

For a weight $\lambda$ let $C=W_\lambda\mathbin\cdot\lambda$ be its
integral-reflection linkage class in the sense of
[[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]]; it is contained in the full dot orbit
$W\mathbin\cdot\lambda$, hence finite because $W$ is finite
([[prop-the-weyl-group-is-finite-and-acts-faithfully-on-the-root-system]],
with the identification of the abstract reflections with the $s_\alpha$ of
[[prop-the-roots-form-a-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]]).
A **finite downward-closed ideal** of $C$ is a finite subset $\Gamma\subseteq C$
such that
$$\nu\in\Gamma\ \text{and}\ \mu\in C\ \text{and}\ \mu\le\nu\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu\in\Gamma ,$$
where $\le$ is the root order of [[def-bgg-category-o]] and not the strong
linkage order $\uparrow$ of [[def-strong-linkage-order-on-weights]]. It is a
lower set in the restriction of the partial order $\le$ to $C$. The empty
ideal is allowed; every nonempty such ideal has minimal elements.

For such a $\Gamma$, the **truncation** $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ is the full
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are those $X$ all of whose simple
composition factors are $L(\mu)$ with $\mu\in\Gamma$; composition factors are
those of [[def-composition-series-and-composition-factors-of-an-object]] and
the simple objects of $\mathcal O$ are the $L(\mu)$ of
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]. Because every
object of $\mathcal O$ has finite length
([[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]]) and composition factors of
a composition series are independent of the chosen series
([[thm-jordan-holder-theorem-in-an-abelian-category]]), membership in
$\mathcal O_\Gamma$ depends only on the isomorphism class of the object and
not on a chosen composition series. Consequently $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ contains
the zero object and is closed in $\mathcal O$ under finite direct sums,
subobjects, quotients and extensions
([[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]]); it is the truncation of
the finite label poset of one linkage class.

The Verma-placement claim below also has a direct justification. The highest weight line of $M(\mu)$ is one-dimensional and generates the whole module; hence it cannot be distributed among two nonzero direct summands. The linkage-block decomposition of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] therefore places this Verma in the block of its unique simple quotient $L(\mu)$ ([[thm-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]), so all its composition labels lie in $C$. A label $\eta$ of a composition factor is a weight of $M(\mu)$: in a short exact sequence of $\mathfrak h$-semisimple modules, a weight vector in the quotient lifts in that same weight by extracting that component of any finite weight decomposition of a lift. Iterating through a composition series and using [[prop-weights-of-a-verma-module-lie-below-lambda]] gives $\eta\le\mu$. Thus $\mu\in\Gamma$ and lower closure within $C$ force every such $\eta\in\Gamma$, proving $M(\mu)\in\mathcal O_\Gamma$ without a bound by one greatest label.

Two boundaries are part of the definition. First, $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ is a
condition on the highest-weight labels of simple composition factors, not a
bound on all weights of a Verma module: a Verma module $M(\mu)$ with
$\mu\in\Gamma$ lies in $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ although its weights run over the
whole cone $\mu-Q^+$. Second, $\Gamma$ is a finite ideal inside a single
linkage class $C$, not the infinite lower ideal generated by $\lambda$ in the
whole weight lattice; in particular a discrete series truncation is a
different construction.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Gamma$ be a
finite downward-closed ideal of a linkage class $C$
([[def-truncated-category-o-at-a-finite-weight-ideal]]) and let
$\lambda\in\Gamma$ be maximal in $\Gamma$. Then $\Delta(\lambda)=M(\lambda)$
is a projective object of the truncation $\mathcal O_\Gamma$
([[def-projective-object]]).

More precisely, for every $X\in\mathcal O_\Gamma$ evaluation at the
highest-weight generator $v_\lambda$ is a natural isomorphism
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\Gamma}(M(\lambda),X)\to
X^{\mathfrak n^+}_\lambda=X_\lambda$, and $X\mapsto X_\lambda$ is exact, so
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\Gamma}(M(\lambda),-)$ is exact.

Under the fixed positive-Borel convention the essential hypothesis is
maximality of $\lambda$ in the finite ideal $\Gamma$: maximality, not any
antidominance or sufficient-positivity condition, is what makes every
$\lambda$-weight vector singular. For a weight $\lambda$ that is not maximal
in $\Gamma$, $\Delta(\lambda)$ need not be projective in $\mathcal O_\Gamma$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $C$ be a linkage
class and let $\operatorname{pr}_C:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_C$ be the exact
projection of the block decomposition of
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]], i.e. the functor
that keeps the direct summand supported on $C$.

If $P\in\mathcal O$ is projective
([[def-projective-object]]), then $\operatorname{pr}_C(P)$ is projective in
$\mathcal O$. Conversely, if $Q\in\mathcal O_C$ is projective in the full
subcategory $\mathcal O_C$, then $Q$ is projective in $\mathcal O$. The proof
is the two adjunction identities
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\operatorname{pr}_CP,X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,X)$
for $X\in\mathcal O_C$ and
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(Q,\operatorname{pr}_CX)$
for general $X\in\mathcal O$, together with exactness of
$\operatorname{pr}_C$; these reduce exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}$ to the
corresponding exactness in $\mathcal O_C$ or in $\mathcal O$.

For a linkage class $C=W_\lambda\cdot\lambda$, let $\mathcal O_C$ be the full subcategory of objects all of whose simple composition factors have labels in $C$. Then $\mathcal O=\bigoplus_C\mathcal O_C$, and each nonzero $\mathcal O_C$ is indecomposable as a categorical direct summand. These are precisely the blocks. Independently, grouping weights by cosets of the root lattice $Q$ gives a canonical coarser decomposition by weight cosets.

The category is the categorical direct sum $\mathcal O=\bigoplus_\chi\mathcal O_\chi$: objects have finite support in the index $\chi$, morphisms between distinct components vanish, and the canonical component projections are exact.

Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Every object of $\mathcal O$ has a finite composition series and is both Noetherian and Artinian. The length of zero is zero.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The category $\mathcal O$ is closed under submodules, quotients and finite direct sums and is an abelian category. If $0\to A\to E\to B\to0$ is exact, $A,B\in\mathcal O$, and $E$ is $\mathfrak h$-semisimple, then $E\in\mathcal O$. The middle-term weight hypothesis is essential.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

If $E$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module, the functor $M\mapsto E\otimes_{\mathbb C}M$ with diagonal action is exact and maps $\mathcal O$ into itself.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $P$ be a projective
object of $\mathcal O$ ([[def-projective-object]]) and let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]). Then
$E\otimes P$ belongs to $\mathcal O$ and is projective in $\mathcal O$.

The same tensor adjunction shows that if $I$ is injective in $\mathcal O$,
then $E\otimes I$ is injective.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module with weight
multiplicities $\dim E_\eta$
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]). For every
weight $\mu$, the object $E\otimes\Delta(\mu)$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]) whose factors are $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$,
the factor $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$ occurring $\dim E_\eta$ times; the factors can be
ordered so that a real-linear height $\ell$ with $\ell(\alpha_i)=1$ is nonincreasing.

Consequently, if $X\in\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(\nu))$, then $E\otimes X$ has a finite Verma flag and
$$(E\otimes X:\Delta(\mu))=\sum_\eta\dim E_\eta\,(X:\Delta(\mu-\eta)).$$

Every finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak g$-module is a cyclic highest-weight module whose highest weight is dominant integral, and for each dominant integral weight

$$\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\omega_i \qquad (m_i\in \mathbb N_0),$$

there exists, up to isomorphism, a unique finite-dimensional simple module $L(\lambda)$ with highest weight $\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a chosen positive-root system and corresponding Borel, Weyl group $W$, and half-sum $\rho$ of positive roots. Let $\chi_\lambda$ and $\chi_\mu$ be the central characters obtained from highest weights $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ for this Borel. Then

$$\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu \quad \text{if and only if} \quad \mu\in W\cdot \lambda,$$

where $W\cdot \lambda:=\{w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho : w\in W\}$.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring. Then the polynomial ring $R[x]$ is a
Noetherian commutative ring.

No hypothesis beyond Noetherianity is placed on $R$: it may have zero divisors,
and it may be the zero ring.

Every finite-dimensional representation of a finite-dimensional semisimple
Lie algebra over any characteristic-zero field is completely reducible.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.

derivations.claim: In type A the integral reflections are precisely the transpositions of indices whose $a$ coordinates differ integrally. Thus $W_\lambda$ is the product of symmetric groups on these coordinate cosets. For $w$ in that product, subtract the common complex scalar from each coset. Each remaining list is real, integral up to a common real scalar, and decreasing in its original index order. For every initial index segment its sum is at least the sum of any equally large subset in that coset. Consequently every initial partial sum of $a-wa$ is a nonnegative integer, and its total sum is zero. Expressing a sum-zero vector in the adjacent simple-root basis gives these partial sums as its coefficients; hence $a-wa\in Q^+$. This makes $\lambda$ greatest, in particular maximal, in its linkage class. By [F1], $\Delta(\lambda)$ is projective in $\mathcal O$, and [F3] makes every $E\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$ projective.

Let $
u$ be dominant integral and suppose $b=a+
u$ is regular and decreasing within the original coset pattern. Put $E=L(
u)$. The weight set of $E$ is Weyl stable: each simple-root $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ decomposition has symmetric finite strings, and the reflections generate $W$. For each weight $\xi$, move it to a dominant weight $\xi^+$. Highest-weight support gives $
u-\xi^+\in Q^+$, and dominance of $
u+\xi^+$ gives $\|
u\|^2-\|\xi^+\|^2=\langle
u-\xi^+,
u+\xi^+angle\ge0$. Thus $\|\xi\|\le\|
u\|$. All weights of $E$ differ from $
u$ by roots; their coordinate residues differ by the same common scalar. If a Verma factor in [F3]'s flag has central character $\chi_{\lambda+
u}$, [F4] says its tensor weight is $\xi=w(a+
u)-a$. Coordinatewise congruences force $w$ to preserve the original coset partition. For such $w$, use the complex-bilinear extension of the Euclidean square (the weights $\xi,
u$ themselves are real):
$$\|w(a+
u)-a\|^2-\|
u\|^2=\|wa-a\|^2+2\langle
u,a-w^{-1}aangle.$$
The common complex scalar on every coset cancels. The second term is nonnegative by step 1.1 and dominance of $
u$, while the first is strictly positive for $w
e1$ by regularity. The weight bound excludes these $w$. For $w=1$ the highest weight $
u$ occurs once. Exact central projection of the flag therefore yields precisely $\Delta(\lambda+
u)$, a direct summand of $L(
u)\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$.

The enveloping algebra $U\otimes U^{\mathrm{op}}$ is filtered with polynomial associated graded by PBW, and is noetherian: an ascending chain of left ideals gives a chain of graded ideals, which stabilizes by Hilbert basis; lifting leading symbols and inducting on degree makes the original chain stabilize. Kernels and cokernels of bimodule maps between finitely generated bimodules are consequently finitely generated. Local adjoint finiteness passes to submodules and quotients. Every locally finite adjoint module is semisimple and its finite-dimensional multiplicity functors are exact: to lift a map from finite-dimensional $E$ through a quotient, lift a basis and place all lifts in a finite-dimensional stable submodule, then split its map onto its image by [F4]'s complete reducibility. Thus $\mathcal H_\chi$ is abelian and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,-_{\mathrm{ad}})$ is exact there.

For any simple $L(\eta)$ in $\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$ choose a sufficiently large even integer $n$ and set $\eta'=\eta+n\rho$. The evenness puts $n\rho$ in the root lattice in type A. Since $\eta-\lambda\in P$, the weight $\nu=\eta'-\lambda$ is integral; its simple coroot pairings are those of $\eta-\lambda$ plus $n$, hence are nonnegative for large $n$. The coordinate differences of $\eta'+\rho$ inside each original coset become strictly positive in index order for large $n$, since those of $n\rho$ strictly decrease. The coordinate coset partition is unchanged, as elements of $P$ change residues by one common scalar. Enlarge $n$ further to satisfy [F2]'s reach bound. Step 1.2 makes $\Delta(\eta')$ a direct summand of $L(\nu)\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$, while [F2] gives an epimorphism $L(n\rho)\otimes\Delta(\eta')\twoheadrightarrow L(\eta)$. Composing the split projection gives an epimorphism from a finite-dimensional tensor of the fixed $\Delta(\lambda)$ onto $L(\eta)$.

Choose finite bimodule generators of $B$ and take their finite-dimensional adjoint-stable span $E$. It also generates $B$ as a right module: moving left generators to the right uses $xb=b x+(\mathrm{ad}\,x)b$, with the adjoint term still in $E$, followed by induction on PBW degree. Therefore $e\otimes u\mapsto eu$ is an epimorphism $\Phi_E\twoheadrightarrow B$. A bimodule map from $\Phi_E$ is uniquely determined by the adjoint-equivariant map $e\mapsto f(e\otimes1)$; conversely every such map extends by right multiplication. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal H_\chi}(\Phi_E,B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,B_{\mathrm{ad}})$, making $\Phi_E$ projective by step 1.3. Present the kernel the same way to obtain a finite presentation of $B$.

Devissage gives an epimorphism from one fixed-source tensor projective onto every object $M$ of $\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$. For an extension with simple quotient, lift the generator epimorphism onto that simple using its source's projectivity, and adjoin the epimorphism onto the smaller-length subobject. Finite sums of tensor generators are again tensor generators. The kernel belongs to $\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$ by [F2], so a second such epimorphism presents $M$. These arguments impose no central-character condition on $M$.

Tensoring over $U$ is right exact, and $T_\lambda(\Phi_E)=E\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$ canonically; using step 2.2's presentation shows that $T_\lambda(B)$ belongs to $\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$. For generator Hom spaces, step 2.2 gives $(E^*\otimes F\otimes U_\chi)^{\mathfrak g}$. Ordinary finite-dimensional tensor-Hom adjunction gives the other Hom space as $(E^*\otimes F\otimes\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}\Delta(\lambda))^{\mathfrak g}$. Every invariant tensor has adjoint-finite endomorphism coefficients, since contracting its finite-dimensional factors gives an equivariant map from a finite-dimensional module into the endomorphism module. [F5] therefore identifies the two invariant spaces. On an elementary matrix it sends $u$ to its action on $\Delta(\lambda)$, exactly the map induced by $T_\lambda$; evaluation and composition are preserved because this action is an algebra map.

For any $C\in\mathcal H_\chi$, apply Hom from $\Phi_E$ to a presentation $\Phi_{F_1}\to\Phi_{F_0}\to C\to0$. This yields a right exact sequence of Hom spaces by projectivity; apply Hom from $E\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$ to the right exact image presentation, also using projectivity. Step 3.2 identifies the two generator Hom rows and their maps, hence their cokernels. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(\Phi_E,C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T_\lambda\Phi_E,T_\lambda C)$ is an isomorphism. For arbitrary $B$, its generator presentation identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(B,C)$ as the kernel of the map between the corresponding two Hom spaces; the same holds for $T_\lambda B$. The just-proved identifications of those spaces identify their kernels. Therefore $T_\lambda$ is fully faithful.

Step 3.1 presents any target object by tensor generators; step 3.2 uniquely lifts its presentation map to a map of the corresponding $\Phi$ generators. Its cokernel maps to the given object by right exactness. Thus $T_\lambda$ is essentially surjective and hence an equivalence. An equivalence of abelian categories preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties, so it is exact. For finite-dimensional $X$, associativity identifies $T_\lambda(X\otimes B)=X\otimes T_\lambda(B)$; the identification is natural, and respects associativity, evaluation and composition on elementary tensors.

For $\mathfrak{gl}_N=\mathfrak{sl}_N\oplus\mathbb C z$, $\mathfrak h$-semisimplicity and finite generation split any $\mathcal O$ object into finitely many scalar $z$-eigenspaces. Each is an $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ object. The finite-dimensional integral-coordinate tensors are the finite-dimensional $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ modules with compatible integral central scalar, obtained by adjoining that scalar; determinant powers allow all dominant integral coordinate highest weights. In step 2.1 take $\eta-\lambda\in\mathbb Z^N$ and even $n$; then $\nu\in\mathbb Z^N$ with the exact required scalar central action. The same norm argument holds after splitting off this common real central scalar. On the HC side the stipulated semisimple adjoint centre splits into integer eigenspaces; complete reducibility in each is the semisimple result, so the presentation proof still applies. Since the right centre acts by $\chi_\lambda(z)$, its left scalar differs by the adjoint integer scalar. In [F5]'s endomorphism module the adjoint centre is zero and the right central quotient reduces to the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ central quotient, giving exactly the same action isomorphism. All preceding comparisons therefore retain integral coordinate shifts and the genuine scalar centre, proving the stated $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ version. Choice is inherited from the projectivity and finite-length suppliers and from the semisimple module decompositions.
