and the density $dV$. The **Laplacians** are

$$\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d,\qquad \Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial,\qquad \Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial ,$$

and $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

**(3) Rational pure Hodge structures.** Let $k\in\mathbb Z$. A **rational pure
Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space
$V$ together with a direct-sum decomposition by $\mathbb C$-subspaces

$$V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q},\qquad \overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p},$$

where conjugation is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear involution
$v\otimes\lambda\mapsto v\otimes\bar\lambda$. The sum is finite because
$V_{\mathbb C}$ is finite dimensional, and it is direct by definition. The **Weil
operator** $C$ is the $\mathbb C$-linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathbb C}$ acting
as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$; the conjugation symmetry makes $C$ commute with
conjugation, so $C$ is the complexification of a real-linear endomorphism
of $V_{\mathbb R}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$. It need not preserve $V$.

A **polarization** of such a Hodge structure is a nondegenerate $\mathbb Q$-bilinear
form $Q:V\times V\to\mathbb Q$, extended $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to $V_{\mathbb C}$,
such that

- $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$ for all $x,y$;
- $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$;
- $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $V_{\mathbb C}$.

A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace
$U\subseteq V$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$.
The **Tate shift** $V(-r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, keeps the underlying $\mathbb Q$-vector
space, the Weil operator and $Q$ as they are and moves the bidegrees to
$(p+r,q+r)$, so that the weight becomes $k+2r$; equivalently, $(V(-r))^{p,q}=V^{p-r,q-r}$.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j$ and
$P'=\prod_{j=1}^n D'_j$ be finite open coordinate polydiscs such that each
closed coordinate disc $\overline{D'_j}$ is a compact subset of $D_j$. Let
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, and let $\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ be a
smooth form with $\bar\partial\eta=0$. Then there is a smooth
$\psi\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P')$ such that
$$\bar\partial\psi=\eta|_{P'}.$$

Assume AC. Let $R$ be a commutative PID and $X,Y$ spaces such that every $H_q(Y;R)$ is a finite free $R$-module. For every $n\ge0$ the additive singular cohomology cross product gives an isomorphism
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(X;R)\otimes_RH^q(Y;R)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(X\times Y;R).$$
All indices are nonnegative. The symmetric assertion holds when every $H_p(X;R)$ is finite free instead. No bound on the number of nonzero homology degrees and no finite-rank hypothesis on the singular chain groups is required.

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.
Thus $H_0(S^n;G)\cong G$ for $n\ge1$, whereas
$H_0(S^0;G)\cong G\oplus G$.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

A **rational mixed Hodge structure** consists of a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$
with a finite basis ([[def-linear-basis]]) together with

- a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the **weight filtration**, and
- a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of
  $H_{\mathbb C}:=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the **Hodge filtration**
  ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),

such that the following opposition condition holds on every weight-graded
piece. Here a filtration is **finite** when $W_aH=0$ for all sufficiently
negative $a$ and $W_aH=H$ for all sufficiently positive $a$, and dually
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$ for $a\ll0$ and $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=0$ for
$a\gg0$ ([[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]]).

**Complexification and conjugation.** Complex scalars act by
$c(h\otimes z)=h\otimes cz$; this respects the rational balancing relations.
A finite rational basis of $H$ identifies $H_{\mathbb C}$ with the corresponding
finite-dimensional coordinate space over $\mathbb C$. The
$\mathbb{Q}$-linear involution $\sigma$ of
$H_{\mathbb C}$, defined on generators by
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and extended $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly,
satisfies $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma(cz)=\bar c\,\sigma(z)$ for
$c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). It preserves the
subspace $W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ for every $a$,
so it descends to each graded piece
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=W_aH_{\mathbb C}/W_{a-1}H_{\mathbb C}$
([[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]). The **conjugate
Hodge filtration** is $\bar F^q:=\sigma(F^q)$, a finite decreasing filtration
of $H_{\mathbb C}$.

**Opposition.** Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with
finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$, and let $n$ be an integer. The
two filtrations are **$n$-opposed** when the natural map
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\bigl(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV\bigr)\longrightarrow V,\qquad (v_{p,q})_{p+q=n}\longmapsto\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q},$$
is an isomorphism. Applied to $V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ this
condition is required for every $n$, with the *induced* filtrations: $F^p$
acts on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ through the image of
$F^p\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$, and $\bar F^q$ through the image of
$\bar F^q\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. Writing
$$H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}\cap \bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C},$$
the requirement is therefore the direct sum decomposition
$$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n \qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z .$$
Since $\sigma$ interchanges the induced filtrations $F^p$ and $\bar F^p$ and
preserves $W$, it maps $H^{p,q}_n$ onto $H^{q,p}_n$, so
$\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$. Equivalently, the opposition condition requires both
$F^pV\cap\bar F^qV=0$ whenever $p+q>n$ and
$F^pV+\bar F^{n+1-p}V=V$ for every $p$, on
$V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. The conjunction, rather than either
condition alone, is equivalent to the displayed decomposition: the spanning
condition and the modular law give
$F^pV=F^{p+1}V+(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, and the vanishing condition makes
this sum direct; descending induction through the finite filtration gives
$F^pV=\bigoplus_{a\ge p}(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$ and then the decomposition
of $V$. Conversely, the decomposition gives these two conditions by grouping
its summands by the first and second indices.

**Morphisms.** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map with $f(W_aH)\subseteq W_aK$ for all $a$ and
$f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $p$, where
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$. Such an $f$ commutes with the
conjugations $\sigma$, hence also satisfies
$f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\bar F^pK_{\mathbb C}$.

**Substructures, pure structures, Tate.** A subspace $H'\subseteq H$ with the
induced filtrations $W_aH'=H'\cap W_aH$ and
$F^pH'_{\mathbb C}=H'_{\mathbb C}\cap F^pH_{\mathbb C}$ is a **substructure**
when the induced filtrations again satisfy the opposition condition on every
graded piece, and a quotient $H\to Q$ with the quotient filtrations is a
**quotient structure** under the same requirement; that the kernel, image and
cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is not part of the definition
and is proved in the strictness lemma below. A structure is **pure of weight
$n$** when $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nH=H$; the opposition condition then says that
$H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}$ with
$H^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$, and $\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$. The **Tate
structure** $\mathbb Q(r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, is the pure structure of
weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type
$(-r,-r)$, that is $H^{-r,-r}=\mathbb C$ and $H^{p,q}=0$ for
$(p,q)\ne(-r,-r)$.

**Tensor and dual conventions.** The tensor product $H\otimes K$ carries
$$W_a(H\otimes K)=\sum_{b+c=a}W_bH\otimes W_cK,\qquad F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{b+c=p}F^bH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^cK_{\mathbb C},$$
where the weight sum is taken over $\mathbb Q$ and the Hodge sum over
$\mathbb C$, using $(H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}K)_{\mathbb C}\cong
H_{\mathbb C}\otimes_{\mathbb C}K_{\mathbb C}$; the dual
$H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H,\mathbb Q)$ carries
$$W_aH^*=\{u:u(W_{-a-1}H)=0\},\qquad F^pH^*_{\mathbb C}=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}.$$

**Polarizability.** A pure rational Hodge structure $H$ of weight $n$ is
**polarizable** when it carries a rational bilinear form $Q$ of parity
$(-1)^n$ that pairs only complementary Hodge types, i.e.
$Q(H^{p,q},H^{p',q'})=0$ unless $p'=n-p$ and $q'=n-q$, and whose
Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(u,v):=Q(Cu,\bar v)$, where the Weil operator
$C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $H^{p,q}$, is positive definite.

No mixed structure in this definition is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or
over $\mathbb Q$; the Deligne splitting constructed below is a decomposition
over $\mathbb C$ only.

A **rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex** consists of

(a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector
spaces with an increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each
cochain group;

(b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with an
increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a decreasing filtration $F$ by
subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group;

(c) a morphism of complexes
$\alpha\colon K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$
compatible with the weight filtrations, such that for every $w$ the induced map
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_w\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism,

subject to the following axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded
complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its
differential (induced by $d_K$) is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and
for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on
$H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational
comparison
$H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb Q})\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to
H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, is a pure Hodge structure of weight
$r+w$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

Here a cochain complex is a complex in the sense of
[[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], a filtration by subcomplexes is
a filtered complex in the sense of [[def-filtered-chain-complex]], a morphism
compatible with the weight filtrations is a filtered chain map in the sense of
[[def-filtered-chain-map]], quasi-isomorphism means
[[def-quasi-isomorphism]], and finiteness on a cochain group $K^n$ means
$W_aK^n=0$ for all sufficiently negative $a$ and $W_aK^n=K^n$ for all
sufficiently positive $a$, with bounds depending on $n$; dually $F^pK^n=K^n$
for $p\ll0$ and $F^pK^n=0$ for $p\gg0$.

**The weight filtration on cohomology** is the shifted image filtration
$$W_mH^n(K):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr).$$
The shift is essential: it is what makes the axiom's weight $r+w$ on the graded
complexes compatible with the weight of $H^n$, and pole-count weight on a
logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The differential
strictness in the axiom is Deligne's condition (GH1); the equivalent
formulation that the $F$-spectral sequence of the graded complex degenerates at
its first page is recorded in the sources but is neither asserted nor used
here, so no degeneration theorem enters this definition.

**Morphisms and the sheaf case.** A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge
complexes is a pair of chain maps $K_{\mathbb Q}\to L_{\mathbb Q}$ and
$K_{\mathbb C}\to L_{\mathbb C}$ compatible with both filtrations and with the
comparisons; compatible filtered homotopies are permitted. The same
definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a topological space
when the complexes are replaced by their derived global sections and the
resolutions used preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions
for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are
constructed, not here.

(i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex
([[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]). Then for every $n$ the vector
space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight
filtration is the shifted image filtration
$W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge
filtration is the image filtration
$F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$.
In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$
one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge
filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on
every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures.

(ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge
complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees: cochain complexes
$K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the
cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, whose differentials
are strict for the Hodge filtration, and with $H^q(K^p)$, together with the
induced $F$ and the rational comparison, a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$
for all $p,q$ (the axioms (GH1)-(GH2) of a cohomological Hodge complex of
weight zero). The Hodge filtration is finite on each cochain group; the coface
and codegeneracy maps are chain maps preserving it and commuting with the
levelwise rational comparisons. Form its simple
complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration
$L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$
is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the
Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence
$E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of
$H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.

Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for
$W$ and for $F$:
$$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$
for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient
filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is
exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is
$W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has
pure image of weight $n$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space. Then
the abelian category $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has
enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module embeds into an injective
$\mathcal O_X$-module, and the functorial injective embedding supplied by the
Grothendieck injective-embedding theorem for Grothendieck categories supplies,
by iteration of cokernels, one specific injective resolution
$$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots$$
to each $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with no further selection
([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]). The Axiom of Choice
enters exactly through that embedding theorem applied to
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$; the category-theoretic verification below is
choice-free.

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

Assume AC. Every smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ admits a smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with reduced boundary a simple normal crossings divisor $D$. Given finitely many such compactifications, there is another dominating all of them and restricting to the identity on $U$. A morphism of smooth quasiprojective varieties extends to a morphism of such compactifications after modifying the source compactification outside its open variety.

Assume AC. Let $p:X'\to X$ be a proper morphism between smooth projective complex varieties of equal pure dimension, restricting to the identity on a common open variety $U$. Then $H^n(X,\mathbb Q)$ and $H^n(X',\mathbb Q)$ have the same image in $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ for every $n$. Consequently the compactification-image formula of logarithmic weights extends from an SNC compactification to every smooth projective compactification.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb C$ be holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). Then $f$ is
continuous on $U$ and separately holomorphic on $U$
([[def-separately-holomorphic-function]]). Moreover, for $a\in U$ and $k<m$ the
slice $f_{a,k}$ is complex differentiable at $a_k$ with derivative
$Df(a)e_k$, and

$$Df(a)e_k=\partial_{z_k}f(a),\qquad Df(a)h=\sum_{k<m}\bigl(\partial_{z_k}f(a)\bigr)h_k .$$

Fix $m\ge1$, $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and a polyradius $\rho$, let
$f:\Delta_\rho(a)\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and separately holomorphic, let $r$
be a polyradius with $r_k<\rho_k$ for every $k<m$, and let
$C_k(t)=a_k+r_k\exp(it)$ on $[0,2\pi]$. For each multi-index $\alpha$ set

$$c_\alpha:=\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{C_0}\!\cdots\!\int_{C_{m-1}} f(\zeta)\prod_{k<m}(\zeta_k-a_k)^{-\alpha_k-1}\,d\zeta_{m-1}\cdots d\zeta_0 ,$$

an iterated integral as in the polydisc Cauchy formula. Then, with
$M=\sup_{\Gamma_r(a)}|f|$,

$$|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k},$$

and for every real $\theta$ with $0<\theta<1$ the series
$\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha$ converges absolutely and uniformly on
$\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)$ with

$$f(z)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha\qquad(z\in\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)).$$

derivations.claim: (Compactification and strata.) By [F7] choose the SNC smooth projective compactification; the constructions below apply separately to its finitely many smooth connected components when dimensions differ. At a closed point of $X$, the SNC equations are a subset of a regular system of parameters; their differentials extend to a cotangent basis in a smooth chart. The parameter map has invertible complex Jacobian, so [F8] makes these parameters holomorphic coordinates, giving the coordinate divisor model of [F1]. Order the finitely many boundary components to fix residue signs. Their $a$-fold intersections and disjoint unions $D^{[a]}$ are smooth projective by [F1], so [F3] applies to each component. Empty strata contribute zero.

(Logarithmic forms and the pole filtration.) Put $e_i=dz_i/z_i$ for the $s$ local boundary coordinates. The logarithmic complex $L=\Omega_X^\bullet(\log D)$ is locally generated by $e_1,\ldots,e_s,dz_{s+1},\ldots,dz_d$ over holomorphic functions; regular normal differentials are included because $dz_i=z_ie_i$. Define in degree $k$ the pole-count filtration by $W_aL^k=\sum_{|I|\le a}e_I\wedge\Omega_X^{k-|I|}$, with arbitrary regular holomorphic forms in the second factor, not merely tangential forms. Thus $W_0L=\Omega_X^\bullet$, $W_aL=0$ for $a<0$, and $W_dL=L$. Changing a boundary equation by a unit adds a regular $d\log u$, so this definition is intrinsic. Since $de_i=0$ and differentiating a regular coefficient produces a regular form, $d$ preserves $W$. The degree filtration $F^pL=\Omega_X^{\ge p}(\log D)$ is also a finite filtration by subcomplexes.

(Residues, signs and the Hodge shift.) For each ordered set $I$ of $a$ distinct components, write a term of $W_aL^k$ as $e_I\wedge\eta_I$ with $\eta_I$ regular, and restrict $\eta_I$ to $D_I$. These are separate residue coordinates on the separate summands of $D^{[a]}$. Terms with fewer poles restrict to zero in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_a$; a regular normal differential restricts to zero, and a coefficient vanishing on $D_I$ lies in the ideal generated by its normal coordinates, each factor $z_i$ converting $e_i$ to the regular form $dz_i$ and reducing the pole count. These observations prove that the kernel of the residue map on $W_a$ is exactly $W_{a-1}$. Conversely every regular stratum form extends locally in the normal coordinates and lifts as $e_I\wedge\eta_I$, proving surjectivity. Changes of local equations add only lower-pole terms, so these maps glue. The differential is $d(e_I\wedge\eta_I)=(-1)^a e_I\wedge d\eta_I$, agreeing with the differential of the shifted complex $[-a]$. Hence $\operatorname{Gr}^W_aL\cong i_{a*}\Omega_{D^{[a]}}^\bullet[-a]$, and $F^p$ corresponds to the stratum degree filtration $F^{p-a}$, the shift appropriate to a Tate twist $(-a)$.

(A pole-preserving local contraction.) Work on a smaller polydisc centered at a boundary point with $s$ normal coordinates. (Every canonical truncation and the rational normalization.) Take the sheafification $\mathcal S_U^\bullet$ of smooth singular cochains on $U$. The flasque-resolution construction of [F6] applies to smooth simplices as well: barycentric subdivision and its prism operators preserve smoothness, local polydisc contractions are smooth, and the global small-simplex representative argument is unchanged. Thus $\mathcal S_U^\bullet$ resolves $\mathbb C_U$ and its terms are acyclic on every open subset. They are therefore $j_*$-acyclic, and $j_*\mathcal S_U^\bullet$ represents $Rj_*\mathbb C_U$. Integration of logarithmic forms on smooth simplices in $U$, with the cochain map and normalization of [F2], gives the chain map $L\to j_*\mathcal S_U^\bullet$. On the polydiscs of step 2.2 the target stalk cohomology is the cohomology of $(\Delta^*)^s\times\Delta^{d-s}$, the exterior algebra on meridians by [F4]. Integration gives $\int_{\gamma_i}e_j=2\pi i\delta_{ij}$, so the comparison is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. Let $\tau_{\le a}$ denote the canonical truncation, with degree $a$ equal to the kernel of the next differential. Since every degree-$k$ logarithmic form has at most $k$ poles, the identity gives a genuine chain inclusion $\tau_{\le a}L\to W_aL$. By step 2.2 it induces an isomorphism in degrees at most $a$ and both sides have no cohomology above $a$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism for every $a$. These inclusions commute with the maps as $a$ increases. We therefore have the filtered comparison zigzag $(Rj_*\mathbb Q_U\otimes\mathbb C,\tau)\to(Rj_*\mathbb C_U,\tau)\leftarrow(L,\tau)\to(L,W)$, all arrows graded quasi-isomorphisms; exact scalar extension and the local finite torus cohomology establish the first arrow. On each graded sheaf the rational meridian wedge corresponds to $(2\pi i)^{-a}e_I$, which pairs by $1$ with the degree-$a$ meridian torus, not a degree-$2a$ class. Ordered residues thus identify $R^aj_*\mathbb Q_U$ with $i_{a*}\mathbb Q_{D^{[a]}}$ and place its comparison lattice in $(2\pi i)^{-a}\mathbb Q$, exactly the rational Tate normalization $(-a)$.

(Actual filtered global-section models and a single comparison.) The sheaf comparison in step 3.1 is a zigzag, so it must not be treated as a nonexistent direct sheaf map in the opposite direction. Resolve the complexes and their filtrations by the exact Godement construction: $C^0(A)(V)=\prod_{x\in V}A_x$, with the natural embedding and successive cokernels. Stalks and products are exact for vector spaces under AC. Moreover $C^0(A)=\prod_{x\in X}i_{x*}A_x$ is an injective sheaf of field-vector spaces: each $A_x$ is injective over its field by extension of linear maps along a chosen complement, the exact stalk functor is left adjoint to $i_{x*}$, and a product of injectives is injective because the component extension maps can be chosen simultaneously under AC. The successive cokernel construction therefore gives an actual injective resolution. Exactness of $C^0$ and the short exact augmentation sequences give exactness of each successive cokernel functor by the snake lemma, so the resulting functorial resolution is exact on filtration levels, their finite intersections and both associated gradings; its global-section total computes derived global sections. Apply it to $L$ with $W,F$ and to the other weight-filtered models in the zigzag. Replace the rational and comparison models by $\tau_{\le d}$ first; their cohomology sheaves above $d$ vanish by the local torus calculation, so this is a quasi-isomorphism and leaves a finite weight range $0\le a\le d$. After resolution and global sections the complex-coefficient arrows in the zigzag are maps of weight-filtered vector-space complexes with graded quasi-isomorphisms. For the rational scalar-extension arrow, the global graded comparison is the isomorphism $H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)\otimes\mathbb C\to H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb C)$ from [F3], with the normalization of step 3.1; this proves it is a graded quasi-isomorphism without interchanging tensor product with an infinite product of stalks. Such a map admits a weight-filtered homotopy inverse: its cone has acyclic weight-graded complexes; a cycle in $W_a$ has a leading graded preimage, and subtracting its differential lowers the cycle to $W_{a-1}$, so finite induction supplies a preimage in $W_a$. Thus the cone is acyclic with a $W$-strict differential. Choose filtration-compatible complements of its cycles and right inverses of its differential; the resulting degree-minus-one homotopy contracts the cone and preserves $W$, and the cone homotopy equations give a $W$-filtered homotopy inverse of the original map. AC permits these linear complements. Inverting the leftward comparison in step 3.1 and composing the remaining arrows gives an actual $W$-filtered chain map $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$, with $K_{\mathbb C}=\Gamma(X,C^\bullet(L))$ carrying the original $W,F$. Its graded maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Different inverse choices are filtered-homotopic, so their induced comparison and image filtrations on cohomology agree. These are bounded-below degreewise-finite filtered models of the type required in [F5].

(Strictness on the weight-graded global models.) Exactness of the resolution and step 2.1 identify $\operatorname{Gr}^W_aK_{\mathbb C}$ with a global-section resolution of $\Omega_{D^{[a]}}^\bullet[-a]$, with its degree Hodge filtration shifted by $a$. Its Hodge spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ by [F3]. This implies strictness of the differential of this actual filtered vector-space complex: if $dx$ belongs to $F^p$, take the leading $F$ index $b<p$ of $x$; its class in the associated-graded complex is a cycle. Degeneration means this $E_1$ class lifts to an actual cycle $y\in F^b$, up to an element of $F^{b+1}$ and a boundary in $F^b$. Subtract that cycle and boundary from $x$, preserving $dx$ and raising the filtration index of the preimage. Repeat through the finite filtration until a preimage of $dx$ lies in $F^p$. Thus $\operatorname{im}d\cap F^p=d(F^p)$. Moreover its degree-$r$ cohomology is $H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)$ under the comparison of step 3.1, with the induced $F$, pure of weight $r-a+2a=r+a$ and finite-dimensional by [F3]. Hence the global comparison models of step 4.1 satisfy every graded axiom of a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex, including strictness and the full induced Hodge filtration.

(The mixed structure and its spectral sequence.) Apply the full conclusion of [F5] to the proved mixed Hodge complex of step 5.1. Its cohomology is $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$ by steps 3.1-5.1 and [F6], and it carries the image Hodge filtration and shifted weight filtration $W_mH^n(U)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$. The weight spectral sequence is $E_1^{-a,q}=H^{q-2a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)$, pure of weight $q$, degenerates at $E_2$, and gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(U)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ with its induced Hodge filtration. In particular this step uses the supplied recurrent-to-image-filtration proof, not an assumption that higher differentials preserve the desired filtration.

(Lower weight bound and compactification image.) The pole index $a$ is nonnegative, so a term contributing to total degree $n=q-a$ has weight $q=n+a\ge n$. Hence step 6.1 gives $W_{n-1}H^n(U)=0$. Also $W_nH^n(U)$ is the image of $H^n(W_0K)$. On the complex side $W_0L=\Omega_X^\bullet$ by step 1.2; on the rational side $\tau_{\le0}Rj_*\mathbb Q_U=\mathbb Q_X$, since a punctured-coordinate polydisc is connected. Its map to $Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$ is restriction. Thus both sides identify $W_nH^n(U)$ with the actual image of $j^*:H^n(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$, compatibly with the rational comparison and Hodge filtration.

(Functoriality and independence.) A compactified extension $f:(X,D)\to(Y,E)$ of an open morphism satisfies $f^{-1}(E)\subseteq D$. A target boundary equation pulls back to a nonzero regular germ on each source component, since the dense open source maps into the target open. Its zero set is contained in $D$, so [F8] factors it locally as a unit times powers of source boundary equations with nonnegative integer exponents, so $f^*d\log t=d\log u+\sum_i m_i d\log z_i$. Wedges preserve pole count and degree, hence $f^*$ preserves $W,F$ on the logarithmic complexes and is compatible with the rational meridian comparison. The functorial resolutions and filtered comparison homotopies of step 4.1 produce the same natural pullback on cohomology; [F5] therefore makes it a mixed Hodge morphism. The graph-extension construction in [F7] supplies such compactified extensions after modifying the source. For two SNC compactifications of one $U$, a common SNC domination gives pullback comparison maps between their logarithmic mixed Hodge structures on $H^n(U)$, whose underlying rational maps are the identity. Strictness in [F5] makes these identity maps isomorphisms for both filtrations, proving independence. For any smooth projective compactification with arbitrary boundary, the modification-image clause of [F7] identifies its restriction image with the SNC one, so the formula of step 7.1 holds for it too.

(Choice and boundary cases.) AC is inherited through the typed suppliers in [A1] and is also used exactly in step 4.1 for exact products in the Godement resolution and filtration-compatible vector-space complements to strictify the comparison zigzag. The monomial contractions, residues, rational meridian normalization, finite filtrations and weight bookkeeping are otherwise choice-free. With empty boundary $L=\Omega_X^\bullet$ and $W_0=L$, recovering the pure projective structure; empty $U$ may be represented by empty compactification and has zero cohomology, while the SNC compactification hypotheses already require density on every nonempty component. Components of differing dimensions are handled separately, empty strata vanish, and degrees outside the cohomological range give zero groups. This completes the retained full mixed Hodge, functoriality, independence, lower-weight and image claims.

checked_proof_evidence.quote: 3.1 (The flasque resolution.) The augmentation $k_X\to\mathcal C^0$ sends a locally constant function to the same function on points. By [F6], [F13], the cohomology of its stalk complex at $x$ is the colimit of the singular cohomology of neighbourhoods of $x$. Contractible open neighbourhoods are cofinal. A contraction and the cochain dual of [F5] identify their cohomology with that of a point. The ordinary singular cochain complex of a point has $k$ in every nonnegative degree, with differential $k\to k$ equal to zero in even degrees and the identity in odd degrees, because the boundary is the alternating sum of $n+1$ identical faces. Its cohomology is consequently $k$ in degree zero and zero otherwise. The augmentation induces the degree-zero stalk isomorphism, and all positive stalk cohomology vanishes. Therefore $k_X\to\mathcal C^0\to\mathcal C^1\to\cdots$ is exact. By steps 1.1 and 2.1 its terms are acyclic, and [F12] applies: the injective datum [F7] is defined on every successive kernel. Its section complex computes the $k$-linear derived cohomology. The same resolution consists of acyclic underlying abelian sheaves by step 1.1; applying [F12] with [F14] identifies its section cohomology also with the published abelian-sheaf convention. [F5, F6, F7, F12, F13, F14, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.
Thus $H_0(S^n;G)\cong G$ for $n\ge1$, whereas
$H_0(S^0;G)\cong G\oplus G$.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$

A **rational mixed Hodge structure** consists of a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$
with a finite basis ([[def-linear-basis]]) together with

- a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the **weight filtration**, and
- a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of
  $H_{\mathbb C}:=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the **Hodge filtration**
  ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),

such that the following opposition condition holds on every weight-graded
piece. Here a filtration is **finite** when $W_aH=0$ for all sufficiently
negative $a$ and $W_aH=H$ for all sufficiently positive $a$, and dually
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$ for $a\ll0$ and $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=0$ for
$a\gg0$ ([[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]]).

**Complexification and conjugation.** Complex scalars act by
$c(h\otimes z)=h\otimes cz$; this respects the rational balancing relations.
A finite rational basis of $H$ identifies $H_{\mathbb C}$ with the corresponding
finite-dimensional coordinate space over $\mathbb C$. The
$\mathbb{Q}$-linear involution $\sigma$ of
$H_{\mathbb C}$, defined on generators by
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and extended $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly,
satisfies $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma(cz)=\bar c\,\sigma(z)$ for
$c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). It preserves the
subspace $W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ for every $a$,
so it descends to each graded piece
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=W_aH_{\mathbb C}/W_{a-1}H_{\mathbb C}$
([[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]). The **conjugate
Hodge filtration** is $\bar F^q:=\sigma(F^q)$, a finite decreasing filtration
of $H_{\mathbb C}$.

**Opposition.** Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with
finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$, and let $n$ be an integer. The
two filtrations are **$n$-opposed** when the natural map
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\bigl(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV\bigr)\longrightarrow V,\qquad (v_{p,q})_{p+q=n}\longmapsto\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q},$$
is an isomorphism. Applied to $V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ this
condition is required for every $n$, with the *induced* filtrations: $F^p$
acts on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ through the image of
$F^p\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$, and $\bar F^q$ through the image of
$\bar F^q\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. Writing
$$H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}\cap \bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C},$$
the requirement is therefore the direct sum decomposition
$$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n \qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z .$$
Since $\sigma$ interchanges the induced filtrations $F^p$ and $\bar F^p$ and
preserves $W$, it maps $H^{p,q}_n$ onto $H^{q,p}_n$, so
$\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$. Equivalently, the opposition condition requires both
$F^pV\cap\bar F^qV=0$ whenever $p+q>n$ and
$F^pV+\bar F^{n+1-p}V=V$ for every $p$, on
$V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. The conjunction, rather than either
condition alone, is equivalent to the displayed decomposition: the spanning
condition and the modular law give
$F^pV=F^{p+1}V+(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, and the vanishing condition makes
this sum direct; descending induction through the finite filtration gives
$F^pV=\bigoplus_{a\ge p}(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$ and then the decomposition
of $V$. Conversely, the decomposition gives these two conditions by grouping
its summands by the first and second indices.

**Morphisms.** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map with $f(W_aH)\subseteq W_aK$ for all $a$ and
$f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $p$, where
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$. Such an $f$ commutes with the
conjugations $\sigma$, hence also satisfies
$f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\bar F^pK_{\mathbb C}$.

**Substructures, pure structures, Tate.** A subspace $H'\subseteq H$ with the
induced filtrations $W_aH'=H'\cap W_aH$ and
$F^pH'_{\mathbb C}=H'_{\mathbb C}\cap F^pH_{\mathbb C}$ is a **substructure**
when the induced filtrations again satisfy the opposition condition on every
graded piece, and a quotient $H\to Q$ with the quotient filtrations is a
**quotient structure** under the same requirement; that the kernel, image and
cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is not part of the definition
and is proved in the strictness lemma below. A structure is **pure of weight
$n$** when $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nH=H$; the opposition condition then says that
$H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}$ with
$H^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$, and $\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$. The **Tate
structure** $\mathbb Q(r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, is the pure structure of
weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type
$(-r,-r)$, that is $H^{-r,-r}=\mathbb C$ and $H^{p,q}=0$ for
$(p,q)\ne(-r,-r)$.

**Tensor and dual conventions.** The tensor product $H\otimes K$ carries
$$W_a(H\otimes K)=\sum_{b+c=a}W_bH\otimes W_cK,\qquad F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{b+c=p}F^bH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^cK_{\mathbb C},$$
where the weight sum is taken over $\mathbb Q$ and the Hodge sum over
$\mathbb C$, using $(H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}K)_{\mathbb C}\cong
H_{\mathbb C}\otimes_{\mathbb C}K_{\mathbb C}$; the dual
$H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H,\mathbb Q)$ carries
$$W_aH^*=\{u:u(W_{-a-1}H)=0\},\qquad F^pH^*_{\mathbb C}=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}.$$

**Polarizability.** A pure rational Hodge structure $H$ of weight $n$ is
**polarizable** when it carries a rational bilinear form $Q$ of parity
$(-1)^n$ that pairs only complementary Hodge types, i.e.
$Q(H^{p,q},H^{p',q'})=0$ unless $p'=n-p$ and $q'=n-q$, and whose
Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(u,v):=Q(Cu,\bar v)$, where the Weil operator
$C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $H^{p,q}$, is positive definite.

No mixed structure in this definition is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or
over $\mathbb Q$; the Deligne splitting constructed below is a decomposition
over $\mathbb C$ only.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let
$$S^2:=\{(x,y,t)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+t^2=1\}.$$
Define
$$\Sigma(z)=\left(\frac{2\operatorname{Re}z}{1+|z|^2},\ \frac{2\operatorname{Im}z}{1+|z|^2},\ \frac{|z|^2-1}{1+|z|^2}\right)\qquad(z\in\mathbb C)$$
and $\Sigma(\infty)=(0,0,1)$. Then $\Sigma:\widehat{\mathbb C}\to S^2$ is a
homeomorphism, with inverse
$$\Pi(x,y,t)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x+iy}{1-t},&(x,y,t)\neq(0,0,1),\\ \infty,&(x,y,t)=(0,0,1).\end{cases}$$

Let $n\ge1$, put $P=\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, and let $S^{n-1}\subseteq P$ be the unit sphere. Radial normalisation

$$r:P\to S^{n-1},\qquad r(x)=\frac{x}{\lVert x\rVert_2},$$

is a retraction, and

$$H(x,t)=\left((1-t)+\frac{t}{\lVert x\rVert_2}\right)x$$

is a deformation retraction of $P$ onto $S^{n-1}$.

If $A$ is a deformation retract of a topological space $X$, then for every
$n\geq 0$ and every abelian group $G$ the inclusion $i:A\hookrightarrow X$
induces an isomorphism
$$H_n^{\mathrm{sing}}(i_\#):H_n^{\mathrm{sing}}(A;G)\to H_n^{\mathrm{sing}}(X;G).$$

By the residue normalization of [F3] the class $(2\pi i)^{-1}dz/z$ is a nonzero rational class in $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ pairing by $1$ with the positively oriented meridian, so it generates the one-dimensional space $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ of step 1.1; its normalized rational residue coordinates at $0$ and $\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, because in the coordinate $w=1/z$ at infinity the form $dz/z$ equals $-dw/w$.

The weight spectral sequence. Only $a=0,1$ contribute. The $a=0$ column has $E_1^{0,0}=\mathbb Q(0)$, $E_1^{0,1}=0$, $E_1^{0,2}=H^2(\mathbb P^1;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$, pure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$; the $a=1$ column has $E_1^{-1,2}=\mathbb Q(-1)^2$ and is otherwise zero. The sole possible nonzero differential is $d_1:E_1^{-1,2}\to E_1^{0,2}$, a pure Hodge morphism. Since the sequence degenerates at $E_2$ and $H^2(U)=0$ by step 1.1, its cokernel is zero, so its rank is one. The global closed logarithmic form of step 2.1 has normalized residue vector $(1,-1)$, which must survive this differential because it represents an actual cohomology class; hence this vector lies in its kernel. A rank-one map from a two-dimensional space has one-dimensional kernel, so $\ker d_1=\mathbb Q(1,-1)\cong\mathbb Q(-1)$. Equivalently, in a rational target generator normalized to the nonzero image of $(1,0)$, $d_1(r_0,r_\infty)=r_0+r_\infty$. Thus $E_2^{-1,2}=\mathbb Q(-1)$, $E_2^{0,2}=0$, $E_2^{0,0}=\mathbb Q(0)$, and all remaining terms vanish. This computes the required weight-graded piece without assuming an unproved Gysin normalization.

The mixed Hodge structure on $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)$. By [F3] the weight-graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ is $E_2^{1-m,m}$, so by step 3.1 it is $\mathbb Q(-1)$ for $m=2$ and vanishes for every other $m$; in particular $W_1H^1(U;\mathbb Q)=0$ and $W_2H^1(U;\mathbb Q)=H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$, which also agrees with the weights-at-least-$1$ and image formulas of [F3] and with $H^1(X;\mathbb Q)=0$ from step 1.1. By [F4] the class supported in weight $2$ with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_2=\mathbb Q(-1)$ makes $H^1(U;\mathbb Q)$ pure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$, so $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$; the classical generator $(2\pi i)^{-1}dz/z$ of step 2.1 is a rational class of this structure.

Conclusion and boundaries. The weight of $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)$ is $2$, strictly larger than the cohomological degree $1$, and the only nonzero Hodge number is $h^{1,1}=1$. checked_proof_evidence.quote: 3.1 (Every canonical truncation and the rational normalization.) Take the sheafification $\mathcal S_U^\bullet$ of smooth singular cochains on $U$. The flasque-resolution construction of [F6] applies to smooth simplices as well: barycentric subdivision and its prism operators preserve smoothness, local polydisc contractions are smooth, and the global small-simplex representative argument is unchanged. Thus $\mathcal S_U^\bullet$ resolves $\mathbb C_U$ and its terms are acyclic on every open subset. They are therefore $j_*$-acyclic, and $j_*\mathcal S_U^\bullet$ represents $Rj_*\mathbb C_U$. Integration of logarithmic forms on smooth simplices in $U$, with the cochain map and normalization of [F2], gives the chain map $L\to j_*\mathcal S_U^\bullet$. On the polydiscs of step 2.2 the target stalk cohomology is the cohomology of $(\Delta^*)^s\times\Delta^{d-s}$, the exterior algebra on meridians by [F4]. Integration gives $\int_{\gamma_i}e_j=2\pi i\delta_{ij}$, so the comparison is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. Let $\tau_{\le a}$ denote the canonical truncation, with degree $a$ equal to the kernel of the next differential. Since every degree-$k$ logarithmic form has at most $k$ poles, the identity gives a genuine chain inclusion $\tau_{\le a}L\to W_aL$. By step 2.2 it induces an isomorphism in degrees at most $a$ and both sides have no cohomology above $a$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism for every $a$. These inclusions commute with the maps as $a$ increases. We therefore have the filtered comparison zigzag $(Rj_*\mathbb Q_U\otimes\mathbb C,\tau)\to(Rj_*\mathbb C_U,\tau)\leftarrow(L,\tau)\to(L,W)$, all arrows graded quasi-isomorphisms; exact scalar extension and the local finite torus cohomology establish the first arrow. On each graded sheaf the rational meridian wedge corresponds to $(2\pi i)^{-a}e_I$, which pairs by $1$ with the degree-$a$ meridian torus, not a degree-$2a$ class. Ordered residues thus identify $R^aj_*\mathbb Q_U$ with $i_{a*}\mathbb Q_{D^{[a]}}$ and place its comparison lattice in $(2\pi i)^{-a}\mathbb Q$, exactly the rational Tate normalization $(-a)$.
