citations.quote: Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.

Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a locally
compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ be the category of sheaves of
abelian groups on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]) and let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\longrightarrow\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]],
[[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]). For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on
$X$ define the **compactly supported global sections** of $\mathcal F$ to be the
subgroup
$$\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=\{\,s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F):\operatorname{Supp}(s)\ \text{is a compact subset of }X\,\}\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal F),$$
where the support of a section is the set of points at which its germ is
nonzero ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]], [[def-germ-of-section]],
[[def-compact-space]]). This is a subgroup: the zero section has empty support, negation preserves
support, and the support of a sum is closed in $X$ and contained in the finite
union of the two compact supports, hence compact
([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]).
A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian
sheaves induces a map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ by restriction of
$\Gamma(X,\varphi)$, and this makes $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ an additive functor
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$ ([[def-additive-functor]],
[[def-morphism-of-presheaves]]). Six consistency facts hold; all are immediate
from the definitions, and they record the interface used by the compact-support
calculus.

1. **Well-definedness of $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$.** If $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$
   ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]]), and since the stalk maps of a morphism commute
   with the germ maps, $\varphi(s)_x=\varphi_x(s_x)=0$, so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. A support
   $\operatorname{Supp}(t)$ is closed in $X$: if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(t)$ then $t$ agrees with the zero section on some open
   neighbourhood of $x$, by the description of equality of germs
   ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]]). Hence
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))$ is a closed subset of $X$ contained in the
   compact set $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$; being closed in $X$ it is closed in the
   subspace $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, so it is a compact subset of that compact
   space ([[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]) and therefore
   a compact subset of $X$ ([[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]]), and
   $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ maps $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ into
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal G)$. Composites and identities are computed
   componentwise, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is a functor; it is additive because
   $\Gamma(X,-)$ is.
2. **Sheaves of $k$-vector spaces.** If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of
   $k$-vector spaces, then $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ is a $k$-vector subspace of
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$: the support of $c\cdot s$ is
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ for $c\ne0$ and $\varnothing$ for $c=0$, and the
   zero section has empty support. For a morphism $\varphi$ of sheaves of
   $k$-vector spaces the map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ is $k$-linear, since
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is. The higher derived functors below are computed from
   an injective resolution datum on abelian sheaves, so they are abelian
   groups; the degree-zero part is the $k$-vector space
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$.
3. **Left exactness.** For every short exact sequence
   $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F''\to0$
   of abelian sheaves the sequence
   $$0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi')}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi)}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$$
   is exact. Injectivity: a monomorphism of sheaves has injective stalk maps
   ([[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]), so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=\operatorname{Supp}(s')$ and a section
   killed by $\varphi'$ has all germs zero, hence is zero. Exactness at the
   middle: the kernel of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is the image of
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi')$ by left exactness of global sections
   ([[lem-global-sections-left-exact]]); if $s=\varphi'(s')$ has compact
   support, then $s'$ has the same support,
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s')=\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$, because $\varphi'$ is stalk-injective, so $s'$ lies
   in $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate from
   $\varphi\circ\varphi'=0$. Thus $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive left exact
   functor on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]).
4. **The derived functors.** Abelian sheaves on $X$ have enough injectives, and
   the embeddings of [[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]] supply one
   functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
   on the whole category $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, under the Axiom of Choice
   ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). The
   **compactly supported cohomology** of $\mathcal F$ is
   $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\qquad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\quad(q<0),$$
   the cohomology of the deleted resolution, as in the pattern of
   [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]; for a morphism $\varphi$ we
   write $H^q_c(X,\varphi):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map.
5. **Independence of the datum.** If $J$ is another supplied injective
   resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, then $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from
   $J$ is naturally isomorphic to $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from $I$
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]);
   the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that comparison follows from AC
   ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum up to this
   canonical natural isomorphism.
6. **Delta functor and the compact case.** Since $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is additive
   and left exact and the datum is defined on all of $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, the
   functors $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$, $q\ge0$, carry connecting maps that make them a
   cohomological delta functor with $R^0\Gamma_c(X,-)\cong\Gamma_c(X,-)$, and
   every short exact sequence of abelian sheaves has a long exact
   compact-support cohomology sequence, natural in the sequence
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor]]). If $X$
   is compact, then for every global section $s$ its support is closed in $X$ by
   fact 1, hence a closed subset of the compact space $X$ and therefore
   compact, so every global section is compactly supported; hence
   $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ for every $q$, where $H^q(X,-)$ is
   the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]
   computed from the same datum.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

Let $M\in D^-(\mathcal A)$ and $N\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, with termwise bounded representatives. With supplied bounded-above projective models under [[thm-projective-complexes-model-the-bounded-above-derived-category]], define $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)=Q\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,N)$. Alternatively, with supplied bounded-below injective models under [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]], use $Q\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,I_N)$. The target is $D^+(\mathbf{Ab})$.

Here the cochain form of [[def-hom-complex-of-chain-complexes]] has degree-$r$ term $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(M^i,N^{i+r})$ and differential $du=d_Nu-(-1)^ru d_M$. If $M^i=0$ above $b$ and $N^j=0$ below $a$, nonzero factors require $a-r\leq i\leq b$, a finite interval, and the whole term is zero for $r<a-b$.

This construction is a bifunctor on the declared derived categories. Indeed homotopies in either variable induce Hom-complex homotopies. Replacing a projective model by a homotopy equivalent one therefore changes its Hom complex by a homotopy equivalence. A quasi-isomorphism in the target has acyclic cone, whose Hom from $P_M$ is acyclic by K-projectivity; hence the Hom map is a quasi-isomorphism. This also follows degree by degree from [[prop-morphisms-from-a-homotopically-projective-complex-need-no-roof]], which identifies each Hom-complex cohomology with the corresponding derived Hom. The injective argument uses [[prop-morphisms-into-a-homotopically-injective-complex-need-no-roof]] and reverses the roles of source and target. Thus both variables descend through localization. When both systems exist, the quasi-isomorphisms $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,N)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_M,I_N)\leftarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,I_N)$ give their natural identification. Either one-sided resolution hypothesis suffices.

Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]])
viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived
categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]).
For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$
([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open
$V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed
support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness
being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma
[[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
$Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective
replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$
([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective
construction of
[[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]
([[def-sheaf-hom]]).

Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of
[[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds,
and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put
$K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]],
[[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$,
define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with
open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$.
[[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]]
proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen
resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the
terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible
restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts
a generic six-functor axiom.

The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse
image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the
base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property for every sheaf is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem
recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image
[[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the
terms of the chosen finite resolution are fibrewise $c$-soft, not
necessarily $c$-soft on $X$. Their acyclicity for $f_!$ follows from the
fibre formula in its well-definedness theorem; the restricted fibre sheaves
are compact-support acyclic by
[[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]].
The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC supplies the injective replacements and finite fibrewise-soft
resolution; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the
exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological
shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of
$\varnothing$, the following two conditions hold.

**Locality.** If $s,t\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy
$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

**Gluing.** If sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy
$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

By locality, such a section $s$ is automatically unique. Thus a sheaf is
exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

citations.quote: Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.
citations.proof_quote: 7.1 For one morphism between quasi-projective varieties, choose a locally closed embedding of its source into $\mathbb P^N$ and take the reduced closure of its graph in $\mathbb P^N\times Y$. The graph is locally closed, hence open in that closure; thus the map factors as an open inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ followed by the projective projection $p:\overline X\to Y$. The closure is quasi-projective and $p$ is analytically proper by [F1]. Each algebraic fibre has a deleted-boundary model of dimension at most twice the source dimension by [F3]; [F6] therefore bounds compact-support cohomology of every sheaf on every fibre open by that same integer. Thus the support operations satisfy their required all-fibre-open hypothesis, rather than merely a bound for constructible coefficients. Choose [F1]'s one-map Whitney strata for $p$, respecting the boundary $\overline X\setminus X$ and the finite input supports. Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact; $Rj_*$ is locally computed by the ordinary sections on the open part of [F2]'s controlled link-cone chart, and [F3] and [F4] give the bounded finite, locally constant complex-stratum model and its actual restriction maps. The proper whole-fibre local trivializations of [F2] give, over a small ball in each target stratum, a product with a compact stratified fibre. The same derived product reconstruction used in [F3] identifies the constructible input there with a fibre object constant in the ball direction, so its pushforward is its finite fibre cochain complex constant along that ball. Finitely many target strata give a uniform amplitude bound; ordinary direct-image composition (inverse image is exact, so direct image preserves injectives) and the proper-support factorization of step 4.1 show $Rp_*Rj_*$ and $Rp_*j_!$ compute $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ respectively. All models and comparisons commute with field extension by [F3] and [F4]. For a general separated finite-type map, work over an affine target chart, take a finite affine cover of its source preimage and finite intersections, and apply this construction to their finite disjoint union mapping to the target. Prescribe the needed supports in that one-map construction, obtaining one target stratification for the finitely many terms. The actual finite open-cover derived augmentation of [F5] then assembles ordinary pushforward; its extension-by-zero support resolution of step 4.1 assembles proper-support pushforward. Thus the outputs are bounded algebraically constructible locally on the target and hence globally by a finite affine cover. This proof uses a constructed projective factorization on each quasi-projective piece and proper whole-fibre triviality, rather than inferring whole-fibre control from local source charts. No joint stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram is required. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models and $B$ in the stated constructible subcategory on the base, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.
The distinguished cone triangles in $K(\mathcal A)$ satisfy TR4.

Let $S$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), let $k$ be a field
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $S$
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]). Then $\mathcal F$ is **locally
constant of finite rank** if every point $x\in S$ has an open neighbourhood
$U\subseteq S$ for which there are an integer $n\ge0$ and an isomorphism of
sheaves on $U$
$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;k_U^{\,n},$$
where $k_U$ is the constant sheaf on $U$ with value $k$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ is
the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to the open subspace $U$
([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]], [[def-morphism-of-presheaves]],
[[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]]). A sheaf with
this property is also called a **finite-rank local system of $k$-vector spaces**
on $S$. This is a property of the sheaf on the space; no identification of such
sheaves with functors on the fundamental groupoid is part of the definition.

The sheaf $k_U^{\,n}$ is the $n$-fold direct sum of $k_U$ in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces, with $k_U^{\,0}$ the zero sheaf; its sections over
an open $W\subseteq U$ are the locally constant functions $W\to k^n$. The
integer $n$ is quantified locally, so no global rank is asserted and the rank
may differ from point to point; the definition asserts no existence of a global
trivialization. The final sentence records only that a functorial groupoid
presentation of local systems is a different, uncompared object here.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of
$\varnothing$, the following two conditions hold.

**Locality.** If $s,t\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy
$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

**Gluing.** If sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy
$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

By locality, such a section $s$ is automatically unique. Thus a sheaf is
exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

The canonical pair is a t-structure on $D(\mathcal A)$ and on each of $D^-,D^+,D^b$ by intersection. More generally if $H^i(X)=0$ for $i>a$ and $H^j(Y)=0$ for $j<b$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[n])=0$ for $n<b-a$, and naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[b-a])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(H^aX,H^bY)$.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The **internal Hom sheaf**
$$
\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)
$$
is the sheaf on $X$ defined by
$$U\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X|_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$$
for each open set $U \subseteq X$.

Restriction to a smaller open set $V \subseteq U$ sends a morphism
$\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ to its restriction
$\mathcal F|_V\to\mathcal G|_V$. Multiplication by a local section
$a\in \mathcal O_X(U)$ acts on a morphism $\varphi$ by either pre- or
post-composition with multiplication by $a$, giving
$\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ the structure of an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of
$\varnothing$, the following two conditions hold.

**Locality.** If $s,t\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy
$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

**Gluing.** If sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy
$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

By locality, such a section $s$ is automatically unique. Thus a sheaf is
exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). Every bounded-below
complex also has a bounded-below termwise injective replacement
([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]]). With the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded-below derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).
Its full subcategory of bounded-below injective complexes with bounded
cohomology models $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements; the replacements need
not have bounded terms.

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for
every $x\in X$, the induced map on stalks
$$\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\longrightarrow\mathcal G_x$$
is a bijection.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For complexes of vector spaces over a field $k$ with finite diagonals, cross product is a natural isomorphism $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H_pC\otimes_kH_qD\cong H_n(C\otimes_kD)$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $Y$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on $X$. Then there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_Y(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F).$$

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The local comparison and the fiber model.** Let $V\subseteq S$ be a product chart with trivialization $Y|_V\cong V\times F$ and projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$. By [F1] there is a natural comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B_V\simeq B_V\otimes_kC^*(F;k)$ for bounded $B_V\in D_c^b(V;k)$, compatible with restriction to smaller charts and carrying the adjunction unit to $B_V\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. By [F2] the chart and the fiber carry finite deleted-boundary models, so $C^*(F;k)$ is a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces whose cohomology is $k$ in degree zero, in the sense that the structure map $k\to C^*(F;k)$ identifies $k$ with $H^0$, and is zero in degrees $1\le j\le r$. The comparison is compatible with the global adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [F3] over the chart: restriction to $V$ is inverse image along the open inclusion, inverse image commutes with $f^*$, $Rf_*$ commutes with restriction to the open base for open inclusions by [F3] and [F8], and the unit is natural, so the restriction of the global unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ to $V$ is the chart unit.

**The cone bound.** Let $\tilde C:=\operatorname{Cone}(k\to C^*(F;k))$, a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces with $H^0(\tilde C)=0$ and $H^j(\tilde C)=H^j(C^*(F;k))=0$ for $1\le j\le r$; hence $H^j(\tilde C)=0$ for all $j\le r$. Now let $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$, so $H^p(B)=0$ for $p<b$. By [F7] the cohomology of $B_V\otimes_k\tilde C$ is the direct sum of the terms $H^p(B_V)\otimes_kH^q(\tilde C)$ with $p+q=n$, and a nonzero such term needs $p\ge b$ and $q\ge r+1$, hence $n\ge b+r+1$; therefore $H^n(B_V\otimes_k\tilde C)=0$ for $n\le b+r$. Since the unit of the chart comparison is $B_V\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$, its cone is $B_V\otimes_k\tilde C$ up to canonical isomorphism, so the cone of the chart unit lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$ on every chart. The charts cover $S$, the restriction of the global unit to each chart is the chart unit by step 1.1, and vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of a complex is a local condition [F6], so the cone of the global unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$, which proves claim 1.

**The Hom comparison.** Let $B\to Rf_*f^*B\to C\to B[1]$ be the distinguished triangle of the unit, with $C\in D^{\ge b+r+1}$ by step 2.1, and let $A\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$ and $m\le b+r-a$. By [F5], $C[m]\in D^{\ge b+r+1-m}$ and $C[m-1]\in D^{\ge b+r+2-m}$; since $m\le b+r-a$ gives $b+r+1-m>a$ and $b+r+2-m>a$, orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le a},D^{\ge a+1})=0$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m])=0=\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m-1])$. The long exact Hom sequence of [F4] applied to the triangle, shifted by $[m]$, therefore shows that the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*f^*B[m])$ is a bijection. Under the derived adjunction of [F3] this map corresponds to the composition with the unit, $u\mapsto\eta_{B[m]}\circ u$, whose adjoint is exactly pullback $u\mapsto f^*u$; since the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*f^*B[m])$ carries $f^*u$ to $\eta_{B[m]}\circ u$ by naturality of the unit, the induced pullback map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ is a bijection. This proves claim 2.

**The image criterion.** Assume $a-b\le r$ and put $\Phi=f^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ and $\Psi=\tau^{\le a}\circ Rf_*$. For $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}\subseteq D^{\ge a+1}$ by step 2.1 and $b+r+1>a$, so the truncated unit $B\to\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B$ is an isomorphism; its inverse gives $\Psi\Phi\cong\operatorname{id}$. Now let $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$. Since $C\in D^{\ge b}$ and $Rf_*$ preserves lower bounds (a bounded-below complex can be resolved in degrees at least $b$ by [F4], and $f_*$ of a complex vanishing below $b$ vanishes below $b$), we get $Rf_*C\in D^{\ge b}(S;k)$, and by the setting $Rf_*C$ has bounded constructible cohomology; hence $\Psi C=\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Let $\gamma_C:\Phi\Psi C\to C$ be the composite of $\Phi(\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to Rf_*C)$ with the counit $\varepsilon_C:\Phi Rf_*C\to C$ of the adjunction. If $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism, then $C\cong\Phi(\Psi C)$ with $\Psi C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$, so $C$ lies in the image of $\Phi$. Conversely, let $C=\Phi B=f^*B$ with $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Then $\Psi C=\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B$, and the truncation $\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B\to Rf_*f^*B$ factors, up to the canonical isomorphism $\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B\cong B$ supplied by the previous paragraph, as the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$; the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{f^*B}\circ f^*(\eta_B)=\operatorname{id}_{f^*B}$, together with exactness of $f^*$, therefore shows that $\gamma_{f^*B}$ is an isomorphism. Hence for $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ the counit $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism exactly when $C$ is a pullback, which is the first assertion of claim 4.

**Full faithfulness.** If $a-b\le r$, then $0\le b+r-a$, so claim 2 with $m=0$ gives that $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B)$ is a bijection for all objects $A,B$ of $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Inverse image is exact and preserves the canonical t-structure and algebraic constructibility by [F3] and [F6], so $f^*$ maps $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$ into $D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$; a functor between categories that is bijective on all Hom sets is fully faithful, so claim 3 follows.

**Retracts.** Let $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ be a direct summand of $\Phi B=f^*B$ for some $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$, with maps $i:C\to\Phi B$ and $p:\Phi B\to C$ satisfying $pi=\operatorname{id}_C$. The counit $\gamma$ is a natural transformation $\Phi\Psi\to\operatorname{id}$; naturality in the form $u\circ\gamma_X=\gamma_Y\circ\Phi\Psi(u)$ for $u:X\to Y$, applied to $u=i$ and $u=p$, gives $p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\Phi\Psi(i)=p\circ i\circ\gamma_C=\gamma_C$ and $\gamma_C\circ\Phi\Psi(p)=p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}$. By step 3.2 the map $\gamma_{\Phi B}$ is an isomorphism. Define $\delta:=\Phi\Psi(p)\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ i:C\to\Phi\Psi C$. Then $\delta\circ\gamma_C=\Phi\Psi(p)\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\Phi\Psi(i)=\Phi\Psi(pi)=\operatorname{id}_{\Phi\Psi C}$ and $\gamma_C\circ\delta=p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ i=pi=\operatorname{id}_C$, using the two displayed identities. Hence $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism and, by step 3.2, $C$ lies in the image of $\Phi$, which proves closure under direct summands.

**Extensions under the strict bound.** Assume $r\ge a-b+1$ and let $C'\to C\to C''\to C'[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ whose outer objects lie in the image: $C'=f^*B'$ and $C''=f^*B''$ with $B',B''\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Let $\varphi:C''\to C'[1]$ be its connecting morphism. Because $1\le b+r-a$ by the strict bound, claim 2 applies with $A=B''\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$, $B=B'\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ and $m=1$; the isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(B'',B'[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*B'',f^*B'[1])$ being pullback along $f^*$, there is a unique $\bar\varphi:B''\to B'[1]$ with $f^*\bar\varphi=\varphi$. By TR1 the morphism $\bar\varphi$ is completed to a distinguished triangle $B'\to\bar B\to B''\to B'[1]$ in $D^b(S;k)$ ([F5]). The long exact cohomology sequence of this triangle and $B',B''\in D^{[b,a]}$ show $H^j(\bar B)=0$ for $j<b$ and for $j>a$: the exact segment $H^j(B')\to H^j(\bar B)\to H^j(B'')$ has zero outer terms in both ranges. By [F6] the cone $\bar B$ of a morphism of bounded algebraically constructible complexes is bounded and algebraically constructible, so $\bar B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Exactness of $f^*$ [F3] turns the triangle on $\bar\varphi$ into a distinguished triangle with connecting morphism $f^*\bar\varphi=\varphi$; two distinguished triangles with the same connecting morphism are isomorphic on their third objects, because TR2 and TR3 applied to the identity on the source and target of the connecting morphism give a morphism between the two triangles whose first two components are identities and hence, by the five-lemma applied to the long exact Hom sequences of [F4], an isomorphism on the third objects. Thus $C\cong f^*\bar B$ lies in the image of $\Phi$. This proves the extension-closure clause of claim 4; at the boundary $r=a-b$ the degree-one comparison $1\le b+r-a$ fails and the argument is deliberately not used.

**Conclusion and the local nature of the comparison.** Step 2.1 proves the cone claim 1; step 3.1 proves the Hom comparison claim 2, step 4.1 full faithfulness claim 3, and steps 3.2, 4.2 and 4.3 the image criterion and the closure properties of claim 4. The comparison used in step 2.1 is the local product comparison on product charts, not a global splitting: no isomorphism $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is asserted, and the argument uses only the cone of the unit and the degreewise vanishing of the fiber model, so nonzero characteristic-class transgressions of the bundle are preserved. The only choice-theoretic inputs are those recorded in [A1].

boundaries.evidence: The Statement assumes the fiber is nonempty and connected; for an empty base S the chart cover of step 2.1 is empty, the cone bound is vacuous chartwise, and all Hom groups compared in step 3.1 vanish.

The degenerate acyclicity r=0 is covered explicitly: step 1.1 identifies the fiber model with vanishing reduced cohomology only in degree zero, steps 3.1 and 3.2 with r=0 give the degree-zero comparison and the image criterion at width zero, and step 4.3 records that extension closure fails at the boundary r=a-b.

The unit component is isolated in step 1.1 and used in step 2.1: the structure map k to C^*(F;k) identifies k with H^0 and the cone has vanishing cohomology through degree r; this is exactly the hypothesis H^0(F;k)=k of the Statement.

The map is explicitly algebraic as well as a locally trivial bundle. In the product case step 1.1 is the local comparison and step 2.1 gives the global unit-cone bound. Algebraic pullback preservation is required; arbitrary analytic local constructibility is not asserted.

The two critical endpoints are the degree bound m=b+r-a of claim 2, proved in step 3.1, and the width endpoint a-b=r of claim 4, where step 4.3 proves retract closure and image characterization but deliberately does not prove extension closure.

Step 5.1 closes the argument by recording that the only choice-theoretic inputs are those of [A1]: the injective replacements and the AC-assumed suppliers [F1] and [F2]; the cone, truncation, gluing and Hom arguments are choice-free.
The forward direction of the image criterion in claim 4 is proved in step 3.2: if C lies in the image of f^* then the counit gamma_C is an isomorphism, by the triangle identity for C=f^*B.
The reverse direction of the image criterion is proved in step 3.2: if gamma_C is an isomorphism then C is canonically isomorphic to Phi(Psi C) with Psi C in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k), so C lies in the image.

citations.quote:
Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

Let $(v_0,\ldots,v_{r-1})$ be a finite linearly independent list in a real or complex inner product space. There is an orthonormal list $(e_0,\ldots,e_{r-1})$ such that, for every $k\le r$,

$$\operatorname{span}(e_0,\ldots,e_{k-1})=\operatorname{span}(v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}).$$

It is obtained recursively from

$$u_k=v_k-\sum_{j<k}\langle v_k,e_j\rangle e_j,\qquad e_k=\frac{u_k}{\lVert u_k\rVert}.$$

For $r=0$, both lists are empty.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be a smooth map.

- $F$ is an **immersion at $p\in M$** when $dF_p$ is injective.
- $F$ is a **submersion at $p\in M$** when $dF_p$ is surjective.
- $F$ has **constant rank $r$ on $A\subseteq M$** when
  $\operatorname{rank}_pF=r$ for every $p\in A$
  ([[def-rank-of-a-smooth-map-at-a-point]]).

The map is an **immersion** or **submersion** without qualification when the
corresponding pointwise condition holds at every point of $M$.

Let $f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$, $k\ge1$, and let $c$ be a regular value. Near each point, a regular level set is a $C^k$ graph over $\ker Df(a)$ of dimension $m-n$.

More precisely, for $a\in f^{-1}(c)$ put $K=\ker Df(a)$ and $E=K^\perp$, so $\mathbb R^m=K\oplus E$. There are neighbourhoods $P\subseteq K$ of $0$ and $Q\subseteq E$ of $0$ and a $C^k$ map $g:P\to Q$ with $g(0)=0$ and $Dg(0)=0$ such that, near $a$,
$$f^{-1}(c)=\{a+u+g(u):u\in P\}.$$
The empty fibre satisfies the regular-value convention vacuously, and when $m=n$ the local graph has zero-dimensional domain and is the isolated point $a$.

A **smooth $n$-manifold** is a pair $(M,\mathcal S)$ in which $M$ is a
topological $n$-manifold
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]) and $\mathcal S$ is a **smooth
structure** on $M$: a maximal smooth atlas
([[thm-each-smooth-atlas-is-contained-in-a-unique-maximal-smooth-atlas]]).
Because
[[thm-each-smooth-atlas-is-contained-in-a-unique-maximal-smooth-atlas]] sends
every smooth atlas to the unique maximal atlas containing it, a smooth manifold
is equivalently specified by a topological manifold $M$ together with any one
smooth atlas $\mathcal A$, the structure being the generated $[\mathcal A]$. A
chart $(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal S$ is called a **smooth chart** (or a **chart of
the smooth structure**); its domain is a **coordinate domain** and its
coordinate functions are **smooth coordinates** on $U$. When the structure is
clear from context, the manifold itself is written $M$ in place of
$(M,\mathcal S)$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and $\mathrm{DC}$. If $n\ge1$ and $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ is nonempty, then the following conditions are equivalent: compactness; closedness and boundedness; pseudocompactness; attainment of a maximum and minimum by every continuous $A\to\mathbb{R}$; countable compactness; sequential compactness; limit point compactness; and completeness together with total boundedness.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and
the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is
dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second
countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$
and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner
points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be
compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.
Corner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of
closed faces is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation
$f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its
differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the
tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise
preserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite
union construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same
relative conclusion applies to a fixed corner-adapted triangulated closed neighbourhood piece
whose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is
performed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary
incompatible boundary data is asserted.

Let $(V,K)$ be an abstract simplicial complex. Its **geometric realization**
$|K|$ is the set of functions $\alpha:V \to [0,1]$ such that:

1. $\alpha(v)=0$ for all but finitely many $v \in V$;
2. $\sum_{v \in V}\alpha(v)=1$;
3. the support $\operatorname{supp}(\alpha):=\{v \in V:\alpha(v)\neq 0\}$ is a simplex of $K$.

For each simplex $\sigma=\{v_0,\dots,v_n\}$ of $K$, write
$$|\sigma|:=\{\alpha \in |K| : \operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq \sigma\}.$$
Sending $\alpha$ to the barycentric tuple
$(\alpha(v_0),\dots,\alpha(v_n))$ identifies $|\sigma|$ with the geometric
simplex spanned by the standard basis vectors indexed by $v_0,\dots,v_n$, so
$|\sigma|$ carries its Euclidean simplex topology.

We give $|K|$ the **weak topology** with respect to these simplex inclusions:
a subset $U\subseteq |K|$ is declared open exactly when $U\cap|\sigma|$ is open
in $|\sigma|$ for every simplex $\sigma$ of $K$.

A **CW complex** is a Hausdorff space $X$ with a filtration
$$\varnothing=X^{-1}\subseteq X^0\subseteq X^1\subseteq\cdots,\qquad X=\bigcup_{n\geq0}X^n,$$
where $X^0$ is discrete and $X^n$ is obtained from $X^{n-1}$ by attaching a (possibly infinite) family of $n$-disks along maps $S^{n-1}\to X^{n-1}$ as in [[def-cell-attachment-by-a-characteristic-map]]. The images of the disk interiors are its **open $n$-cells** $e^n_\alpha$, and the disk maps are their characteristic maps. It moreover satisfies: (C) each closed cell $\overline {e^n_\alpha}$ meets only finitely many cells; and (W) $A\subseteq X$ is closed exactly when $A\cap\overline e$ is closed in $\overline e$ for every cell $e$. These are closure finiteness and the weak topology.

A **locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $F$** is a continuous map $p:E\to B$, an open cover $(U_i)_{i\in S}$ of $B$, and homeomorphisms
$$\theta_i:p^{-1}(U_i)\longrightarrow U_i\times F,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1\theta_i=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i)}.$$
Here bundle charts, including those used later for principal and associated bundles, are charts in ordinary topological spaces with ordinary product and subspace topologies. A bundle whose spaces are CGWH in addition can be considered in the CGWH fibration convention; we do not silently replace an ordinary product chart by a weaker k-product-chart assumption. Products and homeomorphisms have the meanings of [[thm-product-universal-property]] and [[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]].

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the coordinate change has the form $(b,x)\mapsto(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$, with continuous inverse $(b,y)\mapsto(b,g_{ij}(b,y))$. In particular each $g_{ji}(b,-)$ is a homeomorphism of $F$. The identities $g_{ii}(b,x)=x$ and $g_{ki}(b,x)=g_{kj}(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$ hold because the corresponding chart composites cancel. No topology on a homeomorphism group of $F$ is assumed.

The bundle is **numerable** when the data include a partition $(\rho_i:B\to[0,1])_{i\in S}$ with locally finite cozero sets, sum one, and
$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)=\overline{\{b:\rho_i(b)>0\}}\subseteq U_i.$$
This is the support-subordinate convention of [[def-partition-of-unity-subordinate-to-a-cover]]. Repeating a chart with multiple indices is allowed, so a partition subordinate to a refinement can be accompanied by an explicitly assigned original chart. Merely having pointwise finite sums or cozero containment is not this specified numerating data.

An empty base forces $E$ empty and allows the empty cover and partition. The fiber $F$ may be empty: then every chart domain, hence $E$, is empty even when $B$ is nonempty. When $F$ is nonempty the charts imply surjectivity by taking one point in the chart fiber for each particular base point; this assertion does not require choosing a simultaneous section. Over a point a chart identifies $E$ with $F$. No AC is assumed in the definition.
Every compact topological space is paracompact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice. Every open cover
of a compact Hausdorff space admits a finite partition of unity subordinate to
that cover.

Assume AC. Every numerable fiber bundle, with its supplied ordinary local product charts and support-subordinate locally finite partition of unity, is a Hurewicz fibration in all ordinary spaces. In particular a bundle of CGWH spaces with these charts is a Hurewicz fibration in CGWH. AC is used to well-order the set of finite chart words. No selection of a chart for every base point or of a separate lift for every path is made.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Serre fibration over a
path-connected CW complex and let $R$ be a commutative unital ring. The
decreasing skeletal filtration gives a natural first-quadrant cohomological
spectral sequence
$$E_2^{a,b}\cong H^a\bigl(B;\mathcal H^b(p;R)\bigr),\qquad d_r:E_r^{a,b}\longrightarrow E_r^{a+r,b-r+1},$$
strongly converging to $H^{a+b}(E;R)$ with the finite image filtration
$$F^aH^n(E;R)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(E,E_{a-1};R)\to H^n(E;R)\bigr),\qquad H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0.$$
Its stable terms have the specified natural identifications
$$E_\infty^{a,n-a}\cong F^aH^n(E;R)/F^{a+1}H^n(E;R).$$

For a square of fibrations over a cellular map $f:B\to B'$ with total map
$u:E\to E'$, naturality is contravariant: $u^*$ gives page maps from the
sequence for $p'$ to that for $p$, and on $E_2$ it is the local-coefficient
map for $f$ and the coefficient morphism
$f^*\mathcal H^b(p';R)\to\mathcal H^b(p;R)$ induced by the strict-fiber maps.

The raw cochain filtration is not asserted to be degreewise finite. Strong
convergence follows from the finite-quotient comparison below. AC is used in
the cohomological local-system/cellular comparison and in the cohomological
universal coefficient argument; it is not hidden.

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.
Thus $H_0(S^n;G)\cong G$ for $n\ge1$, whereas

$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally

Throughout, $I := [0,1] = \{\, t \in \mathbb{R} : 0 \le t \le 1 \,\}$
([[def-interval]]) carries the subspace topology inherited from $\mathbb{R}$ with
its usual topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]],
[[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]], [[def-metric-topology]],
[[def-metrizable-space]]). It is called the **unit interval**.

Let $X$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]) and let
$x, y \in X$.

- A **path in $X$ from $x$ to $y$** is a continuous map $\gamma : I \to X$
  ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) with $\gamma(0) = x$ and $\gamma(1) = y$. Its
  **image** is $\gamma[I]$.
- $X$ is **path-connected** when for every pair $x, y \in X$ there is a path in
  $X$ from $x$ to $y$. A subset $A \subseteq X$ is a **path-connected subset**
  when the space $A$ with its subspace topology is path-connected; equivalently,
  when any two of its points are joined by a path whose image lies in $A$, by the
  characteristic property of a map into a subspace
  ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).
- Write $x \sim y$ when a path in $X$ from $x$ to $y$ exists. The **path
  component** of $x$ is its equivalence class
  $$P(x) \;:=\; \{\, y \in X : x \sim y \,\} .$$
- The empty space is path-connected, the defining condition quantifying over no
  pair of points, and so is every one-point space, the constant path joining its
  point to itself.

**$\sim$ is an equivalence relation on $X$, and the obligation is discharged
here**, so that "equivalence class" above denotes.

*Reflexive.* The constant map $\gamma(t) = x$ is continuous, every preimage being
$\varnothing$ or $I$ ([[def-continuous-map-top]]), and joins $x$ to $x$.

*Symmetric.* If $\gamma$ joins $x$ to $y$, put $\bar\gamma(t) := \gamma(1-t)$.
The map $r : I \to I$, $r(t) = 1 - t$, is continuous: for $s, t \in I$ one has
$|r(s) - r(t)| = |s - t|$, so a ball of radius $\varepsilon$ around $r(t)$ pulls
back to contain the ball of radius $\varepsilon$ around $t$
([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-metrizable-space]]). Hence
$\bar\gamma = \gamma \circ r$ is continuous ([[lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes]],
claim 1) and joins $y$ to $x$.

*Transitive.* Let $\gamma_1$ join $x$ to $y$ and $\gamma_2$ join $y$ to $z$.
Define $\delta : I \to X$ by

$$\delta(t) \;:=\; \begin{cases} \gamma_1(2t), & 0 \le t \le 1/2, \\ \gamma_2(2t - 1), & 1/2 \le t \le 1. \end{cases}$$

The two clauses agree at $t = 1/2$, both giving $\gamma_1(1) = y = \gamma_2(0)$,
so $\delta$ is a well-defined function. The sets $[0,1/2]$ and $[1/2,1]$ are
closed in $I$ and cover it, and there are **two** of them, so the finite closed
form of the pasting lemma applies ([[lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes]],
claim 3). On $[0,1/2]$ the map $\delta$ is $\gamma_1 \circ a_1$ with
$a_1(t) = 2t$, and on $[1/2,1]$ it is $\gamma_2 \circ a_2$ with
$a_2(t) = 2t - 1$; each $a_k$ is continuous into $I$, since
$|a_k(s) - a_k(t)| = 2|s-t|$, so the ball of radius $\varepsilon/2$ around $t$
maps into the ball of radius $\varepsilon$ around $a_k(t)$
([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-metrizable-space]],
[[def-subspace-topology-top]]). So both restrictions are continuous by
[[lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes]] claim 1, hence $\delta$ is continuous, and
it joins $x$ to $z$.

**The path components partition $X$**, being the classes of an equivalence
relation, and each is a path-connected subset of $X$: two points of $P(x)$ are
joined to $x$, hence to each other by the transitivity construction above, and
the resulting path has image inside $P(x)$: if $\delta$ is a path from $x$ and
$s \in I$, then $t \mapsto \delta(st)$ is a path from $x$ to $\delta(s)$,
continuous because $t \mapsto st$ satisfies $|st_1 - st_2| \le |t_1 - t_2|$ and
is therefore continuous into $I$ by the ball criterion used above, so every point
of the image is itself joined to $x$.

every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-metrizable-space]],
[[def-subspace-topology-top]]). So both restrictions are continuous by

A **locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $F$** is a continuous map $p:E\to B$, an open cover $(U_i)_{i\in S}$ of $B$, and homeomorphisms
$$\theta_i:p^{-1}(U_i)\longrightarrow U_i\times F,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1\theta_i=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i)}.$$
Here bundle charts, including those used later for principal and associated bundles, are charts in ordinary topological spaces with ordinary product and subspace topologies. A bundle whose spaces are CGWH in addition can be considered in the CGWH fibration convention; we do not silently replace an ordinary product chart by a weaker k-product-chart assumption. Products and homeomorphisms have the meanings of [[thm-product-universal-property]] and [[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]].

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the coordinate change has the form $(b,x)\mapsto(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$, with continuous inverse $(b,y)\mapsto(b,g_{ij}(b,y))$. In particular each $g_{ji}(b,-)$ is a homeomorphism of $F$. The identities $g_{ii}(b,x)=x$ and $g_{ki}(b,x)=g_{kj}(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$ hold because the corresponding chart composites cancel. No topology on a homeomorphism group of $F$ is assumed.

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)=\overline{\{b:\rho_i(b)>0\}}\subseteq U_i.$$
