citations.quote: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.

Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
gives a locally small triangulated category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with conservative
restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift, and its morphism groups are
computed by the coinduced simplicial injectives of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]. Locally
split free-action descent identifies its finite general linear Stiefel
resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$, and
the bounded Hom and image comparisons, the degree-zero ring comparison and
retract closure of
[[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]
hold for it. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness
of restriction to $X$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

derivations.claim: **Smooth comparison and image preservation.** On each quasi-projective source piece over an affine target, [F4] factors the map as an open inclusion into its graph closure in $\mathbb P^n\times Y$, followed by proper projection. The open-inclusion smooth exchange of [F1] followed by proper base change gives smooth exchange for $Rf_*$ on this piece. A finite affine source cover and its intersections compute ordinary pushforward by finite open-cover derived descent [F4]; smooth inverse image is exact, so the piece comparisons give the canonical smooth exchange for the general map. The comparison respects composition because its maps are the ordinary units and base-change maps. Proper-support exchange for arbitrary maps is [F5]; smooth exchange for tensor, internal Hom and normalized duality follows locally by adjoining a contractible smooth ball to their finite cochain models. For a fixed frame resolution, write $D^N_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_{X_N}[-2s_N])$. Smooth orientation gives $q_N^*D^N_XQ_N(A)\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*D_XA_X$, since smooth orientation gives $q_N^*\omega_{X_N}=\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X[2s_N]$ and both dualizing shifts cancel the dimensions $u_N=g+s_N$. The smooth comparison for the square formed by $q_N$, $f_N$ and $\mathrm{id}_{U_N}\times f$, followed by the product projection to $f$, therefore gives $q_N^*Rf_{N*}Q_N(A)\cong\operatorname{pr}_Y^*Rf_*A_X$ and likewise for $Rf_{N!}$. Inverse image and tensor have this comparison directly; internal Hom has it by its smooth comparison; $f_N^!=D^N_Xf_N^*D^N_Y$ has it by duality. Thus every ordinary operation on the resolution representatives satisfies the frame-pullback image criterion [F3], with an ordinary bounded constructible object downstairs. Its unshifted cohomological amplitude equals the downstairs amplitude, because both $q_N^*$ and $\operatorname{pr}_X^*$ are exact and conservative. These are bounds independent of $N$.

**Transport of operations and adjunctions.** For each fixed finite collection of inputs, outputs and adjunction maps, choose $N$ whose gap exceeds the widths of their unshifted ordinary amplitudes and the finitely many Hom comparison bounds. By step 1.1 all the ordinary resolution operations lie in the finite-resolution image, so [F3] transports them to $D^b_{G,c}$. On a common product resolution the smooth comparisons identify the two constructions canonically; their coherence gives the cocycle on triple products, hence independence of the choice of $N$. Every bounded input is treated this way; no decomposition of an object into its cohomology sheaves is assumed. The ordinary adjunction Hom bijections, their units and counits, transport through the fully faithful comparisons. Naturality and the triangle identities are equations of these maps and are reflected by a sufficiently large faithful comparison. This proves $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ and the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction on the actual bounded equivariant category.

**Coherence.** Composition of maps, identity comparisons, support localization, the projection formula, trace and Cartesian pasting are equations between morphisms built from unit and counit maps of the ordinary adjunctions. By [F1] these equations hold at the level of the resolution varieties, and naturality of the resolution comparisons plus their full faithfulness on the intervals means that an equation holding after transport to $X_N,Y_N$ holds in $D^b_{G,c}$; more precisely, the comparison functors are faithful on the relevant Hom groups by [F3], so the two sides of each coherence equation, which agree after transport, agree before it. The general proper-support exchange and its pasting transfer from [F5] in the same way; proper equality $Rf_!=Rf_*$ transfers from [F1]. This proves the first part of claim 2.

**Normalization.** For a frame resolution $P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N$ with base $B_N$ and maps $a_{X_N}:X_N\to B_N$, $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ and $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$, put $u_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}U_N$, $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$ and $s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N=u_N-g$, and define the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G_{X_N}:=\omega_{X_N}\otimes_k a_{X_N}^*\omega_{B_N}^{-1}$, the inverse taken in the tensor category of bounded constructible sheaves on $B_N$; here $B_N$ is a smooth complex $s_N$-fold, so by [F2] its dualizing object is $\omega_{B_N}\simeq k_{B_N}[2s_N]$ and $a_{X_N}^*\omega_{B_N}^{-1}\simeq k_{X_N}[-2s_N]$. Transitivity of dualizing objects for the smooth maps $\operatorname{pr}_X$ of relative dimension $u_N$ and $q_N$ of relative dimension $g$ gives $\omega_{P_N}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X[2u_N]\simeq q_N^*\omega_{X_N}[2g]$, hence $q_N^*\omega_{X_N}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X[2s_N]$ and therefore $q_N^*\omega^G_{X_N}\simeq q_N^*\omega_{X_N}[-2s_N]\simeq\operatorname{pr}_X^*\omega_X$: the normalization cancels exactly the base contribution, so $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary $\omega_X$ under the forgetful maps of [F3]. On a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$, complex orientation gives $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$ by [F2], and no extra shift survives because the normalization removes exactly the base contribution: this is the exclusion of the unnormalized quotient-stack dualizing shift recorded in the Statement. This proves claim 3.

**Dual exchange and pasting.** On a resolution over the common base $B_N$, let $D^N_T=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_{T_N}[-2s_N])$ for each corner $T$. The common shift preserves involutivity and the ordinary duality identities [F2]. Applying [F5] to $D^N_XA$ and then dualizing gives $D^N_{Y'}u^*Rf_!D^N_XA\simeq D^N_{Y'}Rf'_!v^*D^N_XA$, whose two sides are $u^!Rf_*A$ and $Rf'_*v^!A$ respectively. Thus the extraordinary exchange holds for arbitrary $f$, rather than only proper $f$. Transport through the normalized comparison of step 3.2 and the fully faithful resolution comparisons gives the equivariant exchange. Duality carries the pasting identities of [F5] to the dual pasting identities, so these comparisons have the required coherence. This completes claim 2.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 prove claims 1 to 3. Every comparison is induced by the ordinary coherent structure of [F1] and [F5] and the normalization of step 3.2; no unnormalized dualizing shift and no unproved base-change identity is introduced. AC enters as recorded in [A1].

boundaries.evidence: Statement and step 1.1: For empty X and nonempty Y, X_N is empty and Y_N need not be empty: inverse image lands in the zero category and the two direct-image functors send the zero object to zero. A map to empty Y forces X empty. The adjunction and comparison equations remain meaningful in these cases.

The zero case of the normalization is d=0 in step 3.2: a smooth complex zero-fold has omega_X=k_X, and no extra shift survives after the base normalization; the zero object is included in every operation.

The tensor unit and its internal-Hom adjunction are part of claim 1 and are transferred from the ordinary adjunction in step 1.1; the identity comparison is the base of the composition coherence of step 3.1.

The degenerate group case of the trivial product is covered because the resolution-comparison transport of steps 1.1 and 3.1 does not use any nontriviality of G; all equations hold in the ordinary category already.

The normalization endpoint d=0 and general d are both covered in step 3.2, and the proper-support endpoint of the exchange identities is covered in step 4.1 where proper maps satisfy Rf_! equal to Rf_* and the dual mate is derived.

The concluding step 5.1 records the AC audit of [A1]: choice enters through the injective replacements, the ordinary six-operation and duality suppliers and the finite resolutions, while the pasting and normalization comparisons below are canonical.

citations.quote: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $a:X\to Y$ be a smooth algebraic map of pure relative complex dimension $d$ between separated finite-type complex varieties, over an arbitrary coefficient field $k$. Then $a^*[d]$ is exact for the ordinary middle-perverse t structures of [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] on $D_c^b(-;k)$, and it commutes with their truncation and cohomology functors. Complex orientation gives $a^!=a^*[2d]$. If $a$ is surjective, its normalized pullback is conservative and reflects the perverse support and cosupport inequalities. The compatible finite stratifications used are those of [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]].

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
gives a locally small triangulated category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with conservative
restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift, and its morphism groups are
computed by the coinduced simplicial injectives of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]. Locally
split free-action descent identifies its finite general linear Stiefel
resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$, and
the bounded Hom and image comparisons, the degree-zero ring comparison and
retract closure of
[[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]
hold for it. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness
of restriction to $X$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $U_N$ has the right action $u\cdot g=u\circ g$ and the quotient uses
$(u,x)\cdot g=(ug,g^{-1}x)$. For the action nerve use the equivalent left
action $g\cdot(u,x)=(ug^{-1},gx)$, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct

derivations.claim: **The equivariant t-structure.** For $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ define $A\in{}^pD_G^{\le a}$ if and only if the restriction $A_X$ lies in the ordinary aisle ${}^pD^{\le a}(X;k)$, and ${}^pD_G^{\ge a}$ dually. By [F1] this is equivalent to $Q_N(A)[s_N]\in{}^pD^{\le a}(X_N;k)$ for every sufficiently large $N$, so the definition is independent of the resolution. The pair $({}^pD_G^{\le0},{}^pD_G^{\ge0})$ satisfies the t-structure axioms because the defining conditions are those of a t-structure pointwise: closure under shifts and extensions follows from the corresponding ordinary closures and the conservativity of restriction, orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}({}^pD_G^{\le0},{}^pD_G^{\ge1})=0$ follows from the ordinary orthogonality transported through the fully faithful Hom comparison of [F1], and truncation triangles exist by the lifting clause of [F1]. The structure is bounded because the ordinary one is and restriction to $X$ is conservative. This proves the t-structure and detection assertions.

**Gluing and independence of refinement.** The inequalities of the Statement are checked stratumwise and are therefore independent of compatible refinement by the ordinary clause of [F3]; gluing across an algebraic open/closed decomposition uses the localization triangles of [F2] and the ordinary gluing theorem: for a $G$-invariant open immersion $j$ and its closed complement $i$, the Čech-style recollement conditions $j^*i_*=0$, the triangles $j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}\to i_*i^*$ and $i_*i^!\to\mathrm{id}\to j_*j^*$ hold in $D^b_{G,c}$ by [F2], and the transport of step 1.1 reduces the glued t-structure statement to the ordinary one.

**Heart and finite length.** Kernel and cokernel of a morphism of the heart are the perverse cohomology objects in degrees $-1$ and $0$ of its cone, computed by the truncation functors of step 1.1; hence the heart is abelian. Restriction to $X$ is perverse exact and conservative on the heart by [F1], so a strictly increasing or decreasing chain of subobjects in the equivariant heart gives a strictly increasing or decreasing chain in the ordinary heart; the ordinary heart has finite length by [F3], so the equivariant heart does. For heart objects $A,B$ and $m<0$, $B[m]$ lies in ${}^pD_G^{\ge1}$ while $A$ lies in ${}^pD_G^{\le0}$, so orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$.

**Local systems and intermediate extension.** The group $G$ is path connected: elementary matrices and nonzero diagonal matrices are joined to the identity, and Gaussian elimination expresses every invertible complex matrix as their product. Let $L$ be an equivariant local system on an invariant smooth open $U$, with action isomorphism $\phi:\operatorname{pr}_U^*L\simeq a^*L$ on $G\times U$. For any ordinary sub-local-system $M\subset L$, the sub-local-systems $\phi(\operatorname{pr}_U^*M)$ and $a^*M$ agree on $\{e\}\times U$ by the identity condition. Every point $(g,x)$ is joined to $(e,x)$ by a path in $G\times U$; parallel transport therefore makes these sub-local-systems agree everywhere. Restricting $\phi$ supplies equivariant data on $M$, and the identity and cocycle equations restrict as well. In the action-nerve model this is a Cartesian sub-sheaf, hence an equivariant local system. Thus $L$ is simple equivariantly if and only if it is simple ordinarily. For irreducible invariant $Z$ and invariant dense smooth $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ of dimension $d$, a simple $L$ gives the simple ordinary perverse object $L[d]$ by [F3], and exact conservative restriction [F1] makes it simple in the equivariant heart too. Define $j_{!*}(L[d])=\operatorname{im}({}^pH^0j_!L[d]\to{}^pH^0Rj_*L[d])$. The first term has no boundary quotient and the second no boundary subobject, by the localization adjunctions [F2], so the image has neither. Any extension with neither property is this image: its adjunction maps from the first term and into the second have boundary cokernel and kernel, hence are epic and monic. A subobject of this image restricts either to zero or to all of $L[d]$; the boundary subobject or resulting boundary quotient must then vanish. Closed pushforward $i_{Z*}$ is exact and fully faithful on hearts by the same localization and detection, so $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=i_{Z*}j_{!*}(L[d])$ is simple.

**Classification of simple objects.** Let $A$ be a nonzero simple equivariant heart object, and let $T$ be the closed support of $A_X$. Localization identifies $A$ with closed pushforward of a heart object on $T$, which we again call $A$. Equivariance preserves $T$ and its smooth local-system locus. Its finitely many irreducible components are individually invariant because connected $G$ cannot permute them nontrivially. In the smooth locus of each component away from all component intersections, algebraic constructibility gives a dense algebraic open on which the cohomology of $A_X$ is locally constant. Its $G$-saturation is still an algebraic open in this locus, and equivariance makes the cohomology locally constant there. These saturations form disjoint invariant smooth opens $W_i$; set $W=\bigsqcup_i W_i$. Write $h:W\hookrightarrow T$. The perverse inequalities give $h^*A=\bigoplus_i L_i[\dim W_i]$, with every $L_i$ nonzero. The left heart adjunction supplies a map ${}^pH^0h_!(L_i[\dim W_i])\to A$ whose restriction is the inclusion of this summand. Its image is nonzero, hence all of $A$ by simplicity. Exact open restriction then forces this summand to equal $h^*A$, excluding every other support component. Thus $T=Z$ is irreducible. On its invariant dense smooth open $U$, write $j^*A=L[\dim Z]$. A nonzero proper equivariant sub-local-system $M\subset L$ would similarly give an image subobject of $A$ restricting to $M[\dim Z]$, contradicting simplicity. Hence $L$ is simple equivariantly, and therefore ordinarily by step 3.1. Simplicity of $A$ and $j^*A\ne0$ exclude boundary subobjects and quotients. The characterization of step 3.1 identifies $A$ with the intermediate extension, and closed pushforward gives precisely $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)$ on $X$.

**Endomorphism rings.** Let $S$ be a simple heart object and $f:S\to S$ a nonzero endomorphism. Its kernel is a subobject of $S$ and hence zero, and its image is a nonzero subobject and hence all of $S$; thus $f$ is invertible. Therefore $\operatorname{End}(S)$ is a division $k$-algebra, and it is not asserted to equal $k$. This completes the proof.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give the t-structure, its independence of refinement and gluing; steps 2.2, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1 give the heart, its finite length, the negative-Hom vanishing and the intersection-complex classification with division endomorphism rings. AC enters as recorded in [A1], and no semisimplicity or characteristic restriction beyond characteristic zero is used.

$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],

$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put

simplicial map of the two action nerves

the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$

Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.

$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The **tensor-product presheaf**
$$
\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G
$$
is defined by
$$(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(U) := \mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)$$
for each open set $U \subseteq X$, with restriction induced from the
restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.

The **tensor-product sheaf** is the sheafification of this presheaf:
$$\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G := a(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G).$$

The canonical pair is a t-structure on $D(\mathcal A)$ and on each of $D^-,D^+,D^b$ by intersection. More generally if $H^i(X)=0$ for $i>a$ and $H^j(Y)=0$ for $j<b$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[n])=0$ for $n<b-a$, and naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[b-a])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(H^aX,H^bY)$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Finiteness and vanishing.** Let $A,B$ be bounded constructible with $A\le a$ and $B\ge b$, fix $m$, and let $I$ be an ordinary cohomological interval containing the amplitudes of $A$ and of $B[m]$. Choose $N_i\ge n_i+1$ with $r_N\ge\operatorname{length}(I)$; such a choice is possible because $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$ grows without bound with the $N_i$. By [F1] there is a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$, and by [F2] the right-hand side is computed by a bounded finite-dimensional cochain model on the finite-type variety $X_N$, hence is finite-dimensional. If $b-a>m$, then $B[m]\ge b-m>a$ and the ordinary t-structure orthogonality makes $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<b-a$, so the groups vanish for sufficiently negative $m$. This proves claim 1.

**Scalar extension.** Coefficient extension on the simplicial category is termwise tensor with $K$, hence exact by [F4], and it commutes with inverse image and with the free-quotient descent used to define $Q_N$ because those constructions are given locally by exact inverse image along algebraic sections together with gluing. Therefore $Q_N(A_K)\cong(Q_N(A))_K$ and $Q_N(B_K)\cong(Q_N(B))_K$, and the same $N$ works over $k$ and over $K$: the fiber-gap vanishing of [F1] is field-independent and the finite models of [F2] commute with coefficient extension, so the interval bookkeeping is unchanged. In the resulting commutative square of Hom comparisons the vertical arrows are the full-faithfulness isomorphisms of [F1] over $k$ and over $K$, and the bottom horizontal arrow is the ordinary bounded constructible Hom coefficient-extension isomorphism of [F2]; hence the top horizontal arrow, which is the canonical map $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$, is an isomorphism. Naturality in $A$ and $B$ and compatibility with shifts hold because all maps are induced by functors and by the termwise base change, and compatibility with Yoneda composition holds because the comparisons are induced by functors and one sufficiently large $N$ serves the finitely many composable classes of a Yoneda product. No infinite totalization or infinite product of injectives is tensored with $K$. This proves claim 2.

**Commutation with the operations and the perverse structure.** The ordinary coherent six operations and normalized Verdier duality are determined on the finite constructible models of [F2], and the ordinary coefficient-extension clause of [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] shows that termwise exact coefficient extension commutes with inverse image, finite cochain pushforward, tensor, internal Hom and the finite-dimensional duality comparisons of [F3]; transporting through the finite-resolution comparisons as in step 1.2 gives the commutation with the equivariant operations and with normalized duality. For the perverse structure, exact coefficient extension preserves the upper support inequalities on ordinary restriction. It also preserves the lower inequalities, since it commutes with ordinary Verdier duality and that duality exchanges the two aisles. Hence it is perverse t-exact in the equivariant category detected by restriction [F3]. Applying it to a truncation triangle gives the unique truncation triangle over $K$, so perverse truncations and cohomology commute with extension. Its induced functor on the abelian hearts is exact and therefore preserves the image defining $j_{!*}$; the already proved commutation with $j_!$ and $Rj_*$ gives intermediate-extension commutation. This proves claim 3. Simplicity under extension is deliberately not asserted: a simple local system may fail to remain simple after extending scalars.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 prove claims 1 to 3. The proof is finite-stage: one sufficiently large resolution handles a fixed bounded object and its finitely many shifted targets, and no infinite-dimensional total Ext space is used. The total Ext space is not claimed to be finite, and simplicity is not claimed to be preserved. AC enters as recorded in [A1].

The degree m=0 case is included in step 1.1: Ext_G^0 is a finite-dimensional Hom space by the finite model, and the vanishing statement is about sufficiently negative m, with no claim that degree zero vanishes.
The trivial coefficient extension K=k is the identity case of claim 2 in step 1.2: the canonical map Ext tensor k to Ext is the identity isomorphism, natural in A and B.

The degenerate cases A=0 or B=0 are included in step 1.1: the comparison range is vacuous or both sides vanish, so the finite-dimensionality and vanishing conclusions hold trivially and no nondegeneracy is assumed.

The endpoint of the vanishing assertion is the sufficiently negative degree threshold b-a determined in step 1.1; the theorem deliberately makes no finiteness claim about the total direct sum, as recalled in the concluding step and realized by the companion example.

The concluding step 3.1 records the AC audit of [A1]: choice enters through the finite-resolution comparison [F1] and the constructible models [F2], while the finite-dimensional Hom, tensor and truncation comparisons themselves are choice-free.

$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $U_N$ has the right action $u\cdot g=u\circ g$ and the quotient uses
$(u,x)\cdot g=(ug,g^{-1}x)$. For the action nerve use the equivalent left
action $g\cdot(u,x)=(ug^{-1},gx)$, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$ and $B_N$ are points and $X_N=X$, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

The finite local comparisons do not assert a global tensor splitting for an
arbitrary bundle with fibre $U_N$, such as the comparison projections
$X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $X_{N,M}\to X_M$.

Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

For an integer $n\ge1$, **complex projective space** is the set of complex lines in $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ with the quotient topology
$$\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C):=(\mathbb C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times,\qquad [z_0:\cdots:z_n]:=\mathbb C^\times(z_0,\ldots,z_n).$$
The quotient projection is continuous and surjective. Its restriction to the unit sphere $S^{2n+1}\subset\mathbb C^{n+1}$ is still surjective, so $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ is compact. It is Hausdorff: the map sending a nonzero vector $z$ to the orthogonal projection $zz^*/\lVert z\rVert^2$ is continuous and constant on each complex line, hence descends by the quotient topology to a continuous injection from $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ into the Hausdorff space of complex matrices. A continuous injection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism onto its image.

For open $V\subseteq\mathbb C^r$, a map $H:V\to\mathbb C^s$ is **holomorphic** if at every $a\in V$ there is a complex-linear map $A_a:\mathbb C^r\to\mathbb C^s$ such that $H(a+h)=H(a)+A_a h+R_a(h)$ with $\lVert R_a(h)\rVert/\lVert h\rVert\to0$ as $h\to0$, $h\ne0$. When $r=1$, this is equivalent to each component being holomorphic in the sense of [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]], since a finite vector of scalar difference quotients converges exactly when each component does. A complex atlas consists of charts into $\mathbb C^n$ with holomorphic transitions in both directions.

For $j\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ let $U_j:=\{[z_0:\cdots:z_n]:z_j\ne0\}$. These open sets cover projective space: their inverse images under the quotient projection are the open saturated sets where $z_j\ne0$. The **standard chart** is
$$\varphi_j:U_j\longrightarrow\mathbb C^n,\qquad [z_0:\cdots:z_n]\longmapsto (z_0/z_j,\ldots,\widehat{z_j/z_j},\ldots,z_n/z_j),$$
where the $j$th coordinate is omitted. It is well defined under rescaling. The coordinate-ratio map on the inverse image of $U_j$ is continuous and constant on each quotient fibre, so the quotient topology makes $\varphi_j$ continuous; its inverse inserts $1$ in the $j$th position and is continuous by composition with the quotient projection. Hence it is a homeomorphism. On $U_j\cap U_k$ the transition from the $j$th chart to the $k$th chart sends each coordinate $w_\ell=z_\ell/z_j$ ($\ell\ne j$) to $w_\ell/w_k$ for $\ell\ne k$, with the omitted $j$th coordinate equal to $1/w_k$. To check holomorphy at $a$ with $a_k\ne0$, set $a_j=1$ and $h_j=0$ for the omitted source coordinate. Each target coordinate has the expansion $(a_\ell+h_\ell)/(a_k+h_k)=a_\ell/a_k+h_\ell/a_k-a_\ell h_k/a_k^2+O(\lVert h\rVert^2)$ for $\ell\ne k$. The linear term is complex-linear, and the remainder estimate follows by expanding the reciprocal at the nonzero $a_k$. The inverse transition has the same form, so both are holomorphic. Thus these charts make $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ a complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ and a topological manifold of real dimension $2n$ in the sense of [[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]. The finite chart cover by second-countable copies of $\mathbb C^n$ gives a countable base. Its rational transition functions have smooth real coordinate expressions on their domains, so the atlas also defines the smooth structure in the sense of [[def-smooth-manifold]]. The space is path-connected: distinct lines represented by $u,v$ give the path $t\mapsto[(1-t)u+tv]$, whose vector never vanishes because $u,v$ are linearly independent; equal lines give a constant path. In particular, $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ is a Riemann surface in the sense of [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]].

A map $F:X\to\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ from a Riemann surface is **holomorphic** when it is continuous and every component of each chart expression $\varphi_j\circ F$, written in a local coordinate of $X$, is holomorphic on the open set $F^{-1}(U_j)$. On an overlap, the new components are $f_\ell/f_k$ and $1/f_k$, where the $f_\ell$ are the old components and $f_k\ne0$. The scalar quotient rule gives their holomorphy ([[thm-algebra-of-complex-derivatives]]), so it suffices to check one target chart locally. Changing the source coordinate composes each scalar component with a one-variable holomorphic chart transition, where [[thm-chain-rule-for-complex-derivatives]] applies ([[def-holomorphic-and-meromorphic-map-of-riemann-surfaces]]). A **projective line** is the image in $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ of a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$. Every invertible linear map of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ induces a holomorphic projective linear transformation: in source and target standard charts its coordinates are ratios of affine-linear functions with nonzero denominator, and the same reciprocal expansion gives a complex-linear derivative; these transformations act transitively on $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$.

A **CW complex** is a Hausdorff space $X$ with a filtration
$$\varnothing=X^{-1}\subseteq X^0\subseteq X^1\subseteq\cdots,\qquad X=\bigcup_{n\geq0}X^n,$$
where $X^0$ is discrete and $X^n$ is obtained from $X^{n-1}$ by attaching a (possibly infinite) family of $n$-disks along maps $S^{n-1}\to X^{n-1}$ as in [[def-cell-attachment-by-a-characteristic-map]]. The images of the disk interiors are its **open $n$-cells** $e^n_\alpha$, and the disk maps are their characteristic maps. It moreover satisfies: (C) each closed cell $\overline {e^n_\alpha}$ meets only finitely many cells; and (W) $A\subseteq X$ is closed exactly when $A\cap\overline e$ is closed in $\overline e$ for every cell $e$. These are closure finiteness and the weak topology.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups acting algebraically on a separated finite-type complex
algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero. For
bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the equivariant category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]:

1. every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ is
   finite-dimensional over $k$ and vanishes for all sufficiently negative $m$;
2. for every field extension $k\to K$ of characteristic-zero fields, the
   canonical map
   $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$
   is an isomorphism, natural in $A$ and $B$ and compatible with shifts and
   with Yoneda composition;
3. coefficient extension commutes with the coherent six operations, normalized
   Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these
   bounded constructible objects.

The total Ext space $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ need not be
finite-dimensional, and simplicity is not asserted to be preserved under
coefficient extension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space
$(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$
([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally
small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and
iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific
injective resolution
([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). Every bounded-below
complex also has a bounded-below termwise injective replacement
([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]]). With the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded-below derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).
Its full subcategory of bounded-below injective complexes with bounded
cohomology models $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements; the replacements need
not have bounded terms.

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: The group $\mathbb C^\times$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{pt}$, and the frame space is $U_N=\mathbb C^N\setminus\{0\}$; the quotient $U_N/\mathbb C^\times$ is the space of complex lines in $\mathbb C^N$, i.e. $\mathbb P^{N-1}$. Under the resolution triple, the constant equivariant object $k$ corresponds to the pair $(k,\ k_{\mathbb P^{N-1}})$ because the pullback of $k$ along $U_N\to\operatorname{pt}$ is the constant sheaf $k_{U_N}$, which descends along the $\mathbb C^\times$-bundle to $k_{\mathbb P^{N-1}}$. So $Q_N(k)=k_{X_N}=k_{\mathbb P^{N-1}}$.

**The finite cells.** Use the filtration $\mathbb P^0\subset\mathbb P^1\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P^{N-1}$ by coordinate subspaces. For $j\ge1$, the map from the closed unit ball in $\mathbb C^j$ to $\mathbb P^j$ given by $v\mapsto[v:\sqrt{1-\lVert v\rVert^2}]$ sends its boundary to $\mathbb P^{j-1}$ by $v\mapsto[v:0]$, and is a homeomorphism on the interior to the affine chart complementary to $\mathbb P^{j-1}$; its inverse chart coordinate is $z\mapsto z/\sqrt{1+\lVert z\rVert^2}$. The adjunction space formed by attaching this ball to $\mathbb P^{j-1}$ maps continuously and bijectively to $\mathbb P^j$. It is compact and the target is Hausdorff by [F3], so this map is a homeomorphism. Induction gives a finite CW structure with one cell in each degree $0,2,\ldots,2(N-1)$ and no odd cells. Its cellular cochain differentials vanish; [F4] consequently gives singular cohomology $k$ in those even degrees and zero otherwise. Projective space is metrizable (embed a line as its orthogonal projection matrix) and its smooth ball charts give contractible-open bases; [F7] identifies this computation with constant-sheaf cohomology and hence with $\operatorname{Hom}(k,k[m])$.

Fix $m\ge0$. Choose $N$ with $r_N=2(N-1)\ge m$, so that the comparison range of [F2] applies; then $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb P^{N-1}}(k,k[m])\cong H^m(\mathbb P^{N-1};k)$ by [F7] and step 1.2, which is $k$ for even $m$ and $0$ for odd $m$. For $m<0$ choose any $N$ with $2(N-1)\ge|m|$; the same comparison applies and $H^m(\mathbb P^{N-1};k)=0$ because a CW complex has no negative cohomology. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)\cong k$ for even $m\ge0$ and vanishes otherwise, which is the displayed computation.

The computation of step 2.1 is degreewise finite: each group is either $k$ or $0$. Infinitely many even degrees are nonzero, namely all $m=2j$ with $j\ge0$, so the total direct sum $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)$ contains a copy of $k$ in infinitely many degrees and is infinite-dimensional.

On the ordinary point, [F6] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b(\operatorname{pt})}(k,k[2])=0$, while the equivariant group $\operatorname{Ext}_G^2(k,k)$ is $k$ by step 2.1. The restriction functor to the ordinary point would have to induce the comparison map $\operatorname{Ext}_G^2(k,k)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{pt}}(k,k[2])$ on these Hom groups, and this map cannot be injective because its target is zero and its source is nonzero; hence restriction is not derived fully faithful. This proves all three assertions. AC is present only as recorded in [A1].

boundaries.reason: The Example is set on the one-point space with the trivial C^*-action; no empty space or empty resolution occurs, and the finite Stiefel approximations are nonempty for every N.

boundaries.evidence: The degree-zero case m=0 is covered by step 2.1: Ext_G^0(k,k) is k, the first nonzero group in the displayed even-degree pattern, and negative degrees m<0 are disposed of there as well by the vanishing of negative cohomology of the projective space.

Statement and step 2.1: The smallest admitted frame parameter is N=2, since the consumed comparison assumes N>=n+1. The cell induction uses P^0 as its auxiliary point base but does not invoke the stabilization supplier at N=1.

The Example is itself the fully degenerate case: the action of C^* on the point is trivial, no orbit stratification is used, and step 1.1 identifies the quotient U_N/C^* with projective space directly through the principal bundle.

The stable-range endpoints are handled in step 2.1: the even degree m=2(N-1) at the top of H^*(P^{N-1};k) is k, the next even degree m=2(N-1)+2 is chosen with a larger N, and the odd endpoint m=1 vanishes there as everywhere odd.
The example inherits AC through the frame comparisons, cellular-cochain theorem and constant-sheaf comparison. The explicit disk attachment and even-degree count require no additional choices.
The even-degree forward case of the displayed formula is proved in step 2.1: for even m at least 0 the comparison identifies Ext_G^m(k,k) with H^m(P^{N-1};k), which is k in the stable range.

The odd and negative cases are proved in the same step 2.1: for odd m the projective-space cohomology vanishes, and for m<0 the comparison applies with a large N and negative cohomology vanishes, so the formula holds in both directions.

risk_review.notes: Checked N=2 as smallest admitted resolution, P0 only as auxiliary cell base, m=0, m=2 at the exact gap, odd m and every negative m, zero ordinary positive Ext and nonzero equivariant degree 2. N is chosen among admissible N≥2; arbitrarily large N handles each fixed degree. Constant coefficients descend by explicit local sections and are constructible on projective space itself, which is connected by the explicit projective charts/path argument. The coinduced simplicial injective comparison and uniform unit cone use only the proved topological Cech part, the exact t-structure and the field-independent frame gap; no generic connected-strata supplier is required for these constant objects. Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field and let $J=J(A)$. Then
$J$ is nilpotent, and the quotient algebra $A/J$ is semisimple.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional associative $\mathbb C$-algebra with unit, and let
$(\cdot,\cdot):A\times A\to\mathbb C$ be the **trace form**
$$(a,b):=\operatorname{tr}(L_{ab}),$$
where $L_c:A\to A$ is left multiplication by $c$, $L_c(x)=cx$, and the trace is
that of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Then:

1. $(\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symmetric associative bilinear form:
$(a,b)=(b,a)$ and $(ab,c)=(a,bc)$ for all $a,b,c\in A$;
2. $(\cdot,\cdot)$ is nondegenerate if and only if $A$ is semisimple
([[def-semisimple-ring]]);
3. if $A$ is semisimple, then either $A=0$ or
$A\cong\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$ with $r\ge1$, $d_i\ge1$,
the simple left $A$-modules are the natural $d_i$-dimensional modules of the
factors ([[thm-simple-modules-over-semisimple-rings]]), and under such an
isomorphism the trace form corresponds to
$$((X_i),(Y_i))\longmapsto\sum_{i=1}^r d_i\,\operatorname{tr}(X_iY_i),$$
a sum of nondegenerate matrix trace pairings. No statement of this item uses the
Axiom of Choice.

Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring. Then $R$ is semisimple if and only if $$R\cong\prod_{i=1}^rM_{n_i}(D_i)$$ for positive integers $r,n_i$ and division rings $D_i$. See [[thm-endomorphism-ring-of-the-left-regular-module-is-opposite]].

Let $r\ge1$, let every $n_i\ge1$, let every $D_i$ be a division ring, and put $R=\prod_{i=1}^rM_{n_i}(D_i)$. Then every simple left $R$-module is supported on exactly one factor and is isomorphic to that factor's column module $D_i^{n_i}$. These column modules give all simple left $R$-module isomorphism classes, with one class for each factor. See [[thm-wedderburn-artin-theorem]].

For a finite-length module, the direct-sum, sum-of-simples, and complement characterizations of semisimplicity are equivalent without any choice principle. See [[thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-semisimple-modules]].
A left $R$-module is **semisimple** when it is an internal direct sum of simple submodules, allowing the empty direct sum. Hence the zero module is semisimple.

For a left $R$-module $M$, the **socle** is $$\operatorname{Soc}(M):=\sum\{S\le M:S\text{ is simple}\}.$$ Concretely it is the submodule generated by the union of all simple submodules. If there are none, the sum is $0$, so the definition is always meaningful.

derivations.claim: Identify the radical of the regular trace form with $J$. The ideal $J$ is nilpotent and $B/J$ is semisimple, by [F1]. Choose a composition series of the left regular $B$-module; the simple factors are killed by $J$, since $JS=S$ for a simple factor would give $J^kS=S$ for every $k$, contradicting nilpotence. Each simple type of $B/J$ occurs among these factors: $B/J$ is a quotient of $B$, so its left regular module is a quotient of the regular module and its composition factors, namely $d_i\ge1$ copies of each column module, occur in the series. In a basis adapted to the series the diagonal blocks of $L_b$ are the factor actions, so $\operatorname{tr}(L_b)=\sum_im_i\operatorname{tr}(\overline b_i)$ with multiplicities $m_i\ge1$. Therefore the radical $\{b:(b,c)=0\text{ for all }c\}$ of the trace form is exactly $J$: it contains $J$, and on $B/J$ the induced form is the sum over $i$ of $m_i$ times the nondegenerate matrix trace pairing of the factor $M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$, which is nondegenerate because $m_i\ne0$ and $\mathbb C$ has characteristic zero, by [F2].

Descend the kernel to a rational subspace. Evaluate the trace form in the rational basis $a_1,\dots,a_d$ of $A$: the Gram matrix $T=(\operatorname{tr}(L_{a_ia_j}))_{i,j}$ has rational entries, because each $L_{a_ia_j}$ is the extension to $\mathbb C$ of the rational endomorphism of $A$ given by left multiplication by $a_ia_j$, and the trace of such an extension is the trace of a rational matrix. By step 1.1 its kernel in $B$ is $J$. Let $J_0=\{a\in A:Ta=0\}\subseteq A$ be the kernel computed in $\mathbb Q$-coordinates, a rational subspace; then $J_0\otimes\mathbb C=J$, since a rational linear system has the same solutions after extension of scalars and its solution space over $\mathbb C$ is the complexification of its rational solution space. Since $J$ is a two-sided ideal of $B$, the intersection $J_0=J\cap A$ is a two-sided ideal of $A$, and $W=\{v\in V:J_0v=0\}$ is a rational $A$-submodule of $V$.

Identify $W_{\mathbb C}$ with the socle. Because $J_0\otimes\mathbb C=J$, one has $W_{\mathbb C}=\{v\in V_{\mathbb C}:Jv=0\}$: choose a finite rational basis $j_1,\ldots,j_a$ of $J_0$, so $W$ is the kernel of $V\to V^a$, $v\mapsto(j_1v,\ldots,j_av)$. Write an element of $V_{\mathbb C}$ as $\sum_{i=1}^k v_i\otimes\lambda_i$ with the finitely many $\lambda_i$ rationally independent, obtained by reducing the span of its original coefficients. The equations $j_a\sum_i v_i\otimes\lambda_i=0$ imply $j_av_i=0$ for each $a,i$, by comparing coordinates in a finite rational basis of the span of the vectors $j_av_i$. Thus it lies in $W\otimes\mathbb C$; the reverse inclusion is immediate. No basis of an infinite-dimensional space is selected. Every simple $B$-submodule $S\subseteq V_{\mathbb C}$ is killed by $J$: otherwise $JS=S$, and then $J^kS=S$ for all $k$, contradicting nilpotence of $J$. Hence the socle of $V_{\mathbb C}$ is contained in $\{v:Jv=0\}$. Conversely $\{v:Jv=0\}$ is a module over the semisimple algebra $B/J$, and it is a sum of simple modules: for each of its vectors $v$, the cyclic module $(B/J)v$ is a quotient of the regular $B/J$-module, and that regular module is a finite direct sum of the column modules of [F2], so its image is a sum of simple modules. Each cyclic module is finite-dimensional, so [F3] makes its sum of simple images a finite direct sum. Every vector of $\{v:Jv=0\}$ therefore belongs to a sum of simple $B$-submodules, and this annihilator, containing every simple submodule, is exactly the socle. This argument does not require $V$ to be finite-dimensional. Thus the socle of $V_{\mathbb C}$ equals $W_{\mathbb C}=W\otimes\mathbb C$, a rational $A$-submodule complexified.

A unital ring $R$ is **semisimple** when its left regular module ${}_R R$ is semisimple. This is a left-module definition and uses no Jacobson radical. For the zero ring, the regular module is zero and hence semisimple; the Wedderburn-Artin theorem below is stated for nonzero rings.

([[def-semisimple-ring]]);

derivations.claim: Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ be the $\mathbb Q$-span of the monodromy matrices. It contains the identity and is closed under multiplication, because a product of monodromy matrices is a monodromy matrix, so it is a finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra. For every field $E$ over $\mathbb Q$ the canonical map $A\otimes_{\mathbb Q}E\to\operatorname{End}_E(V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}E)$ is injective: rationally independent matrices stay independent after extending scalars, as one sees by comparing coordinates in a rational basis of $V$. Its image is the $E$-span of the monodromy matrices, so submodules for this image are exactly the monodromy-invariant subspaces of $V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}E$; in particular the action of $A_{\mathbb C}=A\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ on $V_{\mathbb C}$ is faithful.

Assume $V_{\mathbb C}$ is semisimple. Let $J=J(A_{\mathbb C})$. If $T\subseteq V_{\mathbb C}$ is a simple submodule, then $JT$ is a submodule equal to $0$ or $T$, and $JT=T$ would give $J^kT=T$ for every $k\ge1$, contradicting the nilpotence of $J$ from [F1]. Hence $J$ kills every simple summand of $V_{\mathbb C}$ and therefore kills all of $V_{\mathbb C}$, since a semisimple module is a direct sum of simple submodules by [F4]. Faithfulness of the action, established in step 1.1, then forces $J=0$: an element of $J$ acts as zero on $V_{\mathbb C}$. Therefore $A_{\mathbb C}$ is semisimple.

Choose the rational basis $a_1,\dots,a_d$ of $A$ and let $T=(\operatorname{tr}(L_{a_ia_j}))_{i,j}$ be the Gram matrix of the regular trace form of $A$ in this basis. Its entries are rational: passing from $A$ to $A_{\mathbb C}$ extends the rational matrix of left multiplication by $a_ia_j$ to a complex matrix with the same trace. By step 2.1 and [F2] the regular trace form of $A_{\mathbb C}$ is nondegenerate, so $\det T\ne0$ as a complex number, and since $\det T\in\mathbb Q$ it is a nonzero rational number. For every field $k$ the scalar extension $\mathbb Q\hookrightarrow k$ therefore makes $T$, viewed over $k$, a nondegenerate matrix. No embedding of $k$ into $\mathbb C$ is used.

Let $k$ be any characteristic-zero field and put $A_k=A\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$. For $x\in J(A_k)$ and $b\in A_k$ the product $xb$ lies in the nilpotent ideal $J(A_k)$ by [F1], so $(xb)^n=0$ for some $n$ and the endomorphism $L_{xb}$ of $A_k$ is nilpotent; by [F3] its trace vanishes. Nondegeneracy of the extended matrix $T$ from step 3.1 then forces $x=0$, so $J(A_k)=0$. By [F1] the quotient $A_k/J(A_k)=A_k$ is a semisimple ring.

Finally $V_k=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$ is semisimple over $A_k$. Choose a $\mathbb Q$-basis $v_1,\dots,v_d$ of $V$. The map $(A_k)^d\to V_k$, $(x_1,\dots,x_d)\mapsto\sum_ix_iv_i$, is a surjective $A_k$-module homomorphism, and the regular module of the semisimple ring $A_k$ is a direct sum of simple modules by [F1]. Hence $V_k$ is a sum of images of simple modules, each of which is simple or zero, and $V_k$ has finite length over $k$; by [F4] it is a finite direct sum of simple modules, that is, semisimple. By step 1.1 this is exactly semisimplicity of the monodromy module, equivalently every invariant subspace has an invariant complement by [F4], which is semisimplicity of the local system $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes k$. The zero fiber is the empty direct sum and is included.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth, and let $Z\subseteq N$ be an embedded submanifold.
Then $F$ is **transverse to $Z$**, written $F\pitchfork Z$, when for every
$p\in F^{-1}(Z)$,

$$dF_p(T_pM)+T_{F(p)}Z=T_{F(p)}N.$$

If $F(M)\cap Z=\varnothing$, this condition is vacuous, so $F\pitchfork Z$
still holds.

If $F:M\to N$ is a submersion, then $F\pitchfork Z$ for every embedded
submanifold $Z\subseteq N$.

Let $M$, $S$, and $N$ be smooth manifolds. A **smooth family of maps from $M$
to $N$ parametrized by $S$** is a smooth map

$$\mathcal F:M\times S\to N.$$

For each $s\in S$, its **slice map** is

$$\mathcal F_s:M\to N,\qquad \mathcal F_s(p):=\mathcal F(p,s).$$

The map $\mathcal F$ itself is the **evaluation map** of the family.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $f:M\to N$ be smooth. Then there exist an open ball
$$ B\subseteq\mathbb R^m $$
containing $0$ and a smooth family of maps
$$ \mathcal F:M\times B\to N $$
such that $\mathcal F_0=f$ and, for every $p\in M$, the parameter map
$$ \mathcal F_p:B\to N,\qquad a\longmapsto \mathcal F(p,a), $$
is a submersion. In particular, the evaluation map $\mathcal F$ is a
submersion, so it is transverse to every closed embedded submanifold
$Z\subseteq N$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:M\to N$ be continuous, let $A\subseteq M$ be closed, and suppose $F$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $A$. Then there exist a smooth map $\widetilde F:M\to N$ and an open neighbourhood $W$ of $A$ such that $\widetilde F=F$ on $W$ and $F$ is homotopic to $\widetilde F$ by a homotopy fixed on $W$, hence relative to $A$. No compactness of $A$ or its neighbourhood is assumed.

Let $M$ be a smooth $m$-manifold, and let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth atlas on
$M$. A subset $A\subseteq M$ is **$\mathcal A$-null** when, for every chart
$(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal A$, the set

$$\varphi(A\cap U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$$

is null in the Euclidean sense of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]] when
$m\ge 1$, and is empty when $m=0$. Equivalently, on a $0$-manifold the only
null subset is the empty set.

Under the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the next proposition shows that this
condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas. Under that premise one
