Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for
$W$ and for $F$:
$$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$
for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient
filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is
exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is
$W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has
pure image of weight $n$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty
Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then
$U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every
$s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).

Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.

derivations.claim: Leray edge map in the family case. Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth projective and put $H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$. By [F3] choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$. Work first on the open-and-closed part $X_d$ where the smooth morphism has relative dimension $d$; there are finitely many such parts, and their derived images sum to $Rf_*\mathbb Q$. Each restriction remains smooth projective. The relatively ample Chern class is a morphism $\mathbb Q_{X_d}\to\mathbb Q_{X_d}[2]$: an injective resolution identifies degree-two cohomology with morphisms from the constant sheaf to its shift. Push it forward in [F6] and shift by $d$ to obtain $L:K\to K[2]$ for $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_{X_d}[d]$, whose stalk action is the cup-product Lefschetz action of [F1]. Now $H^{-a}(K)=R^{d-a}f_*\mathbb Q_{X_d}$ and $H^a(K)=R^{d+a}f_*\mathbb Q_{X_d}$, and $L^a$ between these sheaves is an isomorphism by fibrewise rational hard Lefschetz and proper base change [F2, F6]. Thus the centered hypothesis of [F2] applies to $K$, and shifting back and summing over $d$ gives $Rf_*\mathbb Q\cong\bigoplus_jR^jf_*\mathbb Q[-j]$. Precompose this isomorphism with the inverses of its induced automorphisms on the summands $R^j$ so that it induces the identity on every cohomology sheaf. Under the Leray identification $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\cong H^m(S,Rf_*\mathbb Q)$ supplied by [F6], this decomposition expresses $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)$ as the direct sum of the groups $H^{m-j}(S,R^jf_*\mathbb Q)$; the $j=m$ summand is a right inverse to the canonical edge map $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$, since the normalized summand inclusion induces the identity on $R^m$; hence the edge map is surjective. Equivalently the normalized decomposition makes that edge map the projection onto this summand. The stalk of $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ at $s$ is $H^m(X_s;\mathbb Q)$ by proper base change [F6], and evaluation at $s$ from the global flat sections $H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ is injective because $S$ is connected; its image is exactly the monodromy-invariant subspace $H^m(X_s;\mathbb Q)^{\pi_1(S,s)}$. Consequently the composite $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s;\mathbb Q)$ has image the invariant subspace.

Weights and strictness identify the invariant subspace. The space $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)$ carries the mixed Hodge structure of [F3], whose weights are at least $m$; the target $H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is pure of weight $m$, because $X_s$ is a smooth projective variety and the restriction $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures by the smooth-open functoriality of [F3], applied to the algebraic fibre inclusion; the compact fibre structure agrees with its pure structure because its boundary is empty. Strictness [F4] applied to this morphism, whose target has $W_{m-1}=0$ and $W_m=H$, gives that the image of $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)$ equals the image of its minimal weight part $W_mH^m(X,\mathbb Q)$; by [F3] that minimal weight part is the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X,\mathbb Q)$. Combining with step 1.1, the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ equals the image of $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$, which is the monodromy-invariant subspace. Since $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)$ and $H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ are pure of weight $m$ and the restriction is a Hodge morphism by [F1], its image is a Hodge substructure; this proves that the invariant subspace is a Hodge substructure in the family case.

Base-point independence and flatness of Hodge components in the family case. The restriction $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ factors through the canonical map $E:H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ followed by evaluation at $s$, and $E$ is independent of $s$. Its kernel $K=\ker E$ is therefore one fixed rational subspace, and evaluation identifies $H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ with the quotient $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)/K$, carrying the quotient Hodge structure, at every base point simultaneously; this is the asserted one constant Hodge structure on the invariant spaces. Now let $v$ be a global flat section of $H_{\mathbb C}$. Since the invariant space at $s$ is a Hodge substructure by step 2.1, the Hodge components of the value $v_s$ lie again in the complexified invariant space, hence are values of global flat sections $w_1,\dots,w_r$; their sum $\sum_iw_i$ is a global flat section with the same value at $s$ as $v$, so it equals $v$ by connectedness. Since the Hodge decomposition of the invariant fibre is the fixed quotient structure of step 2.1, the section $w_i$ is the Hodge component of $v$ of the corresponding type at every fibre. This proves, in the family case, both that the invariant subspace is a Hodge substructure and that the Hodge components of global flat sections are global flat sections.

Reduction of a general geometric variation to the realization open. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a nonempty Zariski open on which $H$ has an algebraic realization: $H|_U$ is the image of a flat rational idempotent $p$ that is a Hodge morphism at every point, inside $A=\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i)$ for smooth projective $f_i:X_i\to U$; this is the definition of a geometric variation, and each summand is a finite direct sum of weight pieces. By steps 1.1-3.1 applied to each $f_i$ over $U$ (note $U$ is again connected smooth quasiprojective), the statement holds for every $R^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i)$: its invariant part is a constant Hodge substructure and the Hodge components of its global flat sections are flat. Finite direct sums and Tate twists preserve both assertions, because monodromy acts componentwise and the twist changes only the weight; hence the statement holds for $A|_U$. Because $p$ is flat and a Hodge morphism, it commutes with monodromy and with the Hodge decompositions, so the invariant space of $H|_U$ is the image under $p$ of the invariant space of $A|_U$, and it inherits the constant Hodge structure; the Hodge components of a flat section of $H|_U$ are the images under $p$ of the components of a lift and are therefore flat. This proves the assertions for $H|_U$.

Extension from $U$ to $S$. The inclusion $U\hookrightarrow S$ induces a surjection $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ by [F5]. Therefore a vector of $H_s$ fixed by $\pi_1(U,s)$ is fixed by $\pi_1(S,s)$, so restriction of flat sections $H^0(S,H)\to H^0(U,H|_U)$ is an isomorphism: it is injective because $S$ is connected, and surjective by the preceding sentence. Apply this restriction isomorphism also after complexification. Given a global flat section $v$ of $H_{\mathbb C}$, its restriction to $U$ has, by step 4.1, Hodge components that are flat sections of $H_{\mathbb C}|_U$; each extends uniquely to a global flat section $w_i$ of $H_{\mathbb C}$, and $v-\sum_iw_i$ is a global complex flat section vanishing on the dense open $U$, hence vanishes by continuity. For each type $(a,b)$, the corresponding $w_i$ takes its values in the continuous Hodge subbundle of that type on $U$. Membership in this subbundle is a closed condition: in a local trivialization its continuously varying projection has kernel describing the complement, and the difference between $w_i$ and its type projection is continuous. This difference vanishes on the dense open $U$, hence on all of $S$. Thus $w_i$ has the prescribed type everywhere; uniqueness of the fiber decomposition makes these global flat sections exactly the Hodge components of $v$. In particular the complexification of $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$, consisting of values of global complex flat sections, is stable under all Hodge type projections. The rational invariant space is therefore a Hodge substructure with the induced pure decomposition.

Independence of the base point for a general variation. Evaluation identifies the rational space $E=H^0(S,H)$ with each invariant fiber $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$. Transport along a path identifies these invariant fibers through this one space $E$, since a global flat section is transported to its own value. Step 5.1 proves that the Hodge components of every global flat section are again global flat sections. On the realization open $U$, steps 3.1 and 4.1 identify these type decompositions with one fixed quotient Hodge structure on $E$, and the closed-membership argument of step 5.1 extends those same types to every point of $S$. Consequently evaluation gives one Hodge structure on $E$ independent of $s$, and transport restricted to the invariant fibers preserves that structure. This assertion concerns the invariant constant subsystem; it does not assume that transport on the full variation preserves the moving Hodge decomposition. Finite sums of pure weights are handled one weight at a time, proving every clause of the statement.

citations.quote:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a geometric polarizable rational
Hodge variation ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]) on a connected
smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$. For each base point $s$, the
monodromy-invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$
([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is a Hodge substructure of
$H_s$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), and parallel transport
identifies these spaces as one constant Hodge structure. Equivalently, the Hodge
components of every global flat section are global flat sections. For
$H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with $f:X\to S$ smooth projective and an SNC smooth
projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$, the image of
$H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is exactly the invariant
space.

Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional
rational algebra. The socle ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]) of the
$A_{\mathbb C}$-module $V_{\mathbb C}$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: it is
$W\otimes\mathbb C$ for a rational $A$-submodule $W\subseteq V$. If $V\ne0$,
then $W\ne0$.

For a left $R$-module $M$, the **socle** is $$\operatorname{Soc}(M):=\sum\{S\le M:S\text{ is simple}\}.$$ Concretely it is the submodule generated by the union of all simple submodules. If there are none, the sum is $0$, so the definition is always meaningful.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a smooth projective morphism
$f:X\to S$ of smooth quasiprojective complex varieties, $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a
finite-rank local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]),
with full monodromy-stable integral lattice obtained from
$R^mf_*\mathbb Z$ modulo torsion, and with a continuous pure Hodge
decomposition of weight $m$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]). A
relatively ample line bundle supplies flat Lefschetz operators and a flat
rational polarization of this variation. Products, sums, Tate twists, exterior
powers and Hodge direct summands have the corresponding geometric realizations
and full integral lattices. Pullbacks of algebraic maps between smooth
projective fibers preserve rational Hodge structures.

For a finite-length module, the direct-sum, sum-of-simples, and complement characterizations of semisimplicity are equivalent without any choice principle. See [[thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-semisimple-modules]].
A left $R$-module is **semisimple** when it is an internal direct sum of simple submodules, allowing the empty direct sum. Hence the zero module is semisimple.

Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$ and let $\bigl(x^{(j)}\bigr)_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$
be a sequence in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose range
$\{\, x^{(j)} : j \in \mathbb{N} \,\}$ is a bounded subset of
$(\mathbb{R}^{n}, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]], [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).
Then there are a strictly increasing $i : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
([[def-sequence]], [[lem-index-map-grows]]) and a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$
with

$$x^{(i_j)} \longrightarrow p \quad \text{in } (\mathbb{R}^{n}, d_2)$$

([[def-metric-convergence]]). By [[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]] the same
statement holds with $d_2$ replaced by the metric of any norm on
$\mathbb{R}^{n}$, boundedness and convergence both being unchanged by that
replacement ([[def-equivalent-norms]]).

**This is assembled from published theorems and is not proved again by
bisection.** The bisection is in [[thm-heine-borel-rn]], published at order 120;
what is added here is the passage from compactness to sequential compactness and
the reading of the conclusion in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.

**Choice cost: none.** [[thm-heine-borel-rn]] is proved by bisection and uses no
choice principle, and "compact implies sequentially compact" is a theorem of ZF
([[thm-compact-implies-the-other-compactness-forms]]). The five-way equivalence
[[thm-metric-compactness-equivalences]] is **not** used, precisely because it is
stated under countable choice and dependent choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) and
would overcharge this corollary; the arrow-by-arrow account is
[[rem-compactness-choice-ledger-metric]].

Let $S$ be connected and let $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}$ be a finite-rank rational
local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). If
$\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple, then
$\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes k$ is semisimple for every characteristic-zero
field $k$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]). In particular this applies to rational
Gauss-Manin local systems after complex geometric semisimplicity has been
proved. The field $k$ need not embed in $\mathbb C$. Semisimplicity means that
every monodromy-invariant subspace has an invariant complement, equivalently
that the monodromy module is a finite direct sum of simple modules.

derivations.claim: Rational descent of the socle and its lattice. Let $H$ be a nonzero pure geometric object of rank $r$ over the connected base $S$, and let $W_{\mathbb C}$ be the socle of the complex monodromy module $V_{s,\mathbb C}$, a nonzero finite-dimensional complex module by [F2]. By [F2] there is a rational flat subspace $W_{\mathbb Q}\subseteq V_s$ with $W_{\mathbb C}=W_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$; since it is monodromy-invariant it is the fibre at $s$ of a local subsystem of $H$, which we again call $W$. Let $H_{\mathbb Z}$ be the full monodromy-stable integral lattice of [F3] and put $W_{\mathbb Z}=W_{\mathbb Q}\cap H_{\mathbb Z}$; a rational basis of $W_{\mathbb Q}$ becomes integral after clearing denominators, so $W_{\mathbb Z}$ is a full lattice in $W_{\mathbb Q}$, and the monodromy preserves it and acts by invertible integral matrices. On the determinant line $\det W=\bigwedge^{e}W$, $e=\dim_{\mathbb Q}W_{\mathbb Q}$, the monodromy therefore acts by $\pm1$, so $(\det W)^{\otimes2}$ is a constant rank-one local subsystem of the geometric tensor object $\bigwedge^eH\otimes\bigwedge^eH$ of [F3], generated by a global horizontal section.

Torus images of simple summands are flat. Write the complex socle as $W_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_i S_i$ by [F4]. Fix a summand $T$ of dimension $d$ and its flat complement $T'=\bigoplus_{S_i\ne T}S_i$ in $W_{\mathbb C}$, using the chosen summand indices. Put $A=\bigwedge^dH_{\mathbb C}\otimes\bigwedge^{e-d}H_{\mathbb C}$ and $V=\bigwedge^dT\otimes\bigwedge^{e-d}T'\subset A$. The determinant identification for $W=T\oplus T'$ is flat, so step 1.1 makes $V^{\otimes2}\subset A^{\otimes2}$ a constant line. The rational object underlying $A^{\otimes2}$ is geometric by [F3]; its complex invariant part is the complexification of its rational invariant part, because invariants are common kernels of rational matrices, reducible to finitely many linear equations in a finite-dimensional fibre. By [F1] this fixed part is a constant Hodge structure. For any Hodge-torus element $t$, the image $t(V^{\otimes2})=(tV)^{\otimes2}$ is therefore a flat line in that fixed part. In a local flat frame choose a nonzero continuous generator $\sigma$ of $tV$; its squared projective class is constant. The map $[u]\mapsto[u\otimes u]$ is injective: if $u\otimes u$ and $v\otimes v$ are proportional, contraction with a functional nonzero on $u$ shows $v$ is proportional to $u$. Thus $[\sigma]$ is constant and $tV$ is flat. A decomposable tensor line in $E\otimes F$ determines its factor lines by contraction with $F^*$ and $E^*$; applying this to $tV$ shows that $\bigwedge^d(tT)$ is flat. Finally the Plücker line determines $tT$ by $tT=\{v:v\wedge p=0\}$ for any nonzero $p\in\bigwedge^d(tT)$, as is checked by completing a basis of $tT$ to a basis of the ambient space. This identity commutes with transport, so $tT$ is flat for every $t$. The case $e=d$ uses the constant zeroth exterior power and satisfies the same argument.

Openness of irreducibility and torus-stability of the socle. For $t$ near $1$ the flat subspace $tT$ is simple: were there $t_n\to1$ with $t_nT$ reducible, there would be, for each $n$, a proper nonzero flat subspace $U_n\subset t_nT$; their dimensions have finitely many possible values $\varrho$, $1\le\varrho<d$; pass to a subsequence with fixed $\varrho$, then use [F5] to make the orthogonal projections $P_n$ onto $U_n$ converge to a rank-$\varrho$ projection $P$. The inclusions $U_n\subset t_nT$ give $\operatorname{im}P\subset T$. For each monodromy matrix $M$, invariance is the closed matrix equation $(I-P_n)MP_n=0$; taking limits gives $(I-P)MP=0$ for every $M$. No finite generation of the fundamental group is assumed. Thus $U=\operatorname{im}P$ is a nonzero proper flat subspace of $T$, contradicting simplicity of $T$. Hence, for $t$ in a neighbourhood of $1$, each $tS_i$ is a simple flat subspace of $H_{\mathbb C}$, and every simple flat subspace is contained in the socle $W_{\mathbb C}$ by [F2]; summing over the finitely many $S_i$ gives $tW\subseteq W$, hence $tW=W$ by dimension. Thus the stabilizer of $W$ in $\mathbb C^\times$ contains a neighbourhood of the identity; a subgroup of a topological group with nonempty interior is open, and the connected group $\mathbb C^\times$ has no proper nonempty open subgroup, so $tW=W$ for every $t\in\mathbb C^\times$. Consequently $W_s$ is stable under the Hodge torus at every point $s$, so $W_{\mathbb Q}$ is a Hodge substructure of $H$ at every point; since it is already flat, it is a Hodge subvariation.

Polarization splitting and induction. Let $Q$ be a polarization of the pure object $H$. Its restriction to the Hodge subvariation $W$ is nondegenerate: if $v\in W_{s,\mathbb C}$ were a nonzero radical vector, then with the Weil operator $C$ of the Hodge structure the vector $C\bar v$ lies in $W_{s,\mathbb C}$ because $W_s$ is a Hodge substructure, so the positivity of the Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(v,v)=Q(Cv,\bar v)=(-1)^nQ(v,C\bar v)$ would give the contradiction $0=Q(v,C\bar v)\ne0$. Hence the $Q$-orthogonal complement $W^\perp$ is a flat Hodge subvariation and $H=W\oplus W^\perp$; the orthogonal projection onto $W$ is a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism, so $W^\perp$ is a geometric direct summand of $H$ by [F3], of smaller rank unless $W=H$. The submodule $W_{\mathbb C}$ is a direct sum of simples by construction, and by induction over the rank the complex monodromy module of $W^\perp$ is semisimple; a direct sum of semisimple modules is semisimple, so the complex monodromy module of $H$ is semisimple. A non-pure object is a finite direct sum of pure weight pieces, handled one weight at a time, and the rank-zero case is the empty direct sum.

Coefficient fields and the Gauss-Manin case. Complex semisimplicity of the monodromy module of $H$ means exactly that the complex local system $H\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple in the sense of [F4]. By [F6] the rational local system $H$ is then semisimple over $\mathbb Q$ and over every characteristic-zero field, with no embedding of that field into $\mathbb C$ used. For a smooth projective $f:X\to S$, the local systems $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ are geometric and polarizable by [F3], so step 4.1 and [F6] apply to give their semisimplicity over $\mathbb Q$ and over every characteristic-zero field. This proves both asserted clauses; the algebraic realization and the integral lattice were used exactly in steps 1.1 and 2.1, and no statement is made about an arbitrary polarized analytic variation on a punctured disk.

derivations.claim: Geometric structure and the local system. The graph $\{(t,[u:v])\in\mathbb C^\times\times\mathbb P^1:u^r=tv^r\}$ is closed, and $z\mapsto(z^r,[z:1])$ identifies $\mathbb C^\times$ with it over $\mathbb C^\times$, so $f$ is projective and proper and its fibres are the $r$ distinct $r$-th roots of the base point. On coordinate rings $f$ is module-finite, the source ring being generated over the target ring by $1,z,\dots,z^{r-1}$; and it is smooth of relative dimension zero because the derivative $rz^{r-1}$ is a unit on $\mathbb C^\times$, so the Jacobian criterion [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]] applies and the relative dimension is $1-1=0$, which is exactly étaleness by the definition [[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]. Thus $f$ is finite étale. Therefore $R^0f_*\mathbb Q$ is a finite-rank local system of rank $r$ in the sense of [[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]: over each base point the fibre is $H^0$ of $r$ reduced points, with the sheet-indicator functions as a rational basis, and these bases are transported by the deck identifications of the fibres. Every indicator function is locally constant of Hodge type $(0,0)$, so the local system is pure of weight zero. The standard positive definite dot product in the indicator basis is rational, flat because transport permutes the basis vectors and hence preserves the form, and positive on every fibre; it is therefore the polarization required for a geometric polarizable weight-zero variation, whose algebraic realization is $f$ itself on the open $U=\mathbb C^\times$. [given, construct, algebra]

Monodromy and semisimplicity. The homotopy $z\mapsto((1-u)+u|t_0|/|z|)z$ gives a deformation retraction of $\mathbb C^\times$ to the circle of radius $|t_0|$, fixing $t_0$ throughout. Multiplication $w\mapsto t_0w$ identifies that circle, based at $t_0$, with the geometric unit circle, based at $1$. Hence [[cor-geometric-unit-circle-has-fundamental-group-z]] makes $\gamma(t)=e^{2\pi it}t_0$ a positive generator at $t_0$. Label the roots by $z_a=\zeta^az_0$ and their indicator functions by $e_a$, where $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/r}$ has order $r$ by [[thm-complex-nth-roots-and-roots-of-unity]]. The lifted loop $t\mapsto e^{2\pi it/r}z_a$ ends at $z_{a+1}$. Covariant cohomology transport is the inverse pullback, so $T_\gamma e_a=e_{a+1}$. The left monodromy convention of [[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]] uses $\rho(\gamma)=T_{\bar\gamma}$, hence $\rho(\gamma)e_a=e_{a-1}$. Therefore $v_j=\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}\zeta^{ja}e_a$ satisfies $\rho(\gamma)v_j=\zeta^jv_j$. These vectors form a basis: the geometric-sum identity $\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}\zeta^{ka}=0$ for $r\nmid k$ and $r$ otherwise gives the inverse Fourier matrix $r^{-1}(\zeta^{-ja})$. Thus the complexification is a direct sum of the $r$ distinct one-dimensional characters, including the trivial character when $r=1$, and is semisimple. Finally [[thm-smooth-projective-gauss-manin-local-systems-are-semisimple]] applies to this smooth projective morphism and proves semisimplicity over every characteristic-zero coefficient field, including fields without the $r$-th roots of unity. [step 1.1, given, construct, algebra] ∎

citations.quote: For a projective morphism $f:X\to Y$ of classical varieties, the set $E_r=\{y\in Y:\dim X_y\ge r\}$ is closed for every integer $r$.

For an irreducible classical variety $X$ and morphism $f:X\to Y$, the reduced closure $Z=\overline{f(X)}$ is irreducible and $\dim X=\dim Z+r$, where $r$ is the common dimension of the nonempty fibres on a nonempty open of $Z$.
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Let $X\subseteq\mathbf P_k^N$ be irreducible of dimension $d\ge1$.

A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of classical varieties is projective here if there is an integer $N\ge0$ and a factorization $X\hookrightarrow Y\times\mathbf P_k^N\to Y$ in which the first map is a closed immersion and the second is projection.
For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of classical varieties and a closed point $y\in Y$, let $X_y=f^{-1}(y)$ have its reduced closed-subvariety structure.
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

derivations.claim: The universal incidence $\mathcal X=\{(x,H):x\in X\cap H\}\subseteq X\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ is a projective-space bundle of relative dimension $d-1$ over $X$: at each $x$ the hyperplanes containing $x$ are the linear forms vanishing at $x$, a rank-$d$ subbundle of the rank-$(d+1)$ bundle of linear forms, so the fibres are projective spaces of dimension $d-1$. Hence $\mathcal X$ is smooth, irreducible and of dimension $n+d-1$, and the fibre of $g$ at $(y,H)$ is $f^{-1}(y)\cap H$. A nonempty hyperplane cut of a projective variety of dimension $i+1$ has dimension $i$ unless the hyperplane contains a top-dimensional component, in which case its dimension is $i+1$; this is exactly [F4] applied component by component, taking the zero-dimensional components to be either contained in $H$ or disjoint from it.

Partition the universal locus of fibre dimension $i$ into $A_i=\{(y,H):y\in Y_i,\ \dim(f^{-1}(y)\cap H)=i\}$ and $B_i=\{(y,H):y\in Y_{i+1},\ \dim(f^{-1}(y)\cap H)=i\}$; both are constructible by [F1]. For fixed $y\in Y_i$ the fibre of $A_i$ over $y$ consists of the hyperplanes containing at least one of the finitely many top-dimensional components of $f^{-1}(y)$. Such a component spans a projective linear subspace of dimension at least $i$, so the hyperplanes containing it form a projective subspace of the dual of dimension at most $d-i-1$; hence every fibre of $A_i\to Y_i$ has dimension at most $d-i-1$, and [F2] applied to the finitely many components of $\overline{A_i}$ gives $\dim A_i\le\dim Y_i+d-i-1$. The projection $B_i\to Y_{i+1}$ has fibres of dimension at most $d$ because the hyperplane parameter is free, so $\dim B_i\le\dim Y_{i+1}+d$. Subtracting the source dimension $n+d-1$ of $g$ from twice the fibre dimension plus these parameter dimensions gives contributions at most $r(f)-i$ for $A_i$ and at most $r(f)-1$ for $B_i$; for $i=0$ the $A_0$ contribution is $\dim Y_0-n\le0$ because $\dim Y_0\le\dim\overline{f(X)}\le n$ by [F2].

If $r(f)>0$, both bounds in step 2.1 are at most $r(f)-1$, including the separately treated $i=0$ case, so $r(g)\le r(f)-1$. If $r(f)=0$, the bounds are strictly negative for every $i>0$; for $i=0$ the contribution is zero, attained because $r(f)=0$ forces generic fibre dimension zero by [F2], so $g$ is generically finite on its image and has defect zero, while the strict bounds for positive fibre dimension prove smallness.

For the fixed-hyperplane claim, project each of the finitely many locally closed components of the $A_i$ and $B_i$ to $(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$; a component whose image is not dense is absent from a general parameter fibre, and for a component with dense image [F2] bounds its general parameter fibre dimension by its dimension minus $d$. Intersecting the finitely many resulting nonempty parameter opens with the smooth-section open of [F3] gives a nonempty Zariski open; on it the same estimates as step 2.1 hold with $\dim A_i-d$, $\dim B_i-d$ and source dimension $n-1$ for $X_H$, so the identical arithmetic gives the fixed-hyperplane conclusions, For iteration, a smooth nonempty hyperplane section is pure of dimension one less by [F4], but need not be irreducible. The estimates of steps 1.1 and 2.1 apply unchanged to a smooth pure-dimensional finite union: all incidence components have the same source dimension, and [F2] is applied componentwise throughout. The defect is nonnegative, since on any irreducible component of dimension $m$ with generic fibre dimension $j$ its image has dimension $m-j$, so the corresponding full fibre locus contributes at least $j\ge0$. Thus the positive-defect inequality applies at every successive smooth nonempty section, without an irreducibility assumption on those sections. Transversality of a prescribed finite algebraic Whitney stratification is the separately supplied condition named in the Statement, not a consequence of ordinary Bertini alone.

derivations.claim: For a smooth stratum $S$ of complex dimension $s$, its algebraic conormal bundle $C_S\subset T^*\mathbb C^N$ has complex dimension $N$: on a Jacobian chart the independent differentials of local equations span the conormal fibres, of rank $N-s$, giving a locally trivial algebraic bundle. On each irreducible component the closure of $C_S$ has dimension $N$ and its boundary has dimension at most $N-1$, since a proper closed subset of an irreducible variety of dimension $N$ has dimension at most $N-1$. Let $D$ be the finite union of these conormal boundaries. If a covector $\lambda$ kills a limiting tangent plane $Q=\lim T_{p_m}S$ at a point outside $S$, then $\lambda$ lies in that boundary: the orthogonal projections of $\lambda$ onto the annihilators of $T_{p_m}S$ are conormal covectors at the points $p_m$ and converge to the projection of $\lambda$ onto $Q^\perp$, which is $\lambda$ because $\lambda$ kills $Q$. Thus every bad limiting-tangent covector lies in the complex algebraic set $D$ of complex dimension at most $N-1$.

Consider the real critical incidence $I_S=\{(a,z):z\in S,\ d(\phi_a|S)_z=0\}$. Differentiation in $a$ surjects onto $T_z^*S$, since every real covector on $T_zS$ extends to one on the ambient Euclidean space; concretely $I_S$ is the real normal bundle via $(z,v)\mapsto(a=z+v,z)$ with $v\perp T_zS$, and the smooth Gram-matrix charts of that normal bundle exhibit it as a smooth real manifold of dimension $2s+(2N-2s)=2N$. In local stratum coordinates its tangent equation is $H_zv+B_z\delta a=0$, where $H_z$ is the Hessian of $\phi_a|S$ and $B_z$ is the surjective parameter derivative. The differential of $(a,z)\mapsto a$ from $I_S$ to $\mathbb C^N$ has kernel $\{(0,v):H_zv=0\}$; since source and target have equal real dimension, it is surjective exactly where $H_z$ is invertible. Hence [F1] makes the parameters with a degenerate stratum critical point null, and a finite union over the strata preserves nullity.

Identify real ambient covectors with complex covectors by $\lambda\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\lambda$. The map $(a,z)\mapsto(z,d\phi_a(z))$ from $\mathbb C^N\times\mathbb C^N$ to the real cotangent bundle is a real smooth diffeomorphism, because $d\phi_a(z)$ is twice the real covector corresponding to $\overline{z-a}$. Therefore the inverse image of each smooth algebraic stratum of $D$ has real dimension at most $2N-2$, and its projection to the $a$-coordinate is a smooth map whose source dimension is smaller than its target dimension $2N$, so every point is critical and [F1] makes the image null; a finite algebraic stratification of $D$ is obtained by successively taking each component's smooth locus and its lower-dimensional singular complement, which terminates because the dimension strictly decreases, and the finite union of the null images is null. Outside this null set, $d\phi_a$ kills no forbidden limiting tangent space.

Finiteness of the critical set uses algebraic geometry rather than a finiteness claim for real analytic sets. Complexify the squared distance to $F_{u,v}(z,w)=\sum_{k=1}^N(z_k-u_k)(w_k-v_k)$ on $S\times\overline S$, where $\overline S$ is obtained by conjugating the equations of $S$. Its complex critical incidence over the parameter space $\mathbb C^N\times\mathbb C^N$ is the algebraic incidence cut out by the two conormal conditions $w-v\perp T_zS$ and $z-u\perp T_w\overline S$; it is isomorphic to the algebraic conormal bundle of $S\times\overline S$, of complex dimension $2N$, equal to the parameter dimension, because the two gradient coefficients $w-v$ and $z-u$ are exactly the conormal vectors that uniquely determine $(u,v)$ for given $(z,w)$. If an irreducible component projects dominantly, [F2] gives a nonempty open of parameters over which its fibres are zero-dimensional and hence finite by [F2]; if not, one avoids its proper closed image closure. The set of parameters $a$ with $(a,\bar a)$ in this nonempty complex Zariski open is Euclidean open and dense. Indeed, a nonzero polynomial vanishing on its proper algebraic complement restricts to a nonzero polynomial in the real coordinates $(x,y)$ under the invertible substitution $(a,\bar a)=(x+iy,x-iy)$; such a polynomial cannot vanish on any nonempty real open box. Thus the inverse image of the complement has empty interior. This inverse image involves complex conjugation, so no complex Zariski openness of the good real-parameter set is asserted. Therefore the prescribed nonempty real open subset meets it in a nonempty real open set, which cannot be contained in the null exceptional sets of steps 1.2 and 2.1; choose such a real parameter $a$. Its real stratum critical points lie in the finite complex fibre over $(a,\bar a)$ just constructed: at $(z,\bar z)$ the real diagonal tangent vectors $(t,\bar t)$ span $T_zS\times T_{\bar z}\overline S$ over $\mathbb C$, and the complex differential of $F$ on them is the real differential of $\phi_a$, so vanishing on the real form implies vanishing on the whole complex tangent.

Choose such an $a$. The Euclidean square distance is bounded below and proper on the closed subset $Z$, and its ambient Levi form is the positive definite Euclidean Hermitian form, so its restriction to every positive-dimensional complex stratum is strongly plurisubharmonic and the sublevel sets exhaust $Z$; on the singular variety the strong plurisubharmonicity statement is the stated inline verification for the concrete function $\|z-a\|^2$, whose ambient complex Hessian is the identity. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 give exactly the nondegeneracy, limiting-tangent and finiteness conclusions: on a zero-dimensional stratum the Hessian condition is vacuous because its tangent space is zero, and the ambient differential condition there is the step 2.1 exclusion, while the stratum contributes only its finitely many points, and the empty variety has no critical points. smooth ambient manifold, and let $f:W\to B$ be the restriction of a smooth
ambient map that is a submersion on every stratum. Every smooth base field
admits, after tube shrinking, a stratumwise smooth locally bounded controlled
lift. Its stratumwise ODE solutions form a jointly continuous
stratum-preserving local flow with jointly continuous inverse. Each source
point has a stratum-preserving product neighborhood over a small coordinate box
in $B$. If $f$ is proper, every base point has a whole-fiber
stratum-preserving bundle trivialization. No global simplicial model of $f$ is

Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a
classical variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its
analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite
smooth algebraic frontier stratifications
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,

all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. derivations.claim: If $P$ is in the upper perverse aisle, a support of $\mathcal H^{q+d}(P)$ has dimension at most $-(q+d)$. Its inverse image under a smooth relative-$d$ map has dimension at most $-(q+d)+d=-q$. Since ordinary pullback is exact for field-module sheaves, this is exactly the support condition for $a^*P[d]$, so $a^*[d]$ preserves the upper aisle. Its relative disk bundle is complex oriented, so the smooth exceptional pullback formula in [F2] gives $a^!=a^*[2d]$. Then $D(a^*P[d])=a^!DP[-d]=a^*DP[d]$, so the upper-aisle calculation for $DP$ also proves preservation of the lower aisle.

Suppose $P$ is in the upper perverse aisle and constructible for $\mathfrak S$. The nonzero stalk loci of its cohomology sheaves are unions of strata, each of dimension bounded by the corresponding support dimension. For a transverse embedding $i$, a stratum $S$ of dimension $s$ meets $Z$ either trivially or in dimension $s-c$, so the support of $\mathcal H^{q-c}(P)$ meets $Z$ in dimension at most $-(q-c)-c=-q$; this is the upper perverse condition for $i^*P[-c]$. The exact shift uses transversality on every stratum supporting that cohomology sheaf.

In a local controlled product $W\times D^{2c}$ from [F1], shrink $W$ to a finite conical local model of its induced stratification and triangulate it compatibly by [F3]; the disk also has a finite deleted-boundary model. The pullback of $P$ to this product has bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each simplex times the disk. Such a piece is contractible, so its cohomology sheaves are constant by local-system transport along paths and contracting homotopies. Apply [F3] with base a point and this contractible product as fiber: pullback from the point is fully faithful, and its essential image is closed under finite extensions because connecting morphisms lift. Ordinary truncation triangles therefore show that the complex on each piece is pulled back from a finite coefficient complex. Filter $W$ by closed skeleta. Pullback along $\operatorname{pr}:W\times D^{2c}\to W$ commutes with open extension by zero and closed pushforward: their natural comparisons are isomorphisms on stalks, including zero stalks off the relevant product subsets. On each skeleton [F3] makes this pullback fully faithful; lifting the connecting morphisms in the open/closed triangles and taking their cones proves inductively that $P|_{W\times D^{2c}}\cong\operatorname{pr}^*B$, with $B$ its zero-slice restriction. Support localization [F2], computed in the finite product models [F3], now identifies its exceptional zero-slice restriction with $B\otimes_k C^*(D^{2c},D^{2c}\setminus\{0\};k)$. The relative normal complex has its sole cohomology $k$ in degree $2c$, with the complex-oriented generator, giving $i^!P\cong i^*P[-2c]$. For $c=0$ this is the identity calculation. These are the natural support comparisons with the oriented normal class; transitions preserve the orientation of the complex normal bundle, so they agree on overlaps and glue.

Verdier duality preserves constructibility for $\mathfrak S$, by the stratumwise finite conical coefficient models in [F3] and duality in [F2]. Dualizing gives $D(i^*P[-c])=i^!DP[c]=i^*DP[-c]$; apply step 1.2 to $DP$ and use [F2] to obtain lower perverse exactness on that subcategory. Together with steps 1.1 and 1.3 this proves both exactness assertions and both oriented exceptional-pullback formulas, including the cases of relative dimension or codimension zero.

derivations.claim: Let $U$ be smooth irreducible affine of dimension $i\ge1$ and let $L$ be a nonzero finite-rank local system. By [F3] choose $i$ functions with finite nonempty common zero set $S$. Local complex orientation and local constancy identify $H_S^{2i}(U,L)$ with $\bigoplus_{s\in S}L_s$, which is nonzero, while [F1] gives $H^{2i}(U,L)=0$. The support long exact sequence therefore gives $H^{2i-1}(U\setminus S,L)\ne0$. Cover $U\setminus S$ by the $i$ principal opens $D(f_j)$. Every finite intersection is affine, so [F1] bounds its ordinary cohomology by $i$; the Čech index is at most $i-1$. In total degree $2i-1$ only the term $H^i(D(f_1\cdots f_i),L)$ can contribute, and nonvanishing of the total group forces it to be nonzero. For $i=0$ the detector is simply the nonzero stalk on an isolated point.

The forward direction of the affine-open characterization is [F1], applied to each restriction. Conversely suppose all positive $H^q(V,K)$ vanish. Write $U_i=Y\setminus F_{i-1}$ and argue downwards in $i$ that the stalk degrees on $U_i$ obey the upper perverse support bound. Suppose the assertion is established on all larger-dimensional layers. On $U_i$ let $A=\tau_{\le-i}K$ and $Q=\tau_{>-i}K$. On higher-dimensional layers the induction hypothesis already gives the upper perverse stalk bound, preserved by ordinary truncation; on $W_i$ truncation makes the degree at most $-i$. These are exactly the upper perverse bounds for $A$ on $U_i$, without any claim that $U_i$ has dimension $i$. Thus on each affine $V\subset U_i$, [F1] and the triangle $A\to K\to Q$ give $H^q(V,Q)=0$ for $q>0$. All ordinary cohomology sheaves of $Q$ are supported on the closed smooth layer $W_i\subset U_i$ and are local systems there.

If $Q$ is nonzero, let $b>-i$ be its largest nonzero cohomological degree and let $L=\mathcal H^b(Q)|_{W_i}$ be nonzero on a connected component. The finitely many smooth irreducible components of $W_i$ are disjoint and closed in $U_i$; remove the components where $L$ is zero and all but one nonzero component, and choose an affine open $V_0\subset U_i$ in the resulting open, meeting the retained component. Then $V_0\cap W_i$ is smooth affine and $L$ is a nonzero local system on it. Step 1.1 supplies a principal open of it with nonzero $H^i(L)$. Since $W_i\cap V_0$ is closed in the affine $V_0$, the defining function lifts from its coordinate-ring quotient to a function on $V_0$; localizing the latter gives an affine $V\subset U_i$ with $H^i(V\cap W_i,L)\ne0$. The closed embedding $e:V\cap W_i\hookrightarrow V$ has exact pushforward, and $Q|_V=e_*e^*Q|_V$ because all its cohomology is supported there. Thus $H^a(V,\mathcal H^t(Q))=H^a(V\cap W_i,\mathcal H^t(Q)|_{W_i})$. In the bounded spectral sequence $H^a(V\cap W_i,\mathcal H^t(Q)|_{W_i})\Rightarrow H^{a+t}(V,Q)$, [F1] gives $a\le i$ and maximality of $b$ gives $t\le b$. The nonzero term $(i,b)$ has no incoming differential, since those would start at a larger $t$, and no outgoing differential, since those would end at a larger $a$. It is the sole term in its total degree $i+b>0$, contradicting step 1.2. Hence $Q=0$, completing the descending dimension induction and the converse.

Let $P\in{}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$. For every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ its inverse image under the affine morphism $u$ is affine, and derived composition with [F1] gives $H^q(V,Ru_*P)=H^q(u^{-1}V,P)=0$ for $q>0$; the characterization proved in step 2.1 therefore puts $Ru_*P$ in the upper perverse aisle. For $P$ in the lower aisle, apply this to $DP$ and dualize by [F2] to obtain the claimed lower-aisle preservation by $Ru_!$. All zero and empty cases follow from the same zero triangles.

On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle over a
paracompact Hausdorff CW complex, with $n\geq1$. Let $P(E)$, $\gamma_E$,
and $x=e((\gamma_E)_{\mathbb R})$ have the conventions of
[[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]].
For each $b\in B$, choose a complex-linear identification $E_b\cong\mathbb C^n$
and denote the resulting fiber inclusion by
$j_b:\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}\to P(E)$.

With the complex orientation on both tautological lines,
$j_b^*x=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})=:x_{\mathrm{taut}}$. For $n\geq2$ this is a
generator of $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^{n-1};\mathbb Z)$, and
$1,j_b^*x,\ldots,(j_b^*x)^{n-1}$ is an integral cohomology basis. Its
coefficient reductions are a basis over every prime field $\mathbb F_p$.
For $n=1$ the fiber is a point, $j_b^*x=0$, and the basis is $1$.
A comparison with a generator given the opposite normalization introduces
one fixed sign; with the tautological Euler normalization above the sign is
$+1$, independently of $b$ and the chosen complex-linear identification.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex
algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed
algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex
algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$
respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps
surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic
stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth
complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper
in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic
morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is
proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is
asserted proper.

derivations.claim: By [F2], $p'{}^*K[d]$ is perverse and $i^*[-1]$ is perverse-exact on these product strata, so $M=i^*p'{}^*K[d-1]$ is perverse. Let $j:X'\setminus\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ and $u=(f\times1)j$. Over an affine chart of the hyperplane parameter space the complement of the incidence in $\mathbb P^d$ is an affine $d$-space bundle, and $X'\setminus\mathcal X$ is closed in the corresponding bundle over $Y'$; thus $u$ is affine. Apply $R(f\times1)_!$ to the localization triangle $j_!j^*p'^*K[d]\to p'^*K[d]\to i_*i^*p'^*K[d]\to$. By [F1] the first term lies in the perverse lower aisle, so it has no negative perverse cohomology; by proper base change and [F2] the second is $p^*Rf_*K[d]$ and the third is $Rg_*M[1]$. The long exact perverse sequence gives the restriction isomorphisms and the monomorphism. Dualizing the whole construction and using $Di_*=i_!D$, $i^!K'=i^*K'[-2]$ from [F2] gives the Gysin isomorphisms and the epimorphism for $l=1$.

The projective-space cohomology formula gives $Rp_*p^*T=\bigoplus_{a=0}^dT[-2a]$ for every constructible complex $T$, and the identical formula with $d-1$ holds for $p'i:\mathcal X\to X$. To justify the formula as a morphism and not only stalk ranks, cup powers of the tautological Euler class pulled back from $(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ define the map from the direct sum, and on every fibre its map is the usual projective-space cohomology basis, hence an isomorphism by proper base change; the integral power basis is [[lem-complex-tautological-euler-class-restricts-to-the-projective-fiber-generator]], and tensoring the finite cellular cochain complex with $k$ preserves the basis by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]. For heart objects $A,B$, adjunction therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(p^*A[d],p^*B[d])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)$: all terms $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[-2a])$ for $a>0$ vanish by [F3].

Write $F=p^*[d]$. For the product projection $p$, the normal slices to $S\times\mathbb P^d$ are precisely the normal slices to $S$. Thus the stalk and costalk boundary conditions characterizing intermediate extension in [F3] are preserved: on a boundary stratum of dimension $s$ their strict bounds $q<-s$ and $q>-s$ become $q<-(s+d)$ and $q>-(s+d)$ after the shift $[d]$. On the dense open, pullback is the shifted pulled-back local system. The no-boundary characterization in [F3] therefore shows that $F$ takes $\operatorname{IC}_S(L)$ to $\operatorname{IC}_{S\times\mathbb P^d}(p^*L)$, with both intersection complexes normalized by their respective support dimensions. The local system $p^*L$ remains irreducible: a sub-local-system restricts along the section $y\mapsto(y,H_0)$ to a sub-local-system of $L$, hence to zero or all of $L$. Its rank is constant on each connected projective-space fibre (any two points lie on a projective line), so those two alternatives give zero or all of $p^*L$ on the whole product. Hence $F$ is exact, fully faithful by step 1.2, and preserves simples. Every composition factor of $F(A)$ is therefore a pulled-back simple; for a subobject $B\subseteq F(A)$ choose a simple $F(S)\subseteq B$, lift its inclusion to $S\subseteq A$ by full faithfulness, and induct on $B/F(S)\subseteq F(A/S)$. The lifted inclusion of the resulting base object into $A/S$ has a preimage in $A$, whose exact image under $F$ is $B$. This proves the image of $F$ is closed under subobjects and quotients. The derived right adjoint $Rp_*[-d]$ preserves the lower aisle: for $E\in{}^pD^{\ge0}$ and $B\in{}^pD^{\le-1}$, adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(B,Rp_*E[-d])=\operatorname{Hom}(F(B),E)=0$. Thus $Rp_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge q}$ into ${}^pD^{\ge q-d}$. Its heart right adjoint is $r={}^pH^{-d}Rp_*$, since the positive-degree truncation of $Rp_*C[-d]$ has no Hom from a heart object. The analogous left adjoint is $\ell={}^pH^dRp_!$, using $p^!=p^*[2d]$. Full faithfulness gives $rF=1$. The kernel of the counit $Fr(C)\to C$ lies in the image of $F$ by subobject closure, and applying the left-exact $r$ shows that kernel is zero, by the adjunction identity $r(\varepsilon_C)=1$. Every subobject $F(B)\hookrightarrow C$ factors through this counit by adjunction. Consequently $Fr(C)$ is exactly the largest subobject coming from $Y$; duality gives the largest quotient $F\ell(C)$.

Put $T=Rf_*K$, $V=R(f\times1)_*p'^*K$ and $U=Rg_*i^*p'^*K$. The graph of $(f,X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d)$ is a closed embedding $a:X\hookrightarrow Y\times\mathbb P^d$ and $f=q a$, where $q$ is the projection. Closed pushforward is perverse-exact directly from the two stratum inequalities in [F3]: on strata inside the image its stalks and costalks are those of $K$, and on the complement they vanish. Applying the lower-aisle calculation of step 2.1 to $q$ therefore gives $T=Rq_*a_*K\in{}^pD^{\ge-d}$. Under the cup-power bases of step 1.2, the map $Rp_*V\to Rp_*U$ is a matrix $(1,\beta):\bigoplus_{a=0}^{d-1}T[-2a]\oplus T[-2d]\to\bigoplus_{a=0}^{d-1}T[-2a]$: restriction carries each of the first $d$ parameter-class powers to the identical power on the incidence bundle, while the last power may be a linear combination involving base classes. Changing coordinates by $(x,z)\mapsto(x+\beta z,z)$ identifies this map with projection. Its discarded summand $T[-2d]$ lies in ${}^pD^{\ge d}$, so the map induces isomorphisms in every perverse degree below $d$, including degrees $-1$ and $0$ for all $d\ge1$. This uses no decomposition of $T$ into its perverse cohomology.

Set $n=d-1$. Step 1.1 gives an isomorphism $L={}^p\tau_{<n}V\simeq{}^p\tau_{<n}U$ and a monomorphism $\iota:{}^pH^nV\hookrightarrow{}^pH^nU$. Apply $Rp_*$ to the two triangles $L\to V\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}V\to$ and $L\to U\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}U\to$. Their five-term exact sequences are ${}^pH^{-1}Rp_*L\to{}^pH^{-1}Rp_*V\to{}^pH^{-1}Rp_*{}^p\tau_{\ge n}V\to{}^pH^0Rp_*L\to{}^pH^0Rp_*V$ and the same sequence for $U$. The first and fourth vertical maps are identities, and the second and fifth are isomorphisms by step 3.1; the five lemma proves that the middle map is an isomorphism. For either $W=V$ or $W=U$, the triangle $({}^pH^nW)[-n]\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}W\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n+1}W\to$ has last term whose $Rp_*$ lies in ${}^pD^{\ge n+1-d}={}^pD^{\ge0}$, by step 2.1. Its perverse cohomology in degrees $-2$ and $-1$ vanishes. The resulting exact sequence gives, naturally in $W$, ${}^pH^{-1}(Rp_*{}^p\tau_{\ge n}W)\simeq{}^pH^{-1-n}(Rp_*{}^pH^nW)=r({}^pH^nW)$, since $-1-n=-d$. Thus $r(\iota)$ is an isomorphism. Proper base change and exact $F$ give ${}^pH^nV=F({}^pH^{-1}T)$, so its right adjoint is ${}^pH^{-1}T$. Adjunction factors $\iota$ as the counit $Fr({}^pH^nU)\to{}^pH^nU$ preceded by the isomorphism $F(r(\iota))$. By step 2.1 its image is exactly the largest pullback subobject of ${}^pH^nU={}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$. Apply this result to $DK$ and dualize using [F2] and [F3]; the middle object is dualized, perverse degrees change sign, and largest subobject becomes largest quotient $F({}^pH^1T)$. This proves every assertion.

boundaries.evidence: If X is empty, K and M are zero; all localization and truncation triangles and both maximal pullback objects are zero by steps 1.1–4.1.
For K=0 the localization, pushforward and truncation triangles in steps1.1 and4.1 are zero and the largest subobject and quotient are zero
The codimension-one incidence is the case used throughout, with transversality supplied by fact F2 in step 1.1.
For d=1 incidence fibers over X are points and the discarded T[-2] is in perverse degrees at least1 by step3.1, so both truncation comparisons of step4.1 still apply
The degree endpoints l=-1 and l=1 are the monomorphism and epimorphism clauses of step 1.1.
AC is inherited through the affine-exactness and noncharacteristic suppliers as stated and used in step 1.1.

boundaries.reason: The statement is an identification of maps and largest subobjects, not a biconditional.
Only the displayed identifications and largest-subobject statements are asserted, not their converses.

risk_review.notes: Checked all five steps, all nine exact supplier interfaces and the raw-hash-bound reader diff. Old 2.1 applied an extra [d] to an already support-dimension-normalized product IC; for d>=1 a nonzero shifted heart object cannot remain perverse. Current F=p^*[d] sends IC_S(L) to the normalized IC on S times P^d with no extra shift. The section and connected fibres prove irreducibility without a fundamental-group premise; the finite-length subobject proof explicitly takes the base preimage of the lifted quotient inclusion. F is exact and fully faithful by cup-power projective-bundle comparison and negative heart Hom. Its heart adjoints r=pH^{-d}Rp_* and ell=pH^dRp_! give the largest subobject/quotient by subquotient closure and the counit kernel argument. Incidence transversality and affine complement localization give M perverse and relative weak Lefschetz at l<=-2/-1, with dual Gysin at l>=2/1. Factoring f through the closed graph and relative-d smooth projection gives T=Rf_*K in pD^{>=-d}. The cup-power restriction matrix (1,beta) is conjugate to projection, with discarded T[-2d] in pD^{>=d}, hence isomorphisms in pushforward degrees -1 and 0 even for d=1. The two five-term truncation sequences then give r(iota) an isomorphism: n=d-1, the upper tail pushes into pD^{>=0}, and -1-n=-d. Adjunction identifies iota with the maximal-subobject counit; duality gives the maximal quotient. Empty X and K=0, d=1, endpoint degrees, arbitrary fields and inherited AC were checked. Recomputed the support-normalized IC and both truncation indices independently, including the contrary-sign exceptional-pullback typo in the DCM display. Reader and empty refuter evidence are consistent with the local deduction; no decomposition or arithmetic-purity premise is used.

citations.quote: Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.

Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every closed immersion of schemes is finite, hence
proper; the empty closed immersion is included, no Noetherian, reducedness or
nonemptiness hypothesis is used, and the Axiom of Choice enters through the
affine quotient structure of closed immersions and the properness of finite
morphisms.

Assume AC.  Every $R$-oriented rank-$n$ numerable vector bundle over a CW
complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type, has a unique
normalized Thom class $u_\xi$, and
$$a\longmapsto\pi^*a\smile u_\xi:H^k(B;R)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$$
for every $k$.  Without a supplied orientation, the canonical twisted form is
$$H^k(B;\mathcal O_R(\xi))\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R).$$
The finite supplied-trivializing-cover theorem is a choice-free special case.

Assume AC.  For ordered oriented bundles $\xi\to B$ and $\eta\to C$ of ranks
$n,m$, the canonical product-pair identification gives
$$u_{\xi\times\eta}=u_\xi\times u_\eta.$$
For bundles over one base, diagonal pullback gives
$$u_{\xi\oplus\eta}=u_\xi\smile u_\eta.$$
Interchanging the ordered summands changes the orientation and the displayed
class by the Koszul sign $(-1)^{nm}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly as in the general Thom theorem, and let
$\xi\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real rank-$n$ vector bundle over a
base in the scope of that theorem. Let $u_\xi\in H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$ be its
normalized Thom class, let
$$j^*:H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)\longrightarrow H^n(D(\xi);R)$$ be the relative-to-absolute map of the pair sequence, and let $s:B\to D(\xi)$ be the zero section. The **Euler class** of $\xi$ is $$e(\xi)=e_{\rm Th}(\xi):=s^*j^*(u_\xi)\in H^n(B;R).$$
This is the class already introduced in
[[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]]: on this page we write
$e(\xi)$ for it, and the shorthand $s^*u_\xi$ always means the composite
$s^*j^*(u_\xi)$, the relative-to-absolute map being understood. For rank zero
with supplied orientation $o\in H^0(B;R)$, normalization gives $u_\xi=o$ and
$j$ and $s$ are identities, so
$$e(0_B,o)=o\in H^0(B;R).$$
In particular, the standard unit orientation gives $e(0_B,1)=1$.
For $R=\mathbb F_2$ every real bundle is canonically $\mathbb F_2$-oriented by
[[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]], so in that
case $e_2(\xi):=e(\xi)\in H^n(B;\mathbb F_2)$ is defined for every real
bundle in the Thom scope; for $R=\mathbb Z$ the class depends on the chosen
integral orientation, and reversing the orientation negates it.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Purity and the supported Thom morphism. Put $Y=M\times M$. By [F1] and [F2], $\Delta^!k_Y=\Delta^!\omega_Y[-4d]=\omega_M[-4d]=k_M[-2d]$. The positive orientation identifies the identity of $k_M[-2d]$ with the Thom class in $H^{2d}_{\Delta(M)}(Y;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_M,\Delta^!k_Y[2d])$. Its adjoint is the purity counit $g_\Delta:\Delta_*k_M[-2d]\to k_Y$, equivalently $\Delta_*k_M\to k_Y[2d]$. In a complex normal ball this is the positive generator of the relative disk pair; complex chart transitions preserve that generator. This fixes a global supported morphism through the orientation isomorphism and its counit, rather than inferring equality of arbitrary global maps from their restrictions to balls.

Pullback and cap product on arbitrary supports. Put $S=A\times B$. Proper base change along $F=(q,u)$ identifies $F^*\Delta_*k_M[-2d]$ with $\theta_*k_T[-2d]$, so $F^*g_\Delta$ gives $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d]\to k_S$. For a dualizing class $c:k_S\to\omega_S[-n]$, compose $c\circ g_F$ and use $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ and $\theta^!\omega_S=\omega_T$. The resulting map $k_T\to\omega_T[2d-n]$ is a Borel–Moore class of degree $n-2d$ on $T$. This defines the supported cap operation even if $T$ is singular or has excess dimension; no purity of $\theta$ is asserted. The external product uses $\omega_A\boxtimes\omega_B=\omega_S$: on the supplied finite local product cochain models, compact-support cochains tensor, and their finite-dimensional duals tensor as well, giving this canonical comparison and its restriction compatibility.

Comparison with the exchange mate. For a constructible $C$ on $M$, the mate is the adjoint of $b_!a^*q^!C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^{-1}}u^*q_!q^!C\xrightarrow{u^*\epsilon_q}u^*C$, where the arbitrary-map proper-support exchange of [F1] supplies $\mathrm{BC}:u^*q_!\xrightarrow{\sim}b_!a^*$ and $\epsilon_q$ is the exceptional counit. To identify its dualizing evaluation with step 2.1, factor $q$ as its graph $\Gamma_q:A\hookrightarrow A\times M$ followed by the second projection. The graph is the pullback of $\Delta$ along $(q,\operatorname{id}_M):A\times M\to M\times M$; its supported orientation map is that pullback of $g_\Delta$. Base change of the graph along $\operatorname{id}_A\times u$ is exactly $\theta$, so its supported orientation map after this second pullback is $g_F$. For the product projection, tensor–Hom evaluation with the relative dualizing factor $\omega_A$ computes the counit; this is the finite product cochain evaluation of step 2.1. Composing the graph counit and that evaluation gives $\epsilon_q$ by the composition-of-counits identity in [F1]. Cartesian pasting therefore makes its base-changed composite exactly $u^*\epsilon_q\circ\mathrm{BC}^{-1}$ above. Taking adjoints and using $q^!k_M=\omega_A[-2d]$ proves that the exchange, paired with the second dualizing class by tensor evaluation, is $c\circ g_F$ under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$. Every map retains support on $T$ throughout this factorization.

Ordered iterated diagonals. For two ordered smooth middle factors the normal model of the product diagonal is the ordered direct sum of the two complex normal bundles, and on the product of normal coordinate disks the relative cup product of the two positive generators evaluates to $+1$ on the ordered product disk, which is the positive generator of the direct sum; local uniqueness as in step 1.1 and base-change mate pasting as in steps 2.1 and 3.1 therefore give the composed refined operation on every support, in the given order and without an interchange of factors. All real degrees involved are even, so reordering the two complex summands introduces no sign: the only possible sign is $(-1)^{(2d_1)(2d_2)}=+1$. Under the additional hypotheses of [F3], the equivariant form holds verbatim, which supplies the same localization, exchange and normalized orientation clauses in $D^b_{G,c}$, with $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$ rather than a quotient-stack shift.

Zero sections and Euler classes. Let $V\to X$ have complex rank $c$ and zero section $s$. In a bundle chart the normal pair is the product with $(\mathbb C^c,\mathbb C^c\setminus\{0\})$, so the same relative cochain calculation gives $s^!k_V=k_X[-2c]$ and its positive supported counit; here $c$ is the bundle rank, independently of $\dim X$. These local orientations glue because the complex transition matrices preserve the positive fiber generator. characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace.
