citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the
relative Proj and scheme-properness suppliers. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite loopless
quiver, with arbitrary finitely many arrows between two distinct vertices. Let
$V=\bigoplus_iV_i$ be a finite-dimensional complex graded vector space,
$\beta_i=\dim V_i$, $E_V=\bigoplus_{h:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}(V_i,V_j)$ and
$G_V=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}(V_i)$. Let $\nu=(\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_m)$ be a word
with $\beta_i$ occurrences of $i$. Let $\mathcal F_\nu$ be the variety of
increasing full graded flags $0=F^0\subset F^1\subset\cdots\subset F^m=V$ with
$F^r/F^{r-1}$ of color $\nu_r$. Then
$X_\nu=\{(x,F):x_hF_i^r\subset F_j^r\text{ for all }h:i\to j,r\}$ is a
$G_V$-equivariant vector subbundle $W_\nu$ of $E_V\times\mathcal F_\nu$. Its rank
is $\sum_{h:i\to j}\#\{(p,q):\nu_p=i,\nu_q=j,q<p\}$ and its dimension is that
rank plus $\sum_i\beta_i(\beta_i-1)/2$. The map $\pi_\nu:X_\nu\to E_V$ is
projective.

Put $\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(U)=\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{Sym}(U^\vee)$.
Then the bundle inclusion defines a $G_V$-equivariant projective map
$\bar\pi_\nu:\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(W_\nu\oplus\mathcal O)\to\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(E_V\oplus\mathbb C)$
whose source is smooth projective and whose restriction over the affine chart
$t\ne0$ is exactly $\pi_\nu$. The analogous associated-bundle construction over
any finite product of complex Grassmannians formed from tautological bundles is
a projective map between smooth projective varieties, restricting over its
affine chart to the associated incidence map.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $U_N$ has the right action $u\cdot g=u\circ g$ and the quotient uses
$(u,x)\cdot g=(ug,g^{-1}x)$. For the action nerve use the equivalent left
action $g\cdot(u,x)=(ug^{-1},gx)$, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$ and $B_N$ are points and $X_N=X$, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

The finite local comparisons do not assert a global tensor splitting for an
arbitrary bundle with fibre $U_N$, such as the comparison projections
$X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $X_{N,M}\to X_M$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
gives a locally small triangulated category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with conservative
restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift, and its morphism groups are
computed by the coinduced simplicial injectives of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]. Locally
split free-action descent identifies its finite general linear Stiefel
resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$, and
the bounded Hom and image comparisons, the degree-zero ring comparison and
retract closure of
[[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]
hold for it. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness
of restriction to $X$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the finite general
linear Stiefel resolution
$P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N=P_N/G$ of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]
for $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ acting on the separated
finite-type complex variety $X$, with base $B_N$, frame space $U_N$,
$u_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}U_N$, $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$ and
$s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N=u_N-g$. Write $Q_N$ for the finite-resolution functor
and let $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$, $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ be the two
projections. Then:

1. the middle-perverse t-structure on $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is detected by
   restriction to $X$: for every sufficiently large $N$ and every $a$,
   $A\in{}^pD_G^{\le a}$ holds if and only if the restriction of $A$ to $X$
   lies in ${}^pD^{\le a}(X;k)$, if and only if $Q_N(A)[s_N]$ lies in
   ${}^pD^{\le a}(X_N;k)$, and independently of the sufficiently large $N$;
2. the functor $A\mapsto Q_N(A)[s_N]$ is exact for these middle-perverse
   t-structures and conservative in the sense that $Q_N(A)=0$ if and only if
   $A=0$;
3. perverse truncations lift: for $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ and all sufficiently
   large $N$ there is an equivariant perverse truncation
   ${}^p\tau_G^{\le a}A$ with
   $Q_N({}^p\tau_G^{\le a}A)[s_N]\cong{}^p\tau^{\le a}\bigl(Q_N(A)[s_N]\bigr)$,
   canonical up to unique isomorphism, and the family is independent of $N$;
4. at the degree-zero Hom stabilization bound $r_N\ge a-b$ for objects
   concentrated in ordinary degrees $[b,a]$, the ring comparison
   $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ lifts finite
   families of orthogonal idempotents, and after the common shift $s_N$ the
   normalized functor preserves and reflects perverse concentration and
   simplicity.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero. On the equivariant constructible derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]],
middle perversity is tested on the ordinary restriction $A_X$ and its
smooth complex constructibility strata $S$ by the two
inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A_X)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and
$H^q(i_S^!A_X)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$, where $i_S$ is the inclusion of a
stratum. These inequalities give a bounded t-structure independent of
compatible refinement and gluing across $G$-invariant algebraic open/closed
decompositions, and the perverse aisles are detected by restriction to $X$. Its heart is
abelian of finite length, and its simple objects are the intermediate
extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=i_{Z*}j_{!*}(L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z])$ of simple
finite-rank local systems $L$ on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports
$Z$, where $Z$ and the dense open are $G$-invariant, $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$
is the closed inclusion, $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is the dense open inclusion,
and $L$ has equivariant data. If $A,B$ lie in the
heart, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's
endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra, not asserted to equal $k$.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $k$ be any characteristic-zero coefficient field. Then $Rf_*k_X[n]$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple perverse sheaves on $Y$; equivalently all its perverse cohomology objects are semisimple and it splits into their shifted sum. This holds without any assumption that $k$ embeds in $\mathbb C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty
Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then
$U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every
$s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every projective morphism in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention of this page is proper: if $f:X\to S$ factors over $S$
as
$$X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
with $n\ge0$, $i$ a closed immersion and the second arrow the projection, then
$f$ is proper. The empty source, the empty base and the case $n=0$ are
included, and no Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix; let $W$ and $\ell$ be the presented group and its length and let $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ be the geometric representation, as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], with reflection set $T$ and sign-change sets $\Phi(w)$ as in that lemma. 1. **Braid moves.** Call two words in $S$ *braid-equivalent* when one is obtained from the other by finitely many replacements of an alternating subword $s\,t\,s\,t\cdots$ of length $m(s,t)<\infty$ by the alternating word $t\,s\,t\,s\cdots$ of the same length. Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).
3. **Singleton detection in dihedral subgroups.** Fix distinct $s,t\in S$ and put $m:=m(s,t)$. The subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ is dihedral of order $2m$ when $m<\infty$ and infinite dihedral when $m=\infty$; every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ acts on the quotient $E/\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ as the identity, while for every $u\in S\setminus\{s,t\}$ one has $\sigma_u(\alpha_u)-\alpha_u=-2\alpha_u\notin\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ (no induced quotient map for $\sigma_u$ is assumed). $$S\cap\langle s,t\rangle=\{s,t\},$$
and every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ has a reduced expression with all letters in $\{s,t\}$ (so the alternating words of length $q\le m$, and any $q$ when $m=\infty$, are reduced in $W$).

Fix a graded $k$-algebra $A$ and let $P$ be a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). The category
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ of graded left $A$-modules and degree-zero maps is
abelian ([[lem-graded-module-kernels-cokernels-and-biproducts-are-degreewise]]).

**Graded projective.** $P$ is **graded projective** when it is a projective
object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ ([[def-projective-object]]): for every
degree-zero epimorphism $q:E\twoheadrightarrow M$ and every degree-zero
$f:P\to M$ there exists a degree-zero $\widetilde f:P\to E$ with
$q\widetilde f=f$. Thus projectivity is tested only against degree-zero
epimorphisms and degree-zero maps, and the lift need not be unique.

**Finitely generated.** $P$ is **finitely generated as a graded left
$A$-module**, or generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, when for some
$n\ge0$ there are homogeneous elements $p_1,\dots,p_n\in P$ with

$$P=A p_1+\cdots+A p_n .$$

By [[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]] this is the same
notion as finite generation of the underlying $A$-module: a finite homogeneous
family is a finite family, and conversely, if $P=\langle S\rangle_A$ for a
finite set $S$, then writing each $s=\sum_es_e$ as its finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components gives, for every $x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s s\in P$,

$$x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s\sum_es_e=\sum_{s,e}a_s s_e,$$

a finite $A$-linear combination of the homogeneous elements $s_e\in P$; so the
finitely many components of the members of $S$ generate $P$. In particular the
notion does not depend on the chosen finite generating set.

**Finite graded projective.** $P$ is **finite graded projective** when it is
graded projective and generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, that is,
when it is graded projective and finitely generated as an $A$-module. The family
may be empty: $n=0$ gives $P=Ap_1+\cdots+Ap_n=0$, so the zero module is
generated by the empty homogeneous family, and the corresponding finite direct
sum of shifts in the characterization below is the empty direct sum. Its finite
shifted-free characterization is the next result
([[thm-finite-graded-projectives-are-summands-of-finite-graded-free-modules]]),
and it uses this same notion of finite generation throughout: a finite
homogeneous generating family there is exactly a family as above. No choice
principle is used in the equivalence above, which only rewrites a given finite
expression.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra. A **graded-simple module** here means a
nonzero finite-dimensional graded left $A$-module whose only graded submodules
are $0$ and itself. Internal shift acts on graded-simple isomorphism classes
by $[S]\mapsto[S\{r\}]$ for $r\in\mathbb Z$. There are finitely many shift
orbits of graded-simple isomorphism classes. For each orbit choose a
representative $S_i$ and a finite graded projective cover
$p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$, whose kernel is superfluous among graded
submodules. Then

$$
\{[S_i]\}_i\text{ is a }\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]\text{-basis of }G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A), \qquad \{[P_i]\}_i\text{ is a }\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]\text{-basis of }K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A).
$$

In particular, both modules have the same finite rank, the number of graded
simple shift orbits. If $A=0$, both bases are empty and both groups are zero.
No positivity assumption on the grading of $A$ is made.

derivations.claim: (Central polynomial subalgebra and freeness.) Let $C_\beta$ be the color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra: on the summand $e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\nu)$ it is the polynomial ring in the elementary symmetric functions of the dots of each color separately. It is central: unequal crossings permute dot positions, and equal-color divided differences $\partial_a$ commute with symmetric polynomials in $x_a,x_{a+1}$ by the Leibniz rule $\partial_a(fg)=\partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)\partial_a(g)$ applied to $s_a$-invariant $f$. For a color occurring $m$ times, start with $A_0=k[E_1,\dots,E_m]$ and $f_0(T)=T^m-E_1T^{m-1}+\cdots+(-1)^mE_m$. Successively put $A_r=A_{r-1}[X_r]/(f_{r-1}(X_r))$ and $f_r(T)=f_{r-1}(T)/(T-X_r)$ for $1\le r\le m$; the division has zero remainder in $A_r[T]$ and $f_r$ is monic of degree $m-r$. Monic division makes $A_r$ free of rank $m-r+1$ over $A_{r-1}$, with basis $1,X_r,\dots,X_r^{m-r}$. In $A_m$ the identity $f_0(T)=\prod_{r=1}^m(T-X_r)$ identifies $E_j$ with the elementary symmetric polynomial in the $X_r$. Thus $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to A_m$, $x_r\mapsto X_r$, is surjective, and its inverse sends $X_r\mapsto x_r$ and $E_j$ to that elementary symmetric polynomial: each successive root relation holds under this substitution. Consequently $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ is free of rank $m!$ over its symmetric coefficient subring, on the Artin monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_m^{a_m}$ with $0\le a_r\le m-r$; only the first extension, not the full polynomial ring, has rank $m$. Combining with the PBW basis [F1], whose dot monomials factor over the color blocks, gives that $R(\beta)$ is a finite free $C_\beta$-module, of rank $(|\beta|!)^2$ per weight counting the permutation basis; only centrality and this freeness are used below.

(Krull-Schmidt and splitting.) Every finitely generated graded module is bounded below and locally finite by [F1]. Choose finitely many homogeneous generators of degrees $d_j$; evaluation on the generators injects $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ into the finite product of the finitely many finite-dimensional pieces $M_{d_j}$, so every degree-zero endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional, and a nontrivial homogeneous idempotent splits $M$ into two nonzero summands with strictly smaller endomorphism algebras; splitting terminates. For an indecomposable $M$, every endomorphism $f$ satisfies a polynomial minimal equation because $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ is finite-dimensional; factoring it as $T^rg(T)$ with $g(0)\ne0$, Bezout gives a polynomial projector separating the nilpotent part from the invertible part, so indecomposability forces $f$ or $1-f$ to be invertible. Hence the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal, and the usual comparison of two decompositions $\bigoplus p_ii_jp_j=\mathrm{id}$ produces a matching summand and cancellation, proving uniqueness in the degree-zero category; the shifts are recorded as part of each summand.

(Simples and covers.) For a graded simple $S$ and a positive-degree central $c\in C_\beta^+$, the kernel and image of $c$ are graded submodules; if $c$ acted nontrivially it would be injective and hence surjective, contradicting the least nonzero degree of the bounded-below module $S$; so $C_\beta^+S=0$ and $S$ is finite-dimensional because $\bar R=R(\beta)/C_\beta^+R(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional by step 1.1. The finite-dimensional basis theorem [F3] applies to $\bar R$: it has finitely many graded simple shift orbits, and the same then holds for $R(\beta)$, since any simple $R(\beta)$-module is one. Projective covers are then lifted to $R(\beta)$: choose a finite shifted-free $R$-module $F$ whose reduction $\bar F$ surjects onto the projective cover $\bar Q\twoheadrightarrow\bar S$. That surjection splits by projectivity of $\bar Q$, giving an idempotent of $\operatorname{End}^0_{\bar R}(\bar F)$; entrywise reduction $\operatorname{End}^0_R(F)\to\operatorname{End}^0_{\bar R}(\bar F)$ is surjective; the reduction kernel in $\operatorname{End}^0_R(F)$ is nilpotent because its entries have positive central degree and a long product has degree exceeding every fixed difference of generator degrees minus the lower bound of $F$, so the projector onto $\bar Q$ is lifted by the finite nilpotent-ideal idempotent-lifting iteration $e\mapsto e-(2e-1)(e^2-e)$; the image $Q$ of the lifted projector is projective, its kernel is graded superfluous (after reduction by $C^+$ it is superfluous for $\bar Q$, and a bounded-below graded quotient $X=C^+X$ vanishes by its least nonzero degree), so $Q$ is an indecomposable projective cover, and every indecomposable projective is such a cover up to shift.

(Orbit bases.) Finite decompositions into indecomposables give that $K_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of indecomposable finite graded projectives, with $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$, and finite length of finite-dimensional modules gives that $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the simple shift orbits; both are $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-modules in the sense of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], the shift action is free because a nonzero finite-dimensional graded module is not isomorphic to a nonzero shift of itself (compare its least and greatest degrees), and the finite-dimensional theorem [F3] gives the same statement for the quotient categories. For a projective cover $P_b$ and simple $S_c$ with their selected shifts, $\operatorname{Hom}(P_b,S_c)=0$ unless $b=c$ at the selected shift, when it equals $\operatorname{End}(S_b)$ by the uniqueness of the cover, whose degree-zero endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra by Schur's argument; finite-dimensionality alone does not identify it with $k$; this is the diagonal-entry computation of the Hom pairing of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]. The stronger statement that the diagonal scalar rings equal $k$ over every field, and the associated unscaled dual-basis conclusion, are not inferred here from finite-dimensional algebra alone and are proved separately later on this page; nothing above uses them.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

Let $A$ and $B$ be graded $k$-algebras and $M$ a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule. Write
$\Phi_M:=M\otimes_A-$ for the functor that sends a graded left $A$-module $N$ to
the graded left $B$-module $M\otimes_AN$ of the total-degree grading.

1. **Exactness.** If $M$ is flat as an underlying right $A$-module, then
$\Phi_M$ is exact on graded left $A$-modules.

2. **Projectives.** If $M$ is finite graded projective as a left $B$-module,
then $\Phi_M$ carries every finite graded projective left $A$-module to a finite
graded projective left $B$-module.

Neither hypothesis is asserted to imply the other; the companion page exhibits
a right-flat $M$ whose output is not projective and a left-projective $M$ whose
tensor functor is not exact.

Let $A$ and $B$ be graded $k$-algebras, let $M$ be a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule, $X$
a graded left $A$-module and $Y$ a graded left $B$-module. Then currying

$$\Theta:\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(M\otimes_AX,Y)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}\bigl(X,\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)\bigr),\qquad \Theta(F)(x)(m):=F(m\otimes x),$$

is a natural bijection in $X$ and $Y$, where
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is the graded left $A$-module of finite sums of
homogeneous $B$-linear maps with the associative action
$(a\cdot f)(m)=f(ma)$. Its inverse sends $f$ to the map $m\otimes x\mapsto
f(x)(m)$ on elementary tensors.

Separately, the same formulas give a natural bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M\otimes_AX,Y)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(X,\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M,Y))$
between ungraded module maps. Here $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is the direct sum
of its homogeneous parts and can be properly contained in
$\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M,Y)$, so the graded statement cannot be
replaced by one with all ungraded maps on the right.

**Total internal degree on the balanced tensor product.** Let $A$ be a graded
$k$-algebra, $M$ a graded right $A$-module and $N$ a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). First use the canonical
decomposition of the ordinary tensor product of the underlying abelian groups
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in\mathbb Z}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j.$$
Its inverse sends $m\otimes n$ to the finite sum
$\sum_{i,j}m_i\otimes n_j$, where $m=\sum_i m_i$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are their
homogeneous decompositions; the two maps are inverse because they agree with
the identity on homogeneous elementary tensors. Give the summand
$M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$ total degree $i+j$, and write
$G_d:=\bigoplus_{i+j=d}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$.

The balanced tensor product
$M\otimes_AN=(M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N)/\mathcal R_A$
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), where
$\mathcal R_A$ is generated by the balance relations
$(ma)\otimes n-m\otimes(an)$. These relations are generated by the homogeneous
ones: for $m=\sum_i m_i$, $a=\sum_\ell a_\ell$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the relation
is the finite sum of
$(m_i a_\ell)\otimes n_j-m_i\otimes(a_\ell n_j)$ over $i,\ell,j$. Each such
homogeneous relation belongs to $G_{i+\ell+j}$, since the two module actions
preserve total degree. Thus $\mathcal R_A=\bigoplus_d(\mathcal R_A\cap G_d)$,
and

$$M\otimes_AN=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(M\otimes_AN)_d,\qquad (M\otimes_AN)_d:=(G_d+\mathcal R_A)/\mathcal R_A,$$

is a graded abelian group. For homogeneous $m\in M_i$ and $n\in N_j$ the
elementary tensor $m\otimes n$ has **total internal degree** $i+j$; every tensor
is a finite sum of homogeneous elementary tensors, and the balancing relations
used in the quotient are homogeneous. This grading is the only grading used
below, and it introduces no sign.

**Outer actions.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a graded left
$A$-module, then the action $b(m\otimes n):=(bm)\otimes n$ of
[[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded
left $B$-module: the action is homogeneous because homogeneous $b\in B_l$ sends
$m\otimes n$ of degree $i+j$ to an element of degree $l+i+j$. Symmetrically, if
$N$ is a graded $(A,C)$-bimodule, the action
$(m\otimes n)c:=m\otimes(nc)$ makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded right $C$-module, and
the two outer actions commute when both are present.

**Homogeneous Hom.** For graded left $A$-modules $P,Q$, with
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$ the abelian group of all $A$-linear
maps $P\to Q$, put

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q):=\bigl\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)\mid f(P_i)\subseteq Q_{i+d}\ \text{for all }i\in\mathbb Z\bigr\},\qquad \operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q):=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q).$$

Each $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$ is a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$, and the sum is direct: if
$f=\sum_df_d=\sum_df'_d$ with $f_d,f'_d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}$, then for
$p\in P_i$ the element $f(p)$ has homogeneous components
$f_d(p)\in Q_{i+d}$, and comparison of the graded components in $Q$ gives
$f_d(p)=f'_d(p)$ for every $d$ and $p$, so $f_d=f'_d$. Thus
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$ is a graded abelian group whose degree-$d$ part is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$, and the degree-zero morphisms are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(P,Q)$. By definition $\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$
consists of the finite sums of homogeneous $A$-linear maps, so
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$
with equality only when every $A$-linear map has bounded spread in degree.

**The associative left action.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $Y$ a
graded left $B$-module, then $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ carries a left
$A$-module structure

$$(a\cdot f)(m):=f(ma)\qquad(a\in A,\ m\in M),$$

which is homogeneous: for $a\in A_i$ and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d}(M,Y)$ one
has $ma\in M_{l+i}$ for $m\in M_l$, hence $(a\cdot f)(m)\in Y_{l+i+d}$ and
$a\cdot f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d+i}(M,Y)$. The action is associative and
unital by the module axioms of $M$, so $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is a graded
left $A$-module and an object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$. The same formula
defines an action on the full ungraded $\operatorname{Hom}$ group, where it is
denoted by the same symbol.

derivations.claim: (Shuffle decomposition and freeness.) Choose reduced PBW words adapted to the parabolic subgroup $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$. For each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ and minimal right coset representative $w$, the vectors $\tau_we(\xi)b$, with $b$ ranging through the PBW basis of $e(\xi)B$, form precisely the PBW basis of the right $B$-module $Ae$: the permutation is a minimal shuffle followed by an internal block permutation, with additive length, and the right idempotent records the source word in the corner $e$. Thus $Ae\cong\bigoplus_{w,\xi}e(\xi)B\{\delta_R(w,\xi)\}$, with the displayed degree of $\tau_we(\xi)$. Reversal of products fixing dots, crossings and idempotents preserves the defining relations and is an anti-involution; it sends $Ae$ to $eA$ and $\tau_we(\xi)$ to $e(\xi)\tau_{w^{-1}}$, giving the left $B$-module decomposition of $eA$ into the corresponding $Be(\xi)$ with shifts $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)$. Both decompositions are finite sums of principal graded projectives. Ungraded, for each shuffle the sum over all concatenated $\xi$ is one copy of $B$, so both ranks are $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. Neither bimodule is replaced by $eAe$: its unconstrained opposite endpoint is essential for the shuffle basis.

(Left adjunction.) For a graded left $B$-module $X$ and a graded left $A$-module $L$, currying gives the natural degree-zero bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(Ae\otimes_BX,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(X,eL)$, $\Phi\mapsto(x\mapsto\Phi(e\otimes x))$, with inverse $f\mapsto(ae\otimes x\mapsto a\,f(x))$, well defined on balanced tensors and inverse by the idempotence of $e$; this is the adjunction of [F3] for the $(A,B)$-bimodule $Ae$.

(Exactness and projectivity.) The right $B$-module $Ae$ is projective, hence flat, by step 1.1, so $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ is exact by [F2]. Idempotent restriction is exact on left modules: for a surjection $L\to N$, a vector $en\in eN$ lifts to $e\ell\in eL$, and kernels and images commute with multiplication by the degree-zero idempotent $e$; no right action on $L$ is required. A finitely generated graded projective left $B$-module is a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $B$, so its induction is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $Ae$. As a left $A$-module $Ae$ is the image of the degree-zero idempotent endomorphism $a\mapsto ae$ of $A$, hence is finitely generated graded projective. Similarly, if $P$ is a finitely generated graded projective left $A$-module, realize $P$ as a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $A$ and apply $e(-)$ to its split inclusion and projection. Then $eP$ is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $eA$, which is finitely generated graded projective as a left $B$-module by step 1.1. Internal shifts commute with induction and restriction because their balance relations and idempotent action have degree zero. This proves exactness, shift compatibility and both finite-projective preservation clauses.

(Coinduction and the longest shuffle.) The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$ by [F3] applied to $M=eA$, and explicit currying gives $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$. For the second-adjunction formula let $y$ be the longest block shuffle of the two blocks, of degree $-c$ (each of the $|\beta||\gamma|$ crossed positions contributes the negative pairing of the two colours), and let $e'=e(\gamma,\beta)$ be the reversed-block idempotent. By PBW there is a well-defined $B$-balanced coefficient map $t:eAe'\to B$ projecting onto the $y$-coefficient, where the reversed block order is read in $B$ through the flip equivalence $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)\to R(\gamma)\otimes_kR(\beta)$; dot slides and block crossings preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient, while every dot or braid correction in a shorter shuffle has strictly smaller shuffle length and is killed by $t$. Hence the map $\Phi:Ae'\to\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)$, $z\mapsto(u\mapsto t(uz))$, is a degree-$c$ map of $(A,B)$-bimodules, and it is compatible with the flip identification.

(Mackey filtration.) Fix a second flag with idempotent $e'=e(\beta',\gamma')$ and choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row block permutation group and the column block permutation group acting on the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ positions. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner $eAe'$ by the four intersection blocks $(a,b;c,d)$ with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, and filter by the crossing length of the double-coset representatives. The span of the double cosets of strictly smaller length is a $(B,B')$-sub-bimodule: sliding a block generator across a representative either stays in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or produces a quadratic/braid correction of strictly smaller length, which lies in the smaller span. In the associated quotient only the monomials whose permutation is the minimal double-coset representative survive; they are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases of the four blocks composed with the row and column induced bimodules and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks, which carries the shift $-(b\mid c)$ because the crossed colours are precisely $b$ and $c$. The basis bijection defines inverse maps between the associated quotient and the composite four-block restriction/induction bimodule, so the filtration is proved and not merely a character identity; iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block statement.

(Triangularity and the functor formula.) Pair the right $B$-module shuffle basis of $Ae'$ (through the block flip) with the left $B$-module shuffle basis of $eA$ by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, the coefficient matrix of the pairing $u\mapsto t(uz)$ is triangular: a complementary pair is exactly the reduced longest shuffle with coefficient $1$ up to the absorbed equal-colour signs, and a noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic or braid correction to strictly smaller length, hence vanishes in the associated graded. Finite triangular elimination over $B$ (division by the diagonal units $1$) inverts the matrix, so $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of graded $(A,B)$-bimodules; consequently $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\cong Ae'\{c\}$ with the $B$-action transported by the block flip. Since $eA$ is finite projective over $B$ by step 1.1, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\otimes_BX\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,X)$ for every graded $B$-module $X$ (checked on finite free modules and finite summands), and tracking the outer right $B$-action through the flip gives the functorial isomorphism $\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}$.

All clauses of the statement are now proved: step 1.1 gives the freeness and the labelled shuffle shifts, step 2.1 the exactness, shift compatibility and projective preservation, step 1.2 the left adjunction, steps 2.2 and 3.1 the right adjoint and its exact reversed-block formula, and step 2.3 the finite Mackey filtration and its multi-block version.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

derivations.claim: (Nil-Hecke tail and its matrix units.) The constant-colour block $NH_r=R(r\alpha_i)$ acts on its polynomial column over $C_r=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]^{S_r}$. The Artin monomial basis and perfect symmetric-variable-linear trace of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] give integral matrix units and identify the full algebra with graded endomorphisms of that free rank-$r!$ column, hence with matrices over $C_r$ carrying the Artin degree shifts. Reducing the positive-degree central elementary symmetric functions to zero gives the graded matrix quotient over $k$; its column simple $L(i^r)$ is absolutely simple, and the divided idempotent cuts out a one-dimensional image. Its full-algebra polynomial-column graded projective cover has degree-zero endomorphism ring $k$, although its entire endomorphism ring is $C_r$. If $T$ is a finite-dimensional graded simple over $R(\mu)\otimes_kNH_r$, a positive-degree central operator has graded kernel and image. A nonzero such operator would therefore be invertible by graded simplicity, which is impossible on the finite nonzero degree support of $T$. Thus the positive tail center annihilates $T$, and it factors through $R(\mu)\otimes_k\operatorname{Mat}_{r!}(k)$ with the indicated shifts. Matrix units identify $T$ with $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ for a graded simple $R(\mu)$-module $N$, unique up to shift. This uses the augmentation matrix quotient for finite simples, not a false identification of the full nil-Hecke algebra with matrices over the ground field.

(Maximal restriction.) Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional graded simple with $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ maximal. The finite-dimensional module $\Delta_i^rS$ is nonzero by the definition of $\epsilon_i$ and has a simple submodule; by step 1.1 it is of the form $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ for a graded simple $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$. If $N$ carried a word ending in $i$, then concatenating any nonzero nil-Hecke tail word would produce a nonzero vector in $S$ of tail $r+1$, contradicting maximality, so $\epsilon_i(N)=0$. By the left adjunction of [F2] the inclusion $N\boxtimes L(i^r)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^rS$ corresponds to a nonzero map $M:=\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))\to S$, which is surjective since $S$ is simple. In the Mackey filtration of $\Delta_i^rM$ every shuffle bringing $t>0$ colours $i$ from the first block into the final tail contains a factor $\Delta_i^tN$ and is zero; the only surviving filtration quotient is $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with zero crossing shift, so $\Delta_i^rM=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ exactly. This is a one-surviving-quotient computation, not a semisimplicity assumption.

(Unique head and simplicity.) Every nonzero quotient $Q$ of $M$ has nonzero defining corner: if $eQ=0$ with $e=e( eta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)$, then the composite $Ae\otimes_B(N oxtimes L(i^r))	o M	o Q$ is zero by the tensor/Res adjunction, hence $Q=0$. The finite graded semisimple head of $M$ therefore has exactly one simple summand, occurring once, because its exact $e$-restriction is a quotient of the simple $eM=N oxtimes L(i^r)$; this head is $S$, and $eM	o eS$ is an isomorphism, so exactness gives $e\ker(M	o S)=0$ and every other composition factor of $M$ has smaller tail. Underlying and absolute simplicity of $S$: induct on the height of $ eta$. For positive height choose $i$ with $r>0$; by step 2.1 and induction $N$ and $L(i^r)$ are absolutely simple, so $eS=N oxtimes L(i^r)$ has endomorphism ring $k$; if $U\le S$ is any ungraded submodule with $eU
e0$, then $eU=eS$ and $U=S$ because $S$ is generated by $eS$; if $eU=0$ and $U
e0$, filter $S$ by $F_dS= igoplus_{j\le d}S_j$ and $U$ by $F_dU=U\cap F_dS$. Every homogeneous algebra element of degree $a$ sends $F_dU$ into $F_{d+a}U$, so $\operatorname{gr}U$ embeds as a nonzero graded submodule of $\operatorname{gr}S=S$. Since $e$ has degree $0$ and annihilates $U$, it annihilates $\operatorname{gr}U$; graded simplicity gives $\operatorname{gr}U=S$, contradicting $eS
e0$. Thus $S$ is simple as an ungraded module, and every $R$-endomorphism of $S$ is determined on $eS$, giving $\operatorname{End}_R(S)=k$. The finite-density matrix argument then shows absolute simplicity over every field: any $m$ linearly independent vectors can be sent to arbitrary targets by one algebra element, by induction on $m$ and the commutant $k$ clause, so the action realizes all $k$-linear matrices and remains simple after field extension.

(Triangular divided-string basis.) Choose a cyclic order of the finite colour support and recursively strip maximal $i$-tails, producing for each simple shift orbit a finite tuple $Y_b$ of ordered divided powers; two simples with the same tuple agree by the unique-head recursion of step 3.1. Form $P(Y_b)$ from the reversed ordered normalized divided blocks. Its homogeneous Hom to $S_c$ is the corresponding product of divided idempotents acting on $S_c$; comparing tuples lexicographically, if $Y_b>Y_c$ at the first differing entry then the required tail exceeds the maximal tail of the successively stripped simple $S_c$, and the corner is zero. When the tuples agree, every maximal restriction is the simple tensor computed in step 2.1 and each nil-Hecke divided idempotent reduces the tail to one dimension, so by induction the diagonal Hom is a single Laurent monomial with coefficient $1$. Shifting each $S_b$ makes the diagonal $1$. The finite matrix is triangular over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ with diagonal $1$; Krull-Schmidt and the projective-cover/simple Hom pairing (now with $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ from step 3.1) identify it with the matrix expressing the projective classes in the cover basis, and successive integral triangular elimination proves that the selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ are an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; the whole family of divided words spans because the recursion covers every simple, while redundancy of non-selected words is allowed. This completes the integral surjectivity argument without a PBW rank or flat-family shortcut.

(First-color version.) For maximal FIRST-color blocks use the defining idempotent $e(r\alpha_i,\mu)$ and $M=\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$ with $\epsilon_i^L(N)=0$; a simple submodule of the maximal first-block restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}S$ has the form $L(i^r)\boxtimes N$ by the same nil-Hecke matrix units of step 1.1, and any first-colour support of $N$ would extend the maximal first block, so it vanishes. In the Mackey restriction of $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}M$ every nontrivial shuffle bringing a positive number $t$ of $i$-colours from $N$ into the first block contains $\Delta_i^{(L,t)}N$ and is zero, so the sole uncrossed quotient is $L(i^r)\boxtimes N$ with shift $0$; the defining-corner generation and exact-head argument of steps 3.1 and 3.1 are unchanged. Thus the first-block assertions are proved directly, with no unsigned star-crystal preservation assumed.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

derivations.claim: (Induction algebra and restriction coalgebra.) The induction product is associative and unital: the balanced identifications of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] for the two parenthesizations of three blocks are inverse degree-zero isomorphisms, and the unit is $[R(0)]=[k]$. For the block algebra $B$, the positive-center quotient is the tensor product of the two finite-dimensional graded quotients from [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Their simples are absolutely simple by [[lem-klr-maximal-tail-restriction-and-induction-have-a-unique-simple-head]], so their graded semisimple quotients are products of split graded matrix algebras. Tensoring these matrix blocks gives all simple shift orbits of $B$; tensor products of the factor projective covers cover them, by reducing their kernels and using the graded least-degree argument. Uniqueness of covers therefore identifies $K_0(B)$ with $K_0(R(\beta))\otimes_AK_0(R(\gamma))$. Restriction is coassociative with counit the weight-zero component, because iterated idempotent restriction multiplies the corresponding block idempotents, and the two orders of multiplication agree. To prove that $[\mathrm{Res}]$ respects the twisted multiplication, apply the Mackey filtration [F1] to the corner $e_{\beta,\gamma}Re_{\beta',\gamma'}$: PBW partitions its basis by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length, and multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms; the associated quotient is exactly the four-block restriction/induction bimodule shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives $[\mathrm{Res}](xy)=\sum q^{-(|y_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ with the twisted product, so $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism; no use of the second adjunction is needed.

(Explicit Serre contraction.) Fix $i\ne j$, write $d=-a_{ij}$, $D=d+1$, $N=d+2$, and $t=[u^d]Q_{ij}\ne0$. For $0\le r\le D$, let $E_r$ be the product of the reflected nil-Hecke idempotents on the two $i$-blocks in $i^rji^{D-r}$, let $s_r=-d_i(\binom r2+\binom{D-r}2)$, and put $C_r=R E_r\{s_r\}$. Use right multiplication by $a_r=E_r\tau_{N-1}\cdots\tau_{r+1}E_{r+1}$ for $C_r\to C_{r+1}$ and by $b_r=E_{r+1}\tau_1\cdots\tau_{r+1}E_r$ in the reverse direction. Each string crosses $j$ once and respectively $D-r-1$ or $r$ equal-color pairs, so its degrees are $d_id-2d_i(D-r-1)$ and $d_id-2d_ir$. As $s_{r+1}-s_r=d_i(D-2r-1)$, both maps have degree zero between the shifted columns. The nil-Hecke identities $\tau_aE_r=0$ for equal-color crossings internal to its divided blocks and the braid moves give $a_{r-1}a_r=0$. At corner $r$, put $L_r=a_rb_r$, $R_r=b_{r-1}a_{r-1}$, with absent endpoint terms zero. Moving far crossings cancels the common strings in $L_r-R_r$; the remaining braid correction is the divided difference of $Q_{ij}$. For a monomial $u^av^b$ its correction is the sum of $a$ monomials of combined outer degree $a-1$, with the native minus sign. The $r-1$ left and $D-r-1$ right equal-color divided differences kill it unless $a\ge d$; homogeneity permits $a=d$ only when $b=0$, and permits no $a>d$. For $a=d$ exactly the staircase exponents $r-1,D-r-1$ survive, each evaluated by the nil-Hecke trace calculation of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]; transporting the variable order on the left block gives $L_r-R_r=(-1)^rtE_r$, including endpoints. Thus $h_r=(-1)^rt^{-1}b_r$ satisfies $a_rh_r+h_{r-1}a_{r-1}=E_r$ on every corner. These degree-zero maps contract the finite complex $(C_r,a_r)$ over every field and every (Q1)–(Q4) parameter.

(Alternating classes and the $a_{ij}=0$ case.) A bounded complex with $dh+hd=1$ is split contractible: choosing the successive splittings gives a contraction with $h^2=0$, and then $d+h$ is an isomorphism from even to odd part; hence the alternating sum of the classes of its terms vanishes, which is exactly $\sum_{a+b=D}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}][P_{j,1}][P_{i,b}]=0$, the displayed Serre relation. If $a_{ij}=0$ then the crossing $\tau$ of the two colours is invertible (its square is the nonzero constant $Q_{ij}$), and right multiplication by it gives a degree-zero isomorphism between the two corners, so $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{ij}]=[P_{ji}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$.

(Descent of $\gamma$.) First define $\gamma$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ from the presentation of the negative Serre half: [F3] identifies the Serre-presented rational negative half with the actual negative subalgebra, and the assignments $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$, extended multiplicatively and $q$-linearly, respect all Serre relations by step 3.1 and the commuting relation, so they define an algebra homomorphism $\gamma_{\mathbb Q}$ on the localization. Since the $A$-form is the $A$-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words [F2], and $[P_{i,1}]^n=[n]_i![P_{i,n}]$ by the nil-Hecke decomposition, so every rational divided power maps to $[P_{i,n}]$. These divided-word images lie in $K_0(R)$, which embeds in its rational scalar extension because its shift-orbit basis is free, the homomorphism restricts to the stated $A$-linear $\gamma$; the formula $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$ is multiplicativity of $\gamma$ together with the definition of $P_\theta$. Coproduct compatibility is the Mackey computation of step 1.1, and bar compatibility is the projective $^\#$ duality of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], which fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ and hence each word class. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve projective ranks.
