Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

derivations.claim: A finite planar routing schedule. Forget dots temporarily and count all transverse intersections, including self-intersections, by $C$. An arc with a self-intersection has an innermost monogon or bigon; two simple arcs with more intersections than their endpoint alternation requires have a bigon. To see the latter, cut along one arc: successive entrances and exits of the other arc in the resulting disk either delimit a bigon or delimit a subarc containing a self-intersection, to which the first case applies. A closed component similarly has a monogon, a bigon with another component, or is a simple disjoint circle: cut along a path from the circle to the exterior and use successive entrances and exits. Clear the chosen disk as follows. An interior arc returning to the same side cuts off a smaller disk; choose that disk first. Otherwise its segment joins two sides, and push the disk corner past its nearest intersection by a triangle move. This removes that intersection from the chosen disk. A whole closed component in the disk is handled first by the same procedure. Thus the number of intersection vertices on or inside the chosen disk, apart from its defining corners, strictly decreases on every main triangle move, until its monogon or bigon is empty. This is a finite schedule: the diagram has finitely many vertices, and selection of a smaller disk strictly decreases that number too. Local extrema are carried along by isotopy; a crossing carried past an extremum is its specified adjunction mate. No new crossing pair is inserted. Once every component is simple and every pair crosses at most once, cut the disk along one component at a time and repeat the same nearest-intersection triangle sweep to route that component to its chosen reduced path. The already routed components remain fixed; the number of unrouted components decreases. This gives a finite sequence of triangle moves between reduced drawings of the same matching.

Algebraic use of the schedule. A triangle move is a downward KLR braid equation or its adjunction mate. Its leading term has the same three crossings, and every correction has fewer crossings. An empty downward bigon is reduced by the quadratic KLR equation; an opposite-orientation bigon is reduced by the prescribed cancellation equation, whose correction has no crossings but may insert a cup and cap. A monogon is reduced by the appropriate curl equation or its adjunction mate, removing its one crossing. Distinct-color opposite bigons have their specified unit cancellation. Move dots along components by cyclicity and the KLR dot equations; every correction again has fewer crossings. Induct first on $C$. At a fixed $C$ use the finite disk schedule of step 1.1, and apply the induction hypothesis separately to each correction. All sums are finite: curl and cancellation coefficients have nonnegative open-dot and bubble indices with fixed total. In particular an inserted cup and cap cannot defeat this induction, since its branch has already lowered $C$. After intersections are reduced, extra extrema on a simple component cancel by the triangles; these decrease the finite extremum count without changing $C$. Move each isolated circle to the far left by the coefficient slides, in decreasing order of its distance from the left edge. For a fixed coefficient every slide is a finite polynomial identity; it creates no intersection and decreases that distance. Replace the reciprocal bubble family by its finite inverse-coefficient recursion. Finally route the reduced open matching as in step 1.1, handling its shorter-crossing corrections by induction, and place the dots at the chosen positions. This proves finite spanning by the stated normal forms; it does not presuppose their independence.

Leading matching coefficients in the actual model. Work over the universal framing ring and then its generic splitting fraction field, localizing distinct root differences and the finitely many nonzero spectator $Q$ values used in the diagram. This is permitted solely to find a nonzero witness, not to prove an identity by specialization. Use the flag summands in which every background or visited $i$ root is a distinct root of the free universal framing polynomial. These summands are indexed by root additions and removals and are one-dimensional over the splitting fraction field. They exist because $r$ may grow while the framing degree grows as $2r+h-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$. The spectator factors of $p$ need not be separable: they are placed entirely in the complementary factor, and their values at these free framing roots are nonzero. Chinese remainder against the separable free framing factor gives the indicated summands even when a spectator factor has repeated roots. A dot multiplies by that root. A native equal-color crossing is $(1-s)/(x-y)$: its root-switching term has coefficient $-1/(x-y)$, and its other term retains the labels and deletes that crossing. A distinct-color crossing switches the labeled roots with coefficient either a unit or a nonzero $Q$ value. The monic coefficient cap at a simple root $z$ has coefficient $1/f'(z)$ up to its specified unit normalization, and its dual cup has the inverse coefficient; these follow by evaluating the dual-power Casimir $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ on the root idempotents. All these coefficients are nonzero. Consequently expanding a reduced matching diagram on these summands has a leading term that carries a root label along each of its matched components, with a nonzero product coefficient. All other terms delete at least one crossing, and hence are smaller in the minimal crossing number of their boundary matching after step 2.1. Choose pairwise distinct free framing roots for the different open $i$ components and independent spectator roots for the other components. The endpoint equalities of this leading term specify exactly its matching: a different matching must identify two labels assigned to different components. In a finite proposed relation select a matching of maximal minimal crossing number. No smaller matching can contribute to its root-labeled leading coefficient, and another matching of the same crossing number has different endpoint equalities. Its coefficient is therefore its dot polynomial on the selected component roots times its bubble polynomial, times a nonzero rational factor. This replaces an invalid independent bending of interior upward endpoints; only the explicit root flags and their already proved cup/cap maps are used.

A faithful witness at a fixed physical weight. Let $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ be fixed, choose spectator background counts $m_j$, and put $A_{\mathrm{spect}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$. For increasing $r$ put $N=h+2r$ and $\lambda_i=N-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$. Choose the universal monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg z_s=2d_is$, independent of the root variables. In the flag model, $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $\mathcal B=p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}U$ with $U_0=1$. Its first $D$ coefficients have the unit triangular form $\mathcal B_s=z_s+\sum_{0<\ell<s}z_\ell U_{s-\ell}+U_s$ for $s\le D$ whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$. Thus substituting bubbles in any nonzero finite downward PBW/bubble combination leaves a nonzero polynomial-operator combination before truncation. By the faithful polynomial representation it has a test vector with nonzero output. Take a homogeneous component of that vector and output, and let $B$ bound their degrees and all framing indices used. These bounds can be fixed while $r$ grows: only the finitely many appended strand variables, bubble indices, and fixed-degree symmetric background coefficients occur in the operator and test vector. Let $L$ bound the number of appended $i$ flags. Every flag/factor coefficient relation encountered has degree at least $2d_i(h+r-L+1)$; all variables have nonnegative degrees. Choose $r$ with $\lambda_i\ge D$ and this bound greater than $B$. No nonzero output of degree at most $B$ can belong to the ideal of these higher-degree relations, so it survives in that actual flag model. For the general-boundary leading coefficient of step 3.1, choose $r$ also large enough to supply distinct free framing roots for every component and at least $D$ unused free complementary roots. The selected component roots are algebraically independent; the first $D$ elementary coefficients of those unused roots are algebraically independent over them. In the factor identity $\mathcal B=b_{N-r}^{\mathrm{rev}}/c_r^{\mathrm{rev}}$, each of the first $D$ coefficients is a unit triangular polynomial in these complementary elementary coefficients. Thus the nonzero dot/bubble coefficient of step 3.1 remains nonzero in this actual localized flag model. Clearing its finitely many nonzero denominators gives an actual nonzero model operator. This proves independence at all boundaries in every characteristic; it uses unit framing or complementary-factor coefficients, not a root coefficient such as $2e_1$.

Basis and confluence. Step 2.1 gives spanning at all boundaries, and steps 3.1–4.1 prove independence in the actual model at all boundaries. Two finite straightening schedules have outputs whose difference represents zero; their basis coefficients therefore agree. This proves the asserted confluence of the output without assuming unchecked critical-pair identities. The same separating witnesses prove joint faithfulness before quotienting.

Forced vacuum coefficients. Write $h_\ell$ for the counterclockwise bubble coefficient with literal $\lambda_i-1+\ell$ dots, with $h_0=1$ and $h_{\ell<0}=0$. Closing the marked relation $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$, for $\ell\ge1$, is lawful in $J$ and gives $h_\ell+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{\ell-\lambda_i}=0$. Thus $\mathsf H_\Lambda a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}=1$ and $A_\Lambda=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}$. Let $S$ be this coefficient-specialization ideal; then $S\subset J$. The basis of step 5.1 shows that specializing these far-left central coefficients alone leaves the ordinary downward corner exactly $R(\beta)$. This conclusion concerns $S$ alone and does not assume the conclusion about $J$. For $\lambda_i=0$, $a_i=1$ kills the first $i$ word and the same recurrence gives $A=\mathsf H=1$.

The correctly typed local closure. Work modulo $S$. A straight vacancy closure with $q\ge0$ dots has clockwise $A$-index $\lambda_i+1+q$, so is zero. The crossed closure on the first physical $G_i$ at input $\Lambda$ is the first-adjunction mate of $R_\Lambda$, whose $H_i$ input is $\Lambda-\alpha_i$ and whose clockwise bubble region is $\Lambda$. In its exact native equation the bubble literal count is $b=-\lambda_i-1+m$ and $a+b=-1$, hence $a=\lambda_i-m$. Its value is consequently $-\sum_{m=0}^{\lambda_i}A_mx^{\lambda_i-m}=-a_i(x)$; its degree is $2d_i\lambda_i$. Taking the mate preserves this polynomial because the dot is cyclic. If $P(u,x)$ gives additional dots on the added and physical strands, the native relation $\tau_1u=x\tau_1+1$ gives $C(uP)=xC(P)+B(P)$ with $B$ a straight closure, up to the fixed cap convention's unit sign. Since $B(P)=0$, induction on the nonnegative exponents gives $C(P)=-a_i(x)P(x,x)$. Before these closures, slide any bubble at the bent source $\Lambda+\alpha_i$ across the added root $z$: $A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda$ and the reciprocal equation for $\mathsf H$. Each coefficient is finite, so this reduces it to polynomial dots and the already specialized vacuum coefficients. No bubble is assigned the wrong ambient weight.

The marked operator at the dominant vacuum. Modulo the killed-upward ideal, the actual positive rank-one matrix identifies $H_iG_iv_\Lambda$ with $D_{\lambda_i}$. Its columns are $v_r=x^r\eta$, $0\le r<\lambda_i$, and its dual rows are the finite bubble-weighted counit rows of the prescribed inverse. A raw row with $s\ge0$ extra dots sends $x^rv_0$ to $h_{r+s-\lambda_i+1}$. Its value on $a_i(x)v_0$ is therefore the zero recurrence of step 6.1 at index $s+1$. Every actual dual row is a finite combination of raw rows, so all projections of $a_i(x)v_0$ vanish; the matrix inverse equation implies the column itself is zero. Multiplying by powers of $x$ kills $a_i(x)$ on all columns and hence on $H_iG_iv_\Lambda$. When $\lambda_i=0$ this object is already zero. This uses the actual inverse rows, rather than assuming raw rows are dual bases.

Every killed-upward factor. A term through $W H_iv_\Lambda$ has factor maps $f:G_uv_\Lambda\to W H_iv_\Lambda$ and $g:W H_iv_\Lambda\to G_vv_\Lambda$. Bend that vacuum $H_i$ in both maps. The triangles recover $gf$ by closing the composite of the bent maps, which has all-downward boundaries with an additional first $i$ strand at source $\Lambda+\alpha_i$. The interior word $W$ need not be downward. Apply step 5.1 to the composite and then the coefficient slide of step 7.1. Put $n=|\beta|$ and let $W_P\subset S_{n+1}$ fix position one. There are two double cosets, $W_P$ and $W_Ps_1W_P$. Removing the distinguished input and output and inserting them in their required positions supplies length-additive representatives $u s_1v$, $u,v\in W_P$, in the second case; the first case uses only $s_2,\ldots,s_n$. Choose these reduced words for PBW. Shorter braid corrections still straighten in this family. In the first case the first strand closes to the zero straight vacancy loop. In the second the exterior words fix position one, whose color is $i$ at both boundaries; therefore both colors at the unique $s_1$ crossing are $i$. The exterior downward diagrams pull past the closure, and its local value from step 7.1 is $-a_i(x_1)P(x_1,x_1)$. Every such term is in the ordinary first-strand $i$ ideal. For $n=0$ only the zero straight closure occurs.

Every marked monic whisker. In a term vertically sandwiching $W(a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda})$, select the chronologically earliest $H_i$ in its intermediate word and move it toward the vacuum. Distinct-color commutation is natural and commutes with the marked $j$ dot. For $h\ge0$ the rank-one isomorphism moves $H_iG_i$ to $G_iH_i$ plus finitely many identity branches; the latter remove an $H_i$. For $h<0$ use the reverse isomorphism $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ and its actual retract maps $\iota=r_h^{-1}j_H$, $\pi=p_Hr_h$, with $\pi\iota=1$. Naturality gives $(H_iG_i)(b)=\pi(G_iH_i)(b)\iota$ for every input endomorphism $b$. Absorb these retract maps into the outer factor maps; the intermediate word has moved its earliest $H_i$ one place toward the vacuum. At the marked first strand, $j\ne i$ gives a killed-upward factor by mixed dot compatibility; $j=i$ gives zero by step 7.2 and the dominant vacuum matrix. The lexicographic measure (number of $H_i$ letters in the intermediate word, distance of its earliest $H_i$ from the vacuum) strictly decreases on each finite branch. It counts the intermediate word, not cups and caps in adapted factor maps. After that word is downward, step 5.1 straightens its factor maps. Consequently all marked whiskers reduce to ordinary first-strand ideal insertions and killed-upward factors, already handled in step 8.1.

Exact intersection. Express an ordinary downward element $x\in J$ as a finite sum of factored whiskers of the defining generators. Specialize $S\subset J$ first. The killed-upward summands land in $I_a$ by step 8.1, and the marked monic summands do so by step 9.1; specialization summands vanish. Step 6.1 shows that specialization leaves the included ordinary element $x$ unchanged. Thus $J\cap e(v)R(\beta)e(u)\subset e(v)I_ae(u)$. The reverse inclusion follows from the defining monic generators and downward compositions. Every downward quotient morphism is represented by an ordinary downward element by step 6.1, giving the corner isomorphism, with composition equal to multiplication.

Generation and transport. Apply the word induction of step 9.1 without a marker. At the vacuum $H_iv_\Lambda$ is zero; positive rank-one branches give finite sums and negative branches give actual retracts, so every word is a retract of a finite sum of downward words. Downward words under the corner identification of step 10.1 are the representable word projectives $e(u)R/I_a$. They generate the finite projectives by additive sums and idempotents; the corner isomorphisms extend to a fully faithful and essentially surjective equivalence of their additive idempotent completions. Appending $G_j$ acts on these representables by the ordinary appended-strand bimodule, hence by actual induction. Transporting the first adjunction identifies $H_i$ with its normalized projective restriction by uniqueness of adjoints. Restriction preserves finite projectives because its values are the transported retracts just proved. The second units and counits transport through the same fully faithful equivalence, so their naturality and both triangles hold as actual bimodule natural transformations. This transports the maps; a claim that their second cap equals a separately prescribed trace would require an additional calculation. All constructions used finite coefficient operations and unit identities over the universal coefficient ring; arbitrary monic specialization gives the ungraded claims.

Proof2.1 gives zero for incompatible empty matching family; Proof10.1 exact ideal quotient and Proof11.1 retract equivalence include zero word projectives.
Proof7.1 computes first physical i-strand crossed closure as exact mate of R_Lambda, equal to −a_i(x); λ_i=0 is treated in Proof6.1/7.2.

Independent flag/model suppliers read at final hashes. No separately transported two-color cap-commutation/full mate theorem is a premise or conclusion of this partial-category helper.

citations.quote:
For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

derivations.claim: Actual cap and index. Apply the ordinary first unit to $e(\eta)$ and decorate its appended strand with $m$ dots; the resulting element is $e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$. The canonical first-adjoint transport preserves that unit by [F1]. Its actual second counit consequently evaluates this element as the transported diagram $\varepsilon'_\mu x^m\eta_\mu$, with $\mu=\Lambda-\gamma$. This is the counterclockwise bubble of [F2], hence $e(\eta)\mathsf H_{\eta,m-h_i+1}$. This calculation identifies the constructed $T_i^\gamma$ itself; it does not replace it by a chosen coefficient functional. Negative indices give zero, and no sign or weight shift is omitted: the literal-dot index is $m-h_i+1$, and its degree is $2d_i(m-h_i+1)=2d_im+\deg T_i^\gamma$.

Slide through the prefix. Starting with the vacuum value in [F2], slide the bubble through the chronological letters of $\eta$. Each coefficient computation is finite because every reversed monic factor has constant coefficient one. The resulting series is $\mathsf H_\eta(t)=\prod_{a:\eta_a=i}(1-x_at)^2/(a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)\prod_{a:\eta_a\ne i}q_{i\eta_a}^{\mathrm{rev}}(x_a,t))$. The numerator has degree $2\#\{a:\eta_a=i\}$ in $z$, the denominator has degree $\lambda_i+\sum_{a:\eta_a\ne i}(-a_{i\eta_a})$, and their difference is $-h_i$. Therefore $R_i^\eta(z)=z^{-h_i}\mathsf H_\eta(z^{-1})$. Extracting coefficient $z^{-1}$ from $z^mR_i^\eta(z)$ extracts precisely index $m-h_i+1$ from $\mathsf H_\eta$. Combined with step 1.1 this proves the actual terminal-dot formula, without restriction on the sign of $h_i$.

Centrality and old algebra factors. For an equal-color adjacent pair in $\eta$, the two factors of $\mathsf H_\eta$ are symmetric in their dot variables, so each coefficient commutes with its crossing by [F3]. For a distinct-color pair, swapping the color-variable pairs sends the coefficient in the $\eta$ summand to the coefficient in the swapped-word summand; its crossing has precisely that dot-permutation relation with no correction. Thus the finite sum of these coefficients over the words commutes with every crossing, every dot and every idempotent, which generate $A$. They are central. Appended terminal dots commute with all old generators. For any $b\in e(\eta)Ae(\eta)$, [F1] consequently evaluates $\iota_i(b)e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$ as $b\,e(\eta)[z^{-1}]z^mR_i^\eta(z)$. By linearity this identifies the actual cap on every polynomial terminal with arbitrary old algebra coefficients.

First actual quadratic contraction. Put the $i$ dot $u$ on the appended prefix $\eta i$. Its actual terminal-$j$ formula of step 2.1 uses $R_j^{\eta i}(v)=t_{ji}R_j^\eta(v)/Q_{ji}(v,u)$. In this identity the inverse is expanded at infinity in $v$ and has polynomial coefficients in $u$ and the old dots. Apply step 3.1 termwise to the polynomial $Q_{ij}(u,v)g(u,v)$: its old coefficients lie in the append image of $A[u]$. Since $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the denominator cancels in the Laurent series before taking the coefficient. The actual inner cap therefore gives $t_{ji}[v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)$. This is a polynomial in $u$ with old algebra coefficients: $g$ has finitely many powers of $u,v$, and only finitely many series coefficients contribute to $v^{-1}$. Apply the actual outer $i$ cap by step 3.1. The result is $t_{ji}[u^{-1}][v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)R_i^\eta(u)$.

Second contraction and common map. Interchange $i,j$ and keep the variables labeled by color. Now the inner $i$ cap uses $R_i^{\eta j}(u)=t_{ij}R_i^\eta(u)/Q_{ij}(u,v)$, giving $t_{ij}[v^{-1}][u^{-1}]g(u,v)R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)$ after the outer $j$ cap. Following the quadratic cancellation, each series depends on only its own terminal variable and the old commuting dots. Their coefficients commute with one another. On the finite polynomial $g$, both extractions use finitely many coefficients and therefore commute. The result of step 4.1 and this result are respectively $t_{ji}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ and $t_{ij}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ in the same old algebra corner. This is an equality of actual cap compositions, with an explicit common residual map before any prefix closure; no common finite flag coefficient ring or symmetric trace was assumed.

Quotients and boundaries. Every input is evaluated by the actual append homomorphisms and actual quotient caps; two polynomial inputs with the same terminal quadratic image give the same cap value. Because $t_{ij},t_{ji}$ are nonzero, the identities also show that $\mathcal D_\eta$ vanishes on each kernel of the corresponding quadratic evaluation. In the standard homogeneous case the degree asserted in step 1.1 agrees with [F1], and the two composite cap degrees agree in the two orders by $d_ia_{ij}=d_ja_{ji}$. Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$

$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

derivations.claim: The typed transfer base. Suppose the old prefix ends in $i$, with last old dot $u$, and append another $i$ with dot $v$. Closing the appended strand on $\tau_n$ is the natural transformation $K=(\varepsilon'_{\mu}G_i)(H_i\tau^{GG})(\eta_\mu G_i)$ on $G_i$ whose input is $\mu+\alpha_i$ and output is $\mu=\Lambda-\gamma$; its intermediate word is $H_iG_iG_i$. The first unit is at the old output weight $\mu$, and the second cap deletes the marked appended flag. First evaluate with an independent universal monic flag polynomial, on the root path $K_0\to J=K_0\cup\{u\}$. The unit sums paths adding $v\notin J$, with coefficient $c_J(v)$. The retained term of the native crossing on ordered additions $(u,v)$ has coefficient $1/(u-v)$, and the subsequent marked deletion returns to $J$ with second-cap coefficient $1/b_J'(v)$. Its switched term instead gives the old subset $K_0\cup\{v\}$; the cap-to-identity component at $J$ is zero by [F4]. Thus the diagonal coefficient of the actual composite is $\sum_{v\notin J}c_J(v)/(b_J'(v)(u-v))$. Polynomial interpolation subtracts these simple poles from $c_J(z)/b_J(z)$; since $c_J(u)=0$, this sum is minus its polynomial part at $u$, hence $-\sum_{a+\ell=-h}u^a\mathsf H_{J,\ell}$. Both sides are integral flag maps; the generic-root computation descends by the projectivity and injection proved in [F4], and then specializes to every framing/spectator polynomial, including repeated spectator factors. Joint faithfulness of the universal partial models in [F1] gives this identity of formal maps on $G_i$, with its bubble in the output region $\mu$. Transport through the quotient and the first-unit-preserving identification of [F1] therefore gives $T_i^\gamma(\tau_ne(\eta i))=-\sum_{a+\ell=-h}u^a\mathsf H_{\eta,\ell}$ in the actual old corner. No faithfulness of the cyclotomic quotient under localization is used.

Two relative PBW summands. Work now in the ordinary generic algebras $\widetilde A=R(\gamma)$ and $\widetilde B_i=R(\gamma+\alpha_i)$, with the same scalar monic framing coefficients used in the series. Choose PBW reduced words adapted to the two double cosets of $S_n$ in $S_{n+1}$. A permutation fixing the appended position gives the summand $\widetilde A[v]$. Every other permutation has a length-additive expression $w_1s_nw_2$, with $w_1,w_2\in S_n$, giving old factors sandwiching $\tau_n v^m$. In the append-$i$ corner, the two colors meeting at this middle crossing must both be $i$: the exterior permutations fix the appended position, whose color is $i$ at both boundaries. Thus these two sorts span the entire append corner as an old-algebra bimodule, by [F3]. Dot powers and coefficients can be moved to the indicated locations with the native dot relations, whose correction terms belong to the same span.

All transfer powers. Put $K_m=T_i^\gamma(\tau_nv^me(\eta i))$. The native dot relation in [F4], old-algebra bilinearity of [F1], and the actual dot formula in [F2] give $K_m=uK_{m-1}-\mathsf H_{\eta,m-h}$ for $m\ge1$. With step 1.1 this yields $K_m=-\sum_{a+\ell=m-h}u^a\mathsf H_{\eta,\ell}$. All indices in the sum are nonnegative. Equivalently $K_m=[v^{-1}]v^mR_i^\eta(v)/(u-v)$, with $(u-v)^{-1}=-\sum_{a\ge0}u^av^{-a-1}$. This is a finite coefficient computation even for $h\le0$.

A single generic lift of the actual cap. Expand a generic downward element in the faithful rational permutation representation of [F3]. Discard the permutation terms that move the appended position, delete that position from all retained permutations, multiply their coefficients by the corresponding word series $R_i^\eta(v)$, and extract $[v^{-1}]$. Denote this explicitly defined map by $\widetilde T_i$. Its output initially lies in rational old permutation operators. The coefficient-by-coefficient centrality calculation in [F2] uses only the generic dot and crossing relations, so it also holds before the cyclotomic quotient. It is an old-algebra bimodule map: old permutations fix $v$, the word-indexed coefficients of $R_i(v)$ commute with the old algebra by [F2], and projection to the subgroup fixing $v$ commutes with multiplication by old permutation operators. On the first summand of step 1.2 it is exactly the dot-cap formula. On the second summand, $\tau_n=(1-s_n)/(u-v)$ has retained coefficient $1/(u-v)$; its switched term cannot fix the appended position after multiplication by either old exterior permutation. Therefore it is exactly the transfer formula of step 2.1, including both old exterior factors. Both summands consequently have outputs in the ordinary polynomial algebra $\widetilde A$, not merely its rational localization. The actual quotient cap agrees with this generic map followed by the cyclotomic quotient on every spanning term. Hence $T_i$ has this one downward lift, and $\widetilde T_i$ sends the generic cyclotomic kernel into the old cyclotomic kernel. This last assertion follows from equality with the actual quotient map, not from localization of the quotient.

A common representation for both colors. For the original prefix use the one ordinary generic algebra $\widetilde B=R(\gamma+\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$ and its representation of [F3]. Give the two terminal labeled variables names $u$ of color $i$ and $v$ of color $j$, independently of their position. Let $\widetilde a\in e_{ij}\widetilde B e_{ji}$ lift $a$. For a term retained after both terminal projections in $\widetilde a p$ or $p\widetilde a$, its permutation in $\widetilde a$ must be $s\pi=\pi s$, where $s$ switches these two terminal positions and $\pi$ fixes them both. It maps the $ji$ word to the $ij$ word and induces the old prefix permutation $\pi$. All other terms are discarded in both orders. This is an exact condition on labeled permutations; it does not require that the original reduced matching itself preserve the terminal pair. In particular, the no-switch terms in equal-color divided differences are retained where necessary in the zero-return and one-return patterns.

The complementary factor is present. Track the two distinguished labeled roots through any expanded generator word contributing the permutation $s\pi$ of step 4.1. Their relative order is reversed, so they undergo an odd number of distinct-color switches. Equal-color retained terms do not switch labels; equal-color switched terms switch roots of the same color and cannot supply this distinguished $i,j$ reversal. With the $Q/1$ factorization of [F3], the net reversed path contains the complementary factor of the reverse terminal crossing; every extra pair of switches contributes a further quadratic factor. Thus the coefficient of $s\pi$ is divisible by that complementary $P$ factor. The only denominators in this expansion are differences of same-color labeled roots. They cannot involve both $u,v$, since $i\ne j$. The divisibility holds termwise and therefore after adding all generator-word contributions. Multiplying by the singled-out crossing in either order gives its complementary factor times its own factor, exactly $Q_{ij}(u,v)$, with the same residual coefficient $g_\pi$ after the variables are identified by color. Indeed $s\pi=\pi s$ and $\pi$ fixes $u,v$, so the two operator products have coefficients $Q_{ij}(u,v)g_\pi$ on the same old permutation $\pi$. The equality includes all native divided-difference signs.

Cancel before taking coefficients. In the $ij$ corner the two actual generic cap weights of step 3.1 have product $R_i^\eta(u)R_j^{\eta i}(v)=t_{ji}R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)/Q_{ij}(u,v)$. In the $ji$ corner their product is $t_{ij}R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)/Q_{ij}(u,v)$ by [F2]. Cancel the $Q$ factor of step 5.1 before coefficient extraction. Every remaining terminal-dependent denominator of $g_\pi$ is a same-color difference involving one terminal variable and old variables of its own color, or an old difference; there is no denominator coupling $u,v$. Expand the first kind at its own terminal infinity and localize only the old same-color differences. The two coefficient operations then commute: each monomial contributing to $[u^{-1}v^{-1}]$ uses finitely many coefficients, and all coefficients lie in the same commutative localized old-dot ring. Consequently the common old permutation operator is $\sum_\pi[u^{-1}v^{-1}]g_\pi R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)\,\pi$. It equals the first actual generic cap composition divided by $t_{ji}$, and the second divided by $t_{ij}$. By step 3.1 these cap compositions belong to $e(\eta)\widetilde A e(\eta)$. Faithfulness of the generic representation implies they are equal there; the rational computation introduces no new relation. This constructs the common polynomial downward residual map.

Actual quotient descent and the three typed patterns. Define $\mathcal D_\eta(a)$ by quotienting the common generic residual of step 6.1. If another lift differs by the cyclotomic ideal, the first cap composition of its product with $p$ has zero image by step 3.1, so division by the nonzero $t_{ji}$ gives zero residual. Thus the map is well defined on the actual opposite corner, and its two compositions are precisely the typed identities in the Statement. To isolate a terminal pattern, expand $\widetilde a$ in reduced PBW matchings and partition them by how many of the two distinguished top terminals meet distinguished bottom terminals, namely $k=0,1,2$. Apply the same projection and coefficient rule of steps 4.1–6.1 to each individual matching term. Restrict the already well-defined map $\mathcal D_\eta$ to the image of the span of the $k$th matching family; this gives $\mathcal D_{\eta,k}$ with the same input and output corners and the same scalar factors. These images may intersect; no direct-sum decomposition of the cyclotomic quotient by matching types is asserted. The expansions include every lower permutation term of the original crossing word. Therefore no unproved slide of external maps or identification of separately transported flag modules is needed for either $k=0$ or $k=1$. For $k=2$ and polynomial terminal inputs the rule is exactly the explicit $\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ of [F2]. Prefix crossings and dots are part of the same common downward lift throughout.

Boundary, specialization and scope. Only the generic ordinary polynomial representation is localized, and its equality has already descended to the ordinary old algebra before taking the quotient. No claim of cyclotomic faithfulness after localization is made. At empty prefix the same computation is monic coefficient extraction; zero corners give zero residuals by step 7.1. Negative $h$, $a_i=1$, repeated roots and arbitrary field characteristic are covered by the finite series formulas and universal integral descent in steps 1.1–2.1. The construction uses only finitely many PBW terms and Laurent coefficients, so no choice principle is needed. Arbitrary monic specialization preserves the identities with grading forgotten; in the homogeneous branch every actual map retains its stated adjunction degree. Finally one may compose both corner identities with the identical actual prefix closure: this gives their crossing scalar ratio without assuming symmetry. Diagonal inversion weights can subsequently cancel those ratios along adjacent exchanges; that global trace assembly and the full adjunction-mate interpretation are separate consequences, not premises of this proof.

For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

Let $p(u)$ be monic of degree $N\geq0$ over a commutative ring $D$. Let $L_r$ be the monic factor ring $p=c_rb_{N-r}$, where $c_r$ is monic of degree $r$, and put $L_r=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>N$. Put
$$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls
$$L_\mu=(H\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G)(H\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H)(G\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H),$$
where $L_\mu$ has input $\mu$ and $R_\mu$ input $\mu-\alpha_i$, with $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=h$. Their formulas are
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h}x^a\mathsf H_j,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h}x^aA_j.$$
All indices in these sums are nonnegative. Mating the two matrix-completeness equations gives the two opposite-crossing cancellation equations with literal-dot sum $a+b+c=-2$: the $HG$ boundary uses $A_{b+h+1}$, and the $GH$ boundary uses $\mathsf H_{b-h+1}$. Single curls instead have literal-dot sum $a+b=-1$.

For a symmetrizable datum and distinguished color $i$, take a dominant integral framing $\lambda_i\geq0$ and
$$p(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}Q_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij},\qquad t_{ij}=[u^{-a_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,y)\in D^\times.$$
This realizes every $r\geq0$, including both signs of $h$, with zero modules past $N$. Every assertion is an integral polynomial identity, hence survives arbitrary monic specialization. Grading is asserted only when the coefficients are homogeneous in their natural degrees.

For the formal category $\mathcal P_i$ of

Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, let $a_j(u)$ be monic of degree
$\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let $J$ be the representable
ideal generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and
$a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$, closed under vertical compositions and all allowed

$$J\cap e(v)R(\beta)e(u)=e(v)I_a(\beta)e(u),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_jR(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum specialization is $A_\Lambda=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}$ and
$\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. The downward Hom corners of
$\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ are therefore exactly the ordinary monic
cyclotomic corners. Here the corner $e(v)R e(u)$ acts as a map $e(u)R	o e(v)R$ between right projectives. Every word in this quotient is a retract of a finite
sum of downward words. Consequently its additive idempotent completion is
equivalent to the category of finite right cyclotomic word projectives, with $G_j$
acting by actual word induction. The first adjunction identifies $H_i$ with
the corresponding normalized projective restriction; the second adjunction
maps transport through this equivalence as actual natural transformations.

These assertions hold for every degree-zero field and every admissible
homogeneous $Q$. The monic deformation is first taken over the universal
graded coefficient ring; arbitrary monic field specializations assert the
ungraded conclusions. No cyclotomic Frobenius theorem is assumed.

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

**Total internal degree on the balanced tensor product.** Let $A$ be a graded
$k$-algebra, $M$ a graded right $A$-module and $N$ a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). First use the canonical
decomposition of the ordinary tensor product of the underlying abelian groups
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in\mathbb Z}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j.$$
Its inverse sends $m\otimes n$ to the finite sum
$\sum_{i,j}m_i\otimes n_j$, where $m=\sum_i m_i$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are their
homogeneous decompositions; the two maps are inverse because they agree with
the identity on homogeneous elementary tensors. Give the summand
$M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$ total degree $i+j$, and write
$G_d:=\bigoplus_{i+j=d}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$.

The balanced tensor product
$M\otimes_AN=(M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N)/\mathcal R_A$
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), where
$\mathcal R_A$ is generated by the balance relations
$(ma)\otimes n-m\otimes(an)$. These relations are generated by the homogeneous
ones: for $m=\sum_i m_i$, $a=\sum_\ell a_\ell$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the relation
is the finite sum of
$(m_i a_\ell)\otimes n_j-m_i\otimes(a_\ell n_j)$ over $i,\ell,j$. Each such
homogeneous relation belongs to $G_{i+\ell+j}$, since the two module actions
preserve total degree. Thus $\mathcal R_A=\bigoplus_d(\mathcal R_A\cap G_d)$,
and

$$M\otimes_AN=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(M\otimes_AN)_d,\qquad (M\otimes_AN)_d:=(G_d+\mathcal R_A)/\mathcal R_A,$$

is a graded abelian group. For homogeneous $m\in M_i$ and $n\in N_j$ the
elementary tensor $m\otimes n$ has **total internal degree** $i+j$; every tensor
is a finite sum of homogeneous elementary tensors, and the balancing relations
used in the quotient are homogeneous. This grading is the only grading used
below, and it introduces no sign.

**Outer actions.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a graded left
$A$-module, then the action $b(m\otimes n):=(bm)\otimes n$ of
[[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded
left $B$-module: the action is homogeneous because homogeneous $b\in B_l$ sends
$m\otimes n$ of degree $i+j$ to an element of degree $l+i+j$. Symmetrically, if
$N$ is a graded $(A,C)$-bimodule, the action
$(m\otimes n)c:=m\otimes(nc)$ makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded right $C$-module, and
the two outer actions commute when both are present.

**Homogeneous Hom.** For graded left $A$-modules $P,Q$, with
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$ the abelian group of all $A$-linear
maps $P\to Q$, put

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q):=\bigl\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)\mid f(P_i)\subseteq Q_{i+d}\ \text{for all }i\in\mathbb Z\bigr\},\qquad \operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q):=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q).$$

Each $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$ is a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$, and the sum is direct: if
$f=\sum_df_d=\sum_df'_d$ with $f_d,f'_d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}$, then for
$p\in P_i$ the element $f(p)$ has homogeneous components
$f_d(p)\in Q_{i+d}$, and comparison of the graded components in $Q$ gives
$f_d(p)=f'_d(p)$ for every $d$ and $p$, so $f_d=f'_d$. Thus
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$ is a graded abelian group whose degree-$d$ part is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$, and the degree-zero morphisms are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(P,Q)$. By definition $\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$
consists of the finite sums of homogeneous $A$-linear maps, so
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$
with equality only when every $A$-linear map has bounded spread in degree.

**The associative left action.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $Y$ a
graded left $B$-module, then $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ carries a left
$A$-module structure

$$(a\cdot f)(m):=f(ma)\qquad(a\in A,\ m\in M),$$

which is homogeneous: for $a\in A_i$ and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d}(M,Y)$ one
has $ma\in M_{l+i}$ for $m\in M_l$, hence $(a\cdot f)(m)\in Y_{l+i+d}$ and
$a\cdot f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d+i}(M,Y)$. The action is associative and
unital by the module axioms of $M$, so $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is a graded
left $A$-module and an object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$. The same formula
defines an action on the full ungraded $\operatorname{Hom}$ group, where it is
denoted by the same symbol.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

Use the standard first-strand cyclotomic KLR quotient over a degree-zero
field, any real symmetrizable datum and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family. The same ungraded assertions hold for arbitrary monic field
specializations $a_i$ of degrees $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle$.
Let $\eta$ be any downward prefix of root weight $\gamma$, let $i\ne j$,
and put $A=R_a^\Lambda(\gamma)$,
$B=R_a^\Lambda(\gamma+\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$,
$e_{ij}=e(\eta ij)$ and $e_{ji}=e(\eta ji)$.
Use the actual caps $T_i^\gamma$ of
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-induction-restriction-bimodules-have-compatible-frobenius-dual-bases]].
There is an explicitly computed linear residual map
$$\mathcal D_\eta:e_{ij}Be_{ji}\longrightarrow e(\eta)Ae(\eta)$$
such that, with $p=\tau_{n+1}e_{ij}\in e_{ji}Be_{ij}$ and $n=|\eta|$,
$$T_i^\gamma T_j^{\gamma+\alpha_i}(ap)=t_{ji}\mathcal D_\eta(a),\qquad T_j^\gamma T_i^{\gamma+\alpha_j}(pa)=t_{ij}\mathcal D_\eta(a).$$
These are exact corner identities after the arbitrary prefix, before any
prefix closure. They hold separately on every reduced matching with
$k=0,1,2$ distinguished terminals connected to distinguished terminals;
all shorter-crossing terms are included. In particular, composing with any
fixed prefix functional gives the same residual evaluation in all three
terminal patterns. No common finite coefficient ring for the separately
transported distinguished-color actions is assumed.

The computation uses a downward generic PBW lift, expands its faithful
polynomial operator by root-labeled permutations, cancels the quadratic
factor attached to the distinguished pair, and extracts the two terminal
Laurent coefficients. This produces an element of the old algebra and is
independent of the lift. It uses no Frobenius symmetry or full two-color
action premise. The typed formulas specify the scalar orientation without
an implicit reversal of source and target corners.

citations.quote:
Let $\mathbb Z[t]$ be the polynomial ring over the integers
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[thm-polynomial-ring-is-a-commutative-ring]]) and let
$$S=\{t^k:k\ge0\}.$$
The set $S$ is multiplicative, and the **Laurent polynomial ring** is the
principal localisation
$$\Lambda_1:=\mathbb Z[t]_S=S^{-1}\mathbb Z[t]$$
([[def-principal-localisation]], [[def-multiplicative-subset-and-localisation]]).
It is a commutative ring with unit $1=t^0$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]). Write
again $t$ for the image of the indeterminate under the localisation map; then
$t$ is a unit with inverse $t^{-1}$
([[prop-units-in-a-localisation]]). Every element of $\Lambda_1$ has a
representative
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k,\qquad a_k\in\mathbb Z,$$
with only finitely many nonzero coefficients, obtained by writing a fraction
$p/t^N$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of the powers
$t^{k-N}$; the finite coefficient sequence is unique: after multiplying two such sums
by a common sufficiently large power of $t$, equality becomes equality of
ordinary polynomials. The localisation map $\mathbb Z[t]\to\Lambda_1$ is
injective because $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain; hence their coefficients agree
([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]]). Equivalently, two such
sums are equal exactly when their coefficient sequences agree
([[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]).

**Universal property.** Let $A$ be a ring with unit and let
$\varphi\colon\mathbb Z[t]\to A$ be a unital ring homomorphism with
$\varphi(t)$ a unit of $A$. Then there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\widetilde\varphi\colon\Lambda_1\to A$ with
$\widetilde\varphi(t)=\varphi(t)$. Equivalently, for every unital ring $A$ and
every unit $u\in A$ there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\Lambda_1\to A$ with $t\mapsto u$ ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]],
[[def-ring-homomorphism]]).

The cited localisation theorem treats commutative target rings. For the
possibly noncommutative target used here, define
$\sum_k a_kt^k\mapsto\sum_k(a_k1_A)u^k$. Unique Laurent coefficients make
this well defined. Integer multiples of $1_A$ are central, and
$u^ku^l=u^{k+l}$ for all integers $k,l$, so finite distributivity proves
additivity, multiplicativity and preservation of $1$. Every unital
homomorphism must send $a_k$ to $a_k1_A$ and $t^k$ to $u^k$, proving
uniqueness. Taking $u=\varphi(t)$ gives the asserted extension of $\varphi$.

**Augmentation.** There is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$$\varepsilon\colon\Lambda_1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \varepsilon\Bigl(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k\Bigr)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k,$$
the **sum-of-coefficients map** ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]]); it
is well defined because the coefficients are summable and their total sum is
unchanged along the relation of
[[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]. Its kernel is the
principal ideal $(t-1)$: indeed $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$, and if
$\varepsilon(x)=0$ then, writing $x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k$ with finite
support and using that $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k=0$, one has
$$x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k(t^k-1)=(t-1)\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k\,(1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}),$$
where $1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}$ denotes the empty sum $0$ for $k=0$ and, for
$k=-j<0$, the negative sum
$-(t^{-1}+t^{-2}+\cdots+t^{-j})$, so that
$t^{-j}-1=-(t-1)(t^{-1}+\cdots+t^{-j})$; hence $x\in(t-1)$, and the reverse
inclusion is $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$.

**Caveats.** This item realises $\Lambda_1$ by localisation and does **not**
identify it with an integral group ring: the additive group underlying
$\Lambda_1$ is $\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z\,t^k$ and its multiplication
is the polynomial one ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]] is not
needed for the ring laws but records that $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain). The
deck-module structures on homology introduced later on this page are defined
separately, by the universal property above.

Let $K$ be a field and let $v$ be a discrete valuation on $K$
([[def-discrete-valuation]]). Its **valuation ring** is
$$ V_v:=\{x\in K:v(x)\ge 0\}. $$
This is a valuation ring in the sense of [[def-valuation-ring]].

A **discrete valuation ring** (DVR) is a subring $V\subseteq K$ of the form
$V=V_v$ for some discrete valuation $v$ on $K$. Because $v$ is surjective,
there is an element of value $1$, so $V$ has a nonunit and is therefore not a
field.

Let $R$ be a ring ([[def-ring]]) with identity $1_R$ and zero $0_R$. For
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $n \cdot 1_R$ be the additive natural power of $1_R$ in
the abelian group $(R,+,0_R)$ ([[def-group-power]], [[def-group]]): thus
$0 \cdot 1_R = 0_R$ and $\sigma(n)\cdot 1_R = n \cdot 1_R + 1_R$. Put

$$T_R \;:=\; \{\, n \in \mathbb{N} \;:\; n \ge 1 \text{ and } n \cdot 1_R = 0_R \,\} \;\subseteq\; \mathbb{N}.$$

The **characteristic** of $R$ is

$$\operatorname{char}(R) \;:=\; \begin{cases} \min T_R & \text{if } T_R \ne \varnothing, \\[2pt] 0 & \text{if } T_R = \varnothing.\end{cases}$$

**Why the least element exists.** $T_R$ is a subset of $\mathbb{N}$, so when it
is nonempty it has a least element by the well-ordering principle
([[thm-well-ordering-principle]]), and that element is unique: two least members
are below one another and hence equal by antisymmetry of the natural-number
order ([[thm-nat-linear-order]], [[def-nat-order]]). So
$\operatorname{char}(R)$ is a well-defined natural number in both cases.

**The clause $n \ge 1$ is not decoration.** $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$
([[def-natural-numbers]]) and $0 \cdot 1_R = 0_R$ holds in every ring, so
without that clause $T_R$ would always contain $0$ and the definition would say
nothing.

**Convention: the value in the empty case is $0$, and this is the OPPOSITE of
the convention for the order of a group element.** [[def-order-in-a-group]]
writes $\operatorname{ord}(g) = \infty$ when no positive power of $g$ is the
identity. Here the value in the corresponding case is the natural number $0$,
not a symbol $\infty$. A reader coming straight from
[[def-order-in-a-group]] should notice the difference: it is deliberate, it is
the standard convention for the characteristic, and it is what makes the
divisibility statement of [[lem-characteristic-and-additive-order]] uniform
across the two cases.

**$\operatorname{char}(R)$ is a natural number, hence a set, not an element of
$R$.** A natural number in this library is a von Neumann natural
([[def-natural-numbers]]), so $\operatorname{char}(R) \notin R$ in general and
the expression $n \cdot 1_R$ is not a product in $R$ but the additive multiple
just described.

**Dictionary for fields.** When $R$ is a field $F$ ([[def-field]]), the element
$n \cdot 1_F$ is exactly the canonical natural $\iota(n)$ of
[[def-canonical-natural]]; this is proved, not assumed, in
[[lem-integer-multiples-agree-with-canonical-natural]]. So for a field
$T_F = \{\, n \ge 1 : \iota(n) = 0_F \,\}$ and the characteristic is the least
$n \ge 1$ with $\iota(n) = 0_F$, or $0$ if there is none.

Construct the valuation. For an ordinary nonzero polynomial $g$, repeated division by $t-1$ terminates as degree decreases, giving a unique factorization $g=(t-1)^a g_0$ with $g_0(1)
