citations.quote:
Work in the charged finite-$e$ specialization of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] at a
dominant weight $\Lambda$ and rank $d$, and let $H=H^\Lambda_d$. For the
canonical CRT projectors supplied by
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]],
denote by $e(\nu)$ the joint residue projector attached to the residue tuple
$\nu$ and by
$$e_\alpha:=\sum_{\nu\ \text{of content}\ \alpha}e(\nu)$$
their sum at content $\alpha$ ([[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]).

**Content sector.** Put
$$H^\Lambda_\alpha:=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d\,e_\alpha,$$
an ideal and unital algebra with unit $e_\alpha$, called the **central content
sector** of content $\alpha$; it may be the zero algebra, and at this stage it
is NOT asserted to be a primitive block. The two descriptions coincide because
$e_\alpha$ is a central idempotent.

**Named nilpotent generators.** On $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ put
$$y_r:=\sum_{\nu\ \text{of content}\ \alpha}(x_r-\nu_r)\,e(\nu)\quad\text{(degenerate branch)},\qquad y_r:=\sum_{\nu\ \text{of content}\ \alpha}\bigl(1-q_H^{-\nu_r}X_r\bigr)e(\nu)\quad\text{(nondegenerate branch)}.$$
By the spectral supplier these named elements are commuting nilpotents on the
sector, and they provide the local variables in which the sector is compared
with the corresponding KLR block.

**Boundary conventions.** For $\alpha=0$ one has $e_{\mathrm{empty}}=1$ and
$H^\Lambda_0=F$ at rank zero. Later primitivity statements may identify the
nonzero sectors with the blocks of $H$, but that identification does not
change the objects named here. This definition introduces no new primitivity
or basis assertion of its own and uses no choice principle.

Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels
$0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant
weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). In the nondegenerate branch the
distinct spectral values of the labels are $q^i$, while in the degenerate
branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$). Fix
$\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put
$\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)\ge0$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The **affine Hecke algebra of type
$A_{d-1}$** at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators
$X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$X_rX_s=X_sX_r,\qquad X_rX_r^{-1}=1,$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1).$$
The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (which forces $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The
**degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with
generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$x_rx_s=x_sx_r,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_s=x_ss_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$s_r^2=1,\qquad s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1},\qquad s_rs_t=s_ts_r\quad(|r-t|>1);$$
its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis by
[[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**Conventions and boundary.** Put $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is
imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator, and $T_r$ acts on positions
$r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one
$\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the algebra $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke
algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$
([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]).
Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of
unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$)
are outside this page's cyclic scope and are recorded as a deferred boundary in
the batch notes. These presentations and the charged quotients are the ones of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no
embedding of the label set $I$ into $F$ is claimed in the nondegenerate branch,
and no choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Finite evaluation. On each projector $e(i)$ the dots are commuting nilpotents by [F1]. If $y_r^{n_r}=0$, every monomial of total degree greater than $\sum_r(n_r-1)$ vanishes. Thus formal series have finite evaluation, and $c+f$ with $c\ne0$ and $f$ of positive degree has inverse $c^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-f/c)^k$. Unequal-colour spectral differences have nonzero scalar constant; equal-colour dot differences will only be used as formal divided differences, never inverted in the cyclotomic algebra.

A faithful formal calculation convention. Temporarily take independent dots $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ and a separate copy of their fraction field for each colour word. Let $S_r$ swap both positions and their dots; write multiplication on the right of $S_r$. For spectral variables $A,B$, put $\widehat p=(A-B)^{-1}$ in DG and $\widehat P=(1-q)B/(B-A)$ in NG, even on equal colours. The affine Hecke operator is $H_r=S_r(1-\widehat p)-\widehat p$ in DG and $H_r=S_r(1-\widehat P)-\widehat P$ in NG. For precision the formal calculation algebra has coefficients $\bigoplus_i F[\![u_1,\ldots,u_d]\!]e(i)$ and the affine generators, with spectral word-sliding: an unequal-colour intertwiner moves $e(i)$ to $e(s_ri)$ and permutes coefficients, while on equal colours the affine mixed relation gives its divided-difference correction. These relations follow in a sector by the CRT projectors and the mixed presentation: multiply the unequal spectral difference by the intertwiner and use its unit inverse; on equal colours use $H+1$. This calculation is faithful before any cyclotomic quotient: move coefficients right by these mixed and word-sliding relations and reduce crossing words by the Coxeter relations to span the finitely many $H_we(i)$; in their crossed-product expansions the coefficient at a reduced permutation $w$ is a product of nonzero rational functions and every proper subword has smaller length. A maximal-length coefficient therefore proves independence, also for formal series coefficients after clearing their finitely many difference denominators. Consequently an identity between regular formal expressions can be checked in this rational model and then evaluated at nilpotent dots. This is a calculation in the affine presentation, not an assumption that its cyclotomic quotient acts faithfully.

Explicit normalization. Write $u=y_r,v=y_{r+1}$, $p=(i_r-i_{r+1}+u-v)^{-1}$ on unequal DG colours, and $A=q^{i_r}(1-u),B=q^{i_{r+1}}(1-v)$ on NG colours. In the order equal, unrelated, forward arrow, backward arrow, double edge, choose $q_r(i)$ to be $1+v-u$, $1-p$, $(1-p^2)/(v-u)$, $1$, $(1-p)/(v-u)$, respectively, and choose $Q_r(i)$ to be $1-q+qv-u$, $(A-qB)/(A-B)$, $(A-qB)/(A-B)^2$, $q^{i_r}$, $q^{i_r}/(A-B)$, respectively. These are the actual five branches, including $e=2$. For DG forward colours $i_r-i_{r+1}=-1$, so $1-p^2=(v-u)(2-u+v)/(1-u+v)^2$; on the double edge the field has characteristic two and $1-p=(v-u)/(1+u-v)$. Thus the forward quotient has constant $2
e0$ unless the pair is a double edge, which uses the separate constant $1$ branch. Unrelated pairs have $i_r-i_{r+1}
e0,\pm1$, so $1-p$ has nonzero constant. In NG the unequal $A-B$ is a unit; $A-qB$ has nonzero constant except for a backward arrow, whose coefficient is prescribed separately. Hence all five coefficients are units; the equal coefficient has constant $1$ in DG and $1-q
e0$ in NG.

The full affine coefficient check. In left-coefficient notation $H_{AB}=a_{AB}S+b_{AB}$, use $(h,t)=(1,0)$ in DG and $(q,q-1)$ in NG, where $b_{AB}=-(A-B)^{-1}$ or $(1-q)B/(A-B)$, respectively, and $a_{AB}=h-b_{AB}$. Direct common-denominator multiplication gives $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$, $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$, and $b_{AB}b_{BC}=b_{AC}(b_{AB}+b_{BC}-t)$. The mixed relations follow by multiplying $A,B$ on either side; the first two identities give $H^2=tH+h$. For three positions, expansion of either braid word has coefficients, in the order $1,S_1,S_2,S_1S_2,S_2S_1,S_1S_2S_1$, equal to $b_{AC}(h+b_{AB}b_{BC})$, $a_{AB}b_{BC}b_{AC}$, $a_{BC}b_{AB}b_{AC}$, $a_{AB}a_{AC}b_{BC}$, $a_{BC}a_{AC}b_{AB}$, $a_{AB}a_{AC}a_{BC}$. For example the first expansion's constant is $b_{AB}^2b_{BC}+a_{AB}a_{BA}b_{AC}$, which reduces to the displayed constant using the three scalar identities. The $S_1$ coefficient reduces from $a_{AB}(b_{AC}b_{BA}+b_{AB}b_{BC})$ in the same way. Thus this six-coefficient check establishes braid for all spectral triples, including any coincidence of colour labels; spectral variables remain independent at this stage. Disjoint positions commute.

Pair products and interchange. Denote the chosen normalizer by $N_{ij}(u,v)$, the piecewise scalar by $p$ in DG or $P=(1-q)B/(B-A)$ in NG, and put $K_{ij}(u,v)=1,v-u,u-v,(v-u)(u-v)$ in the four unequal-colour cases. Substitution gives $p_{ij}+p_{ji}(v,u)=0$ in DG and $P_{ij}+P_{ji}(v,u)=1-q$ in NG. Also $N_{ij}(u,v)N_{ji}(v,u)K_{ij}(u,v)=1-p_{ij}^2$ in DG and $(1-P_{ij})(q+P_{ij})$ in NG. For the latter equality, its right side is $(B-qA)(A-qB)/((B-A)(A-B))$; forward and backward pairs use $B-qA=q^{i_{r+1}}(u-v)$ and $A-qB=q^{i_r}(v-u)$, respectively, and a double edge uses both. These substitutions prove each branch of the pair-product identities without division by a nonunit. Each coefficient depends only on its ordered two colours and their two dots. Therefore swapping a third position gives the same coefficient of the same ordered pair, proving the three-position interchange identities for $p,P,N$. In particular no square root is chosen.

The intertwiners. On unequal colours $\varphi=S(1-p)$ and $\Phi=S(1-P)$, since the scalar term cancels. Hence they permute the word and the two spectral variables, their squares are the pair products in step 3.1, and they commute at distant positions. On equal colours they are $H+1$; their squares are $2\varphi$ and $(1+q)\Phi$. The equal-colour mixed correction is $1+B-A$ in DG and $qB-A$ in NG, obtained by multiplying the operator $H+1$ by $B$ and subtracting $A(H+1)$. The braid defect is zero unless the outer colours coincide. For all equal colours, expanding $(H_1+1)(H_2+1)(H_1+1)$ minus its reversed word gives $h(\varphi_1-\varphi_2)$ in DG and $q(\Phi_1-\Phi_2)$ in NG (here $h=1$ in DG). For outer equal, middle unequal, write $C_{AB}=1-\widehat p_{AB}$ or $1-\widehat P_{AB}$, and $F_{AB}=C_{AB}C_{BA}$. The middle equal-colour intertwiner contributes either its permutation term or its scalar term $C_{AC}$. The former gives equal longest-permutation coefficients in the two words; the latter gives identity coefficients $F_{AB}C_{AC}$ and $F_{BC}C_{AC}$. Their difference is therefore $C_{AC}(F_{AB}-F_{BC})$. In DG put $p_1=1/(A-B),p_2=1/(B-C)$ and use $p_1+p_2=(A-C)p_1p_2$; then this difference is $(p_1-p_2)(p_1p_2-p_1-p_2)$. In NG, substituting $C_{AC}=(A-qC)/(A-C)$ and $F_{AB}=(A-qB)(B-qA)/(-(A-B)^2)$ cancels the factor $A-C$ and gives $(1-q)^2(AC-B^2)(AB-qBC)/((A-B)^2(B-C)^2)$. Adjacent-equal and distinct-colour patterns have no remaining identity term; their permutation coefficients cancel by the scalar identities of step 2.2. These are precisely the intertwiner identities named in the Statement.

A local crossing calculation that will also serve both relation maps. Put $D_r f=(S_rf-f)/(u_r-u_{r+1})$; every inverse dot difference in an operator formula acts by multiplication on the left unless explicitly included in a right coefficient. On equal colours, $H+1=(S+1)(-N/(u-v))$, since $1-\widehat p=-N/(u-v)$ in DG and $1-\widehat P=-N/(u-v)$ in NG; thus $(H+1)N^{-1}=D$. On unequal colours set $c_{ij}(u,v)=(1-p)/N_{ij}$ or $(1-P)/N_{ij}$, so the normalized crossing is $S_rc_{ij}$ and $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$ by step 3.1. For a formal coefficient $f$, direct subtraction gives $Df=(Sf)D+(Sf-f)/(u-v)$ and $D^2=0$; unequal crossings simply permute coefficients. These formulas prove the dot-sliding and quadratic relations and the compatibility $\psi_r^2N_r(i)S_rN_r(s_ri)=1-p_r(i)^2$ or $(1-P_r(i))(q+P_r(i))$ on unequal colours; on equal colours both sides of the original compatibility identity are zero.

Every braid colour pattern. Write $u,v,w$ for the three dots, $W=S_1S_2S_1$, and $c=c_{ik}$. If all colours are distinct, both crossing braid words have right coefficient $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$ at $W$. For $(i,i,k)$ both are $(W-S_1S_2)c(u,w)c(v,w)/(v-w)$; the coefficient product is symmetric in $u,v$, so moving it through $D_1$ adds no divided-difference correction. For $(i,k,k)$ both are $(W-S_2S_1)c(u,v)c(u,w)/(u-v)$, by the same calculation with the product symmetric in $v,w$. In these two formulas the denominator multiplies on the left and the coefficient product multiplies on the right. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest-permutation terms cancel by the ordered-pair interchange of step 3.1; the remaining identity coefficients in $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1$ and $\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$ are $-K_{ij}(u,v)/(u-w)$ and $-K_{ij}(w,v)/(u-w)$. Thus their difference is $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)$, equal to $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$ for unrelated, forward, backward, double-edge pairs. Finally all equal colours give $D_1D_2D_1=D_2D_1D_2=-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. Each displayed quotient is a formal divided difference; the resulting braid correction is polynomial, including characteristic two. This proves all five cases locally.

Regular identities and conclusion. The rational calculations above express every intertwiner, normalization, dot-sliding, quadratic and braid identity as an identity of regular formal expressions in the affine generators. Faithfulness in step 1.2 licenses clearing the temporary differences, and step 1.1 licenses finite evaluation in the sector. The candidate normalizers and their products give all stated identities, retaining $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}y_r(i)$ in NG. Therefore all three assertions of the Statement hold over the original field, with no algebraic closure or choice principle.

Let $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a central content sector (possibly zero) as in
[[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]], with the residue
tuples $i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ contained in a fixed index set $I_\alpha$.

1. Set $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ in the degenerate case and
   $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ in the nondegenerate case
   ($1\le r\le d$). Then $y_1,\dots,y_d$ are commuting nilpotent elements of
   $H^\Lambda_\alpha$; consequently every rational expression displayed below,
   expanded as a power series in the nilpotent $y$'s, is a finite and
   well-defined element of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.
2. The power series
   $$p_r(i):=\begin{cases}1,&i_r=i_{r+1},\\ (i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1},&i_r\ne i_{r+1}\end{cases}$$
   (degenerate case), respectively
   $$P_r(i):=\begin{cases}1,&i_r=i_{r+1},\\ (1-q)\bigl(1-y_r(i)y_{r+1}(i)^{-1}\bigr)^{-1},&i_r\ne i_{r+1},\end{cases} \qquad y_r(i):=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$$
   (nondegenerate case), satisfy (3.23)–(3.25) respectively (4.24)–(4.26),
   (4.28)–(4.30) and (4.32); and the intertwining elements
   $$\varphi_r:=\sum_i\bigl(s_r+p_r(i)\bigr)e(i),\qquad \Phi_r:=\sum_i\bigl(T_r+P_r(i)\bigr)e(i)$$
   satisfy all identities (3.14)–(3.20) of the source's Lemma 3.1,
   respectively (4.14)–(4.20) of its Lemma 4.1.
3. There exist invertible power series $q_r(i)\in F[\![y_r,y_{r+1}]\!]$
   (respectively $Q_r(i)$) satisfying (3.27)–(3.29), respectively
   (4.33)–(4.35); the explicit candidates (3.30) respectively (4.36) do, and
   for them the identity (3.43) respectively (4.44) holds.

Let $F,q,e,I,\Lambda,\lambda_i$ be as in
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]],
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). On the cyclic affine type-A Cartan
datum take the normalized symmetrizers $d_i=1$ and define the **type-A KLR
datum** $Q^{\mathrm A}$ by
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{ii}=0,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1\quad\text{if }a_{ij}=0,$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v\qquad(e\ge3),$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{01}(u,v)=Q^{\mathrm A}_{10}(u,v)=-(u-v)^2\qquad(e=2).$$
Write $R_\alpha$ for the resulting generalized KLR algebra over $F$
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]) and $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ for
the standard cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] (monic first-strand
relations $x_1^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(\nu)=0$).

**The specialization dictionary.** Put $y_r:=x_r$ and $\psi_r:=-\tau_r$. With
these normalizations, the relations (1.6)–(1.15) of the source hold in
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$, and conversely the quotient presented by those relations
is the same algebra; in other words $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the sign-modified
cyclotomic Khovanov–Lauda algebra of the source for the cyclic quiver of
quantum characteristic $e$. The verification of the dictionary is elementary
and is recorded here so that no hidden convention is imported:

1. **(Q1)–(Q4).** Non-adjacent pairs have $a_{ij}=0$ and
   $Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1$, homogeneous of degree $0$. For an adjacent pair
   $(i,i+1)$ with $e\ge3$ one has $b_{ij}=a_{ij}=-1$, and $v-u$ is homogeneous
   of degree $2=-2b_{ij}$ with nonzero extremal coefficients of
   $u^{-a_{ij}}=u$ and $v^{-a_{ji}}=v$; the opposite orientation is the
   transpose, so (Q2) is built into the two formulae. For $e=2$ the pair
   $\{0,1\}$ has $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $b_{01}=-2$, and $-(u-v)^2$ is
   symmetric, homogeneous of degree $4=-2b_{01}$, with top coefficient $-1\ne0$.
2. **Dot sliding.** Relation (1.8) comes from $\tau_re(i)=e(s_ri)\tau_r$;
   relations (1.12)–(1.13) reduce to the dot-sliding constants
   $\tau_ax_a-x_{a+1}\tau_a=e(\nu)$ and
   $\tau_ax_{a+1}-x_a\tau_a=-e(\nu)$ on equal colours, whose sign changes to
   the source's constants $+1$ under $\psi=-\tau$.
3. **Quadratic and braid relations.** Relation (1.14): equal colours give
   $\tau^2=Q_{ii}=0$; non-adjacent colours give $\tau^2=1=e(i)$; a forward
   arrow gives $\tau^2=v-u$, evaluated at $(y_r,y_{r+1})$ as
   $y_{r+1}-y_r$; a backward arrow gives $y_r-y_{r+1}$; the $e=2$ double edge
   gives $(y_{r+1}-y_r)(y_r-y_{r+1})$. Relation (1.15): the divided-difference
   numerator
   $\bigl[Q^{\mathrm A}(x_a,x_{a+1})-Q^{\mathrm A}(x_{a+2},x_{a+1})\bigr]/(x_{a+2}-x_a)$
   equals $\pm1$ in the two single-edge cases with $i_{r+2}=i_r$, equals
   $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ in the $e=2$ double-edge case, and vanishes
   otherwise; the global sign $\psi=-\tau$ matches the source's three cases.
   The product order is explicit: the source difference is
   $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_r-\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}$, which under
   $\psi=-\tau$ equals the native reversed-word difference
   $\tau_{r+1}\tau_r\tau_{r+1}-\tau_r\tau_{r+1}\tau_r$; for
   $Q=-(u-v)^2$ the displayed quotient is $u+w-2v$. Thus no braid-order sign
   is suppressed, also in characteristic two.

Degrees of products are read on the successive permuted colour pairs as in
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. This definition introduces
no new basis, trace or primitive-block assertion, and uses no choice
principle.

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation

$$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition
$(i\ i+1)$. For
$n=0,1$, the trivial group has the empty presentation.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix; let $W$ and $\ell$ be the presented group and its length and let $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ be the geometric representation, as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], with reflection set $T$ and sign-change sets $\Phi(w)$ as in that lemma. Parts (1) and (2) hold for every finite $S$, including the empty and singleton cases; a distinct pair is required only for part (3).

1. **Braid moves.** Call two words in $S$ *braid-equivalent* when one is obtained from the other by finitely many replacements of an alternating subword $s\,t\,s\,t\cdots$ of length $m(s,t)<\infty$ by the alternating word $t\,s\,t\,s\cdots$ of the same length. Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).
3. **Singleton detection in dihedral subgroups.** Fix distinct $s,t\in S$ and put $m:=m(s,t)$. The subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ is dihedral of order $2m$ when $m<\infty$ and infinite dihedral when $m=\infty$; every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ acts on the quotient $E/\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ as the identity, while for every $u\in S\setminus\{s,t\}$ one has $\sigma_u(\alpha_u)-\alpha_u=-2\alpha_u\notin\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ (no induced quotient map for $\sigma_u$ is assumed). Consequently
$$S\cap\langle s,t\rangle=\{s,t\},$$
and every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ has a reduced expression with all letters in $\{s,t\}$ (so the alternating words of length $q\le m$, and any $q$ when $m=\infty$, are reduced in $W$).

derivations.claim: A faithful KLR calculation, before quotient. Take independent dots $u,v,w$ and let $S_r$ swap positions, colours and dots. Define the following rational operators locally: equal crossings act by $D=(S-1)/(u-v)$ and unequal crossings by $Sc_{ij}$, where $c_{ij}=(1-p)/N_{ij}$ in DG or $(1-P)/N_{ij}$ in NG. The scalar pair-product identities [F1] give $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$, with $K=1,v-u,u-v,-(u-v)^2$. On equal colours direct multiplication gives $Df=(Sf)D+(Sf-f)/(u-v)$ and $D^2=0$; on unequal colours $Sc$ simply permutes dot coefficients. Here inverse differences are multiplication on the left, and $c$ is on the right of $S$. For three distinct colours both braid products have right coefficient $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$ at $W=S_1S_2S_1$. For $(i,i,k)$ both are $(W-S_1S_2)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{ik}(v,w)/(v-w)$; for $(i,k,k)$ both are $(W-S_2S_1)c_{ik}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)/(u-v)$, with denominators on the left. These two products of coefficients are symmetric in the equal-colour variables, so their divided-difference corrections vanish. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest terms cancel; the identity terms are $-K_{ij}(u,v)/(u-w)$ and $-K_{ij}(w,v)/(u-w)$, giving difference $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)=0,1,-1,u+w-2v$ in the four unequal cases. When all colours are equal, both words are $-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. These explicit operator products verify all KLR mixed, quadratic and braid relations of [F2]. This representation is faithful for formal dot coefficients: moving dots right by the proved sliding rule, use quadratic relations to remove repeated simple reflections and braid relations to reduce each crossing word to a chosen reduced word plus shorter words. This terminates by length (and the finite braid moves of [F3] at each fixed length), giving a spanning family $\psi_we(i)$. Each braid correction has fewer crossings and each quadratic reduction removes a pair; divided differences of formal series are formal series, so the same reduction works with formal coefficients. Its leading permutation coefficient is a product of nonzero $c_{ij}$ and of $1/(u-v)$ for equal pairs; proper subwords have smaller permutation length. Maximal-length comparison in the matrix crossed product therefore proves independence of the formal coefficients. Clearing finitely many temporary dot differences is legitimate in this faithful affine calculation. It does not assert faithfulness after taking the cyclotomic quotient.

The mixed and quadratic computations. In the representation of step 1.1, the displayed inverse Hecke element $\psi N-p$ (DG) or $\psi N-P$ (NG) is literally $S(1-\widehat p)-\widehat p$ or $S(1-\widehat P)-\widehat P$ on every word. On unequal colours this follows by cancellation of the right coefficient $N$; on equal colours $\psi=D$ and $D N-1=H$ by the equality $H+1=(S+1)(-N/(u-v))$. For a direct check, write this same inverse operator as $H_{AB}=a_{AB}S+b_{AB}$ with $(h,t)=(1,0)$ in DG and $(q,q-1)$ in NG, $b_{AB}=-(A-B)^{-1}$ in DG and $(1-q)B/(A-B)$ in NG, and $a_{AB}=h-b_{AB}$. Substitution gives $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$ and $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$; hence $H^2=tH+h$. Multiplication by $A,B$ gives the mixed relation $Hx_{r+1}-x_rH=1$ in DG, and $HX_rH=qX_{r+1}$ in NG, together with $H^2=1$ or $H^2=(q-1)H+q$. Alternatively the DG mixed constant on an unequal word is $(i_r-i_{r+1}+u-v)p=1$, and on an equal word it is $(u-v)+N=1$; in NG the same spectral substitution gives the stated mixed identity. Commuting dots, distant mixed relations and distant crossings follow because the operators involve disjoint pairs. By step 1.1 these are regular affine-KLR identities and hence evaluate in the nilpotent-dot quotient.

All five Hecke braid patterns. For a triple with distinct colours, adjacent repeated colours $(i,i,k)$ or $(i,k,k)$, outer repeated colours $(i,j,i)$, or all equal colours, the inverse elements of step 2.1 have precisely the same rational Hecke operator $H$ on each successive word. Expansion in the crossed product gives the same six coefficients for both braid words. In the order $1,S_1,S_2,S_1S_2,S_2S_1,S_1S_2S_1$, they are
$$b_{AC}(h+b_{AB}b_{BC}),\quad a_{AB}b_{BC}b_{AC},\quad a_{BC}b_{AB}b_{AC},\quad a_{AB}a_{AC}b_{BC},\quad a_{BC}a_{AC}b_{AB},\quad a_{AB}a_{AC}a_{BC}.$$
For example the first word's constant coefficient is $b_{AB}^2b_{BC}+a_{AB}a_{BA}b_{AC}$ and its $S_1$ coefficient is $a_{AB}(b_{AC}b_{BA}+b_{AB}b_{BC})$; the identities below reduce them to the displayed entries. The other entries follow by choosing the permutation terms in two or three factors; swapping $AB$ and $BC$ treats the other word. These formulas apply to all five patterns because $A,B,C$ are independent spectral variables, even when their colour labels coincide. The required scalar reductions are $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$, $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$, and $b_{AB}b_{BC}=b_{AC}(b_{AB}+b_{BC}-t)$, with $(h,t)=(1,0)$ or $(q,q-1)$. In the outer-repeated pattern the KLR braid correction $u+w-2v$ on a double edge was already included in the faithful model of step 1.1, so it is not suppressed by this table. In the equal pattern $D$ accounts for all divided-difference terms. Equality of the six explicit coefficients, followed by faithfulness, proves Hecke braid inside the formal KLR algebra; its regular expressions descend to the cyclotomic quotient. This proves the missing four cases and the all-equal case without assuming any Hecke intertwiner relation in that algebra.

The cyclotomic relation and the homomorphism. The cyclotomic relation $\prod_i(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$ (respectively $\prod_i(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}=0$) holds because $y_1^{(\Lambda,\alpha_{i_1})}e(i)=0$ is the cyclotomic KLR relation and $x_1=\sum_i(y_1+i_1)e(i)$ (respectively $X_1=\sum_iq^{i_1}(1-y_1)e(i)$) is a shift of the dot. Hence all defining relations of the affine cyclotomic quotient are satisfied, and the universal property of the presentation gives a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_d\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ carrying the generators to the displayed elements.

Identification of $\sigma(e(i))$. By [F2] the algebra $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite-dimensional, so it becomes a finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_d$-module through $\sigma$. Let $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a central content sector (possibly zero) as in
[[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]], with the residue
tuples $i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ contained in a fixed index set $I_\alpha$.

1. Set $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ in the degenerate case and
   $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ in the nondegenerate case
   ($1\le r\le d$). Then $y_1,\dots,y_d$ are commuting nilpotent elements of
   $H^\Lambda_\alpha$; consequently every rational expression displayed below,
   expanded as a power series in the nilpotent $y$'s, is a finite and
   well-defined element of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.
2. The power series
   $$p_r(i):=\begin{cases}1,&i_r=i_{r+1},\\ (i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1},&i_r\ne i_{r+1}\end{cases}$$
   (degenerate case), respectively
   $$P_r(i):=\begin{cases}1,&i_r=i_{r+1},\\ (1-q)\bigl(1-y_r(i)y_{r+1}(i)^{-1}\bigr)^{-1},&i_r\ne i_{r+1},\end{cases} \qquad y_r(i):=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$$
   (nondegenerate case), satisfy (3.23)–(3.25) respectively (4.24)–(4.26),
   (4.28)–(4.30) and (4.32); and the intertwining elements
   $$\varphi_r:=\sum_i\bigl(s_r+p_r(i)\bigr)e(i),\qquad \Phi_r:=\sum_i\bigl(T_r+P_r(i)\bigr)e(i)$$
   satisfy all identities (3.14)–(3.20) of the source's Lemma 3.1,
   respectively (4.14)–(4.20) of its Lemma 4.1.
3. There exist invertible power series $q_r(i)\in F[\![y_r,y_{r+1}]\!]$
   (respectively $Q_r(i)$) satisfying (3.27)–(3.29), respectively
   (4.33)–(4.35); the explicit candidates (3.30) respectively (4.36) do, and
   for them the identity (3.43) respectively (4.44) holds.

Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels
$0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant
weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). In the nondegenerate branch the
distinct spectral values of the labels are $q^i$, while in the degenerate
branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$). Fix
$\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put
$\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)\ge0$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The **affine Hecke algebra of type
$A_{d-1}$** at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators
$X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$X_rX_s=X_sX_r,\qquad X_rX_r^{-1}=1,$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1).$$
The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (which forces $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The
**degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with
generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$x_rx_s=x_sx_r,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_s=x_ss_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$s_r^2=1,\qquad s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1},\qquad s_rs_t=s_ts_r\quad(|r-t|>1);$$
its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis by
[[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**Conventions and boundary.** Put $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is
imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator, and $T_r$ acts on positions
$r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one
$\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the algebra $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke
algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$
([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]).
Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of
unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$)
are outside this page's cyclic scope and are recorded as a deferred boundary in
the batch notes. These presentations and the charged quotients are the ones of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no
embedding of the label set $I$ into $F$ is claimed in the nondegenerate branch,
and no choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: The cyclotomic and dot-sliding relations. Multiply the first-variable cyclotomic relation [F2] by $e(i)$. For every $j\ne i_1$, the factor $x_1-j$ on $e(i)$ in DG has nonzero constant $i_1-j$ plus a nilpotent, and the factor $X_1-q^j$ in NG has nonzero constant $q^{i_1}-q^j$ plus a nilpotent. Each is therefore invertible in that word corner by the finite geometric series. Cancelling these other-residue factors leaves $(x_1-i_1)^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(i)=0$ or $(X_1-q^{i_1})^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(i)=0$, respectively. Since these remaining factors are $y_1$ and $-q^{i_1}y_1$, this is exactly $y_1^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(i)=0$. If $\lambda_{i_1}=0$ it says $e(i)=0$. No invertibility on the complementary summands is needed. The dot and idempotent relations are immediate from the definitions of the idempotents $e(i)$ and the dots $y_r$, and the dot-sliding relations follow from the dot-sliding intertwiner identities, the definitions of $p_r(i),P_r(i)$ and the equal-colour case of the normalization.

Quadratic and all braid patterns. Work first in the faithful formal affine-Hecke calculation of the normalization supplier, then evaluate its regular identities in the sector. On equal colours the normalized intertwiner is $D=(S-1)/(u-v)$, so $D^2=0$ and $Dv-uD=1=vD-Du$. On unequal colours it is $Sc_{ij}(u,v)$, with $c=(1-p)/N$ in DG or $(1-P)/N$ in NG; its square is $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$, giving respectively $1,v-u,u-v,(v-u)(u-v)$. For the braid, put $W=S_1S_2S_1$ and dots $u,v,w$. Distinct colours give both words $Wc_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$. For $(i,i,k)$ both words are $(W-S_1S_2)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{ik}(v,w)/(v-w)$; for $(i,k,k)$ they are $(W-S_2S_1)c_{ik}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)/(u-v)$, with denominators on the left and coefficient products on the right. The products are symmetric in the two equal-colour variables, so their divided differences vanish. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest terms cancel and the identity coefficients differ by $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)$; direct substitution gives $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$. On all equal colours the common value is $-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. These are the supplier's explicit local computations, using only affine-Hecke relations and scalar normalizers, not the opposite relation-map lemma. The double-edge correction and its sign remain valid in characteristic two. Clearing temporary differences in the faithful formal calculation gives regular relations; only those relations, and unit coefficients, are evaluated on nilpotent dots. Hence each of the BK quadratic and braid equations holds in $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

The homomorphism. The verified relations are exactly the presentation of $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ recalled in [F2] and in [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], so the universal property of that presentation gives a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ sending the generators to the displayed elements. No choice principle is used.

Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 verify all relations of the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR presentation for $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$, and step 2.1 invokes the universal property to produce $\rho$. The zero sector is included: all constructions are supported on the projectors $e(i)$, which may vanish.

derivations.claim: The forward composite on dots and crossings. On each KLR word the map $\sigma$ kills all idempotents outside content $\alpha$; in particular, since the inverse polynomial generators of $R$ have exactly the eigenword projectors $e(\nu)$ (the nilpotent dots shift distinct scalar eigenvalues), $\sigma(e_\alpha)=1_R$ and $\sigma$ annihilates every other central sector. The composite $\sigma\rho$ fixes $y_r$ by [F2], and on a crossing $\sigma\bigl(\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}e(i)\bigr) =\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)+P_r(i)\bigr)Q_r(i)^{-1}e(i)=\psi_re(i),$ using the definitions of the local generating elements in [[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]]; the degenerate case is the same computation with $\varphi_r,p_r,q_r$ in place of $\Phi_r,P_r,Q_r$. These are literal ordered expressions, not a commutation of $\psi_r$ with its coefficient. Hence $\sigma\rho$ fixes every presentation generator of $R^\Lambda_\alpha$.

The reverse composite on generators. By [F2] the composite $\rho\sigma$ fixes the idempotents and dots; on a word, $\rho\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)\bigr)e(i) =\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}Q_r(i)e(i)-P_r(i)e(i) =T_re(i)$ in the nondegenerate case, and the same with $s_r$ in the degenerate case. Again the evaluation is a finite expression in the nilpotent variables. For the polynomial generators the computations are $\rho\sigma(x_re_\alpha)=\sum_i((x_r-i_r)+i_r)e(i)=x_re_\alpha$ in DG and $\rho\sigma(X_re_\alpha)=\sum_iq^{i_r}(1-(1-q^{-i_r}X_r))e(i)=X_re_\alpha$ in NG; their inverses are fixed because homomorphisms preserve inverses. Along with the projector identities of [F1], these verify every presentation generator of both algebras, including the correct inverse NG substitution. Hence $\rho\sigma$ fixes every presentation generator of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

Mutual inverses and the zero-sector statement. Both composites fix all generators of their source algebras, so $\rho\sigma=\operatorname{id}$ and $\sigma\rho=\operatorname{id}$; in particular the maps are algebra isomorphisms, and on idempotents they are the literal identity. If $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ then the already constructed $\sigma$ would satisfy $\sigma(e_\alpha)=1_R$ with $e_\alpha=0$, forcing $1_R=0$; conversely the forward identities force $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ if $R^\Lambda_\alpha=0$. Summing the isomorphisms over the finite set of height-$d$ contents and using that the $e_\alpha$ are central orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$ by [F3] gives $H^\Lambda_d\cong\bigoplus_\alpha R^\Lambda_\alpha$. derivations.claim: The associated graded. Give $x_i$ degree $1$ and the symmetric group degree $0$. By [F1] the transported relation has leading term $x_i^\ell$ with all other dot terms of total degree below $\ell$, and the bounded reduction sends monomials of dot degree $\le r$ to bounded monomials of dot degree $\le r$; independence of the bounded basis makes these the filtration steps $F_r$. The leading mixed relations give the variable permutation action of $S_d$, and the transported relations give $x_i^\ell=0$ in the associated graded. Hence the natural surjection $F[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^\ell,\dots,X_d^\ell)\rtimes FS_d \longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}H_d^\Lambda$ is an isomorphism: the bounded monomials of the truncated algebra map degree-by-degree onto the basis of [F1]. [F1, F2, algebra]

Symmetric polynomials are central. For $x=x_i$, $y=x_{i+1}$, $s=s_i$ the relations of [F2] give, by induction on products, $sg(x,y)-g(y,x)s=\frac{g(y,x)-g(x,y)}{x-y}$ for every polynomial $g$; the quotient is a polynomial because the numerator vanishes at $x=y$. Applying this to a polynomial symmetric in $x,y$ shows that it commutes with $s$, and a globally symmetric polynomial commutes with every $s_i$ and every $x_j$, hence is central in $H_d^\Lambda$. No division by an integer or by $x-y$ inside the algebra is used. [F2, algebra]

Cycle coefficients in the graded centralizer. In $B=F[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^\ell,\dots,X_d^\ell)\rtimes FS_d$, put $h_r(I)=\sum X^b$ over $0\le b_i<\ell$ and $\sum_{i\in I}b_i=(|I|-1)(\ell-1)+r$, and $A^{(r)}=h_r(I)A$ for a cycle $A$ on $I$, $0\le r<\ell$. For a coefficient $gA$ commuting with the $X_i$, the equations are $(X_i-X_{A(i)})g=0$. On one cycle they equate coefficients obtained by transferring one unit between consecutive coordinates, with out-of-range coefficients interpreted as zero. At fixed total degree, transfer units until the first $|I|-1$ coordinates are $\ell-1$. If the total is $(|I|-1)(\ell-1)+r$, every coefficient equals the coefficient at $(\ell-1,\dots,\ell-1,r)$; if the total is smaller, the same transfers reach a zero coordinate followed by a transfer to exponent $-1$, and all coefficients vanish. Thus the solutions on that cycle have basis $h_0(I),\dots,h_{\ell-1}(I)$. For disjoint cycles apply these equations separately to each coefficient in the monomial basis of the complementary variables; this gives exactly the products of disjoint colored cycles as the polynomial centralizer basis. This argument also covers $\ell=1$: the truncated polynomial ring is $F$, and its centralizer is $FS_d$. [step 1.1, algebra]

Reduced-degree powers. Write $f(t)=t^\ell+c_1t^{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_\ell$. The mixed relations give $x_{i+1}^\ell=s_ix_i^\ell s_i+\sum_{t=0}^{\ell-1}x_i^t x_{i+1}^{\ell-1-t}s_i$. Starting with $x_1^\ell=-\sum_{a=1}^\ell c_ax_1^{\ell-a}$, induction on $i$ shows that $x_i^\ell$ has filtration degree at most $\ell-1$ and symbol $Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1}$ there, where $Y_i=\sum_{j<i}(j\ i)^{(0)}$. For $k=p\ell+r$, $0\le r<\ell$, it follows that $x_i^k$ has filtration degree at most $p(\ell-1)+r$ and symbol $(Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1})^pX_i^r$. This is a reduced degree: the ordinary degree-$k$ symbol may be zero. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

Orbit sums and colored-cycle multiplication. Conjugation permutes the basis of step 2.1, so its fixed vectors have basis the orbit sums $z_\lambda$, indexed by colored cycle types, including trivial color-zero fixed points to fill rank $d$. No averaging is used. If $|I\cap J|=c>0$, direct multiplication gives $h_r(I)h_s(J)=\ell^{c-1}h_{r+s+(c-1)(\ell-1)}(I\cup J)$. For $c=1$, fixing the exponents away from the common variable fixes its exponent uniquely and gives the asserted coefficient one. For $c=2$, the basic repeated-edge computation is $h_0(i,j)^2=\ell X_i^{\ell-1}X_j^{\ell-1}$: only equal complementary exponents survive, with exactly $\ell$ choices. Joining the remaining common variables successively reduces the general case to these two computations. Consequently disjoint colored cycles commute; two cycles meeting at one point multiply to their merged cycle of color $r+s$; when they meet in at least two points the product vanishes unless $r=s=0$, and otherwise is a scalar times disjoint cycles all of color $\ell-1$. Indeed the displayed exponent equals the maximal degree on the union when $c=2$, and exceeds it when $c>2$ and $\ell>1$; when $\ell=1$ every polynomial coefficient is one and the assertion reduces to ordinary cycle multiplication. Iterating gives disjoint-cycle reductions, never increasing the union of supports. [step 2.1, algebra]

The star-cycle expansion. Let $y_i(p\ell+r)$ be the sum of $(j_1\ \cdots\ j_p\ i)^{(r)}$ over ordered, distinct $j_1,\dots,j_p<i$, and let $y_i(0)=1$. Expanding $Y_i^p$, sequences with distinct leaves give precisely $y_i(p\ell)$: the product of the star transpositions is one cycle, with a unique ordered leaf sequence for each such cycle. Any repeated leaf uses at most $p$ vertices including $i$; at its first repetition the intersecting cycles have at least two common vertices, so step 3.1 turns the result into saturated (color $\ell-1$) disjoint cycles or zero. Further star factors preserve saturation by the one-point rule, or vanish by the multiple-point rule. The term $X_i^{\ell-1}$ is itself a saturated singleton containing $i$; choosing it anywhere in $(Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1})^p$ has the same consequence and uses at most $p$ vertices. Thus this power equals $y_i(p\ell)$ plus saturated disjoint-cycle products on at most $p$ vertices, always with $i$ in their support. Multiplication by $X_i^r$ gives exactly $y_i(p\ell+r)$ when $r>0$, because it raises the color of the distinct-leaf cycle to $r$, while every saturated error containing $i$ vanishes. (For $\ell=1$ there is no $r>0$ case.) This proves the complete power-symbol formula, including $p=0$. [step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

Filtration descent. If $z\in Z(H_d^\Lambda)$ has filtration degree $D$, its degree-$D$ symbol lies in $Z(B)$. By step 5.1 it is a linear combination of degree-$D$ symbols of central symmetric evaluations $p_\mu$; subtract that same combination in $H_d^\Lambda$ to lower the filtration degree. Repeating terminates because degrees are nonnegative; in degree zero the same triangular basis applies, and the next filtration step is zero. Thus every central element is a symmetric-polynomial evaluation, and step 1.2 proves the reverse inclusion. Rank zero was handled separately. No division by $\ell$, $d!$ or the field characteristic occurs. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 5.1] ∎

citations.quote: Let $R=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ with $\ell\ge1$, and let $H_n$ be the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] at the first polynomial $\prod_a(X_1-U_a)$.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with $T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]): 1.

Let $R=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ with $\ell\ge1$, and let $H_n$ be the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] at the first polynomial $\prod_a(X_1-U_a)$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is $$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$ The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.
For $n\ge1$ and $A,B\in M_n(R)$ over a commutative ring, $$\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B).$$

derivations.claim: The trace and its dual basis. Define $\tau\colon H_n\to R$ by $\tau(\mathcal B)=1$ at the zero-dot identity word and $0$ at every other PBW basis element, extended $R$-linearly; by [F1] this is well defined over $R$ and after base change. Put $J_1=1$ and $J_i=q_H^{-1}T_{i-1}J_{i-1}T_{i-1}$ in the finite Hecke subalgebra; the $J_i$ are units. Define the second family $\mathcal C=\bigl\{T_vJ_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_n^{\delta(c_n)} X_1^{c_1}\cdots X_n^{c_n}:0\le c_i<\ell,\ v\in S_n\bigr\},\qquad \delta(0)=0,\ \delta(c)=-1\ (c>0).$ The standard anti-involution fixing the presentation generators fixes each $X_i$, so $\mathcal B^*=\{T_vX^c\}$ is a basis; at each fixed profile $c$, multiplying the finite Hecke factor by the unit $J_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_n^{\delta(c_n)}$ is an invertible $R$-linear change of the finite Hecke basis. Hence $\mathcal C$ is an $R$-basis of $H_n$. [F1, construct]

Cyclicity for $X_1$ via the tower. At rank one the algebra is commutative, so cyclicity is immediate; for the induction assume $n\ge2$. Identify $H_{n-1}$ with the subalgebra on $X_1,\dots,X_{n-1},T_1,\dots,T_{n-2}$; its bounded words are a subset of $\mathcal B$. Put $v_k=s_{n-1}\cdots s_k$ for $1\le k<n$ and $v_n=1$; the decomposition $w=uv_k$ with $u\in S_{n-1}$ is length additive, so $\{X_n^aT_{v_k}:0\le a<\ell,\ 1\le k\le n\}$ is a left $H_{n-1}$-basis of $H_n$. Define the left-linear projection $E_n\colon H_n\to H_{n-1}$ to be $1$ on $X_n^0T_{v_n}$ and $0$ on the other basis elements, and $\tau_n=\tau_{n-1}\circ E_n$. With $V=T_{n-1}\cdots T_1$ and $U=(T_{n-1}-q_H+1)\cdots(T_1-q_H+1)$, the mixed relation gives $VX_1=X_nU$, and [F2] gives $VX_1^m=X_n^mU+J_m$, where every term of $J_m$ has total dot degree $m$ and $X_n$-degree between $1$ and $m-1$ (the leading branch transfers the full exponent, each correction transfers a strictly smaller positive exponent, and no variable above $n$ occurs). For $m\le\ell$ every lower exponent in $J_m$ is below $\ell$, so $E_n(J_m)=0$; likewise $E_n(X_n^mU)=0$ for $1\le m<\ell$. Multiplying the first-dot relation $f(X_1)=0$ by $V$ gives $0=X_n^\ell U+J_\ell+\sum_{m=1}^{\ell-1}c_m(X_n^mU+J_m)+c_0V$, and applying $E_n$ yields $E_n(X_n^\ell U)=0$, which completes the missing case $m=\ell$. To verify right $X_1$-linearity, test the displayed left tower basis $X_n^aT_{v_k}$. For $k\ge2$, $T_{v_k}$ and $X_n$ commute with $X_1$; its projection is zero unless $a=0,k=n$, where the equality is immediate. For $k=1$, $VX_1=X_nU$ gives $E_n(X_n^aVX_1)=E_n(X_n^{a+1}U)=0$ for $0\le a<\ell$: bounded positive exponents project to zero, and the endpoint $a+1=\ell$ was just established. Left $H_{n-1}$-linearity then extends the equality to every $h$. Hence $E_n(hX_1)=E_n(h)X_1$ for all $h$, and by left linearity $E_n(X_1h)=X_1E_n(h)$; induction on $n$ gives $\tau_n(X_1h)=\tau_n(hX_1)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

Cyclicity for the finite generators. Let $p=X^a$ be a bounded dot monomial and $w\in S_n$. By [F2], $T_jp=(s_jp)T_j+(1-q_H)X_{j+1}\frac{p-s_jp}{X_j-X_{j+1}};$ for $p=X_j^aX_{j+1}^b$ times the other variables, the correction monomials have the same total dot degree and both displayed exponents at most $\max(a,b)<\ell$ (the exponents run as $(a-1-k,b+1+k)$ or $(a+k,b-k)$), so when the exponent profile is positive every term on either side of $\tau(T_jpT_w)=\tau(pT_wT_j)$ has a positive bounded profile and evaluates to $0$. When $p=1$, the finite Hecke multiplication formula [F1] gives coefficient of $1$ in $T_jT_w$, respectively $T_wT_j$, equal to $q_H$ if $w=s_j$ and $0$ otherwise. This proves $\tau(T_jh)=\tau(hT_j)$ without using the trace one is proving. [F1, F2, algebra]

Generation and symmetry. The elements $X_1,T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ generate $H_n$ as an $R$-algebra: the constant term $c_0=(-1)^\ell\prod_aQ_a$ is a unit, so $f(X_1)=0$ makes $X_1^{-1}$ a polynomial in $X_1$; each $T_j^{-1}=q_H^{-1}(T_j-q_H+1)$; and $X_r=q_H^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$, with inverses expressed likewise. Moving the generators of a word one at a time around $\tau$, using steps 1.2 and 1.3, gives $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ for every pair of words, hence for all $a,b$ by $R$-bilinearity; the pairing $(a,b)\mapsto\tau(ab)$ is associative and symmetric. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

Restricted-profile zero values. For $0\le j\le n$ let $U_j$ be the span of the PBW words whose dot entries above $j$ vanish, all finite permutations included. It is a right finite-Hecke module. Multiplying its dot part by any polynomial in $X_1,\dots,X_j$ stays in $U_j$: transport the first cyclotomic relation successively only through $T_1,\dots,T_{j-1}$, so each resulting relation reduces a power of $X_i$, $i\le j$, using variables of index at most $i$ and finite words of indices below $i$; repeated Bernstein straightening and the bounded reduction of [F1] therefore never introduce a variable above $j$. In particular $U_j$ is the dot algebra on its first $j$ variables times the finite Hecke algebra. For $1\le k<\ell$ and $h\in U_j$, $\tau(X_{j+1}^kh)=0$, directly from the bounded basis, since the new exponent is positive and bounded. This statement concerns $h\in U_j$, rather than arbitrary $h\in H_n$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

Transferred restricted-profile powers. Write $q=q_H$. For $1\le i\le j+1\le n$, $1\le k\le\ell$ and $h\in U_j$ we claim $\tau(X_{j+1}^kh)=q^{i-j-1}\tau(T_j\cdots T_iX_i^kT_i\cdots T_jh)$, with empty chains when $i=j+1$. The mixed relations give $X_i^k=q^{-1}T_{i-1}X_{i-1}^kT_{i-1}+q^{-1}(q-1)\sum_{c=1}^{k-1}X_i^cX_{i-1}^{k-c}T_{i-1}$, by induction on $k$ using that $T_{i-1}$ commutes with $X_{i-1}X_i$. To descend from $i$ to $i-1$, it suffices to show every correction has trace zero. Put $A=T_j\cdots T_i$, $B=T_i\cdots T_j$. For $0<c<k$, the mixed relation and the formula $X_{j+1}=q^{i-j-1}AX_iB$ give the exact identity $AX_i^cX_{i-1}^{k-c}T_{i-1}Bh=q^{j-i+1}AX_i^{c-1}X_{i-1}^{k-c-1}T_{i-1}A^{-1}X_{j+1}X_{i-1}h$: substitute $B=q^{j-i+1}X_i^{-1}A^{-1}X_{j+1}$ and use $X_iT_{i-1}X_i^{-1}=X_{i-1}^{-1}T_{i-1}X_{i-1}$. Expand $X_i^{c-1}X_{i-1}^{k-c-1}T_{i-1}A^{-1}$ in the reversed PBW order $\sum a_{w,b}T_wX^b$ using $T_a^{-1}=q^{-1}(T_a+1-q)$. Bernstein straightening swaps the two exponents or replaces them by intermediate exponents, so every exponent stays nonnegative and at most $\max(c-1,k-c-1)\le k-2$; variables have index at most $j+1$. Cyclicity from step 2.1 makes the trace of each correction a sum of traces of $X_{j+1}^{1+b_{j+1}}(X_1^{b_1}\cdots X_j^{b_j})X_{i-1}hAT_w$. The parenthesized remaining factor lies in $U_j$ by step 2.2, and $1\le1+b_{j+1}\le k-1<\ell$, so each trace is zero. Downward induction proves the claim, including $k=1$, whose correction sum is empty. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

The cyclotomic endpoint. Apply step 3.1 with $i=1$, $k=\ell$. In $\tau(q^{-j}T_j\cdots T_1X_1^\ell T_1\cdots T_jh)$ replace $X_1^\ell$ using its first cyclotomic relation. Each positive power $X_1^k$, $k<\ell$, transfers back to $X_{j+1}^k$ by step 3.1 and contributes zero by step 2.2. The constant term contributes $\alpha\tau(J_{j+1}h)$, where $\alpha=-f(0)=(-1)^{\ell+1}Q_1\cdots Q_\ell$ and $J_{j+1}=q^{-j}T_j\cdots T_1T_1\cdots T_j$. Thus $\tau(X_{j+1}^\ell h)=\alpha\tau(hJ_{j+1})$ for every $h\in U_j$. For $j=0$ this follows directly from the first polynomial; for $\ell=1$ there are no positive-power intermediate terms. The restriction on $h$ is essential. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

The full Gram blocks. Let $\mathcal B_j$ and $\mathcal C_j$ be the parts of the two bases with entries above $j$ zero, and let $G_j=(\tau(bc))$ be their matrix, of size $N_j=\ell^jn!$. For new profiles $b,c$ at position $j+1$, cyclicity and commuting dots rewrite an entry as $\tau(X_{j+1}^{b+c}hJ_{j+1}^{\delta(c)})$, where $h=X_1^{b_1+c_1}\cdots X_j^{b_j+c_j}T_wT_vJ_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_j^{\delta(c_j)}\in U_j$ by step 2.2; earlier combined exponents may exceed $\ell-1$, and that same reduction argument is why this remains in $U_j$. If $b=c=0$ the block is $G_j$. If $0<b+c<\ell$ it is zero by step 2.2. If $b+c=\ell$, then $c>0$ and step 4.1 cancels the last $J_{j+1}^{-1}$, giving the block $\alpha G_j$. Order rows by $b=0,1,\dots,\ell-1$ and columns by $c=0,\ell-1,\dots,1$. The row and column at zero have only $G_j$ at their intersection. Among positive rows and columns the blocks above the diagonal have $b+c<\ell$ and vanish, the diagonal has $b+c=\ell$, and blocks below may be arbitrary. Hence $G_{j+1}$ is block lower triangular with diagonal $G_j,\alpha G_j,\dots,\alpha G_j$, so $\det G_{j+1}=\pm\alpha^{(\ell-1)N_j}(\det G_j)^\ell$. At $j=0$, $G_0=(\tau(T_wT_v))$ has entry $q^{\operatorname{length}(w)}\delta_{v,w^{-1}}$ by [F1], and its determinant is a unit. Induction gives a unit determinant for $G_n$; since $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$ are bases, the pairing identifies $H_n$ with its $R$-dual. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1, algebra]

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda$ be the set of partitions
of $n$ ordered by dominance $\unrhd$
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]), and for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let
$T(\lambda)=\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ be the set of standard $\lambda$-tableaux
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). Then the **Murphy basis
theorem** holds: the family
$$\mathcal M=\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$$
is an $R$-basis of $H$, and $(\mathcal M,\Lambda)$ is a cellular basis of $H$ in
the sense of [[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]. Explicitly:
(i) $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all $\lambda$ and $s,t$; and (ii) for every
$\lambda$, every $t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ and every $h\in H$ there exist
$r_v\in R$ with
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}},$$
where $H^{\rhd\lambda}$ is spanned by the $m_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. The
theorem holds over every commutative coefficient ring with $q\in R^{\times}$
and assumes no semisimplicity; the total number of Murphy elements is
$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}|\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)|^2=n!$
([[cor-sum-of-squares-of-standard-tableau-numbers]]), matching the rank of $H$.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with
generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with
$T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]):

1. $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$; in particular $H_v(n)$ is
free of rank $n!$ over $A$;
2. for every $w\in S_n$ and every $1\le i\le n-1$,
$$T_wT_i=T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad T_wT_i=(v-1)T_w+v\,T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1,$$
where $\ell$ is the inversion length of $S_n$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]); consequently the rule rewrites
every monomial in the generators as an $A$-linear combination of the $T_w$.

No choice principle is used.

For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation

$$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition
$(i\ i+1)$. For
$n=0,1$, the trivial group has the empty presentation.

For every commutative ring $R$ with invertible parameter $z$, the ordinary
finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_n$ and a composition $\rho$ of $n$, the
permutation module $x_\rho H_n$ has $R$-basis
$$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\rho(s)=S}m_{st},$$
where $S$ ranges over the semistandard tableaux of partition shape and type
$\rho$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of the same shape. It has a Specht
filtration with multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$ of the
ordinary Specht module $S^\lambda$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). The row-double-coset
membership uses each coset word once and no quantum-factorial division. Over
the generic field this number equals the trivial-character multiplicity of the
$\rho$-row parabolic in $S^\lambda$. Moreover the explicit ordinary Garnir
row-coset identity, the additive nonstandard-tableau factorization and the
same-column generator refinement
$$T_am_{st}\equiv-m_{st}+\sum_{u\rhd s}c_um_{ut}\pmod{\text{higher shapes}}$$
hold when $a,a+1$ are in one column of the standard tableau $s$; row-standard straightening has no smaller-shape terms and its same-shape
terms increase tableau-prefix dominance. Shape support uses the already proved
ordinary Murphy dominance ideals
([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]],
[[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]); the finite Garnir
algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before that
dominance refinement.

For every $n\ge0$,
$$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}(f^\lambda)^2=n!,$$
where $f^\lambda$ is the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux and
$f^\varnothing=1$, $0!=1$.

Every component-preserving row-standard multitableau factors its distinguished permutation into a permutation inside the contiguous component intervals followed by the unique shuffle of the intervals preserving internal order; the two inversion sets are disjoint, so the factorization is length-additive. Multiplying by $u_\lambda$ (which commutes with the Hecke generators internal to the intervals), ordinary Murphy straightening applies in each component; higher ordinary component shapes preserve component sizes and strictly increase multipartition dominance, and the final component shuffle relabels each component by an increasing list whose selected entries at any cutoff are an initial segment, so tableau-prefix inequalities are exactly the ordinary ones at the corresponding initial-segment length. For a fixed initial left row and right multiplication by $T_i$: if $ts_i$ is standard the length formula gives the usual standard term (or $q_H$ times it plus $(q_H-1)m_{t^\lambda t}$); if $i,i+1$ share a row the result is $q_Hm$; and if they share a component but the interchange fails standardness, factoring out the increasing component shuffle and applying the ordinary cell law gives same-shape terms with the same initial left row and strictly higher multipartition terms, the required transfer identity $T_cT_i=T_jT_c$ following from $cs_i=s_jc$ and the length/quadratic formula. A cross-component column failure is impossible because column standardness is imposed componentwise. u$, which strictly dominates $\lambda$: the cumulative total through component $k-1$ strictly increases and no later cumulative sum decreases. Hence $x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. For $k=1$, nonemptiness of component $1$ forces $a_s\ge1$ for all $s\ge2$, so $u_b$ contains every factor $(X_1-Q_s)$ and vanishes by the cyclotomic relation; again $x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$.

Right multiplication by $X_1$. Let $t$ be standard with entry $1$ in component $k$, an initial node, and initial label $a+1$ with $a=a_k$. Then $d(t)=(s_a\cdots s_1)w$ with $w$ fixing $1$ and $\ell(d(t))=a+\ell(w)$: pulling label $a+1$ to value $1$ crosses exactly the $a$ smaller initial labels, whose final values exceed $1$. A permutation fixing $1$ has a reduced word in $s_2,\dots,s_{n-1}$, so $T_w$ commutes with $X_1$. Multiplying the identity of step 1.2 on the right by $(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}$ and then by $T_w$ gives $m_\lambda T_{d(t)}X_1=q_H^aQ_km_\lambda(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}T_w +q_H^ax_\lambda u_b(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}T_w,$ whose second term lies in $N^{>\lambda}$ by step 1.2 and finite-generator stability, and whose first term lies modulo $N^{>\lambda}$ in the fixed-initial-row span. Hence that span is stable under $X_1$; multiplying on the left by $T_{d(s)}^*$ and using the left stability of the higher shapes gives the coefficient-independence law $m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$ first for each generator and then for every word, with coefficients independent of $s$, and $*$ makes the higher spans two-sided. Since $X_r=q_H^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$ and the cyclotomic constant term is a unit when the $Q_a$ are invertible, these generators generate the Laurent affine quotient.

Spanning and cellularity. The smallest multipartition $\omega=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$ satisfies $u_\omega=x_\omega=m_\omega=1$, so the generator-stable span of the standard $m_{st}$ contains $1$ and is all of $H_n$: the Murphy family spans. By [[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], $H_n$ is independently free of rank $\ell^nn!$. Counting standard pairs with the ordinary identity $\sum_{\rho\vdash m}f_\rho^2=m!$ at the component sizes $n_a$ contributes $(n!)^2/\prod_an_a!$, and summing over the multipartition compositions gives $\ell^nn!$ by the multinomial theorem. The spanning family therefore has exactly the independent rank; its coefficient matrix in the ordered PBW basis is square and surjective between free modules, hence invertible, so the family is an $R$-basis and the proved involution and coefficient-independence laws are actual cellularity. Tensoring the proved basis and presentation supplies every commutative specialization with unit parameters, including repeated charges in the nondegenerate charged branch and the LM deformation DVR; the additive degenerate branch is a different presentation and is not a Laurent-parameter specialization; no generic-flatness inference is made. Rank zero is the singleton empty basis.

$\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a
basis and a dominance-cellular datum:
$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$

actual two-sided ideals. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters
inherits the cellular basis; in particular the arbitrary-field finite-$e$
nondegenerate charged specializations ($q_H\ne1$) and the LM deformation DVR retain it. The specialization $z=1$ here is the multiplicative presentation with $T_i^2=1$, not the additive degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra. The universal

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$

For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the

$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$

$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$

semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

derivations.claim: Initial-row eigenvalues. Consider only a nonempty component $k$ and put $a=a_k$; empty components contribute no nodes or JM eigenvalues. Then [F1] gives $m_\lambda(X_{a+1}-Q_k)=x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. The internal finite Hecke submodule generated by $m_\lambda$ modulo higher global shapes is spanned by standard internal component permutations; each such permutation fixes the smallest internal label $a+1$ (that label occupies the first node of its component), so its Hecke element has a reduced word in the internal generators with indices at least $a+2$ and commutes with $X_{a+1}$. Hence $X_{a+1}$ acts as the scalar $Q_k$ on that whole submodule, with errors in the two-sided ideal $N^{>\lambda}$. The $X$-recurrence then identifies $X_{a+i}$ on this submodule with $Q_k$ times the ordinary multiplicative Jucys–Murphy element $M_i$ of [F2], by induction from the finite quadratic relation and the additive-JM recurrence (a polynomial identity also at $q_H=1$). Ordinary JM triangularity gives diagonal $Q_kq_H^{c-r}$ at the node $(r,c,k)$ occupied by local entry $i$: the internal label $i$ is not a row index, and no extra subtraction of $i-1$ occurs. For the initial component tableau, which is maximal in tableau dominance, there are no strictly more dominant same-shape terms. Thus for the node $(r,c,k)$ carrying global entry $t$, $m_\lambda X_t\equiv Q_kq_H^{c-r}m_\lambda\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$.

JM triangularity for every standard multitableau. Inducting through a reduced word of $w$, the relations [F1] give $T_wX_r=X_{w(r)}T_w+\sum_{v<w}\sum_ba_{(v,b)}X_bT_v,$ where the corrections are supported on proper Bruhat subwords (at the first correction a generator is deleted, moving its linear $X$-coefficient through preceding generators deletes further generators, and finite quadratic multiplication preserves Bruhat support). Applying this with $w=d(t)$ and multiplying by $m_\lambda$ on the left, step 1.1 evaluates every surviving $X$ coefficient modulo higher shapes; a correction $m_\lambda T_v$ reduces first to a row-standard representative $d(u)$ of its Young-subgroup coset, the removed row subgroup contributing its row eigenvalue, with $d(u)\le v<d(t)$; the Bruhat/tableau-prefix relation on the ordered rows of all components then makes $u$ strictly dominate $t$, and componentwise straightening of $u$ keeps the shape or produces same-shape tableaux at least $u$ in prefix dominance, hence strictly dominating $t$. The leading eigenvalue is $Q_kq_H^{j-i}$ at the node carrying $r$, because $w(r)$ is its initial-row label under $t=t^\lambda\cdot w=w^{-1}\cdot t^\lambda$. Therefore $m_{(t^\lambda,t)}X_r\equiv Q_kq_H^{j-i}m_{(t^\lambda,t)} +\sum_{v\lhd t}a_vm_{(t^\lambda,v)}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}},$ the exact arbitrary-level JM content statement, independent of an affine center theorem, semisimplicity or block classification.

On the resulting Specht module a total ordering extending tableau dominance triangularizes all the $X_r$ simultaneously; the one-dimensional successive quotients have exactly the content characters of step 2.1, so every simultaneous generalized eigenword is among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i\pmod e$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] for the ordinary part); the residue multiplicities of every such word equal the node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$, since permuting the labels of a standard tableau does not change the multiset of node residues. [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], and let

   are $R$-bases of $H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$, and the same two families are bases

2. left multiplication by any nonzero element of the Laurent polynomial

$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$

For every commutative ring $R$ with invertible parameter $z$, the ordinary
finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_n$ and a composition $\rho$ of $n$, the
permutation module $x_\rho H_n$ has $R$-basis
$$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\rho(s)=S}m_{st},$$
where $S$ ranges over the semistandard tableaux of partition shape and type
$\rho$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of the same shape. It has a Specht
filtration with multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$ of the
ordinary Specht module $S^\lambda$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). The row-double-coset
membership uses each coset word once and no quantum-factorial division. Over
the generic field this number equals the trivial-character multiplicity of the
$\rho$-row parabolic in $S^\lambda$. Moreover the explicit ordinary Garnir
row-coset identity, the additive nonstandard-tableau factorization and the
same-column generator refinement
$$T_am_{st}\equiv-m_{st}+\sum_{u\rhd s}c_um_{ut}\pmod{\text{higher shapes}}$$
hold when $a,a+1$ are in one column of the standard tableau $s$; row-standard straightening has no smaller-shape terms and its same-shape
terms increase tableau-prefix dominance. Shape support uses the already proved
ordinary Murphy dominance ideals
([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]],
[[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]); the finite Garnir
algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before that
