citations.quote:
Work with the arbitrary-level Murphy/Schur datum of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over
either (i) the fraction field $K$ of the universal Laurent parameter ring,
including the generic field of the Lyle–Mathas deformation, or (ii) any field
$F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$ under the deformation
$z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$ in $F(t)$. Let $b_\lambda$ be the Murphy cellular
form on the Specht module $V_\lambda$ with basis $v_s$ over standard
tableaux $s$ and $v_0=v_{t^\lambda}$; put
$B_k=\sum_{a\le k}|\nu^{(a)}|$,
$u_\nu=\prod_{k=2}^{\ell}\prod_{r=1}^{B_{k-1}}(X_r-U_k)$,
$x_\nu=\sum_{w\in\mathfrak S_\nu}T_w$, $m_\nu=u_\nu x_\nu$, let $A_\nu$ be
the action of $m_\nu$ on $V_\lambda$, let
$P_\nu(z)=\sum_{w\in\mathfrak S_\nu}z^{\ell(w)}$, and let
$$f_s=v_s+\sum_{r\triangleright s}a_{sr}v_r,\qquad \gamma_s=b_\lambda(f_s,f_s)$$
be the monic simultaneous Jucys–Murphy eigenbasis and its norms. Let
$G_{\lambda\nu}$ be the Schur cellular Gram matrix on the type-$\nu$ basis of
$\Delta(\lambda)$, indexed by the semistandard $T$ of shape $\lambda$ and type
$\nu$, and for such $T$ let $t_T$ be its dominance-minimal standard
refinement, $r_x=U_{a(x)}z^{\operatorname{content}(x)}$ the residue of the node
$x$ of $\lambda$, and $a_T(x)$ the type component of the label of $x$. Then
$$\det G_{\lambda\nu}=\prod_{T\in\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)}\frac{\gamma_{t_T}}{C_{t_T}\,u_T},\qquad C_t=\prod_{i<j\ \mathrm{same\ type\ row}}\frac{z\,r_t(j)-r_t(i)}{r_t(j)-r_t(i)},\qquad u_T=\prod_x\prod_{b>a_T(x)}(r_x-U_b),$$
with empty determinant $1$. The monic transition determinant from the
semistandard basis $(w_T)$ to the chain basis $(g_T)$ is exactly $1$.
Equivalently, with $C(A,B)=\frac{zB-A}{B-A}$,
$R(A,B)=\frac{(zB-A)(B-zA)}{(B-A)^2}$ and
$\mathcal C(T),\mathcal I(T)$ the pair lists of the proof,
$$\det G_{\lambda\nu}=\prod_TB_T\prod_{x<y}C(r_x,r_y)^{c_{xy}}R(r_x,r_y)^{i_{xy}},\qquad B_T=\prod_x\prod_{a(x)<b\le a_T(x)}(r_x-U_b),$$
where $c_{xy},i_{xy}$ are explicit nonnegative semistandard counts. All
factors are nonzero in the stated generic fields, and no quantum factorial is
inverted in the $\mathcal O$-lattice; arbitrary composition series are
auxiliary only.

Let $F$ be a field, let $F[t,t^{-1}]$ be its Laurent polynomial ring
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), and let $v_1$ be the $(t-1)$-adic
valuation on the nonzero elements of $F[t,t^{-1}]$: for $0\ne f$,
$$v_1(f):=\max\{n\ge0:(t-1)^n\mid f\ \text{in}\ F[t,t^{-1}]\},$$
so that $v_1(f)=0$ exactly when $f(1)\ne0$
([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]). Let $A,B\in F\setminus\{0\}$, let $u,v\in\mathbb Z$,
put $N:=u-v$ and $f:=At^u-Bt^v$.

1. If $A\ne B$, then $v_1(f)=0$.
2. If $A=B$ and $N\ne0$, then $v_1(f)=1$ when $\operatorname{char}F=0$, and
   $v_1(f)=p^{v_p(|N|)}$ when $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$; here $v_p$ is the
   exponent of $p$ in $|N|$, i.e. $N=p^r m$ with $p\nmid m$
   ([[def-ring-characteristic]]).
3. If $A=B$ and $N=0$, then $f=0$, and the zero element has no finite valuation.

In the intended application the Laurent polynomials $Q_aq_H^{\,j-i}t^{\,na+j-i}$
(foot residues of the Jantzen expression) are compared by this lemma: it
computes their valuation exactly when their difference is nonzero and prevents
replacing valuations by an equality-of-residues indicator in positive
characteristic.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $[\lambda]$ be its Young diagram
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). A **tableau of shape
$\lambda$**, or $\lambda$-tableau, is a bijection
$$t:[\lambda]\longrightarrow\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$$
We write $t(i,j)$ for the entry of $t$ in the node $(i,j)$, and we display $t$
as the diagram $[\lambda]$ with each node carrying its entry. Thus a tableau
places each of the numbers $1,\dots,n$ in exactly one node of $[\lambda]$. For
$\lambda=\varnothing$ the diagram is empty and the empty map is the unique
tableau of shape $\varnothing$, the **empty tableau**. The **shape** of a
tableau $t$ is the partition $\lambda$ with $t:[\lambda]\to\{1,\dots,n\}$,
which is determined by $t$ because $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$.

**Standard tableaux.** A tableau $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is **standard** if its
entries strictly increase along rows and down columns, that is, if
$$t(i,j)<t(i,j+1)\quad\text{whenever }(i,j),(i,j+1)\in[\lambda],$$
$$t(i,j)<t(i+1,j)\quad\text{whenever }(i,j),(i+1,j)\in[\lambda].$$
The empty tableau is standard, because both conditions are vacuous, and it is
the unique standard tableau of shape $\varnothing$. Following the classical
notation we write $f^\lambda$ for the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux.

**The left action on tableaux.** For $\sigma\in S_n$ and a $\lambda$-tableau
$t$, define
$$(\sigma\cdot t)(i,j):=\sigma\bigl(t(i,j)\bigr)\qquad\bigl((i,j)\in[\lambda]\bigr).$$
Since $t$ is a bijection onto $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $\sigma$ is a bijection of
$\{1,\dots,n\}$, the map $\sigma\cdot t$ is again a bijection
$[\lambda]\to\{1,\dots,n\}$, hence again a $\lambda$-tableau, and
$\mathrm{id}\cdot t=t$, $\sigma\cdot(\tau\cdot t)=(\sigma\tau)\cdot t$ for all
$\sigma,\tau\in S_n$: the rule is a left action of $S_n$ on the set of
$\lambda$-tableaux. For every $\sigma\in S_n$ the row sets of $\sigma\cdot t$
are the images under $\sigma$ of the row sets of $t$, and the column sets of
$\sigma\cdot t$ are the images under $\sigma$ of the column sets of $t$.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and $\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$,
with diagrams $[\lambda]$ and $[\mu]$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). For content counts
only, set $\mu_i:=0$ for $i$ beyond the number of parts of $\mu$; these
zeros are not additional parts of the partition.

A **semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$ and content $\mu$**, also called a
semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$ and **type $\mu$**, is a filling
$T:[\lambda]\to\{1,2,\dots\}$ of the boxes of $[\lambda]$ with positive
integers such that:

1. **content:** for every $i\ge 1$ the entry $i$ occurs in exactly $\mu_i$
   boxes of $[\lambda]$, so the multiset of entries is
   $\{1^{\mu_1},2^{\mu_2},\dots\}$ and in particular every entry lies between
   $1$ and the number of parts of $\mu$;
2. **rows:** the entries weakly increase along every row, that is,
   $T(i,j)\le T(i,j+1)$ whenever $(i,j)$ and $(i,j+1)$ are both in
   $[\lambda]$;
3. **columns:** the entries strictly increase down every column, that is,
   $T(i,j)<T(i+1,j)$ whenever $(i,j)$ and $(i+1,j)$ are both in $[\lambda]$.

The **Kostka number** $K_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the number of semistandard
tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and content $\mu$:
$$K_{\lambda,\mu}:=\#\{\,T:T\text{ is a semistandard }\lambda\text{-tableau of content }\mu\,\}.$$
This is well defined and finite: a filling of the $n$ boxes of $[\lambda]$ by
positive integers has at most $n^n$ possibilities for $n\ge1$ once each entry is required
to lie between $1$ and the number of parts of $\mu$, and conditions 1--3 cut this
finite set down to the semistandard tableaux, so $K_{\lambda,\mu}$ is a
nonnegative integer. It is zero when the conditions cannot be met.

Two entries may be equal inside a row, but never inside a column: a repeated
entry in a column would contradict the strict increase of condition 3, so the
repetitions of a label forced by the content $\mu$ must be spread across
distinct columns of $[\lambda]$. For $\lambda=\mu=\varnothing$ there is a
single filling, the empty one, so
$$K_{\varnothing,\varnothing}=1 .$$

**Relation to standard tableaux.** Because a tableau of content $(1^n)$ uses
each of the numbers $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, its entries are pairwise
distinct, and weak increase along a row is then strict increase along that
row; a filling of $[\lambda]$ with content $(1^n)$ is therefore semistandard
exactly when it is a standard $\lambda$-tableau
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]), that is,
$$K_{\lambda,(1^n)}=f^\lambda ,$$
the number of standard tableaux of shape $\lambda$. In particular, for $n\ge1$,
$K_{(n),(1^n)}=K_{(n),(n)}=1$, since the single row carries either the
standard entries $1,2,\dots,n$ or the $n$ copies of the entry $1$, and
$K_{(1^n),(1^n)}=1$, realized by the single column $1,2,\dots,n$ read from
top to bottom.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is
$$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$
The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.

When $A$ is real, $|\det A|$ means the ordinary real absolute value of its real determinant. It is not alternate notation for the determinant itself.

derivations.claim: Characters as finite symmetric polynomials. Fix $d\ge n$ row labels per type component with ordered variables $x_{(a,r)}$, put $Y_a=\{x_{(b,r)}:b\ge a\}$ with the inherited order, and for a shape $\lambda$ let $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda(x)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SStd}(\lambda)}x^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$. The flag condition says that the physical component $a$ of a semistandard tableau is an ordinary semistandard tableau over the alphabet $Y_a$, and the components are chosen independently, so $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda(x)=\prod_a s_{\lambda^{(a)}}(Y_a)$ with $s_\rho(Y)=\det(h_{\rho_i-i+j}(Y))$. The determinant equals the ordinary semistandard generating polynomial: expand it as signed families of east/north lattice paths from $(-j,1)$ to $(\rho_i-i,m)$ with east steps at height $r$ weighted $y_r$, choose the first intersection in a fixed order and exchange the two tails, an involution that preserves the monomial weight and reverses the permutation sign, so all intersecting families cancel; a nonintersecting family forces the identity matching, and the surviving families are exactly the semistandard tableaux, sign $+1$. Hence the coefficient of $x^\nu$ in $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda$ is the Kostka number $K_{\lambda\nu}$; empty and short-row cases are included.

Beta determinants and rim-hook signs. Choose $N\ge n$, put $\beta_{a,i}=\lambda^{(a)}_i+N-i$ with zero parts appended, and for a nonnegative integer array $v$ define $\chi(v;x)=\prod_a\det\bigl(h_{v_{a,i}-N+j}(Y_a)\bigr)_{i,j}$. If two entries of one component of $v$ agree the determinant has equal rows and is zero; otherwise sorting that component into strictly decreasing order and writing $\rho_i=v'_i-N+i$ gives $\chi(v;x)=\varepsilon(v)\prod_a s_{\rho^{(a)}}(Y_a)$ with $\varepsilon$ the product of the row-sorting signs, so every coefficient is a signed Kostka multiplicity. A beta move lowering a bead from $v+L$ to an unoccupied $v$ is exactly the removal of a rim hook of length $L$: tracing the southeast boundary shows the strip between the two boundary steps has $L$ boxes, its leg is the number of occupied positions strictly between $v$ and $v+L$, its foot content is $v-N+1$, and the associated sorting sign is $(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}}$; the correspondence is a bijection by the reverse move.

The hook side as a complete finite alternating polynomial. Define $B_\lambda(x)$ as the finite alternating sum of step 2.1: for crosscomponent terms, over $a<b$, over beads $i,j$ and lengths $h\le\beta_{a,i}$, of $\chi(\beta-h e_{a,i}+h e_{b,j};x)V(U_az^{\beta_{a,i}-h}-U_bz^{\beta_{b,j}})$; and for same-component terms, over $a$, $i<j$ and $1\le h\le\beta_{a,i}-\beta_{a,j}-1$, of $\chi(\beta-he_{a,i}+he_{a,j};x)V(U_az^{\beta_{a,i}-h}-U_az^{\beta_{a,j}})$; terms whose $\chi$ is the zero polynomial are omitted before any valuation is evaluated. Then $B_\lambda(x)=\sum_{\mu:\lambda\triangleright\mu}J_{\lambda\mu}\operatorname{ch}_\mu(x)$: a crosscomponent move removing from the earlier component $a$ and adding to a later component $b>a$ produces a strictly dominated $\mu$ and occurs exactly once by the bead description; occupied targets give repeated rows and zero; sorting contributes $(-1)^{\text{removed leg}+\text{added leg}}$; and the prefactor $z^{-N+1}$ converts the beta difference to the difference of the deformed foot residues. In one component the two moved beads $i<j$ give a strict dominance decrease precisely for $1\le h<\beta_i-\beta_j$, the exchange case $h=\beta_i-\beta_j$ giving $\mu=\lambda$ and the outward case giving the reverse dominance; occupied intermediate positions again give zero rows, and the range exceeding a component's size gives a repeated or negative bead, hence a zero determinant. Thus no hook pair is lost or added, and the surviving summands are exactly the $J_{\lambda\mu}$ terms.

Nonvanishing of every retained foot difference. For a removable rim hook of length $L$ from a partition of size $M+L$ with foot $(h,j)$, one has $-(M+L-1)\le j-h\le M$: every box left of the foot in its row survives, so $j-1\le M$, and $h\le M+L$ gives the lower bound. If $\lambda$ and $\mu$ remove equal-length hooks in distinct components $a\ne b$ to the same remainder with remainder sizes $M_a,M_b$, their foot contents satisfy $|\gamma_x-\gamma_y|\le M_a+M_b+L-1\le n-1$, so the exponent $n(a-b)+\gamma_x-\gamma_y$ is a nonzero integer; in the same component equal foot content and equal length reconstruct the same inverse hook addition, hence would force $\lambda=\mu$, which the strict-dominance terms exclude. Therefore every retained Laurent difference $U_az^u-U_bz^v$ is nonzero in $F(t)$: it is a unit times a nonzero Laurent monomial times $(z^{N}-1)$-type factors and, by [F2], its valuation is finite, being $0$ when the constant residues differ, $1$ in characteristic zero when they agree, and $p^{v_p(N)}$ in characteristic $p$ when they agree.

The same-component operator. In the same-component beta sum put $D=\beta_i-\beta_j$ and $k=D-h$, so the valuation is $f(k)=V(z^k-1)$ up to unit factors; swapping the two changed determinant rows shows $\chi(\beta-(D-k)e_i+(D-k)e_j;x)=-\chi(\beta-ke_i+ke_j;x)$. Hence the complete coefficient of $f(k)$ is $-\sum_{i<j:\beta_i-\beta_j>k}\chi(\beta-ke_i+ke_j;x)$, which is the strictly dominance-lowering part of $-p_kp_k^\perp$ on the abstract shape basis, where $p_k^\perp$ lowers an occupied bead by $k$ into an unoccupied nonnegative position with sign $(-1)^{\#\text{crossed beads}}$ and $p_k$ raises a bead by $k$ with the same sign rule; the bead-raising formula follows from the alternant identity $\det(y_r^{\beta_i})\sum_ry_r^k=\sum_i\det(y_r^{\beta_i+k\delta_{ij}})$ divided by the Vandermonde, and the removal map is its transpose. After one removal and one addition a non-diagonal lower-dominance result comes only from distinct beads $i<j$ with $0<k<\beta_i-\beta_j$, occupied intermediate positions giving zero repeated rows and the diagonal being removed by the strict projection; this proves the operator identification integrally, in every characteristic.

The crosscomponent operator as exterior currents. On the $N$-fold exterior power of a space with basis $e_0,e_1,\dots$, represent a partition by the ordered wedge of its beta beads and let $E(p,q)$ insert $e_p$ after removing $e_q$, with exterior signs; it vanishes if $q$ is absent or $p$ is occupied, and its sign is the bead-sorting sign. Expanding $E=\text{creation}\cdot\text{contraction}$ gives $[E(p,q),E(r,s)]=\delta_{q,r}E(p,s)-\delta_{p,s}E(r,q)$. The crosscomponent matrix acting on column shape vectors is $J^{\mathrm{cross}}=\sum_{a<b}\sum_{h>0}\sum_{q\ge h,w\ge0}V(U_az^{q-h}-U_bz^w)E_a(q,q-h)E_b(w,w+h)$, a finite operator on each size-$n$ sector; the reverse hook pair has forward current $E_a(q-h,q)E_b(w+h,w)$, and transposing gives exactly this operator with the same signs and valuation.

Horizontal strips and their conjugation. With $S e_q=e_{q+1}$ and $H(x)=(I-xS)^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge0}x^rS^r$, whose entry $H_{p,q}$ is $x^{p-q}$ for $p\ge q$ and $0$ otherwise, the matrix of $\wedge^NH(x)$ between $\beta_\mu$ and $\beta_\rho$ is $x^{|\mu|-|\rho|}\det(1_{\beta_{\mu,i}\ge\beta_{\rho,j}})$. Subtracting consecutive columns of the $0/1$ matrix makes its determinant $1$ exactly when $\beta_{\mu,i}\ge\beta_{\rho,i}>\beta_{\mu,i+1}$ for all $i$, i.e. $\mu_i\ge\rho_i\ge\mu_{i+1}$, the horizontal-strip criterion, and $0$ otherwise; so $\Gamma(x)=\wedge^NH(x)$ adds every horizontal strip once with weight $x^{\text{strip size}}$. For a type component $a$, $\Gamma_a(x)=\prod_{b\le a}\Gamma_b(x)$ adds a horizontal strip in every permitted physical component $b\le a$ and leaves the rest unchanged, so the successive $\Gamma_a$ from the empty shape enumerate exactly the flagged semistandard tableaux and give the branching matrix. Conjugation is explicit: since $H^{-1}=I-xS$ has column vector $e_p-xe_{p+1}$ and row covector $\sum_{r\le q}x^{q-r}e_r^*$, $\Gamma(x)^{-1}E(p,q)\Gamma(x)=\sum_{r=0}^qx^{q-r}\bigl(E(p,r)-xE(p+1,r)\bigr),$ and the two-current conjugation is the ordered product of two such sums.

Strip factors and exact minor expressions. For a permitted strip transition $\rho\to\lambda$ for the next type component $c$, let $\eta=[\lambda]\setminus[\rho]$, $r_x=U_{\operatorname{comp}(x)}z^{\operatorname{content}(x)}$, and put $F^{(c)}_{\lambda\rho}=\prod_{x\in\eta}\prod_{\operatorname{comp}(x)<b\le c}(r_x-U_b)\prod_{x\in[\rho],\,y\in\eta\text{ in one physical row}}C_+(r_x,r_y)\prod_{x<y,\,x,y\in\eta\text{ in different physical rows}}C_+(r_x,r_y)\prod_{x\in\eta,\,y\in[\rho],\,x<y}R(r_x,r_y)$. Splitting the pair lists of [F1] into old/old, old/new and new/new gives this factor, and their product along a semistandard chain is $\gamma_{t_T}/(C_{t_T}u_T)$. Choose $N>n$, write $q_i=\beta_{\lambda,i}$, $p_i=\beta_{\rho,i}$ in each component, and $H(q,p)_{ij}=1_{q_i\ge p_j}$, so $q_N=p_N=0$. Write $\phi(k)=V(z^k-1)$ for $k>0$ and $\psi_{ab}(d)=V(U_az^d-U_b)$. First regard these as independent formal symbols; canceled symbols are never evaluated. By steps 3.1 and 5.1, the same-component row contribution to $J\Gamma$ is $\sum_{i<j}\sum_{0<h<q_i-q_j}\phi(q_i-q_j-h)\det H(q-he_i+he_j,p)$; the column contribution to $\Gamma J$ is $\sum_{i<j}\sum_{h>0}(\phi(p_i-p_j+h)-\phi(h))\det H(q,p+he_i-he_j)$. Negative or repeated shifted beads give zero determinants. For the second formula, the outward source has beads $p_i+h,p_j-h$; its two hook pairs returning to $p$ have lengths $h$ and $p_i-p_j+h$, foot gaps $p_i-p_j+h$ and $h$, and opposite signs because the second pair exchanges the two target beads. This proves the difference of potentials, including crossed inverse sources. A crosscomponent row term replaces $q_{a,i},q_{b,j}$ by $q_{a,i}-h,q_{b,j}+h$ with potential $\psi_{ab}(q_{a,i}-h-q_{b,j})$; its column term replaces $p_{a,i},p_{b,j}$ by $p_{a,i}+h,p_{b,j}-h$ with potential $\psi_{ab}(p_{a,i}-p_{b,j}+h)$. The determinants in the original indexed positions retain all sorting signs.

Norm endpoints. On support $q_i\ge p_i>q_{i+1}$. Put $M_i=q_i-p_i$, $K_j=p_j-q_{j+1}-1$ for $j<N$, $K_N=0$, and $S(m)=\sum_{k=1}^m\phi(k)$. The same-component norm valuation is $\sum_i(S(q_i)-S(p_i)-S(M_i))+\sum_{i<j}\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}(\phi(u-q_j)-\phi(u-p_j+1))$. To verify this directly, put $b_i=N-i$: same-row old/new pairs sum to $S(q_i-b_i)-S(M_i)-S(p_i-b_i)$. For $i<j$, new/new and new-upper/old-lower pairs sum to $\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}(\phi(u-q_j)-\phi(u-p_j+1)+\phi(u-b_j+1)-\phi(u-b_j))$. The last two terms telescope in $u$ to $\phi(q_i-b_j)-\phi(p_i-b_j)$; summing over $j>i$ cancels the baseline $b_i$ terms and gives the formula. Every displayed $\phi$ argument is positive. For $a<b\le c$, the crosscomponent endpoint expression is $\sum_i\sum_{u=p_{a,i}}^{q_{a,i}-1}(\psi_{ab}(u+1)+\sum_{j=1}^N(\psi_{ab}(u-q_{b,j})-\psi_{ab}(u-p_{b,j}+1)))$. Indeed the new/new $C_+$ factors telescope in the lower-component node index $v$ to $\psi(u-q_{b,j})-\psi(u-p_{b,j})$, and the new/old $R$ factors add $\psi(u-p_{b,j})-\psi(u-b_j)$ and the rectangle difference $\sum_{v=b_j}^{p_{b,j}-1}(\psi(u+1-v)-\psi(u-v))$. Telescoping this rectangle in the other direction and adding the boundary factor $\psi(u-N+1)$ gives the displayed formula; the vacuum differences telescope and cancel that boundary. This padded formula is an equality of formal symbols: its $j=N$ term cancels $\psi(u+1)$ before evaluation.

All on-support minors. Here $H$ is the unit upper triangular step matrix. Expanding a replacement row or column in its basis gives $d_i^{\mathrm{row}}(v)=1_{p_i\le v<p_{i-1}}$ and $d_i^{\mathrm{col}}(v)=1_{q_{i+1}<v\le q_i}$, with $p_0=\infty$ and no positive lowering from $p_N=0$. A two-row minor is its direct product minus its crossed product. For the same-component row expression, the direct term has $1\le h\le\min(M_i,K_{j-1})$ and the crossed term, with $k=q_i-q_j-h$, has $1\le k\le\min(M_i,K_{j-1})$. The outward two-column minor has no crossed term and its direct bound is $1\le h\le\min(M_i,K_j)$. Pair direct row index $j+1$ with first-potential column index $j$. For arbitrary symbols $\psi$ the interval identity $\sum_{s=0}^{M-1}(\psi(A+s+K+1)-\psi(A+s+1))=\sum_{h=1}^{\min(M,K)}(\psi(A+M+K+1-h)-\psi(A+h))$ follows by canceling the overlap of the two integer intervals (when $M\le K$ they are disjoint, and when $M>K$ only $K$ endpoints remain). Applying it with $A=p_i-p_j$, the paired contribution is $\sum_{j=i+1}^{N-1}\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}(\phi(u-q_{j+1})-\phi(u-p_j+1))$. Crossed rows cancel the second column potentials except $-S(\min(M_i,K_i))$; the unpaired direct row $j=i+1$, combined with that residual by the same identity at $A=0$, gives $\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}\phi(u-q_{i+1})-S(M_i)$. Summing yields exactly the same-component endpoints of step 7.1. For a crosscomponent pair, row $j+1$ and column $j$ share the bound $\min(M_i,K_{b,j})$ and $A=p_{a,i}-p_{b,j}$. The unpaired first row contributes $\sum_{u=p_{a,i}}^{q_{a,i}-1}\psi(u-q_{b,1})$; the final column vanishes. The same interval identity converts the paired terms to the remaining endpoints of step 7.1. Thus $(J\Gamma-\Gamma J)_{\lambda\rho}=x^{|\lambda|-|\rho|}V(F^{(c)}_{\lambda\rho})$ on support.

Crosscomponent off support. The row of $H$ at bead $v$ is the tail vector starting at threshold $\kappa(v)$, whose interval is $[p_r,p_{r-1})$. Different nonzero tail vectors are independent; hence rank equals the number of distinct thresholds. At rank $N-1$ there is one missing threshold $r$ and two adjacent duplicated rows $i,i+1$. Put $Q=q_i>Q'=q_{i+1}$, $[P,P')=[p_r,p_{r-1})$, $u=e_i-e_{i+1}$ and $v=e_r-e_{r-1}$, omitting $e_0$. The adjugate is $\varepsilon vu^{\mathsf T}$: its nullspaces have those generators, and removing a duplicate row and the appropriate column gives a minor $\pm1$. Thus replacement determinants are $\varepsilon u_l1_{P\le x<P'}$ and $\varepsilon v_l1_{Q'<x\le Q}$ with the same sign. Rank $\le N-2$ kills every one-row/column replacement. A defective earlier component can be repaired only when $Q'\ge P'$ (missing below), and a defective later component only when $Q<P$ (missing above); opposite directions give zero. If only the earlier component is defective, pair normal later row $j+1$ and column $j$ and write $L=q_{b,j+1}$, $M=p_{b,j}$. Their coefficients both give $-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in[P-L,P'-L)\cap(Q'-M,Q-M]}\psi(d)$; the first unpaired row vanishes because its two source signs sum to zero. If only the later component is defective, write its endpoints $R>R'$, $[S,S')$ and let $M=q_{a,i}-p_{a,i}$. The row coefficient at restored position $w$ is $\varepsilon1_{R'+M<w\le R+M}$ on $[S,S')$, and the column coefficient at $t$ is $\varepsilon1_{S\le t+M<S'}$ on $(R',R]$. The translation $w=t+M$ matches their potentials because $q_{a,i}=p_{a,i}+M$. With both components defective, the row coefficient of $\psi(d)$, divided by $\varepsilon_a\varepsilon_b$, is $(1_{S\le Q-d<S'}-1_{S\le Q'-d<S'})(1_{P\le R+d<P'}-1_{P\le R'+d<P'})$; the column coefficient is $(1_{R'<P-d\le R}-1_{R'<P'-d\le R})(1_{Q'<S+d\le Q}-1_{Q'<S'+d\le Q})$. They agree by the endpoint identity $1_{B_0\le A_1-d<B_1}-1_{B_0\le A_0-d<B_1}=1_{A_0<B_0+d\le A_1}-1_{A_0<B_1+d\le A_1}$, obtained by regrouping four half-line indicators. Infinite top endpoints simply omit the virtual source. An untouched defective component kills the product. Components beyond $c$ are empty in the reachable prefix: the forward transfer would create a nonempty forbidden intermediate component, and the inverse transfer would remove a hook from an empty component, so both vanish. This exhausts crosscomponent off-support cases.

Same-component deficiency one, missing below. Keep the rank-one data of step 9.1, with duplicated rows $s,s+1$ and missing threshold $r>s$, so $Q'\ge P'$. A nonzero inward two-row replacement must use one duplicate source and a unique normal row $j\ge r+1$: one new row fills the missing interval and the other restores the unique source threshold. The direct and exchanged assignments have signs $\varepsilon u_l$ and $-\varepsilon u_l$; any other assignment leaves an unchanged duplicate or missing threshold, or violates the strict inward range. Nonzero outward two-column repairs use one endpoint $P,P'$ and a unique column $j\ge r+1$, or the endpoint pair itself. Put $K_j=p_j-q_{j+1}-1$ for $j\ge r$, $K_N=0$. The direct row contribution is $R_j=-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in[P-q_j,P'-q_j)\cap(Q'-p_{j-1},Q-p_{j-1}]}\phi(d)$. Split each unique column contribution into its first and second potentials $C_j^{\mathrm{first}}-C_j^{\mathrm{second}}$ from step 6.1. Then $R_{j+1}=C_j^{\mathrm{first}}$, by the same interval intersection, while $C_j^{\mathrm{second}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^{K_j}\phi(h)(1_{Q'<P+h\le Q}-1_{Q'<P'+h\le Q})$. The exchanged row is $X_j=-\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^{K_{j-1}}\phi(k)(1_{P\le Q-k<P'}-1_{P\le Q'-k<P'})=-C_{j-1}^{\mathrm{second}}$ by endpoint reciprocity. All terms cancel except $R_{r+1}-C_r^{\mathrm{second}}-C^{\mathrm{end}}$. Put $A=Q'-P'\ge0$, $B=P'-P>0$, $L=Q-Q'>0$, $I_0=(A,A+L]$, $I_1=I_0+B$, $K=K_r$. These three terms are respectively $-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap(K,K+B]}\phi(d)$, $\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^{K}\phi(h)(1_{I_1}(h)-1_{I_0}(h))$, and $-\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le K}(\phi(B+h)-\phi(h))$; the endpoint-pair sign is negative because the raised endpoint is $P'$. Their residual is $-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap[1,K+B]}\phi(d)+\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le K}\phi(B+h)=0$ by $d=h+B$. This proves every coefficient cancels, including $K=0$.

Same-component deficiency one, missing above. Here $r\le s$, $P>Q$, and $\varepsilon=(-1)^{s-r}$, obtained by moving the inserted missing threshold from row $s$ to position $r$; the column cofactor has the same sign. If $r=1$, all inward row positions are at most $q_1<p_1$ and cannot fill the missing top threshold; the first column is zero and any outward repair raises it further, so both sums vanish. For $r\ge2$ the only unique row sources are $i\le r-1$, with $M_i=q_i-p_i\ge0$. The direct rows have $R_i=\varepsilon\sum_{d\in(q_i-P',q_i-P]\cap[p_i-Q,p_i-Q')}\phi(d)$. The first column potentials equal $R_i$ for $i\le r-2$, while $C_i^{\mathrm{second}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^{M_i}\phi(h)(1_{Q'<P-h\le Q}-1_{Q'<P'-h\le Q})$. Exchanged rows are $X_i=-\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^{M_i}\phi(k)(1_{P\le Q+k<P'}-1_{P\le Q'+k<P'})=-C_i^{\mathrm{second}}$, again by endpoint reciprocity. This exhausts repairs: the duplicate source must be paired with a head row above the missing interval, and outward column repairs must lower an endpoint paired with a unique head column, or use the endpoint pair. The sole residual is at $i=r-1$. Put $M=q_{r-1}-P'\ge0$, $B=P'-P>0$, $A=P-Q>0$, $L=Q-Q'>0$, $I_0=[A,A+L)$, $I_1=I_0+B$. Then $R_{r-1}=\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap(M,M+B]}\phi(d)$ and $C_{r-1}^{\mathrm{second}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^M\phi(h)(1_{I_0}(h)-1_{I_1}(h))$; the endpoint-pair column term is $C^{\mathrm{end}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le M}(\phi(B+h)-\phi(h))$, with positive cofactor because the lowered endpoint is $P$. Thus $R_{r-1}-C_{r-1}^{\mathrm{second}}-C^{\mathrm{end}}=\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap[1,M+B]}\phi(d)-\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le M}\phi(B+h)=0$. The translation $d=h+B$ is valid since $A>0$.

Same-component deficiency two and higher. At rank $N-2$, the excess threshold copies are one triple or two pairs. Inward row repairs of a triple cannot reach missing thresholds between its source beads. For two pairs with thresholds $r<s$, both missing thresholds must lie strictly between them, say $r<m_1<m_2<s$; otherwise both row and column sums are zero. For columns this follows from $\ell(p_j)=\#\{i:\kappa(q_i)\le j\}$: duplicated row thresholds are jumps, missing thresholds are flats, and outward column repairs require two separate size-two jumps with both flats between. A zero first column also cannot be repaired by raising it. In the active pattern put $Q=q_r>Q'=q_{r+1}$, $R=q_{s-1}>R'=q_s$, $I_1=[P,P')=[p_{m_1},p_{m_1-1})$, $I_2=[S,S')=[p_{m_2},p_{m_2-1})$, $J_Q=(Q',Q]$, $J_R=(R',R]$. The common row/column sign is $\varepsilon=(-1)^{m_1-r+s-1-m_2}$, counted by moving the inserted thresholds to their sorted positions. Switching a source copy or switching the two target thresholds reverses it. Define $A_I(k)=1_{R+k\in I}-1_{R'+k\in I}$ and $B_I(k)=1_{Q-k\in I}-1_{Q'-k\in I}$; define $D_P^\pm(J;k)=1_{P\pm k\in J}-1_{P'\pm k\in J}$ and $D_S^\pm(J;k)=1_{S\pm k\in J}-1_{S'\pm k\in J}$. The complete row coefficient of $\phi(k)$ is $\varepsilon(A_{I_1}(k)B_{I_2}(k)-A_{I_2}(k)B_{I_1}(k))$; the column coefficient is $\varepsilon(D_S^+(J_Q;k)D_P^-(J_R;k)-D_P^+(J_Q;k)D_S^-(J_R;k))$. Indeed putting $k=q_i-q_j-h$ gives row targets $q_j+k,q_i-k$, while the positive and negative column potentials give targets $p_j+k,p_i-k$ and $p_i+k,p_j-k$ respectively. Interval membership implies all required positive-length bounds. Endpoint reciprocity gives $A_{I_1}=D_P^-(J_R)$, $A_{I_2}=D_S^-(J_R)$, $B_{I_1}=D_P^+(J_Q)$, $B_{I_2}=D_S^+(J_Q)$, proving equality. If $m_2=m_1+1$, the repeated column groups share an endpoint; its formal double-source term is zero because its potential is $\phi(h)-\phi(h)$, so the formula still includes adjacent missing thresholds. At rank $\le N-3$, two replacements cannot restore full rank. Together with steps 9.1–10.2 this proves off-support vanishing for every rank and orientation. All identities are formal coefficient equalities; retained terms are actual valid hook currents, so step 3.2 permits their finite arbitrary-characteristic valuation specialization.

Telescoping and the valuation formula. Multiply the $\Gamma$ matrices in increasing type-row-label order and telescope $J\Gamma-\Gamma J$ from $J_0=0$; by steps 8.1–11.1 each commutator inserts exactly $V(F)$ at its strip position, so the $\lambda$-coordinate of the resulting identity is $\sum_T V(\gamma_{t_T}/(C_{t_T}u_T))x^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}=L_\lambda(x)$ on one side and $B_\lambda(x)$ on the other. All padded artificial symbols cancel before the surviving coefficients are evaluated, and every surviving coefficient corresponds to a valid current, hence by step 3.2 to a nonzero foot difference with finite valuation. Comparing with the exact monic product [F1] and the hook side of step 3.1, and taking the coefficient of $x^
u$ at an actual multipartition weight $
u$ (auxiliary compositions only index the same polynomials and never enter the Schur conclusion), gives $V(\det G_{\lambda
u})=\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu
u};$ the empty case $n=0$ gives $0$, all ranks keep the fixed parameters $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$, and arbitrary-composition coefficients are combinatorial only.

derivations.claim: Filtration and radical. For $n=0$ there is one empty multipartition, $S_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O$, $\Delta_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O$ with form $1$, every positive filtration term is $0$, and every $J$ coefficient is $0$, so the assertions follow directly. For $n\ge1$, [F1] gives free standard lattices with nondegenerate generic forms. The Smith reduction of [F4] shows that the defined filtration is by $S_F$-submodules, begins at $\Delta_F(\lambda)$, has first term equal to the form radical, and is zero for all sufficiently large $s$. The rank-one cell actions of the nonzero cellular form force every proper submodule into that radical, so the first term is the module radical. [given, F1, F4]

The auxiliary character identity. Introduce ordered variables for the type-row labels; the auxiliary generating series of flagged semistandard tableaux is the product over physical components $a$ of $s_{\lambda^{(a)}}(Y_a)$, where $Y_a$ is the alphabet of type components at least $a$, and its coefficient at an actual multipartition $\nu$ is $K_{\lambda\nu}$. Successive $\Gamma_a$ matrices add the horizontal strips carrying each next label and therefore enumerate these tableaux once; the path/Jacobi–Trudi cancellation proves this character identity locally. No actual Schur weight or module for another composition is needed. [F1, F3]

The weight-character reduction. Fix an actual multipartition weight $
u$. The selfadjoint orthogonal decomposition by $e_
u$ makes the standard weight space orthogonal to every other weight space, so [F4] gives $\sum_{s>0}\dim_Fe_
u\Delta_F(\lambda)^s=V(\det G_{\lambda
u})$. By [F2] and additivity of the valuation this is the sum over type-$
u$ semistandard $T$ of the valuations of their explicit monic norms; empty weight spaces use determinant $1$ and contribute $0$. [F2, F4, step 1.1]

The beta form of the hook side. Pad the beta lists to $N>n$. Removing a hook of length $h$ lowers one beta bead by $h$ with sorting sign $(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}}$, and adding it raises a bead by $h$ with the corresponding sign; the foot content is the lowered bead position minus $N$ plus $1$, up to the unit foot-residue shift. Thus the full signed equal-length hook side is precisely the finite shifted-beta Jacobi–Trudi polynomial: same-component inward ranges, crosscomponent earlier-to-later ranges, occupied-position zero terms and the unit shift are all covered by [F3]. Its coefficient at $\nu$ is $\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu\nu}$. [F3, step 1.2]

Telescoping the marked-strip commutator. Apply the complete local identity [F3] to the product of successive type-row $\Gamma$ matrices and telescope $J\Gamma-\Gamma J$, starting from the empty shape where $J_0=0$. Each commutator inserts exactly the valuation of the strip factor at that label position, while all other $\Gamma$ factors retain the same tableau chain; summing the inserted positions gives the total valuation of the product of the factors over the chain, hence of the monic norm by [F2] and [F3]. The left endpoint of the telescope is exactly the auxiliary polynomial of step 2.2, so at the actual multipartition coefficient $
u$, $
u_\pi(\det G_{\lambda
u})=\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu
u}$. Every auxiliary rank keeps the final-rank-$n$ parameters $U_a=Q_at^{na}$, with no rank-dependent deformation substituted during the telescope. [F2, F3, step 2.2]

Exactness of the valuations. For a nonzero difference $At^u-Bt^v$, unequal constants give valuation $0$, and equal constants with $u-v\ne0$ give valuation $1$ in characteristic zero or $p^{v_p(|u-v|)}$ in characteristic $p$ by [F5]. Artificial padded symbols in the crosscomponent minor proofs cancel formally before evaluation, and the retained terms are actual valid hook or node pairs whose exponent bound makes their differences nonzero in $K$; hence step 3.1 is valid over every $F$ and retains the higher positive-characteristic multiplicities. [F3, F5, step 3.1]

The integer Grothendieck class identity. Combining steps 2.1 and 3.1 shows that the actual multipartition-weight character of $\sum_{s>0}[\Delta_F(\lambda)^s]$ equals that of $\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}[\Delta_F(\mu)]$. Weight projection is exact, so these are additive characters on the integer $K_0$ group [F4], and the standard classes form its $\mathbb Z$-basis by [F1]; their multipartition-weight matrix is unitriangular, hence invertible over $\mathbb Z$. A zero difference of weight characters therefore has all standard coefficients zero, which proves the asserted integer $K_0$ equality, with no rationalization and no Schur-functor injectivity claim. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

Let $F$ be any field, let $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite multiplicative order $e\ge2$, let $\ell\ge1$ be arbitrary and let $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$ with charges $c_a\in\mathbb Z$. Fix $n\ge0$ and let $S_F$ be the cyclotomic $q$-Schur algebra over $F$ with summands indexed by all $\ell$-multipartitions of $n$.

Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az\text{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). A **central idempotent** of $A$ is an idempotent $e\in Z(A)$; it is **primitive** when $e\ne0$ and $e$ is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category ([[def-abelian-category]]). Its set of isomorphism classes is denoted $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)$. The **Grothendieck group** of $\mathcal C$ is $$ G_0(\mathcal C):=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)]\big/\langle e_Y-e_X-e_Z:\ 0\to X\to Y\to Z\to 0\text{ is short exact in }\mathcal C\rangle.

derivations.claim: Standard classes form a $\mathbb Z$-basis. The matrix of standard classes to simple classes is triangular with diagonal one by [F1], hence [F4] makes the classes $[\Delta(\lambda)]$ a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the integer Grothendieck group of the Schur cover, and the classes of the block projections are independent as well. [F1, F4]

Nonzero $J$-coefficients link the same block. Suppose $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$ and project the Jantzen sum identity of [F2] to all blocks other than the block of $\Delta(\lambda)$. Its left side is zero because each $\Delta_F(\lambda)^i$ is a submodule of the block-pure standard $\Delta(\lambda)$; its right side is a $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of standard classes lying in those other blocks, and the coefficient of $[\Delta(\mu)]$ in it is exactly $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$. Basis independence from step 1.1 forces that coefficient to vanish, a contradiction unless $\Delta(\mu)$ lies in the block of $\Delta(\lambda)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

Blocks and Hecke linkage. By [F1], two standards share a Schur block exactly when they are linked by a finite chain of standards whose neighbouring terms share a simple factor. Step 2.2 converts each such shared factor into a $J$-edge to the common index, and step 2.1 shows every $J$-edge lies inside one block; hence sharing a Schur block is equivalent to $\sim_J$-connectivity. Applying the established Schur/Specht block correspondence of [F1] transfers this equivalence to the Murphy Specht modules and the Hecke algebra. In rank $0$ there is one empty standard, all positive filtration terms vanish, and the single empty class is its own Jantzen class; the argument never reduces $J$ coefficients modulo the field characteristic. [F1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

Over any field $F$, at any level $\ell\ge1$, with $q_H\ne1$ of finite order
$e\ge2$ and charges $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$, use the actual multipartition-summand
Schur cover and standards of
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]] and
the integer $J_{\lambda\mu}$ of
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]. Let
$\sim_J$ be the equivalence relation on multipartitions generated by
$J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$ or $J_{\mu\lambda}\ne0$. Then
$$\lambda\sim_J\mu\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Delta^\lambda,\Delta^\mu\text{ lie in one Schur block}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S^\lambda,S^\mu\text{ lie in one Hecke block}.$$
For rank $0$ there is the single empty class. No residue-content block
assertion is used as an input.

Let $F$ be any field, let $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite multiplicative order
$e\ge2$, let $\ell\ge1$ be arbitrary and let $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$ with charges
$c_a\in\mathbb Z$. Fix $n\ge0$ and let $S_F$ be the cyclotomic $q$-Schur
algebra over $F$ with summands indexed by all $\ell$-multipartitions of $n$.
Put
$$\mathcal O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)},\qquad \pi=t-1,\qquad K=F(t),\qquad z=q_Ht,\qquad U_a=Q_at^{na}.$$
Let $\Delta_{\mathcal O}(\lambda)$ be the standard Weyl lattice with its actual
cellular form, and define
$$\Delta_{\mathcal O}(\lambda)(s)=\{v:\langle v,\Delta_{\mathcal O}(\lambda)\rangle\subseteq\pi^s\mathcal O\},\qquad \Delta_F(\lambda)^s=\bigl(\Delta_{\mathcal O}(\lambda)(s)+\pi\Delta_{\mathcal O}(\lambda)\bigr)/\pi\Delta_{\mathcal O}(\lambda).$$
Then $(\Delta_F(\lambda)^s)_{s\ge0}$ is a filtration by $S_F$-submodules, its
first term is $\operatorname{rad}\Delta_F(\lambda)$ and the filtration
terminates, and in the integer Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional
$S_F$-modules,
$$\sum_{s>0}[\Delta_F(\lambda)^s]=\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}[\Delta_F(\mu)].$$
For a node $x=(i,j,a)$ define the rim hook $r_x^\lambda$ and its foot
$f_x^\lambda=(\lambda'_j,j,a)$ as in Lyle–Mathas,
$\operatorname{leg}(r_x^\lambda)=\lambda'_j-i$, and
$\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal O}(i,j,a)=U_az^{j-i}$. If $\lambda$ strictly
dominates $\mu$, set
$$J_{\lambda\mu}=\sum_{\substack{x\in[\lambda],\ y\in[\mu]\\{}[\lambda]\setminus r_x^\lambda=[\mu]\setminus r_y^\mu}} (-1)^{\operatorname{leg}(r_x^\lambda)+\operatorname{leg}(r_y^\mu)} \nu_\pi\bigl(\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal O}(f_x^\lambda)-\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal O}(f_y^\mu)\bigr),$$
and set $J_{\lambda\mu}=0$ otherwise. Equal remainder diagrams force equal
hook lengths. Every displayed difference is nonzero in $K$, including
same-component terms with distinct labels, by the foot-exponent separation
argument; no level-one or characteristic-zero restriction is present.
The same statement holds for the right Schur standard modules, by applying
the argument to the opposite algebra $S^{\mathrm{op}}$
([[def-opposite-ring]]): $a^{\mathrm{op}}$ acts by right multiplication by
$a$ and $e_\nu M$ becomes $Me_\nu$, with the contravariant form unchanged.
At rank zero the sole form is $1$ and the asserted sum is $0$ directly, with
no word-separation hypothesis needed.

Let $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$ be a level-one fundamental weight and keep the
conventions of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]. Then the
assignments $T_r\mapsto T_r$ ($1\le r<d$) in the nondegenerate case and
$s_r\mapsto s_r$ in the degenerate case extend to $F$-algebra isomorphisms
$$H_{F,q}(S_d)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_d,\qquad FS_d\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_d$$
respectively ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).

Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let $S^{\lambda}$ be the type-A Hecke Specht module of this page in the Dipper-James convention ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) for $\lambda\vdash n$. Then for all partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ the modules $S^{\lambda}$ and $S^{\mu}$ lie in the same block of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Equivalently, for finite $e$, the blocks of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ of size at most $n$ with $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. For $e=\infty$ use $C_\infty(\lambda):=\lambda$; the Hecke algebra is semisimple and its blocks are indexed by partitions of $n$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $e\ge2$, let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let
$X=\{h_1>h_2>\cdots>h_m\}$ be a $\beta$-set for $\lambda$, with first-column
hook lengths $b_i(\lambda)$ and $e$-abacus configuration $A_X$ as in
[[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]; hooks and their lengths
are those of [[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]], and the hook/bead-gap
dictionary is [[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]].

**$e$-core partition.** The partition $\lambda$ is an **$e$-core** when
$e\notin H(\lambda)$, that is, when no hook of $\lambda$ has length $e$; by
[[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]](iii) this is the case exactly
when no bead of $A_X$ has a gap in the position $e$ labels above it on its own
runner. The empty partition is an $e$-core, and so is every $\lambda$ with
$|\lambda|<e$.

**Runner label sets.** For $i\in\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$ let
$$X^{(e)}_i:=\{a\in\mathbb N_0:ae+i\in X\}$$
be the set of row labels of the beads of $A_X$ on runner $i$. The $X^{(e)}_i$
are finite subsets of $\mathbb N_0$ and may overlap. The disjoint union
$\bigsqcup_i\{i\}\times X^{(e)}_i$ records each bead with its runner and row;
the map $(i,a)\mapsto ae+i$ bijects it with $X$.

**$e$-core.** The **top-packed $\beta$-set** of $X$ is
$$X^{(e)}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^{e-1}\{ae+i:0\le a\le|X^{(e)}_i|-1\},$$
the configuration obtained from $A_X$ by sliding every bead up as far as it
goes on its own runner, i.e. into the topmost $|X^{(e)}_i|$ positions of
runner $i$. The **$e$-core** of $\lambda$ is
$$C_e(\lambda):=P(X^{(e)}).$$

**$e$-quotient and $e$-weight.** Choose the $\beta$-set $X$ of $\lambda$ to be
*normalised*, meaning $|X|\equiv0\pmod e$. Then define the **$e$-quotient** of
$\lambda$ to be the $e$-tuple of partitions
$$Q_e(\lambda):=(\lambda^{(0)},\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(e-1)}),\qquad \lambda^{(i)}:=P(X^{(e)}_i),$$
each runner read as a $1$-abacus, and the **$e$-weight** of $\lambda$ to be
$$w_e(\lambda):=|Q_e(\lambda)|:=\textstyle\sum_{i=0}^{e-1}|\lambda^{(i)}|.$$
A normalised $\beta$-set exists: by
[[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]] the $\beta$-sets of
$\lambda$ are the sets $X_\lambda+l$, $l\in\mathbb N_0$, and
$|X_\lambda+l|=|X_\lambda|+l$, so among the $e$ consecutive shifts
$l,\dots,l+e-1$ exactly one has size divisible by $e$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $e\ge2$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-abacus configurations as in
[[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]] and the top-packed set
$X^{(e)}$ of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]. For every $\beta$-set $X$
of $\lambda$ the partition $P(X^{(e)})$ is the same, so the $e$-core
$C_e(\lambda)=P(X^{(e)})$ is a well-defined $e$-core partition, and it is
exactly the terminal partition reached by successively removing removable
border strips of size $e$ from $[\lambda]$ until none is left
([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]],
[[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]). In particular every
maximal sequence of such removals gives the same terminal partition
$C_e(\lambda)$, each removed strip has size exactly $e$, and the terminal
partition contains no hook of length $e$. Moreover any two normalised beta-sets
($e\mid|X|$) give the same ordered quotient $Q_e(\lambda)$ and weight.

No choice principle is used.

Let $e\ge2$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ and
$e$-weight $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$
([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Then
$$n=|\lambda|=|C_e(\lambda)|+e\,w_e(\lambda),$$
so $w_e(\lambda)=(n-|C_e(\lambda)|)/e\in\mathbb N_0$. Equivalently every
sequence of removals of removable border strips of size $e$ from $\lambda$ down
to its $e$-core
([[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]]) has exactly
$w_e(\lambda)$ steps, and $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$ equals both the number
of hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$ and, by the bijection of
[[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]], the number of hooks of
$\lambda$ of length divisible by $e$.

Throughout the proof, $\lambda\setminus H$ means deletion of the rim strip
corresponding to the node hook $H$, as in
[[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]].

No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda'$, $L=\ell(w_\lambda)$ and $N=\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))$. Let $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with its Murphy form $G_{\lambda'}$, and the sign automorphism $\theta$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ be the $\theta$-twisted cell module of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]. Then:

1. There is a base-change compatible isomorphism of right $H$-modules $$\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta,\qquad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda)=m_0,\quad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda h)=m_0\theta(h)\ \ (h\in H),$$ where $m_0$ is the class of $x_{\lambda'}$ in $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and the right side is computed with the ordinary action on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and read in the twist; in particular $\Phi_\lambda(e_t)=m_0\theta(T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)})$ for $t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda')$. For a class $m\in C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and any lift $\widetilde m\in M(\lambda')$, the inverse is $\Phi_\lambda^{-1}(m)=q^{-N}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\theta(\widetilde m)$, independently of the chosen lift.

2. With $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$ the transported form of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] and $u_\lambda(q):=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$, $$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$ over every commutative $R$ with $q\in R^\times$. No unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar occurs: $u_\lambda$ is the explicit unit $q^{N-L}$ in the fixed normalizations of this page.

3. Consequently $\Phi_\lambda$ maps the radical of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ onto the radical of $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$, the induced map between the quotients is an isomorphism, with the corresponding cell-form quotients $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a field, when the quotients are nonzero they are the simple heads; when the forms are identically zero, the displayed quotients are zero and no assertion about the actual module heads is made. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all divisibility submodules and their reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and the twist, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

For every commutative ring $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive
$R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with
$\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star
anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.

2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying
$R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$
is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and
simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.

3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with
$(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite
free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and
$(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.

4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest
element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit
$q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every
form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism
$w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: One component at a time, at level one. Suppose first that the component sizes agree. For a single component $a$ of rank $m$, the actual level-one Hecke algebra is the finite Hecke algebra by [F3]. Its same-core Specht-block clause [F4], together with the level-one case of the Jantzen linkage equivalence [F1], connects any two rank-$m$ partitions with equal $e$-core by level-one Jantzen edges. The exact signed-conjugate bridge is $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\cong P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})^\theta$, where $\theta(T_i)=-zT_i^{-1}$ and $P$ denotes the ordinary Dipper–James Specht module. If $\lambda,\mu$ have equal $e$-cores, their transposes have the equal transposed cores, so [F4] puts $P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})$ and $P(\mu^{\mathsf T})$ in the same ordinary Hecke block. An algebra automorphism sends primitive central idempotents bijectively to primitive central idempotents; its exact module pullback therefore preserves the equivalence of sharing a block. Applying the SAME $\theta$ to both modules gives the required Murphy block equality and then [F1] gives the level-one Jantzen connection. No untwisted conjugate-dual identity or algebraic-closure assumption is used. The rank $m=0$ case has a single empty partition and needs no block theorem.

Equalizing the component weights with charged runners. Choose a component $a$ whose weight exceeds its target and a component $b$ whose weight is deficient. A positive-weight component has a removable rim $e$-hook by [F5]. For each component $c$ use the charged infinite beta set $B_c=\{\lambda_j^{(c)}+c_c-j:j\ge1\}$. This is the ordinary beta display shifted to charge $c_c$, with all sufficiently negative positions occupied and all sufficiently positive positions vacant. A removable hook is a bead move $u\mapsto u-e$ to a gap, and its charged foot residue is $u-e+1$ modulo $e$. To see the foot formula, order the beta positions before and after the move: the affected consecutive rows form the boundary strip between the starting and ending positions, and the leftmost removed box in the last affected row has charged content one more than the ending position. The inverse move wraps a hook whose foot has charged residue one more than its starting position. Let $f$ be the charged foot residue of the hook removed from $a$. In $B_b$, choose the largest occupied integer $v\equiv f-1\pmod e$; it exists by the two tail conditions, and $v+e$ is vacant by maximality. Move $v$ to $v+e$ in component $b$. Its new hook has charged foot residue $v+1=f$. Equivalently, in an uncharged display for component $b$ the runner to use is $f-c_b-1$ modulo $e$, so different component charges cannot be ignored. Both moves stay on their own runners and preserve the component cores and total rank. The earlier of $a,b$ determines the strict dominance orientation: removing boxes there and adding them later decreases every intervening prefix sum; adding boxes there reverses the inequality. In that orientation the equal-remainder hook pair is unique, since the two changed components determine both strips. Its charged foot residues agree, so the foot difference evaluates to zero at $t=1$; it is nonzero over $F(t)$ by [F2], and consequently has a finite positive valuation. Thus the single signed contribution is nonzero, giving a Jantzen edge. If $\delta_c$ is the current component weight minus its target, then $\delta_a\ge1$, $\delta_b\le-1$, and this transfer changes $\sum_c\delta_c^2$ by $-2\delta_a+2\delta_b+2\le-2$. Finitely many such transfers therefore equalize all component weights.

Fixed component sizes. For two full multipartitions that differ only in component $a$, every contributing equal-remainder hook pair in $J$ lies in $a$: the other components are unchanged on both sides and cancelling hooks between two unchanged components would return the same multipartition. The common residue factor $Q_at^{na}$ is a unit of $\mathcal O$, and replacing it by the level-one factor $Q_at^m$ multiplies each foot difference by a Laurent unit, so the valuation is unchanged and the full-level $J$ coefficient equals the level-one coefficient of [F2]. Inserting the level-one paths of step 1.1 in component $a$ and leaving the other components fixed connects all multipartitions with equal component sizes and the same component cores.

Conclusion. Steps 1.2 equalize component sizes along Jantzen edges from any starting multipartition, and step 2.1 connects all multipartitions of fixed component sizes with equal component cores. Composing the two finite chains connects any two multipartitions of rank $n$ with equal componentwise $e$-cores, proving that they are $J$-equivalent; the fixed-size comparison of coefficients is step 2.1.

citations.quote: Let $F$ be any field, let $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite multiplicative order $e\ge2$, let $\ell\ge1$ be arbitrary and let $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$ with charges $c_a\in\mathbb Z$. Fix $n\ge0$ and let $S_F$ be the cyclotomic $q$-Schur algebra over $F$ with summands indexed by all $\ell$-multipartitions of $n$.

Fix finite $e\ge2$, $\ell\ge1$ and integer charges $c_1,\dots,c_\ell$. Give the nodes of component $a$ the residue $c_a+j-i\pmod e$. Write $C_i$ for the residue counts, $\delta_i$ for removable minus addable $i$-nodes, and $m_i:=\#\{a:c_a\equiv i\}$. Then $$\delta_i=2C_i-C_{i-1}-C_{i+1}-m_i,$$ with both neighbouring terms retained (and counted twice) at $e=2$.

Under the arbitrary-field finite-$e$ nondegenerate cyclotomic hypotheses of [[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]], any two $\ell$-multipartitions of a common rank $n$ with equal componentwise $e$-cores are $J$-equivalent, even if their component sizes differ.
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]).

derivations.claim: Necessity. Suppose $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$; then at least one term of its signed integer sum has nonzero valuation, and evaluating that generic foot difference at $t=1$ gives zero, so the two foot eigenvalues coincide and, since $q_H$ has order $e$, their charged foot residues agree. The two hooks have equal length and the same remainder diagram. Along a rim strip, reading from its lowest-left node to its highest-right node increases the content by one at every step, so its residue multiset consists of $h$ consecutive residues starting at its foot; hence the two removed hooks have identical residue counts and $C(\lambda)=C(\mu)$. Transitivity gives the necessity of $C(\lambda)=C(\mu)$ for every $J$-path. [F1, F4, algebra]

Sufficiency setup: cores and lifts. Let $\kappa$ be the componentwise core of a member of the rank-$n$ content class; its size is at most $n$ and congruent to $n$ modulo $e$, and by [F2] all such cores have the same hub and are connected by the prescribed switch sequence. Every intermediate core has size at most $n$ and the same hub, so adding $(n-\text{core size})/e$ $e$-hooks produces a rank-$n$ multipartition of the same content by the equal-hub/equal-size clause of [F2]. [F2, F4]

The explicit one-hook lift across a core switch. Let $\kappa'$ be obtained from $\kappa$ by the oriented switch in rows $i,j$ and components $a,b$ of [F2], with $\gamma\ge2$, so $|\kappa'|=|\kappa|-eD$ with $D=\gamma-2\ge0$. Write $u=i+et_{ia}$, $v=j+e(t_{ja}+1)$, $v'=j+et_{jb}$, $u'=i+e(t_{ib}+1)$: the switch removes bead $u$ and inserts $v$ in component $a$, and removes $v'$ and inserts $u'$ in component $b$. Put $w=(n-|\kappa|)/e\ge0$, form $\lambda$ from $\kappa$ by moving the lowest bead $u$ of the $i$-runner in component $a$ to $u+ew$ (adding $w$ $e$-hooks on this runner), and form $\mu$ from $\kappa'$ by moving its lowest bead $v$ on the $j$-runner in component $a$ to $v+e(w+D)$. Both have size $n$, the same hub, and by [F2] equal content. Their beta sets in component $a$ differ only by replacing $u+ew$ with $v+e(w+D)$, and those in component $b$ only by replacing $v'$ with $u'$. Because $(v-u)+(u'-v')=-eD$, we have $v+e(w+D)-(u+ew)=v'-u'$, so the two components exchange a single rim hook of length $|v'-u'|$, nonzero since $i\ne j$ modulo $e$. If $v'-u'>0$, component $b$ unwraps and $a$ wraps a hook with foot residue $i+1$ modulo $e$; otherwise $a$ unwraps and $b$ wraps one with foot residue $j+1$. In both cases the hook feet have equal residues, and the hook pair is uniquely determined because distinct components change, so the $J$ coefficient of [F1] is a single signed valuation, a nonzero integer with no cancellation. Hence $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are Jantzen-connected by one edge; this supplies the detail abbreviated in the Lyle–Mathas tight lemma. [F1, F2, step 1.2]

Termination and conclusion. The generic difference of the unique hook contribution is nonzero by [F1], and its specialization vanishes because the charged feet agree, so its positive integer valuation cannot disappear under reduction modulo $\operatorname{char}F$. The fixed-core lemma [F3] permits replacing arbitrary lifts by the chosen lifts before and after each switch, and strict descent lowers the nonnegative core size by at least $e$, so the process terminates at a minimum core; all minimum cores have equal size and are connected by $\gamma=2$ switches, whose rank-$n$ lifts are connected by the same explicit construction of step 2.1. Together with the fixed-component-size lifts of [F3], every member of the content class is Jantzen-connected to every other, and step 1.1 gives the converse. The empty rank has only one multipartition and is immediate; no affine-center or primitive-block theorem has entered the proof. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

Use the charged finite-$e$ **field** specialization of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] over any field $F$. Then $H^\Lambda_d$ is finite-dimensional before any basis independence argument.

Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az\text{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). A **central idempotent** of $A$ is an idempotent $e\in Z(A)$; it is **primitive** when $e\ne0$ and $e$ is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents.

Let $F$ be any field of characteristic $e>0$ with $e\ge2$, and let $H_d^\Lambda$ be the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra with the FIRST relation $f(x_1)=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ge1$ ([[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]).

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital algebra over a field $F$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), with commuting elements $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and split joint regular-module generalized-eigenprojectors $p_{\mathrm{word}}\in A$: the $p_{\mathrm{word}}$ are pairwise orthogonal, sum to $1$, and $(x_r-\mathrm{word}_r)p_{\mathrm{word}}$ is nilpotent for every $r$.

For $H_n$ in [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over the universal Laurent parameter ring, the elements $m_{st}$ indexed by all $\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a basis and a dominance-cellular datum: $$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$ with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field $F$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and cell-form quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$. Then:

1. every nonzero $D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple
   $A$-modules occur exactly once this way, and $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0$ implies
   $\lambda\ge\mu$, with $[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$; here
   "nonzero quotient" means nonzero form, not necessarily a nondegenerate form
   on $C_\lambda$;
2. every nonzero cell module, including labels with zero-form quotient, has
   all its composition factors in a single block
   ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
3. two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a
   finite chain of nonzero cell modules whose neighbouring terms share a
   simple composition factor;
4. for one primitive idempotent $e_\mu$ per simple,
   $$\dim_Fe_\mu Ae_\nu=\sum_\lambda[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\,[C_\lambda:D_\nu].$$

If the cellular index set $T(\lambda)$ is empty, then $C_\lambda=D_\lambda=0$.
Its block support, the set of primitive central idempotents $b$ with
$C_\lambda b\ne0$, is empty, and it has no simple composition factors.
It does not participate in the nonzero-cell linkage criterion of (3), and
its term in the corner sum of (4) is zero.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$ acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$ carrying $r$.

Over any field $F$, at any level $\ell\ge1$, with $q_H\ne1$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and charges $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$, use the actual multipartition-summand Schur cover and standards of [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]] and the integer $J_{\lambda\mu}$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]].

derivations.claim: Base cases. At rank $0$ the algebra is $F$, the empty-word projector is $1$, and this is its unique primitive central idempotent. At positive rank and level $0$ the defining polynomial is $1$, so the algebra is $0$ and every content sector is $0$, with no nonzero blocks. Hence assume rank $d\ge1$ and level $\ell\ge1$. [F1]

The degenerate branch. In the branch $q_H=1$ necessarily $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$. The center is the full symmetric-polynomial image over this $F$ by [F3], and [F4] applies to the early CRT projectors and proves that their content sums are zero or primitive. This uses neither a field extension nor a power-sum generation assertion. [F1, F3, F4]

The nondegenerate branch: labels of sectors. In the branch $q_H\ne1$ choose a charge list $c_1,\dots,c_\ell$ repeating each $i$ exactly $\lambda_i$ times, so $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$ and the first polynomial is unchanged. The arbitrary-level Murphy cellular basis and the finite cellular head lemma [F5] supply all simple $H_d^\Lambda$-modules as nonzero Specht quotients $D^\lambda$, and the content-triangular JM action [F6] says every word on $S^\lambda$, hence on $D^\lambda$, has the node content $C(\lambda)$. Thus a simple module lying in a nonzero sector $e_\alpha$ has a label $\lambda$ with $C(\lambda)=\alpha$. [F1, F5, F6]

Primitivity of the nonzero sectors. Any two simple modules in the sector $e_\alpha$ have labels with equal content, so [F7] connects the labels by integer Jantzen edges and [F8] transfers this to a common Hecke block. If $e_\alpha$ decomposed into two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents $u,v$, the nonzero finite algebras $uH_d^\Lambda$ and $vH_d^\Lambda$ would each have a simple module, obtained from a proper right ideal of maximal dimension. Those simple modules cannot lie in one block, because the central idempotent $u$ acts as the identity on the first and as zero on the second, and all modules and extensions split by $u$. This contradicts the one-block assertion, so $e_\alpha$ is primitive. [F1, F7, F8, step 1.3]

Every block is a content sector. In either branch let $b$ be a primitive central idempotent and write $b=\sum_\alpha be_\alpha$. The terms are central orthogonal idempotents, so precisely one is nonzero and $b=be_\alpha$; primitivity of the nonzero $e_\alpha$ from step 1.2 or step 2.1 gives $b=e_\alpha$. Hence the nonzero content sums are exactly all primitive central idempotents and the decomposition $H_d^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha e_\alpha H_d^\Lambda$ is precisely the block decomposition [F2]. All sums are finite, the field characteristic never reduces an integer $K_0$ adjacency, and no affine-block classification or citation-only center theorem is consumed. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

derivations.claim: The mutually inverse early maps. By [F3] the local KLR generators of the nonzero sector satisfy the KLR relations, so there is a unique algebra homomorphism $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ sending $e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $y_r\mapsto y_r$ and $\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$; by [F4] the Hecke generators $X_r,T_r$ (respectively $x_r,s_r$) of the sector satisfy the affine Hecke and cyclotomic relations, so there is a unique homomorphism $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\sigma(e(i))=e(i)$ for $i\in I_\alpha$. The early central sector isomorphism [F2] proves, by explicit generator composites that are literally the identity, that $\rho$ and $\sigma$ are mutually inverse over $F$ for every content, including the zero sectors, with $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ if and only if $R^\Lambda_\alpha=0$. No algebraic closure, root extraction, dimension argument or primitive-block premise was used to construct these maps. [F2, F3, F4]

Primitivity of the sector. By [F1] every nonzero $e_\alpha$ is primitive and every nonzero $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is an actual block. Hence for the content $\alpha$ of the Statement the sector $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is a block of $H^\Lambda_d$, and the block terminology in the Statement is justified rather than assumed. [F1]

The blockwise isomorphism and its normalization. Restricting the mutually inverse maps of step 1.1 to the nonzero sector $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ gives mutually inverse unital $F$-algebra isomorphisms $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ and $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$. Because $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the algebra generated by $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the defining KLR relations and $\rho$ is an isomorphism, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is generated by the images of those generators subject only to those relations. Group multiplication in $\mathbb F_3S_3$ gives $C^2=0$, because the three squares contribute $3=0$ and the six cross products contribute three copies of each 3-cycle; and $Cc=Cs=1+(123)+(132)$. Put $e_+=(1+c)/2$ and $e_-=(1-c)/2$; since $c^2=1$ and $2$ is invertible in $\mathbb F_3$, these are idempotents, and they are the actual joint CRT projectors $e(0,1,2)$ and $e(0,2,1)$ of the two standard residue words. With $x_3=C-c$ one computes $y_1=y_2=0$ and $y_3=C$: indeed $(c-1)e_+=(c-1)(1+c)/2=0$, $(c-2)e_-=(c+1)(1-c)/2=0$, and $x_3-i_3$ equals $C$ on both projectors. All other residue words vanish, and both projectors are nonzero by the group basis. [given, algebra]

There is exactly one block. The full center has basis $1$, $C$, $1+(123)+(132)$ and its augmentation ideal is spanned by the last two elements, with $(1+(123)+(132))^2=0$ and $C(1+(123)+(132))=0$; hence the augmentation ideal is square-zero and contains no nonzero idempotent. Therefore the only central idempotents are $0$ and $1$, so $\mathbb F_3S_3$ is a single block and the two projectors combine as $e_\alpha=e_++e_-=1$. [given, algebra]

Direct group multiplication using $c^2=s^2=1$ and $csc=scs$ gives $\psi_2e_+=e_-\psi_2$, $\psi_2e_-=e_+\psi_2$, $\psi_2^2e_+=Ce_+$, $\psi_2^2e_-=-Ce_-$, and $C\psi_2=\psi_2C=0$. derivations.claim: Transport of the grading. Fix a choice of admissible local normalising series, hence the isomorphism $\rho$ of [F1]. Declare each image of a homogeneous KLR generator to be homogeneous of the same degree; the images generate $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ and the KLR relations of [F2] are homogeneous, so the resulting degree assignment is well defined. Products retain degree addition because $\rho$ is an algebra map, so the degree summands are exactly the transported homogeneous summands. Since the generator images span the algebra, their assigned degrees determine every degree summand and give uniqueness of the grading for that fixed choice, with $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

Independence of the series choice. If $\rho'$ is the isomorphism attached to another admissible series, then $\rho'\circ\rho^{-1}$ sends each homogeneous native generator image of the first choice to the corresponding new image and hence is graded by construction; the two transported algebras are graded-isomorphic, while the underlying identity map on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ need not be graded because the two series differ by units that need not be homogeneous of degree zero. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

Triviality is not excluded. Assigning degree zero to every ordinary Hecke generator makes all defining relations homogeneous, so the degree-zero assignment is a legitimate grading of the ordinary Hecke presentation and no impossibility statement is asserted. A one-dimensional sector has only degree zero, because its unit has degree zero and it equals $F$; in particular the one-dimensional level-one rank-two $e=3$ blocks are trivially graded. [F1, step 1.1]

A concrete nontrivial witness. Consider level one, $e=2$, rank two. Of the four colour words only $(0,1)$ survives: the first-strand exponent zero kills $(1,0)$, and on $(0,0)$ the equal-colour mixed identities give $\psi_1y_2=1$ together with $\psi_1^2=0$, hence $\psi_1=0$ after left multiplication by $\psi_1$, giving $1=0$; so the equal-colour sector is zero, with $y_1=0$ and the crossing zero. The quadratic double-edge relation gives $y_2^2=0$. Conversely $e(0,1)=1$, $y_2=t$, $y_1=\psi_1=0$ in $F[t]/(t^2)$ satisfy all rank-two relations, so that sector is $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg t=2$, and its Brundan–Kleshchev image supplies an actual nontrivial transported grading, including in the characteristic-two degeneration. This is a witness that the construction can be nontrivial, not a claim about all sectors. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

Conclusion. Each fixed admissible series choice transports the KLR homogeneous decomposition to a $\mathbb Z$-grading of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$, unique for the induced generator degrees; different choices give graded-isomorphic transported algebras; and the grading may be nontrivial on some blocks while trivial on others, with the ordinary presentation retaining its degree-zero assignment. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.3] ∎
