Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels
$0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant
weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). In the nondegenerate branch the
distinct spectral values of the labels are $q^i$, while in the degenerate
branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$). Fix
$\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put
$\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)\ge0$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The **affine Hecke algebra of type
$A_{d-1}$** at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators
$X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$X_rX_s=X_sX_r,\qquad X_rX_r^{-1}=1,$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1).$$
The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (which forces $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The
**degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with
generators $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ subject to the relations
$$x_rx_s=x_sx_r,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_s=x_ss_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
$$s_r^2=1,\qquad s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1},\qquad s_rs_t=s_ts_r\quad(|r-t|>1);$$
its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis by
[[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is
$$H^\Lambda_d:=H_d\Big/\bigl\langle\textstyle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\bigr\rangle .$$

**Conventions and boundary.** Put $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is
imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator, and $T_r$ acts on positions
$r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one
$\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the algebra $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke
algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$
([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]).
Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of
unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$)
are outside this page's cyclic scope and are recorded as a deferred boundary in
the batch notes. These presentations and the charged quotients are the ones of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no
embedding of the label set $I$ into $F$ is claimed in the nondegenerate branch,
and no choice principle is used.

With the conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], the images of the ordered
monomials
$$x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w\quad(0\le m_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d)$$
in the degenerate case, respectively
$$X_1^{m_1}\cdots X_d^{m_d}T_w\quad(0\le m_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d)$$
in the nondegenerate case, form an $F$-basis of $H^\Lambda_d$. In particular
$\dim_FH^\Lambda_d=\ell^dd!$ and $H^\Lambda_d$ is finite dimensional. For
$d=0$ the singleton empty word gives $H^\Lambda_0=F$ and dimension one
independently of $\ell$. If $\ell=0$ and $d>0$, the relation $1=0$ gives the
zero algebra and the empty basis; no ambiguous $0^0$ convention is used.

Work in the charged finite-$e$ field conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]. By
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]],
$H^\Lambda_d$ is finite-dimensional and each minimal polynomial of the
polynomial generator $z_r=X_r$ (nondegenerate normalization) respectively
$x_r$ (degenerate normalization) splits over the residues $c_i=q_H^i$
respectively $i\cdot1_F$.

**Residue-sequence idempotents.** Let $\varepsilon_r(i)$ be the canonical CRT
primary idempotent of that generator at the spectral value $c_i$ associated with residue label $i$ (zero when that value is
absent), and put
$$e(\nu)=\prod_{r=1}^{d}\varepsilon_r(\nu_r)$$
for a residue sequence $\nu=(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_d)\in(\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z)^d$. On
every finite $H$-module the element $e(\nu)$ projects onto the joint
generalized residue space, and these mutually orthogonal idempotents sum to
$1$. At content $\alpha$ put
$$e_\alpha=\sum_{\nu\in I_\alpha}e(\nu),$$
the sum over residue sequences of content $\alpha$; it is central, and
$H^\Lambda_d$ is the direct sum of its central ideals
$$H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d\,e_\alpha.$$
By
[[thm-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sectors-are-zero-or-primitive-blocks]],
every nonzero $e_\alpha$ is primitive, so every nonzero $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
an actual block
([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
this block assertion is proved there, not retained as an unused citation.
The algebra basis and dimension convention is that of
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra-basis-and-dimension]].

**Level one.** At level one, $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, the polynomial generators
correspond under the explicit finite-Hecke inverse of
[[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]] to
$$X_r=q_H^j\bigl(1+(q_H-1)L_r\bigr)\quad\text{(nondegenerate)},\qquad x_r=j+L_r\quad\text{(degenerate)},$$
where $L_r$ is the ordinary additive Jucys–Murphy element. Thus on a standard
tableau node of content $m$ their eigenvalues are $q_H^{j+m}$ respectively
$j+m$, while $L_r$ itself has additive $q$-content $[m]_{q_H}$. The nonzero
joint projectors are precisely the residue words of standard tableaux
([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]), and grouping
those words by content gives the block labels.

**Boundary conventions.** At rank zero the empty projector is $1$ and the
unique block is $F$; at level zero and positive rank all projectors and blocks
are zero. The projection, centrality, and block-decomposition assertions
recorded here are exactly the proved content-sector statements of the linked
suppliers; this definition introduces no new primitive-block classification
of its own. It uses no choice principle: all spectra, projectors, and sums are
finite.

Let $F$ be any field, let $q\in F^\times$ have finite quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)\ge2$, let $\Lambda\in P^+$ be dominant and let $\alpha\in Q_+$ have
height $d$ with $e_\alpha\ne0$, in the conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] and
[[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]. Then the
homomorphisms $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and
$\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually
inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Equivalently, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
generated by the Khovanov–Lauda generators
$\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the relations
(1.6)–(1.15), and the isomorphism is normalized by
$\rho(e(i))=e(i)$ and
$$\rho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)\quad(q\ne1),\qquad \rho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)\quad(q=1).$$
The degenerate ($q=1$, $\operatorname{char}F=e$) and nondegenerate
($q\ne1$) cases are proved separately, and both hold in finite quantum
characteristic $e$.

derivations.claim: The positive-rank affine algebra is infinite dimensional. At rank one the affine presentation is $F[X_1^{\pm1}]$ in NG and $F[x_1]$ in DG by [F1], and their distinct powers are independent. More generally for any $d\ge1$, the NG assignments $T_r\mapsto q_H$, $X_r\mapsto q_H^{r-1}t$ give a surjection onto $F[t,t^{-1}]$: the quadratic relation reads $q_H^2=(q_H-1)q_H+q_H$, the Bernstein relation reads $q_H^2q_H^{r-1}t=q_Hq_H^rt$, and the commuting and braid relations are scalar identities. In DG the assignments $s_r\mapsto1$, $x_r\mapsto t+(r-1)1_F$ similarly give a surjection onto $F[t]$, since the adjacent mixed relation reads $t+(r-1)=(t+r)-1$ and all other relations hold. The images contain $t$, so the affine algebras are infinite-dimensional at every positive rank. Every cyclotomic block is finite-dimensional by [F2], and its KLR partner has the same dimension by [F4]; thus neither is isomorphic to the whole positive-rank affine algebra. At rank zero both presentations give $F$, and the obstruction does not apply.

The whole cyclotomic quotient is not one block. Take $\Lambda=\Lambda_0$ (level one), $d=2$, $e=3$ and $q_H$ a primitive cube root of unity. By the level-one identification [F3] the algebra is $H_{F,q}(S_2)\cong F[T]/((T-q_H)(T+1))\cong F\times F$, since $q_H\ne-1$ in characteristic $\ne3$. Here $X_1=1$ and $X_2=q_H^{-1}T_1^2$, so the two factors $T_1=q_H$ and $T_1=-1$ have polynomial eigenwords $(1,q_H)$ and $(1,q_H^2)$, hence residue words $(0,1)$ and $(0,2)$. Thus there are two nonzero blocks $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}$ and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$, each one dimensional with residue sequences $(0,1)$ and $(0,2)$. Therefore $H^\Lambda_2$ has dimension $2$ and is not isomorphic to either one-dimensional block; on the KLR side [F4] gives $R^\Lambda_2=R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}\oplus R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$, which is not isomorphic to a single block.

Conclusion. Both branches of the attempted replacement fail: the affine algebra is infinite dimensional, and the whole cyclotomic quotient decomposes into more than one block. Summing the central-sector isomorphisms on both sides remains valid.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be pairwise comaximal ideals, where $r\ge1$. Then the canonical map
$$ R\longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i,\qquad x\longmapsto(x+I_1,\ldots,x+I_r) $$
is surjective, its kernel is $\bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i$, and
$$ \bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i=\prod_{i=1}^r I_i. $$
Equivalently,
$$ R/\prod_{i=1}^r I_i\cong\prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i. $$

derivations.claim: **Per-position polynomial projectors and integer spectra.** At rank zero, $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ has no polynomial generators, the sole empty-word projector and content projector are $1$, and the sector is the single ground-field block with its usual vector duality. Thus all rank-zero assertions follow directly; the spectral argument below concerns $d\ge1$. The finite-dimensional algebra has a faithful regular representation. For adjacent dots put $\delta=x_r-x_{r+1}$ and $\phi_r=s_r\delta+1$. The native cross relations give $\phi_rx_r=x_{r+1}\phi_r$, $\phi_rx_{r+1}=x_r\phi_r$ and $\phi_r^2=1-\delta^2$. On a generalized joint weight whose adjacent entries differ by neither $1$ nor $-1$, $1-\delta^2$ is invertible by a finite nilpotent geometric series; hence the swapped weight is nonzero. If any entry of a nonzero weight is not integral, move its leftmost nonintegral entry left across all preceding integral entries. The swaps are invertible, but the resulting first entry contradicts $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$. Thus all spectra are integral. For each position separately choose an annihilator $p_r(z)=\prod_{a\in S_r}(z-a)^{N_r}$ from its finite regular spectrum, with $N_r=\dim H_d(m)$ sufficient. Chinese remainder interpolation gives mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors $E_{r,a}(x_r)$ summing to one. Their products $e(i)=\prod_r E_{r,i_r}(x_r)$ give exactly the simultaneous generalized-weight projectors on every finite module; algebra identities follow from regular faithfulness. There is no assertion that the first-position cyclotomic polynomial annihilates other dots.

**The content-block centre comparison.** In an admissible stable realization the actual endomorphism theorem identifies $H:=H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$. Choose $Q=T_\alpha\oplus Q_0$, where $Q_0$ is a projective generator of its genuine category-O block, and put $A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$ and $M=\pi Q$. Full faithfulness on projectives identifies $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)$ with $\operatorname{End}_H(M)$, and $M$ contains the regular left module $\pi T_\alpha=H$. No projectivity of all of $M$ over $H$ is assumed.

**The exact centre calculation.** A central endomorphism $z$ of $M$ commutes with the projection onto its direct summand $H$, so it restricts on $H$ to right multiplication $R_h$. Commuting with every $R_b$ forces $h\in Z(H)$. For each $m\in M$, extend the map $f_m:H\to M$, $a\mapsto am$, by zero on the chosen complement of $H$ in $M$. Commutation with this endomorphism gives $zf_m=f_mR_h$; evaluation at one gives $z(m)=hm$. Conversely multiplication by central $h$ commutes with every $H$-map. These constructions are inverse, proving $Z(\operatorname{End}_H M)=Z(H)$, and passage to opposite rings preserves centres. The stated Choice assumption is inherited only for the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers.

**Central content interpolation.** Symmetric polynomials in the dots commute with crossings by the native cross relations, because $s_r$ commutes with $x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $x_rx_{r+1}$ and with all other dots; these generate the elementary symmetric polynomials. Their elementary symmetric values distinguish the finitely many different multisets of generalized joint eigenvalues. Finite Chinese remainder interpolation in these symmetric operators therefore gives a central multiset projector. Its action on every regular generalized weight is one precisely on that multiset, so it equals the orbit sum $e_\alpha$ of the per-position projectors from step 1.1. This argument does not require the annihilating polynomials for different positions to be equal.

**A single linkage block has no split central idempotent.** $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a single linkage block by [[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]: it admits no decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal factors. A central idempotent $f=f^2\ne0$ of $A$ with $f\ne1$ would split the projective generator $Q=Qf\oplus Q(1-f)$ into two nonzero summands whose Hom-spaces in both directions vanish, because every morphism between them is annihilated by composing with $f$ on either side in the two possible orders; this exhibits $\mathcal O_\alpha$ as the product of the two nonzero full subcategories generated by these summands, contradicting single-linkage. Hence $Z(A)$ has no nontrivial idempotent, and by step 1.2 the same holds for $Z(H)=Z(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$: the stable content component is a single block.

**Symmetric polynomials in the $x_r$ are central.** It suffices to show that the elementary symmetric functions in the $x_r$ are fixed by conjugation with each basic transposition $s_r$, since these generate the symmetric polynomials and commute with all $x_i$ with $i\notin\{r,r+1\}$. The defining cross relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ and $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$; multiplying the first by $s_r$ on the left yields $s_rx_{r+1}s_r=x_r+s_r$, and the second yields $s_rx_rs_r=x_{r+1}-s_r$. Consequently $s_r(x_r+x_{r+1})s_r=x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $s_r(x_rx_{r+1})s_r=(x_{r+1}-s_r)(x_r+s_r)=x_rx_{r+1}$, so the two elementary generators in the pair $\{x_r,x_{r+1}\}$ are fixed, and $s_r^2=1$ makes the same true for every polynomial in them; together with the commuting generators this fixes every symmetric polynomial. Comparing with step 2.1, $e_\alpha$ commutes with every $x_i$ and every $s_r$, hence is central in $H_d(m)$.

**An intrinsic block in a stable realization.** Fix $\alpha$ of height $d$ for any admitted consecutive $I$. Choose an integer $k$ below all its residue supports and all charges, with $q_l=m_l-k+1\ge d$ and $q_l>0$, and put $q_j=m_j-k+1$, $n_{\rm row}=q_1$, and $c_j=m_j-q_j+n_{\rm row}=m_1$. These heights are nonincreasing and the common origin is admissible; the cyclotomic roots of this stable realization are exactly $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Its algebra is therefore the very same presentation $H_d(m)$, with the same named generators. The joint polynomial projectors of step 1.1 are uniquely determined by their regular generalized eigenspaces, so its projector for the fixed multiset $\alpha$ is exactly $e_\alpha$, independently of the auxiliary lower endpoint or the ambient residue interval. The stable endomorphism supplier thus identifies this exact algebra $e_\alpha H_d(m)$ with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$, and step 2.2 proves (b). For any finite list of residue operations choose $k$ stable for every occurring degree and below every occurring residue; the same identity of presentations in adjacent degrees fixes $\iota$, the projectors $u_{\alpha,i}$, and their induction/restriction bimodules. This uses no equivalence between different category-$\mathcal O$ cuts and no transport of Specht modules.

**Simple-preserving duality.** In the stable finite realization, the proof paragraph **Simple images and standard heads** of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] identifies every Hecke simple with $\pi L(A)$ for a standard label. Restricted category-$\mathcal O$ duality fixes $L(A)$, as recorded in [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], and the paragraph **The actual duality comparison** of the Whittaker supplier proves $\pi D\cong(\pi-)^{\circledast}$. Hence $(\pi L(A))^{\circledast}\cong\pi DL(A)\cong\pi L(A)$. The intrinsic block identity of step 3.2 preserves the generator-fixing anti-involution, so the same conclusion holds for arbitrary admitted $I$. Commutation with residue functors alone would not establish this simple-preserving assertion.

**Zero components and local units.** Centrality does not exclude $e_\alpha=0$: steps 2.2 and 3.2 prove primitivity only for nonzero components and do not assert that every content occurs. Suppose $I=[a,b]$. For any nonzero supported component choose the stable realization of step 3.2 with $k<a$. The nonzero object $T_\alpha$ has a simple constituent, hence a strict-column label of weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ by [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]. In this realization the ground column $j$ consists of the letters $k,\ldots,m_j$. Since $\alpha$ is supported on $[a,b]$ and $\alpha_i=\delta_i-\delta_{i+1}$, the multiplicity of every letter $k,\ldots,a-1$ in $\Lambda-\alpha$ is $l$, and that of every letter above $b+1$ is zero. Strictness allows each letter at most once per column, so every lower letter occurs in all columns and no upper letter occurs. Delete the common lower letters. The remaining columns have the fixed heights $m_j-a+1\ge0$ and entries in the finite alphabet $[a,b+1]$. Only finitely many such tableaux exist, independently of $k$ and $d$; their entry multisets determine $\alpha$ uniquely, since the simple roots are linearly independent. Consequently only finitely many supported components are nonzero, and the sum of their identities is a unit of the tower. For arbitrary $I$, finite sums of component identities are local units because every element of the direct sum has finite component support.

**Level zero and the vanishing witness.** At level $0$ the cyclotomic polynomial is the empty product $1$, so $H_d(m)=0$ for $d>0$ and only $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ remains; this is the convention of (2). For the witness, $I=\{0\}$, level $1$, charge $(0)$, $d=2$: the level-one presentation gives $x_1=0$ and $x_2=s_1$, so $H_2(0)=\mathbb C[S_2]$ with eigenvalues $\pm1$ for $x_2$; hence $E_0(x_2)=0$, $e(0,0)=0$, and the supported component $H^\Lambda_{2\alpha_0}=e_{(0,0)}H_2(0)$ is $0$, while $H_2(0)\ne0$. This completes the proof of the two claims (b) and the level-$0$ convention; the exactness and biadjointness clauses of (4) are the declared supplier statements of [[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]], not reproved here.

citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be essentially small abelian categories and let
$\mathcal D,\mathcal D'$ be essentially small additive categories. For any
abelian group $H$, every function
$\chi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)\to H$ satisfying
$\chi(Y)=\chi(X)+\chi(Z)$ for every short exact sequence
$0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\chi\colon G_0(\mathcal C)\to H$ with
$\overline\chi([X])=\chi(X)$. Every function
$\psi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)\to H$ satisfying
$\psi(X\oplus Y)=\psi(X)+\psi(Y)$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\psi\colon K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathcal D)\to H$ with
$\overline\psi([X])=\psi(X)$. Here $\operatorname{Iso}$ is the set of
isomorphism classes, so these are class functions.

An exact functor between essentially small abelian categories induces a
homomorphism on $G_0$, and an additive functor between essentially small
additive categories induces a homomorphism on split $K_0$. These assignments
preserve identities and composition. Naturally isomorphic exact functors, or
naturally isomorphic additive functors, induce equal homomorphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $L(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]].

**The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]].

**The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

**The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$.

**The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a Jordan–Hölder composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):L(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):L(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i).

**Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is its full weightwise $C_0$-dual: at $s=1$, $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ identifies it with $\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z,\alpha},\mathbb Z)$. In particular it is stable under divided powers, since the $e_i^{(n)}$ and $f_i^{(n)}$ are adjoint and preserve the lower lattice. Nondegeneracy identifies their rational scalar extensions, but does not identify the two integral lattices. The ground-generation use is the actual definition $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], specialized at one; it concerns the standard lattice only. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices.

**Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2]. The natural intertwining isomorphisms $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$ of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]], together with the category-O Chevalley action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], show that $[\pi]$ is a module map. Steps 1.1–2.2 identify its kernel with the span of the off-standard simple classes, precisely the kernel of the Fock projection. Thus the induced quotient map $\Phi$ intertwines $e_i,f_i$, proving the ordinary Chevalley clause of (ii). No head, socle or indecomposability assertion is inferred merely from exactness of a quotient.

**Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with both lattices equal to the ground line and every residue operator zero. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v).

**Crystal reachability and composition factors.** The source upper ground component is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space, so over $\mathbb Q$ it identifies the full costandard lattice's scalar extension with the irreducible highest module. Its highest vector therefore generates that module under lowering divided powers. Consequently every basis vector $D_A$ is a rational linear combination of lowering words applied to the ground vector. By step 3.1 each ordinary lowering word is the class of the corresponding exact residue-word module, with nonnegative simple-class coefficients by [F1]. If $D(A)$ occurred in none of these modules, every such word and every rational linear combination would have zero $D_A$ coefficient, contrary to the coefficient one in $D_A$. Thus some residue word contains $D(A)$ as a composition factor. This proves (iv) without requiring integral costandard generation or transport of head and socle through the quotient.

**The maps for arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Fix a finite set of contents and residue words. Choose $J=[k,r]$ so that $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and $J$ contains every intermediate root support; decrease $k$ further to reach the needed stable range. The Hecke-side map is literally the identity on $H_d(m)e_\alpha$: its spectral idempotent is the same sum over words of content $\alpha$, independently of whether the ambient supported interval is $I$ or $J$. It therefore fixes the intrinsic residue corner $u_{\alpha,i}$ and the bimodules defining $e_i,f_i$. On tableaux the lower transition adjoins the prescribed ground entries to every column, and the upper transition regards the same entries in a larger alphabet with no new top entries. Removing that common tail is the inverse on the selected weight. Column ground differences, hence intrinsic Specht partitions, are unchanged. The actual finite-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] gives $D_{\jmath A}=\jmath D_A$, $S_{\jmath B}=\jmath S_B$, $P_{\jmath A}=\jmath P_A$ and commuting normalized highest projections. Thus both upper and lower lattices are identified by their full bases, not just their rational spans. On overlapping cuts these maps compose by adjoining/removing the same ground entries and by the intrinsic Hecke identity; the normalized projections agree by highest-vector uniqueness. Every content, vector and finite residue word fits such a cut. Applying the bounded-below identifications and the rational-cyclicity argument of steps 1.1–4.1 there, and taking the compatible weightwise direct sum, proves all clauses for arbitrary admitted $I$. No full degree algebra is identified with a proper supported cut.

**Rational ground cyclicity.** The normalized $E/F$-contravariant highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space. Thus its weightwise duality identifies $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, interpreted as the direct sum of the costandard weight spaces, with the irreducible rational highest module. The ground vector maps to the normalized highest vector; its orbit under lowering divided powers therefore spans every weight space, as used in step 4.1. This proves the rational clause of (iii). The full unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module is not used.

**The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. The supported degree-one block is $B_0=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ and the supported degree-two block is $M_2(\mathbb C)$, with its simple represented by $x_1=N=E_{12}$, $s_1=-(E_{12}+E_{21})$ and $x_2=-N$. For completeness the whole degree-two presentation gives an isomorphism $H_2(0,0)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$: send $(x_1,x_2,s_1)$ to $(N,-N,-J)$ in the matrix factor and to $(\epsilon,\pm1+\epsilon,\pm1)$ in the other factors. The eight PBW spanning words are $1,x_1,x_2,x_1x_2,s_1,x_1s_1,x_2s_1,x_1x_2s_1$. The central sum $z=x_1+x_2$ has spectra $0,1,-1$ on the three factors; its Hermite polynomials $(1-z^2)^2$ and $\{1-(1-z^2)^2\pm(3z-z^3)/2\}/2$ project onto the three factors. Each factor is generated by the images, making the map onto an eight-dimensional product surjective and hence an isomorphism by the spanning bound. The all-zero-residue cut is exactly the matrix factor. In degree three an all-zero-residue module would have $x_2=-x_1$, $x_1^2=0$ from the matrix factor; $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$ and therefore with $x_2$, so $x_3=s_2x_2s_2+s_2=x_2+s_2$ has eigenvalues $\pm1$, contradiction. The same argument excludes all higher degrees. The first dot is not zero on the matrix simple. Induction from degree zero gives the regular $B_0$-module, with two simple factors. The matrix algebra is right-free of rank two over $B_0$ under $x\mapsto N$, so induction of its one-dimensional simple has dimension two and is the matrix simple; restricting that matrix simple gives the regular $B_0$-module. Restricting the degree-one simple to degree zero has dimension one. Thus the residue Ind/Res computations give $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$ and $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$, with the end actions zero. Their divided squares give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. Therefore $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$ and all their divided powers, contains the ground vector and excludes $D_{01}$. This is a proper integral costandard submodule, whereas over $\mathbb Q$ division by two recovers $D_{01}$. Degree one is not called a corner sitting inside degree two.

**Conclusion.** Step 2.1 identifies $G_0$ with the full integral costandard lattice and step 2.2 computes the Specht classes, proving (i); step 2.3 gives the divided-power integral forms and step 3.1 identifies the residue operators with the Chevalley operators, proving (ii); step 5.1 proves rational ground cyclicity, step 2.3 proves integral ground generation of the standard lattice and step 6.1 exhibits the index-two failure of integral costandard cyclicity, proving (iii) and its sharpness; step 4.1 proves the crystal reachability statement (iv); and step 3.2 (level zero) together with steps 6.1 and 4.2 separates the rational-cyclicity and categorical reachability conclusions from integral costandard cyclicity, as asserted in (v); step 4.2 supplies the arbitrary-$I$ maps and full integral extension. No step identifies $\{D_A\}$ with the standard divided-power lattice, and no integral costandard generation is used.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital algebra over a field $k$. Write
$S_1,\ldots,S_t$ for representatives of the isomorphism classes of simple
left $A$-modules, and choose a finite-dimensional projective cover
$q_i\colon P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ for each $i$. Then the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective left $A$-modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]) is the free abelian
group with basis $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$. In particular, each selected cover is
indecomposable, the $P_i$ are pairwise nonisomorphic, and every finite
dimensional projective is a finite direct sum of them. This result makes no
claim that the Cartan map to the short-exact-sequence group $G_0(A)$ is
invertible.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative $k$-algebra. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent all isomorphism classes of simple left $A$-modules, and let $q_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite-dimensional projective covers. Then $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$ and $[S_1],\ldots,[S_t]$ are bases of $K_0(A)$ and $G_0(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_A=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_A(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ In particular, if $\operatorname{End}_A(S_i)=k$ for every $i$, these bases are dual.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra, let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent the graded-simple shift orbits and let $p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite graded projective covers. Here graded-simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero graded submodule. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. Neither pairing statement asserts unimodularity of the projective-to-module Cartan map or of a projective/projective Cartan matrix. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebra. For a
finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and finite-dimensional left
$A$-module $M$, define the object-level value

$$h(P,M):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,M).$$

If $A$ is $\mathbb Z$-graded and $P,M$ are finite-dimensional graded left $A$-modules,
with $P$ projective in the degree-zero graded category, define

$$h_{\mathrm{gr}}(P,M):=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}v^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M),$$

where $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M)$ consists of $A$-linear maps sending each
$P_i$ into $M_{i+d}$. These are candidate values on object isomorphism
classes; no descent to pairings on $K_0\times G_0$ is asserted here.

Let $k$ be a field and let $A,B$ be finite-dimensional unital associative
$k$-algebras. Write $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$ and
$B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$ for their categories of finite-dimensional
left modules. Let
$F:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$
and
$G:B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}\to A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$
be exact $k$-linear adjoint functors $F\dashv G$, and suppose $F$ sends
finite-dimensional projective modules to finite-dimensional projective
modules. The induced maps
$F_*:K_0(A)\to K_0(B)$ and $G_*:G_0(B)\to G_0(A)$ then satisfy

$\langle F_*[P],[N]\rangle_B=\langle[P],G_*[N]\rangle_A$

for every finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and
finite-dimensional left $B$-module $N$.

For the graded analogue, let $A,B$ be finite-dimensional unital associative
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras, and let $F,G$ be exact $k$-linear adjoints
between their finite-dimensional graded-module categories with degree-zero
maps. Assume $F$ preserves finite graded projectives, and that there are
natural degree-zero isomorphisms
$F(M\{r\})\cong F(M)\{r\}$ and $G(N\{r\})\cong G(N)\{r\}$ for every
$r\in\mathbb Z$. The graded transposition is the one obtained from the
degree-zero adjunction after using these shift isomorphisms. Then the induced
maps
$F_*:K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)\to K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(B)$ and
$G_*:G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(B)\to G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ are
$\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-linear and satisfy

$$\langle F_*x,y\rangle_{B,\mathrm{gr}}=\langle x,G_*y\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}$$

for all $x\in K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and
$y\in G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(B)$. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

derivations.claim: **The split $K_0$ basis of covers.** Every simple finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-module has a projective cover, unique up to isomorphism, and the classes $[Y(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, of the covers of the simples $D(A)$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the split Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules; this is [F1] applied block by block and summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$.

**The left adjoint on projectives.** The Schur quotient $\pi$ has a left adjoint $\pi^*$ which is right exact on all modules and sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $\pi^*(Y(A))=P(A)$ and $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so $\pi^*$ recovers the standard-labelled prinjectives, and its exactness on arbitrary modules is not needed. These are the statements of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]].

**The standard lattice and its ground generation.** The standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ has $\mathbb Z$-basis $\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$, the source vector $P_A$ lies in the highest constituent with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}P_A=P_A$, and at parameter one $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}=G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)$, so $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ is integrally generated by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators: the actual lower lattice is $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. This is the parameter-one specialization of [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the basis statements of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]].

**The identification $K_0\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$.** Define $\Psi$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Psi([Y(A)])=P_A$; by step 1.3 both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules on the same index set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, so $\Psi$ is a group isomorphism onto $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, giving (i). The identification is realized functorially by $\pi^*$: step 1.2 shows that on projective classes the composite of $\pi^*$ with the category-O identification $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ at parameter one (the projective half of the tableau $K_0$/Fock identification of [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], proved in [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]) is $\Psi$, so no exactness of $\pi^*$ on non-projectives is used.

**The inclusion is the lattice inclusion.** The embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules induces a map on Grothendieck groups; in the category of finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-modules a projective class $[Y(A)]$ maps to the class of the same module, which under the identification $\Phi$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] is the costandard coordinate vector of the module $Y(A)$. By step 1.2, $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so this vector equals the image of $[P(A)]$ under the exact quotient, namely $P_A$ by step 1.3. Hence the composite $\Phi\circ(\text{inclusion})\circ\Psi^{-1}$ is the identity on the basis $\{P_A\}$, i.e. the natural inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$. It is injective because the vectors $P_A$ are linearly independent in the rational highest module, and hence also as elements of its full costandard lattice. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space; no claim that the embedded standard and costandard lattices coincide is used. This proves (ii).

**The Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing.** By [F2] the Cartan pairing descends to $K_0\times G_0$ and pairs the two bases dually; under the identifications of step 2.1 and of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the value on basis vectors is computed on the Fock side, where the pairing between the standard and costandard families at parameter one is the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ with $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ by [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. This proves (iii); in particular the costandard vectors entering the pairing are the projected simples $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$, not unprojected monomials.

**Chevalley operators on $K_0$.** Use the actual exact residue biadjunction from the tower supplier. For projective $P$ over the source, $\operatorname{Hom}(f_iP,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_i-)$ is exact, so $f_iP$ is projective; for projective $Q$ over the target, $\operatorname{Hom}(e_iQ,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(Q,f_i-)$ is exact, so $e_iQ$ is projective. Applying an idempotent by itself would not prove projectivity over a different algebra. These functors induce the adjoint operators of [F3] under the Hom pairing. Their $G_0$ counterparts are the already identified Chevalley operators, and the normalized highest pairing makes $e_i,f_i$ adjoint, so the same identification holds on $K_0$.

**The full integral extension.** The arbitrary-$I$ construction of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] fixes each selected finite-dimensional algebra $H_\alpha^\Lambda$, its simple labels and residue bimodules. An algebra identity fixes projective covers of the identified simples, uniquely up to isomorphism, so it fixes their split-$K_0$ basis. The lower lattice map is $P_A\mapsto P_{\jmath A}$ under the same common-ground-tail label map; the actual lower/global cut compatibility makes this an integral basis identification commuting with divided powers and with the pairing against the full upper basis. It therefore transports $\Psi$, the Cartan map and its pairing on each content; overlaps agree by the intrinsic algebra identity and the composable tail maps. Their weightwise direct sum proves (i)–(iv) for every admitted consecutive $I$, without claiming integral ground cyclicity for the costandard lattice.

**Conclusion.** Step 2.1 proves (i), step 3.1 proves the lattice-inclusion statement (ii), step 3.2 proves the pairing statement (iii) with its projected-simple qualification, step 4.1 proves (iv), step 5.1 gives their full integral arbitrary-$I$ extension, and the properties of the right-exact left adjoint stated in step 1.2 are exactly the assertion (v); at no point is exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules, or a recovery of all category-O projectives, assumed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Both identifications and their duality.** By [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the map $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$ identifies $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and is compatible with the standard classes $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$; by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]] the map $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ identifies $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ with the standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, the embedding of projectives induces the lattice inclusion, and the Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. Since the two lattice identifications are the actual source dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]] at parameter one, the identifications hold simultaneously and are mutually dual.

**The actual surviving-head calculation.** Fix $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and let $M=f_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$, or $M=e_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$. The local residue theorem [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] says $M=0$ exactly when the corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise its head is the simple $L(C)$ at that edge, and it is self-dual. The ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ is closed under the two crystal operators by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], so $C$ is standard. The actual detector/corner Hom comparison of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] applies to maps from a Std-head object to a Std-socle object. Applying it to $M$ and $L(B)$ for each standard $B$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_H(\pi M,D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,L(B))$, of dimension $\delta_{CB}$. Since the $D(B)$ are the complete distinct Hecke simples, this computes the head of $\pi M$ as the single simple $D(C)$ and proves $\pi M\ne0$. The natural intertwining of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]] identifies $\pi M$ with the appropriate Hecke translate of $D(A)$, and its natural duality comparison makes that translate self-dual. Its socle is therefore also $D(C)$. A direct sum of two nonzero finite-length modules has at least two nonzero simple head summands, so a module with simple head is indecomposable. If the edge is absent the translate is zero by the same natural isomorphism. This proves (iii) in both directions by a Hom calculation; no arbitrary head or socle preservation by an exact quotient is assumed.

**The parameter-one normalization and label bijections.** At parameter one the quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ and the costandard family is $D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ with $A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ the inverse rectification from standard to reverse-standard tableaux and $\downarrow$ the rectification in the opposite direction, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] and [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]; this gives (iv).

**Level zero.** For level $0$ the tower has $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$ by the level-zero convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], so only $\alpha=0$ and the ground class remain, consistently with the two identifications being the rank-one lattices $\mathbb ZP_\varnothing=\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$.

**The decomposition formula (i).** The formula $[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is the standard-class half of the identification of step 1.1; the coefficient dictionary $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$, $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$ is that of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and the full polynomial transition matrix, its unitriangularity and the restriction to standard simple labels are those of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. This proves (i); no off-standard label is made a simple class.

**The Chevalley operators (ii).** The residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]], and the corresponding statement on $K_0$ for projective classes is [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]; on the category-O side both statements are the integrable Fock action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] transferred by the actual natural residue comparisons. This proves (ii).

**Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set (possibly unbounded above or below), fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations, and choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and upper endpoint $r$ so that the LETTER alphabet $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and the ROOT interval $[k,r]$ contains the support of $\alpha$ and every shifted support occurring in the operations. The common-tail and double-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], shows that added bottom occupancy is maximal in every column (so every new entry is forced ground) and added top occupancy is zero, and that the monomial, bar, global and projected basis equations are unchanged on the selected finite weight set. Hence the Hecke block is the same content component of the same $H_d(m)$, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, projective and simple labels, residue projectors and residue maps, and the blockwise statements of (i)-(iv) glue along these compatible finite pieces to give the arbitrary-$I$ statement. At the level of the block decomposition of the tower, the excluded blocks for $I\ne\mathbb Z$ are real (the supported cut is proper by [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]), and no equality of $H^\Lambda$ with $\bigoplus_dH_d(m)$ is used.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 assembles the simultaneous full upper/lower integral lattice identifications and their perfect mutual pairing; step 1.2 proves the residue head/socle/indecomposability rule; step 1.3 proves the parameter-one normalization with its correctly directed label bijections; steps 2.1–2.2 prove the decomposition formula and Chevalley action; step 2.3 glues the actual same-block and full-basis maps for arbitrary consecutive $I$; and step 1.4 gives the level-zero ground line. These are all clauses of the statement.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$
acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$
carrying $r$. Over a field with $z=q_H$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and
$U_a=q_H^{c_a}$, every simultaneous generalized eigenword of $S_\lambda$ is
among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i$ modulo $e$; every such word
has the fixed node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$. The universal
triangularity also specializes to the LM deformation DVR and the generic
fibre, with no semisimplicity or affine-center premise.

$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,

$\mathsf L(A):=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple

[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module

   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced

   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is

   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.

Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+\max(d-1,0)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$ for $1\le i\le d-1$;
- $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$ for $1\le i\le d-2$;
- $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for $1\le i,j\le d-1$ with $|i-j|>1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$d\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for $d\ge1$ and every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j),\qquad s_i\longmapsto(i\ i+1);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. For $d\ge2$, the cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$. For $d=0$ the algebra $\mathbb C$ has its
degree-zero grading, and for $d=1$ the algebra $\mathbb C[x_1]$ has its
natural polynomial grading.

Let $n\ge1$. (a) The elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ act diagonally in the Young
basis of the previous item: for every standard tableau $T$ of size $n$ and
every $k$, $X_kv_T=c_T(k)v_T$, and the joint eigenspaces are
one-dimensional, indexed by the standard tableaux. (b) A vector
$\alpha=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$ occurs as the joint eigenvalue vector
of a $v_T$, equivalently $\alpha=\operatorname{Cont}(T)$ for a standard
tableau $T$, if and only if: (1) $a_1=0$; (2) for every $q>1$ at least one of
$a_q-1,a_q+1$ occurs among $a_1,\dots,a_{q-1}$; (3) if $a_p=a_q$ with $p<q$,
then both $a_p-1$ and $a_p+1$ occur among $a_{p+1},\dots,a_{q-1}$. The
association $T\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(T)$ is a bijection from the standard
tableaux of size $n$ onto this set.

Assume inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the category-O, Fock/global and quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting, the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], and the Fock data
with the four bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].

identification of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and let $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ be its projective cover in
$\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$. Work at source parameter $s=1$.

Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ of finite-dimensional

The polynomial entries and the chart conventions are those of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].

**The type-$A$ polynomial dictionary.** The explicit transition coefficients are given by the type-$A$ formulas of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]: for the right place action, $w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the entry stabilizer $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, $p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2})$, and the mixed singular/parabolic composition coefficient is the finite Levi cancellation sum $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$. Here $J$ permutes positions within columns and $K$ permutes equal entries of the sorted tuple, so their roles differ even when the subgroups coincide: for two height-one columns with entries $0,1$, both are trivial.

**The O-side multiplicity dictionary.** On the category-O side the standard module $N(B)$ has a composition series whose multiplicities with respect to the simples $L(A)$ are read off in the same chart: the coefficient of $M_B$ in the expansion of $P_A$ is the multiplicity of $L(A)$ in $N(B)$ at parameter one, in the source's reciprocal convention, by [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; combined with step 1.1 this gives $[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for all $A,B$, with $d_{A,B}$ unitriangular, and $[N(B):L(B)]=1$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ in the full square matrix.

**Transfer to the Hecke side.** By [F2] the Schur quotient is exact, sends $N(B)$ to $S(B)$, $L(A)$ to $D(A)$ for standard $A$ and kills the off-standard simples; applying it to a composition series of $N(B)$ and using [F1] gives $[S(B):D(A)]=[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, the sum being finite on each weight block. This proves (i).

**Shape of the matrix.** The full matrix $D=(d_{A,B})$ is unitriangular on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1; restricting rows to the simple labels $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ (all of which occur, and which index the simples by [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]) leaves a rectangular matrix, whose square submatrix on the standard columns is again unitriangular with diagonal entries $1$. The supported weight blocks and labels agree under the actual arbitrary-$I$ cut maps of the $G_0$ theorem, so this same coefficient calculation applies to every admitted consecutive interval. Off standard columns the equation $D(B)=0$ says precisely that $D(B)$ is not a simple module label, so the identity $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ is asserted only for $B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. This proves (ii). The statement is not that the rectangular matrix is invertible, and no off-standard simple is created.

**The polynomial coefficient is not a transposed inverse.** In the coefficient convention used in the proof, the decomposition array has rows the simple labels and columns the Specht labels, and its entries are the coefficients of $D(s)$ at $s=1$; since $R(s)=D(s)^{-1}$, its transpose is $D(s)^{-t}$, which is in general different from the $L$-in-$M$ chart $R(s)$. On the two-factor space with labels $01<10$ one has $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, so $R_{01,10}=-s$ is the negative-entry chart, whereas its inverse has $D_{01,10}=s$, while the true decomposition entry is $d_{01,10}(1)=1$: $S(10)$ is the simple $D(01)$ and not a formal negative combination. Hence with simple rows and Specht columns the decomposition matrix is the standard-row restriction of $D$; with Specht rows and simple columns it is its transpose. Neither convention uses the transpose of $R$. This completes (iii) together with step 1.2, which keeps the roles of the entry stabilizer $K$ and column Levi $J$ separate and gives the finite Levi cancellation values at parameter one; all statements are ungraded.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ in the letter alphabet $I^+$. Use the actual admissible integral-origin stable realization of the tower definition, with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$
(equivalently $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$);

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of
$\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$;

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
