**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being $\uparrow:\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and its inverse rectification $\downarrow:\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks,
intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible
finite pieces give the original arbitrary-$I$ statement. At level $0$ only
$\alpha=0$ and the ground survive.

For every $n\ge0$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ the complex Specht module $S^\lambda$
carries a nondegenerate symmetric $S_n$-invariant bilinear form
$$b(x,y)=\sum_T x_Ty_T$$
given by the coefficientwise product in the tabloid basis, so
$v\mapsto b(v,-)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb C S_n$-modules
$S^\lambda\to(S^\lambda)^*$; equivalently $S^\lambda$ is self-dual.
Consequently $\chi^\lambda(g^{-1})=\chi^\lambda(g)$ for every $g\in S_n$, that
is, every irreducible character of $S_n$ is real-valued.

Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $\lambda'$ be the
conjugate partition. Write $\Omega_\lambda$ for the finite set of
$\lambda$-tabloids and let
$$M^\lambda_F=F^{(\Omega_\lambda)},\qquad S^\lambda_F\subseteq M^\lambda_F,\qquad \kappa_t=\sum_{\gamma\in C_t}\operatorname{sgn}(\gamma)\gamma,\qquad e_t=\kappa_t\{t\}$$
be the field-valued tabloid module, the span of the polytabloids inside it,
the column antisymmetrizer, and the polytabloid of a $\lambda$-tableau $t$
([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). Let
$$\beta_F:M^\lambda_F\times M^\lambda_F\longrightarrow F$$
be the $F$-bilinear form for which the tabloid basis is orthonormal
([[def-integral-tabloid-bilinear-form-and-specht-gram-matrix]]), and for a
subspace $V\subseteq M^\lambda_F$ put
$$V^\perp:=\{x\in M^\lambda_F:\beta_F(x,v)=0\text{ for all }v\in V\}.$$

Let $\operatorname{sgn}$ be the sign representation of $S_n$ on the line
$F w$, so that $\sigma\cdot w=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)w$
([[def-sign-representation-and-restriction-of-a-representation]]), and let
$$S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$$
be the tensor product of $F[S_n]$-modules with the diagonal action
$\sigma\cdot(x\otimes w):=(\sigma\cdot x)\otimes(\sigma\cdot w)$, a
finite-dimensional $F[S_n]$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]). For a
finite-dimensional $F[S_n]$-module $D$ the **dual** is
$D^*=\operatorname{Hom}_F(D,F)$ with $(\sigma\cdot f)(v):=f(\sigma^{-1}v)$.

Fix the **row-filled** $\lambda$-tableau $t_0$, whose $i$-th row carries the
block $B_i=\{\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{i-1}+1,\dots,\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_i\}$
in increasing order, and let $t_0^{\mathsf T}$ be its transpose, a
$\lambda'$-tableau. For a $\lambda'$-tableau $u$ let $\sigma_u\in S_n$ be the
unique permutation with $\sigma_u\cdot t_0^{\mathsf T}=u$, and let
$u^{\mathsf T}$ be the transpose of $u$, a $\lambda$-tableau. Define an
$F$-linear map on the tabloid basis of $M^{\lambda'}_F$ by
$$\theta(\{u\}):=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma_u)\,\bigl(e_{u^{\mathsf T}}\otimes w\bigr) \ \in\ S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}.$$

**Lemma.** With this notation:

1. $\theta$ does not depend on the chosen representative $u$ of the tabloid
   $\{u\}$; it is a well-defined $F[S_n]$-module homomorphism
   $\theta:M^{\lambda'}_F\to S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$ with
   $\theta(\{t_0^{\mathsf T}\})=e_{t_0}\otimes w$.
2. $\theta$ is surjective and
   $\ker\theta=(S^{\lambda'}_F)^\perp$.
3. Consequently $\theta$ induces $F[S_n]$-isomorphisms
   $$M^{\lambda'}_F/(S^{\lambda'}_F)^\perp\cong S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}, \qquad\text{hence}\qquad S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\cong (S^{\lambda'}_F)^*,$$
   the second being the composite with $x\mapsto\beta_F(x,\cdot)|_{S^{\lambda'}_F}$.

No nondegeneracy of $\beta_F$ restricted to $S^{\lambda'}_F$ is assumed, and
the statement includes every prime characteristic, the case $n=0$, and the
case $F=\mathbb Q$ used in step 2.2. No step divides by a group order, none
uses positivity or averaging, and none uses characteristic zero beyond the
explicitly separated rational computation in steps 2.2 and 3.1.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Let $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$ denote the genuine continuous-dual functor of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], and write
$\mathsf L(A):=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Every finite-dimensional representation of a finite-dimensional semisimple
Lie algebra over any characteristic-zero field is completely reducible.

derivations.claim: **The sign automorphism.** The assignments $\sigma(s_r)=-s_r$ and $\sigma(x_r)=-x_r$ respect the defining relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: involution and braid relations hold for the $s_r$ and the $x_r$ commute, and the cross relation $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$ is preserved because the two minus signs in each product cancel and $1$ is fixed, while $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ is preserved the same way. Hence $\sigma$ is an algebra automorphism of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra; it maps the polynomial idempotent $e(i)$ to $e(-i)$ and therefore the block idempotent $e_\alpha$ of $H_d(m)$ to the block idempotent $e_{\alpha^t}$ of $H_d(m^t)$, giving an isomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong H^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$ that intertwines the tower inclusion and the residue projectors $u_{\alpha,i}$ with $u_{\alpha^t,-i}$; twisting modules by $\sigma$ gives exact functors that interchange residue $i$ with residue $-i$ and commute with the duality $\circledast$ (which is defined by the $x_r$- and $s_r$-fixed anti-automorphism and is therefore $\sigma$-stable).

**The transpose of multipartitions.** Write $\lambda^{(j)}_r=A(m_j+1-r,j)-(m_j+1-r)$; these ground differences give a partition in each column. Reversing components and transposing the partitions is an involution. A node $(r,c)$ in component $j$ has residue $m_j+c-r$; its transposed node has residue $-m_j+r-c$, so the content becomes $\alpha^t$. For adjacent charges put $g=m_j-m_{j+1}\ge0$, $\lambda=\lambda^{(j)}$ and $\mu=\lambda^{(j+1)}$. The aligned reverse-standard row inequalities are $\lambda_r+g\ge\mu_r$ for all $r$, whereas standard rows in the reflected shape require $\mu^{\mathsf T}_{a+g}\le\lambda^{\mathsf T}_a$ for all $a\ge1$. These conditions are equivalent: the first makes every row of $\mu$ of length at least $a+g$ a row of $\lambda$ of length at least $a$; conversely, if $\mu_r>\lambda_r+g$, take $a=\lambda_r+1$ to get $\mu^{\mathsf T}_{a+g}\ge r>\lambda^{\mathsf T}_a$. Applying this to every adjacent pair proves the bijection $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$, with inverse the same reversed-component transpose.

**Full faithfulness on all projectives and tiltings.** In the admissible stable realization the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ is fully faithful on ALL category-O projectives and on all tilting objects, the endomorphism isomorphism identifies the Hecke image algebra with the endomorphism algebra of the prinjective detector, and the category-O tilting objects are classified with a standard flag, by [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] and [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]; the Young and signed-Young images are the ones of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]]. The tilting faithfulness use is the local head/socle corner argument: a standard flag gives standard socle labels and duality gives standard head labels; the unit into the right adjoint of the corner is injective with corner-killed cokernel, and a module with only standard head labels has no nonzero map into such a cokernel. Adjunction therefore lifts every corner map uniquely. This argument uses both flags, rather than claiming that exactness alone preserves heads.

**Longest-shuffle induction duality.** Let $P$ be the affine Young subalgebra with original block sizes and $Q$ the reversed block subalgebra. Affine PBW on the right gives $H_d=\bigoplus_{u\in U}uP$, where $U$ consists of minimal right coset representatives. Its unique longest representative $r$ reverses the blocks, preserving their internal orders; its length is the number of cross-block pairs. Let $\theta:Q\to P$ relabel positions by $r^{-1}$ and let $E(\sum up_u)=p_r$. Then $E$ is right $P$-linear and $E(qh)=\theta(q)E(h)$. Indeed straightening $x_ju$ gives $ux_{u^{-1}j}$ plus shorter-permutation terms, which cannot reach the longest coset, and an internal $Q$ reflection preserves that coset with $s_jr=r\theta(s_j)$. For finite $P$-module $M$, give $M^*$ its generator-fixing dual action and transport it to $Q$ through $\theta$. The pairing $\langle a\otimes m,b\otimes\varphi\rangle=\varphi(E(b^*a)m)$ is balanced by these two identities and is contravariant.

Minimal representatives $v$ for $H_d/Q$ satisfy $vr\in U$; $E(v^{-1}u)$ is one precisely when $u=vr$ and zero otherwise. Thus the pairing matrix is a permutation matrix tensored with the ordinary perfect pairing, proving that the dual of induction is the reverse-block induction of the dual.

**The correctly normalized exterior quotient.** Choose a sufficiently low finite cut $k$, put $q_i=m_i+1-k$, $n=q_1$ and $c=n+k-1$. The ordinary parabolic ground has scalar $q_1+\cdots+q_{i-1}+m_i$, obtained from the head character $-\rho_i=\sum_{j\le i}q_j-n$ plus $c$. The finite-W tail shift is a different embedding convention and is not substituted for this character; the transported roots are nevertheless exactly $m_i=c+q_i-n$. For the transposed component partitions $\nu^{(i)}=(\lambda^{(i)})^{\mathsf T}$ form the exterior suffix module $D=\mathbb C_c\otimes\bigotimes_{i=l}^1\bigwedge^{\nu^{(i)}}(V/V_{i-1})$. Its tensor quotient $q:U=\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}\to D$ is parabolic-linear and hence finite-W-linear. Select $d$ distinct longest row names with idempotent $e_S$ and cyclic rightmost-row tensor $w$; regular evaluation identifies $H\to e_SU$, $b\mapsto wb$, with left corner action $a(wb)=w(ab)$. Therefore $K=\ker(q\,\mathrm{reg})$ is a LEFT ideal; no right-Hecke linearity of the exterior quotient is assumed.

**The Specht and reverse-standard simple comparisons.** The evaluation maps have $x_j=m+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$, so [F2] makes each evaluated Specht factor self-dual. Twisting its reflected evaluation by $\sigma$ changes $-m$ to $m$ and every Jucys transposition to its sign twist. Ordinary conjugate-Specht/sign duality, followed by the reversed-induction isomorphism of step 1.5, gives $\sigma^*S(A^t)=S(A)^\circledast$. For $A\in\mathrm{Rev}$ put $B=A^\downarrow$. The actual tilting bottom flag gives an embedding $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)=P(B)$, hence $S(A)\hookrightarrow Y(B)$ by exactness. The symmetric trace identifies a primitive projective cover $He$ with $(eH)^*$; since $Z\mapsto eZ$ is exact, this is the injective hull of its split simple top, with unique essential socle $D(B)$. Every nonzero submodule therefore contains that socle, giving $\operatorname{soc}S(A)=D(B)$: $S(A)$ is nonzero by its affine-PBW induced basis, and the socle of any nonzero submodule of this injective hull is its unique essential simple socle. Duality converts it to the simple head of $S(A)^\circledast$. Since $A^t$ is standard, the target standard-head statement and exact sign pullback now give $\sigma^*D(A^t)=D(A^\downarrow)$. No arbitrary quotient is assumed to preserve a head or socle.

**The full Young generator algebra.** For every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ put $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A):=\pi P_{\mathcal O}(A)$; by step 1.3 full faithfulness on projectives makes these nonzero indecomposable with local endomorphism rings, and makes them pairwise nonisomorphic, while for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ they are the projective covers $Y(A)$ of [F1]. If some $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ were projective, it would be a sum of standard projective covers, and full faithfulness on the distinct O-projectives $P_{\mathcal O}(A)$ would give an identification of two nonisomorphic O-projectives, a contradiction; so off-standard images are nonprojective. Taking the full finite sum $Y_{\mathrm{all}}=\bigoplus_{A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda}Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ (one representative each) and using full faithfulness on the corresponding full projective generator $Q=\bigoplus_AP_{\mathcal O}(A)$ gives $\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$, the quasihereditary Schur-cover algebra of [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]] and [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]. Summing only the standard projective covers would give a Morita generator of $H^\Lambda$, which is symmetric and not quasihereditary in general, and is not the algebra meant here.

**An explicit trace-adjoint covector.** Positions have nonincreasing original column types $t_1\ge\cdots\ge t_d$, constant inside exterior blocks $J$. Put $p=\prod_j\prod_{i<t_j}(x_j-m_i)$, $a_-=\sum_{u\in J}\operatorname{sgn}(u)u$ and $g=pa_-=a_-p=g^*$. The native right dot formula on row tensors of columns $c_j$ is $vx_j=v_{L_j}+m_{c_j}v+\sum_{h<j,c_h\ge c_j}v(hj)-\sum_{h>j,c_h<c_j}v(jh)$. Let $\phi_0$ select the all-column-one tensor with fixed row order. Process the factors of $p$ in order $j=1,\ldots,d$, then $i=1,\ldots,t_j-1$. At that stage the target columns are $t_h$ for $h<j$, $i$ at $j$, and one for $h>j$. Transposing the dot formula has no earlier swap, since $t_h\ge t_j>i$, and no later swap, since $1\le i$; its diagonal is $m_i-m_i=0$. It therefore raises exactly that column by one with coefficient one. Thus $\phi_0R_p=\phi_{\mathbf t}$. The covector $\phi_{\mathbf t}R_{a_-}$ alternates inside each exterior block and vanishes on forbidden columns, so equals $\lambda q$ for an actual exterior covector $\lambda$.

**Descent to the projected lattices at parameter one.** At parameter one the simple classes are the projected vectors $D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and the projective classes are $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; the sign and transpose maps of steps 1.1-1.2 act on these two families by the label rules $A\mapsto A^\downarrow$ for costandard vectors on $\mathrm{Rev}$ and by the inverse rectification for standard vectors, compatibly with the identification of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]. This is the projected-lattice statement of the first paragraph; the map is not asserted to permute all monomials or all simple labels of the full Fock space, since the off-standard monomials have no simple image.

**The signed full generator and Ringel duality.** Likewise put $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A):=\pi T_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$. Full faithfulness on tiltings (step 1.3) makes the full sum $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}=\bigoplus_A\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ satisfy $\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(\bigoplus_AT_{\mathcal O}(A))^{op}$, and the characteristic-tilting endomorphism algebra is the Ringel dual of the Schur-cover algebra, realized as the reversed-Levi/opposite-parabolic block via the functor $F=D\Psi$ with its explicit reverse-column shifts and $F(\overline P(A))=T_{\mathcal O}(A)$, by [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]], [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]] and [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]. For a proper original lower ideal the opposite datum is the matching highest-weight Serre quotient, not the same downset subcategory, and no unqualified longest-Borel twisting equivalence on all of $\mathcal O$ is used. Positive finite multiplicities replace the generator by a Morita-equivalent one with the same module category.

**The exact ideal kernel.** The top PBW trace $\tau$ equals $\phi_0\mathrm{reg}$: only the bounded monomial with all exponents $l-1$ and identity permutation reaches the all-column-one fixed-order tensor in top degree. Consequently $\tau(bg)=\lambda(q\,\mathrm{reg}(b))$. If $b\in K$, every $ab\in K$ and $\tau(abg)=0$ for all $a$, so nondegeneracy gives $bg=0$. Hence $H/K\to Hg$, $b+K\mapsto bg$, is well defined and surjective. The exterior row basis has size $(d!/|J|)\prod_j(l-t_j+1)$. In the truncated polynomial/permutation associated graded, with $b_j=t_j-1$, the words $uX^{\mathbf r+\mathbf b}a_-$, $u\in S_d/J$, $0\le r_j\le l-t_j$, are independent: different cosets have disjoint permutation supports and different exponent vectors have different polynomial supports. Their filtered lifts give that many independent vectors in $Hg$. Dimension comparison proves $K=\operatorname{Ann}_{\rm left}(g)$ and $H/K\cong Hg$. The bare trace adjoint has RIGHT image $gH$; applying the generator-fixing anti-involution gives the contragredient LEFT image $Hg$.
All roots may repeat, since none was divided by a difference.

**Lifting the kernel in category $\mathcal O$.** Let $T=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(I^\Lambda\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ and $E(A)=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(I^\Lambda\otimes D_0)$, with the ordinary ground $I^\Lambda$ and the exterior suffix factor $D_0$ above. Exact parabolic induction supplies $q:T\twoheadrightarrow E(A)$. Natural finite-W transport and regular evaluation identify $\pi(q)$ with the preceding exterior quotient and $\pi(R_g)$ with right multiplication by $g$. A finite total-column-degree filtration makes the nilradical act trivially on its graded finite Levi pieces; complete reducibility refines this to a standard flag of $E(A)$. The projective $T$ also has a standard flag. For any simple submodule $L$ of either standard-filtered object, choose the first flag term meeting $L$ nontrivially; simplicity gives containment there and zero intersection with the preceding term, hence an embedding of $L$ into that standard section. Its label is standard by [F3]. Every nonzero submodule has a simple socle because this is a finite-length chunk, so exactness and the nonzero standard-simple image make $\pi$ detect nonzero SUBMODULES of these two objects. This does not assert conservativity on the whole category. Since $\pi(R_g\ker q)=0$, detection gives $R_g\ker q=0$. Thus $R_g$ factors as $Fq$ with $F:E(A)\to T$. Its Schur image is the injective map $H/K\to Hg\subset H$; detection on submodules of $E(A)$ makes $F$ injective. Hence $\ker q=\ker R_g$ as actual category-$\mathcal O$ submodules.

**A genuine tilting module, not just its character.** The self-dual prinjective ground carries a perfect restricted contravariant form, and its tensor product with the natural tensor dot product gives a symmetric nondegenerate contravariant form $B_T$; Casimir and place permutations are self-adjoint, hence so is $g$. The form $B_E(qt,qu)=B_T(t,R_gu)$ is well defined by the actual kernel equality of step 4.1. If $qt$ is in its radical, self-adjointness and nondegeneracy of $B_T$ force $R_gt=0$, hence $qt=0$. It is symmetric and contravariant, and finite weight spaces make it a perfect restricted form. Thus $E(A)$ is self-dual. Dualizing its already established standard flag gives a costandard flag, so it is a tilting object; arbitrary parabolic induction has not been asserted to preserve tiltings.

**The leading tilting summand.** For a product of wedges with lengths $\nu_s$, occupation of the first $r$ coordinates is at most $\sum_s\min(r,\nu_s)=\sum_{a\le r}\lambda_a$. Equality at the highest weight forces every wedge of length at least $a$ to contain its $a$th initial coordinate; that tensor is unique. In a suffix allocation, slots can move only to later Levi blocks. If $u_{<j}$ slots originally before $j$ move to block $j$ or later, the degree before $j$ drops by $u_{<j}$, while at most $u_{<j}$ moved slots can increase the first $r$ coordinates in block $j$. Thus every resulting highest partition $\beta$ satisfies $\sum_{i<j}|\beta^{(i)}|+\sum_{a\le r}\beta_a^{(j)}\le\sum_{i<j}|\lambda^{(i)}|+\sum_{a\le r}\lambda_a^{(j)}$. Any moved slot gives a strict component boundary; equality everywhere forces the unique original leading tensor. Exact induction consequently gives $[E(A):M(A)]=1$ with all other standards strictly lower in multipartition dominance.

Tilting classification and its leading-standard triangularity then yield $E(A)=T(A)\oplus\bigoplus_{\lambda(B)<\lambda(A)}T(B)^{\oplus m_B}$. This is an actual tilting decomposition obtained after step 5.1, not a module isomorphism inferred from characters alone.

**Ordinary and signed Young extraction on ALL labels.** The ordinary cumulative-column symmetric-power objects in the full-projective copresentation proof are genuine projectives. Schur-Weyl and Specht-to-permutation dominance give their leading standard $M(A)$ once and only multipartitions strictly above $\lambda(A)$ otherwise. BGG projective triangularity therefore gives $P(A)$ once and only projectives of higher multipartition dominance. For the ordinary component types $t_1\le\cdots\le t_d$, put $p_+=\prod_j\prod_{i>t_j}(x_j-m_i)$ and let $a_+$ sum the within-row Young subgroup $J_+$. Acting on the rightmost regular tensor $w$, process $j$ from left to right and the factors at position $j$ from $i=l$ down to $t_j+1$. Earlier positions already have columns $t_h\le t_j<i$, while later ones remain in column $l\ge i$, so the native dot formula has no spectator swaps; subtracting $m_i$ leaves exactly the next left shift. Thus $wp_+$ is exactly the nondecreasing-column tensor, and $wp_+a_+$ is its within-block symmetric sum.

It belongs to the actual cumulative-column symmetric submodule $e_SZ(A)$. The map $Hp_+a_+\to e_SZ(A)$ induced by regular evaluation is injective. Its target has dimension $(d!/|J_+|)\prod_j t_j$. In the associated graded algebra the coset words $uX^{\mathbf r+\mathbf b}a_+$ with $b_j=l-t_j$, $0\le r_j<t_j$, have disjoint polynomial/permutation supports and are independent. Hence the source has at least the target dimension and is exactly that submodule. This proves $\pi Z(A)=Hp_+a_+$ locally. Under reversed transpose, the reflected charges satisfy $m_i^t=-m_{l+1-i}$. Applying $\sigma$ to the displayed ordinary product sends each factor to a unit $-1$ times $(x_j-m_i)$, and the ordinary symmetrizer becomes $a_-$. Its positional bounds become $t_1\ge\cdots\ge t_d$ and its factors exactly $i<t_j$, so its left ideal is precisely $Hg_A$ from step 2.3; transpose reverses multipartition dominance. Consequently the signed module $Hg_A$ has the triangular decomposition with leading $\sigma^*Y_{\rm all}(A^t)$ once and strictly lower terms.

Steps 3.3 and 6.2 give the SAME family of signed modules a triangular decomposition with leading $\pi T(A)$ once and strictly lower terms. Full faithfulness on projectives and tiltings makes both leading families nonzero indecomposable, pairwise nonisomorphic, with local endomorphism rings. Induct upwards through this finite dominance poset. At a minimal label both decompositions have only their leading term. At a later label the previously identified lower terms constitute the same known family (their multiplicities need not be equal); the new leading term cannot be a member of that family because each leading family is pairwise nonisomorphic. Uniqueness of indecomposable summands therefore identifies the two new leading terms, and cancellation then identifies all lower multiplicities. This proves $\pi T(A)\cong\sigma^*Y_{\rm all}(A^t)$ for ALL column-strict labels. It is not inferred only for standard labels.

**Blocks, cuts and the requested consequences.** Every map, form and kernel above commutes with central block projection; the block trace is nondegenerate. Auxiliary ground-row deletion selects the original row names and preserves the forbidden-column and exterior relations, so the natural quotient maps agree with the accepted admissible central-corner transfer. Thus the full-label comparison survives the admitted finite chunks and the reflected global cuts. On reverse-standard labels step 2.1 makes the signed image the projective cover $Y(A^\downarrow)$. The full generator endomorphism algebras are precisely those identified in steps 2.2 and 3.2; positive finite multiplicities change only the Morita generator. The restricted form makes every $T(A)$ self-dual, so the duality-compatible Schur quotient makes every signed image self-dual. The full-label sign comparison, applied in the reflected realization and using that $\sigma$ commutes with $\circledast$, then makes every ordinary Young image self-dual as well; no self-duality of an off-standard category-O projective is assumed.

**Domains.** The global sign statement lives on $I=\mathbb Z$ and on reflected auxiliary finite cuts realizing it, chosen with every charge inside the root interval; its categorical realization uses the finite bounded chunks of the bounded-chunk construction above, not a simultaneously bounded-below index set preserved by negation, and the bounded chunks realize the sign comparison through the finite double-cut identifications of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]. The two domains, global label reversal and finite-chunk categorical duality, are thus kept distinct.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 gives the sign isomorphism and the residue intertwining $i\leftrightarrow-i$; steps 1.2 and 2.1 give the transpose bijection and the Specht/simple comparison with the rectified labels; step 3.1 gives the parameter-one descent to the projected lattices; steps 2.2-3.2 identify the full Young and signed generators with the Schur-cover algebra and its Ringel dual, including the off-standard nonprojectivity and the opposite-parabolic/serre-quotient clauses; step 8.1 gives the signed-Young comparison; and step 9.1 separates the global and bounded-chunk domains. No unqualified twisting equivalence and no off-standard simple label is used.

derivations.claim: **The four monomials and the label sets.** The finite alphabet is $I^+=\{0,1\}$ and each charge-zero factor is its one-box natural module. Hence its tensor-square basis is $M_{00},M_{01},M_{10},M_{11}$. Weakly increasing rows select $00,01,11$, and weakly decreasing rows select $00,10,11$, so these are respectively $\mathrm{Std}$ and $\mathrm{Rev}$; the mixed Bruhat order is $01<10$. The actual coordinate weights are $2\delta_0,\delta_0+\delta_1,\delta_0+\delta_1,2\delta_1$; subtracting each from the vacuum weight $2\delta_0$ gives contents $0,\alpha_0,\alpha_0,2\alpha_0$. In particular $I_{\alpha_0}=\{(0)\}$ and $I_{2\alpha_0}=\{(0,0)\}$: residue sequences have length equal to tower degree, independently of the two tensor factors.

**The transition vectors and the reciprocal convention.** On this mixed space the ordinary Fock bar is $\psi M_{01}=M_{01}$ and $\psi M_{10}=M_{10}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{01}$, with coefficient bar $s\mapsto s^{-1}$. Direct substitution shows that $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$ and $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$ are bar fixed in their respective positive- and negative-power triangular charts; the endpoints and $L_{01}$ equal their monomials. Thus $M_{10}=L_{10}+sL_{01}$, and the ambient inverse-chart coefficient is $d_{01,10}=s$. Its row gives $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}=sT_{10}$. Under $t=s^{-1}$ these same formulas become $L_{10}=M_{10}-t^{-1}M_{01}$, $T_{10}=M_{10}+tM_{01}$ and $P_{01}=M_{01}+t^{-1}M_{10}$; reciprocating the parameter does not transpose the inverse transition matrix.

**The normalized projection.** The source coproduct gives $F_0M_{00}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}=T_{10}$ and $F_0T_{10}=(s+s^{-1})M_{11}$. Hence $T_{10}$ lies in the ground-generated constituent and is fixed by its normalized projection. The ground highest vector is $M_{00}$; $E_0M_{01}=M_{00}$, so $M_{01}$ is not highest. The same coproduct gives $E_0M_{10}=sM_{00}$, $F_0M_{01}=M_{11}$ and $F_0M_{10}=sM_{11}$, so both $E_0$ and $F_0$ kill $L_{10}$. Its weight is zero for $h_0$, hence it spans a trivial constituent, complementary to the three-dimensional ground constituent since $T_{10}$ and $L_{10}$ are linearly independent. Projection onto the ground constituent along this line is a module map fixing the ground, so this directly constructs the normalized projection and its off-standard kernel $\mathbb Q(s)L_{10}$. Since $T_{10}-L_{10}=(s+s^{-1})M_{01}$, applying the projection gives $D_{01}=\pi M_{01}=T_{10}/(s+s^{-1})$ and $\pi M_{10}=sD_{01}$. The endpoints are fixed, and $\pi L_{10}=0$. At $s=1$ this is the half-sum $(M_{01}+M_{10})/2$. All divisions here take place over $\mathbb Q(s)$; they do not identify the projected costandard lattice with the ambient integral monomial lattice.

**The supported blocks.** Set $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$. The defining relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$ and $x^2=0$ in the relevant degree; from $ux^2=0$ and the cross relations one obtains $y^2u=x+y$, hence $y^2=(x+y)u$, and reducing the relation $y^2=(x+y)u$ decreases the $y$-exponent while killing $x$-exponents at least $2$, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-$2$ algebra. Map these generators to $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, to $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ on $B_+=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$, and to $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $B_-=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$; direct matrix computation verifies $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $x^2=0$, $ux=yu-1$ and $uy=xu+1$ in all three factors. The central element $z=x+y$ has images $0$, $1+2\epsilon$ and $-1+2\epsilon$, and the Hermite polynomials $E_0=(1-z^2)^2$, $E_\pm=(1-E_0\pm(3z-z^3)/2)/2$ map to the three separate identities; each factor is generated by its images of $x$ and $u$, so the map from the span of the eight words onto the eight-dimensional product is surjective and hence, by the spanning bound, an isomorphism. The $I=\{0\}$ spectral content cut keeps the factor $M_2(\mathbb C)$ at content $2\alpha_0$ and discards the adjacent-content factors, so the supported degree-$2$ block is $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with simple dimension $2$; degree one is $\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ with simple dimension $1$ at content $\alpha_0$, and degree zero is $\mathbb C$. To verify vanishing independently of categorification, suppose an all-zero-residue supported module exists in degree at least three. Its restriction to the first two strands lies in the displayed $M_2$ factor, hence $x_2=-x_1$ and $x_1^2=0$. Since $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$, it also commutes with $x_2$. The affine recursion gives $x_3=s_2x_2s_2+s_2=x_2+s_2$. But a commuting sum of a square-zero operator and an involution has generalized eigenvalues only $1,-1$: on the two $s_2$ eigenspaces it is $\pm1+x_2$, each invertible with inverse $\pm1-x_2$. This contradicts the nilpotence required by residue zero for $x_3$. Every nonzero finite-dimensional algebra has its nonzero regular module, so no such supported algebra exists in degree three or higher.

**The decomposition matrix by intrinsic modules.** The intrinsic affine-induced Specht presentation in [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] gives, for either single-box label $01$ or $10$, the degree-one module $H_1/H_1x=\mathbb C$; the two different singleton components have the same charge zero. For $11$, with one box in each component, it gives $H_2/(H_2x+H_2y)$, since the inducing algebra is the polynomial algebra on the two strand variables and both act as zero on its one-dimensional inducing module. In the three factors of step 2.2, $x,y$ generate the whole left ideal in $B_+$ and $B_-$ because $y-x=\pm1$; in the matrix factor $y=-x=-N$, so the quotient is $M_2/M_2N$. Here $M_2N$ consists of matrices with first column zero, and the first-column map identifies the quotient with the defining simple $\mathbb C^2$. The degree-zero Specht is $\mathbb C$. Thus each of these four Spechts is the indicated simple, directly giving the displayed $3\times4$ multiplicity matrix. Independently step 1.2 gives $d_{01,10}(1)=1$ and identity on standard columns, so these actual multiplicities agree with [F1]. There is one simple in each of the three supported blocks by step 2.2, so there is no additional simple $D_{10}$. The standard square submatrix is the identity; the rectangular matrix is not asserted invertible.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1-3.1 verify the transition, projection and decomposition statements, including the inverse-chart entry $d_{01,10}(1)=1$ in place of any negative transposed-inverse value, the identity on standard columns and the absence of an off-standard simple $D_{10}$; step 2.2 verifies the block dimensions $1,1,2$ at contents $0,\alpha_0,2\alpha_0$ of the supported tower and the vanishing of higher supported degrees. The two further adjacent-residue degree-$2$ blocks of the full algebra are outside this supported window and are treated in the companion showcase; no unprojected monomial is used as a simple class.

Assume inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the category-O, Fock/global and quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting, the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], and the Fock data
with the four bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].
For $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ let $D(A)$ be the simple module of the
identification of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and let $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ be its projective cover in
$\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$. Work at source parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The assignment $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ is an isomorphism from the split
Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ of finite-dimensional
projective modules onto the standard highest weight lattice
$V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$,
so $\{P_A\}$ is a $\mathbb Z$-basis; at parameter one the source vector $P_A$
coincides with $T_{A^\uparrow}$, and the lattice is integrally generated by its
ground vector under divided powers.

**(ii)** Under the identifications (i) and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
the map $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\to G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ induced
by the embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules is the
natural injective inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$
of the standard lattice into the full costandard lattice.

**(iii)** The Cartan Hom pairing becomes the normalized highest pairing: with
the projected simple vectors $D_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B$ one has
$C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; these are projected simple vectors, not an
unqualified identification of monomials with simples.

**(iv)** Both residue functors $e_i$ and $f_i$ on projective modules induce
operators on $K_0$ that are the Chevalley operators adjoint to their $G_0$
operators of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]].

**(v)** The left adjoint $\pi^*$ of the Schur quotient is right exact on all
modules, sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives and recovers the
standard-labelled prinjectives; exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules is
neither asserted nor needed.

For an arbitrary admitted consecutive $I$, use the compatible finite cuts and the intrinsic Hecke identity of the $G_0$ theorem. They identify the projective covers and the lower integral basis $P_A$ on every selected content. Consequently (i)–(iv) hold for the full supported tower, including unbounded intervals; clause (v) concerns the Schur functor in each actual stable realization.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative $k$-algebra. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent all isomorphism classes of simple left $A$-modules, and let $q_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite-dimensional projective covers. Then $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$ and $[S_1],\ldots,[S_t]$ are bases of $K_0(A)$ and $G_0(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_A=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_A(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ In particular, if $\operatorname{End}_A(S_i)=k$ for every $i$, these bases are dual.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra, let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent the graded-simple shift orbits and let $p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite graded projective covers. Here graded-simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero graded submodule. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. Neither pairing statement asserts unimodularity of the projective-to-module Cartan map or of a projective/projective Cartan matrix. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebra. For a
finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and finite-dimensional left
$A$-module $M$, define the object-level value

$$h(P,M):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,M).$$

If $A$ is $\mathbb Z$-graded and $P,M$ are finite-dimensional graded left $A$-modules,
with $P$ projective in the degree-zero graded category, define

$$h_{\mathrm{gr}}(P,M):=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}v^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M),$$

where $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M)$ consists of $A$-linear maps sending each
$P_i$ into $M_{i+d}$. These are candidate values on object isomorphism
classes; no descent to pairings on $K_0\times G_0$ is asserted here.

derivations.claim: **The degree-one block.** For $I=\{0\}$, level $2$ and charge $(0,0)$ the degree-one cyclotomic quotient is $H^{(0,0)}_1=\mathbb C[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ by the level-two instance of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], and it is already supported, so $B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ with $x=x_1$. Its radical is $(x)$ and its quotient is $\mathbb C$, so $B$ is local; the unique simple is $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ with $x\mapsto0$, the regular module $Y_{01}=B$ is its projective cover, and the regular composition series $0\subset(x)\subset B$ has successive quotients $D_{01},D_{01}$, giving $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$ in $G_0$. Every $B$-linear map $B\to D_{01}$ is determined by the image of $1$, so $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{01},D_{01})=1$.

**The symmetric form on $B$ and self-duality.** The coefficient functional $\tau(a+bx)=b$ is a symmetrizing trace on $B$: it is linear, $\tau(uv)=\tau(vu)$ for all $u,v$ (both sides pick out the $x$-coefficient of the product), and its radical is zero because $\tau(x)\ne0$, so the associated form $\langle u,v\rangle=\tau(uv)$ has matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ in the basis $(1,x)$, which is nonsingular. The anti-involution $\ast$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] that fixes $x$ is the identity of $B$ here, so the form is generator-fixing, and it exhibits an isomorphism $Y_{01}\cong Y_{01}^{\circledast}$: the dual of the regular module with respect to the trace. This is the actual symmetric-algebra proof of cover self-duality, not an inference from self-duality of the head.

**The degree-two block and its simple.** With $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$ the relations give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$, $x^2=0$, and from $ux^2=0$ one gets $y^2=(x+y)u$, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-two algebra; the models $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ and $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ satisfy all relations, and $z=x+y$ is central with images $0,1+2\epsilon,-1+2\epsilon$; the Hermite polynomials $E_0=(1-z^2)^2$, $E_\pm=(1-E_0\pm(3z-z^3)/2)/2$ map to the separate factor identities. Each factor is generated by its images of $x,u$, so the homomorphism is onto the eight-dimensional product; the eight-word spanning bound proves that the span of the eight words is isomorphic to $M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$. The supported content cut at $2\alpha_0$ keeps the factor $M_2(\mathbb C)$; its simple module $\mathbb C^2$ has Gram matrix $J$, since $N^{t}J=JN$ and $(-J)^{t}J=J(-J)$, and it is self-dual and projective, so its projective cover is itself and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$; degree $0$ contributes $\mathbb C$, and Hom-spaces between distinct content blocks vanish because they are different blocks. In particular the one-dimensional Fock weight vector $M_{11}$ is not the two-dimensional module $D_{11}$, and the degree-two projective cover has vector-space dimension $2$ and composition length $1$. Higher supported degrees vanish directly: in an all-zero-residue module on at least three strands, restriction to strands $1,2$ forces $x_2=-x_1$ and $x_1^2=0$ by the matrix factor. Since $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$, it commutes with $x_2$, and the recursion gives $x_3=x_2+s_2$. On either $s_2$ eigenspace this is $x_2\pm1$, which is invertible, contradicting nilpotence of $x_3$ at residue zero. Thus such a nonzero module cannot exist; applying this to the regular module proves the supported algebra is zero in every degree at least three.

**The projected dual bases at parameter one.** In the tensor square at parameter one, $fM_{00}=M_{01}+M_{10}$, $f(M_{01}+M_{10})=2M_{11}$, and $e$ reverses these moves with coefficients $2,1$. Hence the ground constituent has basis $P_{00},P_{01},P_{11}$ as displayed, and its complementary trivial line is $M_{10}-M_{01}$. Projection along this line gives $D_{01}=\pi M_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$ and fixes the endpoints. The normalized form is determined by $C_0(M_{00},M_{00})=1$, $e/f$ adjunction and orthogonality of distinct weights: $C_0(P_{01},P_{01})=C_0(M_{00},eP_{01})=2$, and $2C_0(P_{11},P_{11})=C_0(P_{01},eP_{11})=2$. Thus the mixed vector is $P_{01}=M_{01}+M_{10}$ of $C_0$-norm $2$, so the correct field dual is $D_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$, and the endpoint vectors satisfy $P_{00}=D_{00}=M_{00}$ and $P_{11}=D_{11}=M_{11}$. The Gram matrix in the $D$-basis is $\operatorname{diag}(1,\tfrac12,1)$, and multiplying its first-argument basis by $\operatorname{diag}(1,2,1)$ gives the identity matrix, which is the pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; this directly computes the parameter-one projected-simple dictionary of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]], not an identification of $L_{01}=M_{01}$ with the simple.

**The categorified residue operators.** In these all-zero-residue blocks the residue projectors are the identities, so the bimodules are the explicit tower-inclusion bimodules. Induction from degree $0$ to the degree-one block gives the regular module of $B$; the supported induction from $B$ to the degree-two block $M_2(\mathbb C)$ sends the simple $\mathbb C$ to $\mathbb C^2$ and the regular module $B$ to $M_2(\mathbb C)$, which is two copies of the simple $\mathbb C^2$; explicitly $M_2\otimes_B\mathbb C=M_2/M_2N$ has dimension two and is the unique matrix-factor simple, whereas $M_2\otimes_B B=M_2$; restriction of $\mathbb C^2$ to $B$ is the regular Jordan module $B$ itself (the generator $x$ of $B$ acts on $\mathbb C^2$ as $N$ with $N^2=0$ and $\dim\ker N=1$), and restriction of $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ to degree zero is the one-dimensional $\mathbb C$-module. The right $B$-module $M_2$ is free of rank two: each row is a regular $B$-module for right multiplication by $N$, so these induction functors are exact directly. These explicit bimodules realize the residue functors of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]] and yield the displayed columns $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$, $fD_{11}=0$ and $eD_{00}=0$, $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$; equivalently, in the $D$-basis, $f$ has columns $(0,2,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,0,1)^{\mathsf T},0$ and $e$ has columns $0,(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,2,0)^{\mathsf T}$, so $[e,f]=ef-fe$ is $\operatorname{diag}(2,0,-2)$ in the $sl_2$-normalization of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]].

**The normalized finite identifications.** On projective classes the same bimodules give $f[Y_{00}]=[Y_{01}]$, $f[Y_{01}]=2[Y_{11}]$, $e[Y_{01}]=2[Y_{00}]$ and $e[Y_{11}]=[Y_{01}]$. On simple classes they give step 4.1. Therefore the maps $[Y_A]\mapsto P_A$ and $[D_A]\mapsto D_A$ intertwine both $e$ and $f$ with the explicit Fock matrices of step 3.1 and send the degree-zero class to the normalized ground. Over $\mathbb Q$ each module is ground generated, so these normalized intertwining maps are unique; consequently they agree with any named categorification identification with that normalization, rather than assuming a general bridge to establish this finite instance. Each cover/simple Hom space within a block has dimension one, by step 1.1 and the scalar endomorphism ring in step 2.2, while different degrees give zero Hom in the tower direct sum. Exactness of Hom from a projective makes the pairing additive on short exact sequences, so the pairing matrix is the identity on these bases. Its vector realization is precisely $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ from step 3.1, and the composition Cartan matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(1,2,1)$.

**The index-two lattice and its cyclicity.** The divided powers $f^{(2)}=f^2/2$ and $e^{(2)}=e^2/2$ give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$, and the displayed matrices preserve evenness of the $D_{01}$-coordinate whenever the input has that coordinate even, so the lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$, their divided powers and the toral operators at weights $2,0,-2$. It is generated from the ground because $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$ and $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$. Its elements have $D_{01}$-coordinate even, so it does not contain $D_{01}$; hence it is a proper integral submodule containing the ground, of index $2$ in the full costandard lattice, and $D_{01}$ is not in the integral ground-generated span. Over $\mathbb Q$ division by $2$ is available, so the ground vector generates the whole three-dimensional costandard space; the standard lattice is by step 5.1 the lattice with basis $(P_{00},P_{01},P_{11})$, which is integrally generated by its ground under the divided powers and pairs perfectly with the full costandard lattice by step 3.1. This proves that integral costandard generation fails while the full integral duality and the standard divided-power statement survive.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 verify the degree-one cover, its composition length against its Hom dimension, and the symmetric-form self-duality; step 2.2 and step 3.1 verify the degree-two block, the projected dual bases and the pairing identity; step 4.1 verifies the residue operators, their commutator and the categorified $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$; step 6.1 verifies the exact index-two lattice, its stability, its failure to contain $D_{01}$ and the rational cyclicity. No step identifies the simple image with the unprojected monomial $L_{01}$, and no self-duality is inferred from the head alone.

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+\max(d-1,0)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$ for $1\le i\le d-1$;
- $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$ for $1\le i\le d-2$;
- $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for $1\le i,j\le d-1$ with $|i-j|>1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$d\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for $d\ge1$ and every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j),\qquad s_i\longmapsto(i\ i+1);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. For $d\ge2$, the cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$. For $d=0$ the algebra $\mathbb C$ has its
degree-zero grading, and for $d=1$ the algebra $\mathbb C[x_1]$ has its
natural polynomial grading.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H_0(\mathbf a)=\mathbb C$ for $d=0$, and for $d\ge1$ is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) subject to
$$T_r^2=(z-1)T_r+z,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1),$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

**Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients.** For a monic polynomial
$f(u)=u^{\ell}+a_{\ell-1}u^{\ell-1}+\dots+a_0$ in $A[u]$ of degree $\ell$
impose the single relation $f(X_1)=0$ (respectively $f(x_1)=0$) on the FIRST
polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention
imposed here (cyclotomic relation on $X_1$, and later induction appending on
the right) is the one used on this page.

**The charged cyclic specialization.** Let $A=F$ be a field, let
$z=q_H\in F^{\times}$ have finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the cyclic **label set** of residues, with a
dominant cyclic type-A weight $(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and
$\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). If $q_H\ne1$ use the
nondegenerate presentation and put $c_i:=q_H^{\,i}$; if $q_H=1$ (which forces
$\operatorname{char}F=e$) use the degenerate presentation and put
$c_i:=i\cdot1_F$. Impose
$$f(z_1):=\prod_{i\in I}(z_1-c_i)^{\lambda_i},\qquad f(z_1)=0.$$
on the first generator ($z_1=X_1$ in the nondegenerate branch and $z_1=x_1$ in
the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

**Well-definedness notes.** The nondegenerate parameters $c_i=q_H^i$ are
distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes
$i\cdot1_F\ne j\cdot1_F$ for $0\le i<j<e$. In the nondegenerate branch no
embedding of the label set $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ into $F$ is claimed or used:
$i$ is only a label for the value $q_H^i$. All these definitions are given by
generators, relations and a two-sided quotient ideal and use no choice
principle.

derivations.claim: In the degenerate quotient $x_1=m$ and $sx_2=ms+1$ give $x_2=m+s$. Hence the quotient is generated by $s$ with $s^2=1$. Conversely the assignments $x_1\mapsto m$, $x_2\mapsto m+s$, $s\mapsto s$ in $\mathbb C[s]/(s^2-1)$ satisfy both cross relations and commutativity, so they define an inverse to the map sending $s$ into the quotient. Evaluation at $s=1,-1$ identifies this algebra with $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, with inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(a+b)/2+(a-b)s/2$. In particular it has no nonzero nilpotents and has precisely the two one-dimensional simple modules $s=1,-1$.

At $\xi=-1$, step 1.2 and [F1] give $H_{-1}(2)=\mathbb C[T]/((T+1)^2)$. Setting $\varepsilon=T+1$ identifies it with $B=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$, whose basis is $1,\varepsilon$ by division by the monic polynomial $\varepsilon^2$. Thus $\varepsilon$ is nonzero and nilpotent. Every $a+b\varepsilon$ with $a\ne0$ has inverse $a^{-1}-ba^{-2}\varepsilon$; those with $a=0$ are nonunits. Consequently $(\varepsilon)$ is the unique maximal ideal and is the nonzero radical. Every simple $B$-module is killed by $\varepsilon$: its image under this central operator is a submodule, and if the image were the whole nonzero simple module, its square could not vanish. The unique simple is therefore $B/(\varepsilon)\cong\mathbb C$.

The two algebras cannot be isomorphic: an isomorphism would send the nonzero square-zero element of step 2.1 to a nonzero nilpotent in the algebra of step 1.1. Their decomposition behavior also differs directly. The regular module of $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$ is the direct sum of its two simples. The regular module $B$ has the filtration $0\subset(\varepsilon)\subset B$ with both subquotients equal to its unique simple; it is indecomposable since an idempotent $a+b\varepsilon$ satisfies $a^2=a$ and $2ab=b$, forcing it to be $0$ or $1$. Thus even projective and simple classes cannot be identified across these two specializations by algebra transport.

Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 disprove the claimed universal algebra transport and step 2.2 exhibits its failure in a concrete comparison formula. The witness uses the entire rank-two algebras, with the degenerate full integer residue set; it is not a comparison with a supported cut retaining only the charge $m$. For a finite degenerate cut containing this entire example the root interval must contain $m-1,m,m+1$, since $x_2=m\pm1$ on its two simples. The calculation is choice-free and entirely over $\mathbb C$. It neither extends characteristic-zero canonical-basis identifications to positive characteristic nor replaces the separate root-of-unity comparison and grading theorems.

In the nondegenerate level-one quotient [F3], $X_1=Q$ and $X_2=Q\xi^{-1}T^2$, so it is generated by $T$. Conversely in the finite algebra $H_\xi(2)$ of [F1], $T^{-1}=\xi^{-1}(T-(\xi-1))$. The assignments $X_1\mapsto Q$, $X_2\mapsto Q\xi^{-1}T^2$, $T\mapsto T$ therefore give commuting units satisfying $TX_1T=\xi X_2$ and the cyclotomic relation. They define the inverse of the map from $H_\xi(2)$ into the quotient: both composites fix $T,X_1,X_2$ and their inverses. Hence the whole nondegenerate level-one rank-two quotient is exactly $H_\xi(2)$ for every $\xi\ne0$ and $Q=\xi^m$. This uses only the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions, not a finite-$e$ theorem in the generic branch.

At rank two the limitation can be seen in an actual comparison formula. For $\xi\ne-1$ put $a=(\xi-1)/2$ and $b=(\xi+1)/2$. The map $T\mapsto a+bs$ respects [F1] because its values at $s=1,-1$ are $\xi,-1$; its inverse is $s\mapsto(T-a)/b$, since the quadratic relation implies $(T-a)^2=b^2$. At $\xi=-1$ this inverse is undefined and the specialized map sends $T$ to $-1$, killing the nonzero element $T+1$. This explicit generic comparison therefore does not specialize to an isomorphism. Other rank-two parameters can yield isomorphisms, including some roots of unity; that does not repair the universal assertion.
